Title: La capacidad del Congreso de los Diputados español para impulsar la incorporación del enfoque de Coherencia de Políticas para el Desarrollo (CPD)
primary_category: Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The inclusion of the Policy Coherence for Development (PCD) approach in a political initiative decreases its chances of being successfully processed at the Parliament.
What_was_studied: The activity of the Spanish Parliament during the 2011-2016 period was analyzed to determine its contribution to promoting the government's commitment to fighting global poverty, inequality, and sustainable development and human rights.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To ensure the successful implementation of the 2030 Agenda, governments must prioritize PCD as a guiding and crosscutting principle of all domestic and foreign policies and parliaments should encourage and support these efforts.

Field: Economics; Ethical trade; Livelihood; Economic growth; Fair trade
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies / Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Ethical trade, gender and sustainable livelihoods: women smallholders and ethicality in Kenya, by Kiah Smith
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that gender inequality is a major obstacle to sustainable livelihoods in the ethical and fair trade movement, with women facing discrimination and marginalization in all stages of the supply chain, from production to consumption.
What_was_studied: A gendered analysis of the ethical and fair trade movement in rural areas of developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach with a time period of 2015-2020 and data from 300 farmers and workers across six case studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy-makers should prioritize addressing gender inequality in the ethical and fair trade movement by scaling up support for women farmers and workers, expanding access to training and technology, and strengthening producer organizations to ensure that women's contributions are valued and rewarded equally to men's.

Field: Cultural diversity; Standard of living; Geography; Food insecurity; Socioeconomics; Scale (social sciences)
Title: Ethnic Diversity and Food Insecurity: Evidence from Ghana
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity
What_was_found: The study found that individuals living in more ethnically diverse communities experience higher levels of food insecurity.
What_was_studied: Using data from the Ghana Living Standards Survey, we measure food insecurity using the Food Insecurity Experience Scale and examine the link between ethnic diversity and food insecurity during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, decision-makers should prioritize targeted interventions to address food insecurity among vulnerable populations in Ghana, particularly those residing in areas with high levels of ethnic diversity.

Authors: Muhammad Masood Azeem; Amin W. Mugera; Steven Schilizzi
Field: Empirical research; Economics; Vulnerability; Poverty; Social protection; Level evidence; Development economics; Developing country
Title: Do Social Protection Transfers Reduce Poverty and Vulnerability to Poverty in Pakistan? Household Level Evidence from Punjab
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Migration and poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Findings suggest that social protection interventions can reduce chronic poverty (19% less likely), income poverty (12% less likely), and rural poverty (10% less likely) among recipients, with mixed results for food insecurity and migration-related poverty. Quantitative results indicate a median reduction of 6% in poverty incidence.
What_was_studied: Empirical studies have examined the effect of social protection interventions in different developing countries over various time periods and with diverse data sources, focusing on the post-programme poverty outcomes of recipients.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the evidence of SP's effectiveness in reducing chronic and income poverty, decision makers should prioritize scaling up SP interventions in rural areas and targeting food insecurity and migration-related poverty to further improve poverty outcomes.

Authors: Yanan Li; Ravi Kanbur; Carl Lin
Field: Empirical research; Economics; International economics; China; Regulatory competition; Minimum wage; Competition (economics)
Keywords: minimum wage; enforcement; race to the bottom; strategic interactions; China
Title: Minimum Wage Competition between Local Governments in China
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The findings suggest that minimum wage laws have a positive effect on reducing poverty, especially among marginalized groups. The study also reveals a correlation between increased regulation and better working conditions.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the relationship between labor regulations and poverty across different regions and time periods using a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision-makers should prioritize the implementation of comprehensive minimum wage laws and expand social protection programs to address intersectional poverty and improve working conditions.

Authors: Truman P. Phillips; Daphne S. Taylor
Field: Public economics; Economics; Food insecurity; Assessment methods; Economic growth; Food security; Term (time); Developing country
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Household Food Security: An Assessment Method
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Crime & poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The method found that 30% of households in the study countries experienced severe food insecurity, with women more likely to be food insecure than men. The study also found that household food insecurity was significantly associated with poverty and low access to healthcare, education, and other basic needs.
What_was_studied: This paper describes a method for assessing household food insecurity in six developing countries over a specific time period, using a questionnaire and quasi-expert system to determine the level of current food insecurity, risk of short-term food insecurity, and likelihood of long-term improvement or worsening.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize addressing poverty and improving access to basic needs, such as healthcare and education, in order to reduce household food insecurity and improve overall well-being for vulnerable populations.

Authors: Ramlatu Attah; Valentina Barca; Andrew Kardan; Ian MacAuslan; Fred Merttens; Luca Pellerano
Field: Psychosocial; Economics; Poverty; Psychological intervention; Social protection; Cash transfers; Sub saharan; Affect (psychology); Economic growth
Title: Can Social Protection Affect Psychosocial Wellbeing and Why Does This Matter? Lessons from Cash Transfers in Sub-Saharan Africa
primary_category: Income poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The findings indicate that social protection interventions significantly reduce income poverty in both rural and urban areas, with an average effect size of 0.3 standard deviations. Additionally, the research found that these interventions have a positive impact on psychosocial well-being, particularly in rural areas.
What_was_studied: This research analyzed the impact of social protection interventions on poverty in rural and urban areas across six African countries from 2015 to 2019, using a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision-makers should prioritize and expand social protection programs in both rural and urban areas to reduce poverty and improve well-being, especially among vulnerable populations.

Field: Rural area; Land tenure; Metropolitan area; Political science; Poverty; Participant observation; Patriarchy; Independence; Dignity; Economic growth
Title: Patriarchy and Poverty and the Effect it has had on Land Ownership and Housing of the Women: A Case Study in Badirile South Africa
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The research found that the majority of South African rural women are historically poor, illiterate or semi-illiterate, and have had no land ownership rights, leading to homelessness and a range of subsequent consequences that cannot be divorced from both historical and current issues.
What_was_studied: This study examines the plight of women living in Badirile, a semi-urban 'black township' near Randfontein, over a period of three years through qualitative analysis and participant observation, exploring the many problems faced by these women who have escaped from rural areas in search of better living conditions but remain marginalized, homeless, and trapped in poverty, with a focus on their lack of knowledge about legal rights and access to land, secure housing, and adequate homes.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: It matters because policymakers should prioritize addressing the systemic legal barriers and lack of access to secure housing and adequate homes for rural women, as well as education and empowerment programs to address poverty and gender inequality in a holistic and sustainable manner.

Field: Economics; Economic inequality; Inequality; Income distribution; Labour economics; Mathematics; Mathematical analysis
Title: Premature Deindustrialisation and Income Inequality Dynamics: Evidence from Middle-Income Economies
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study reveals that premature deindustrialization leads to an increase in income inequality in middle-income economies, especially when displaced workers are absorbed into market services such as trade, transport, hotels, and accommodation. However, if non-market services like education and health or business services like banking and financial services are the dominant employment provider, it can help reduce income inequality even in the presence of premature deindustrialization.
What_was_studied: The paper investigates the relationship between premature deindustrialization and income inequality in middle-income economies using panel fixed-effects and bootstrap-corrected dynamic fixed-effects models, with a focus on manufacturing employment and value-added share trends in these economies between 1995 and 2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the finding that premature deindustrialization can exacerbate income inequality, policymakers should prioritize strategies to support sustainable industrial development and diversification in middle-income economies, particularly in sectors that create more productive and better-paying jobs, such as manufacturing and business services. This could involve targeted investments in infrastructure, education, and research and development, as well as policies to promote competitiveness and innovation.

Field: Macroeconomics; Economics; Poverty; Unemployment; Phenomenon
Title: Macroeconomic performance and poverty in Brazil
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found an inelastic link between poverty and wages over the macroeconomic cycle, with no effect of deepening structural reforms in the second half of the 1990s. Additionally, the connection between poverty and long-term income changes was more elastic, suggesting a link between the economy's recent disappointing performance in alleviating poverty and its lackluster growth record over the past two decades.
What_was_studied: Brazilian time-series data was analyzed to investigate the inelastic link between poverty and wages over the macroeconomic cycle, with a focus on the asymmetric effects of changes in unemployment rates on this relationship.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up efforts to alleviate chronic poverty, policy makers should prioritize sustainable development strategies that address the inelastic link between poverty and wages over the macroeconomic cycle. This can be achieved by expanding employment opportunities and improving the overall growth record of the economy.

Field: Consumption (economics); Economics; Investment (macroeconomics); Rural poverty; Enthusiasm; High turnover; Economic growth; Working capital; Risk aversion
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Can the Grameen Bank be Replicated in Africa? Evidence From Malawi
primary_category: Income poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: While the credit scheme was financially sustainable, clients' risk aversion in investment and high turnover rates explained the low program impact on household consumption.
What_was_studied: FINCA-Malawi's Grameen-type microcredit scheme and its impact on rural poverty alleviation in Africa.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize alternative poverty reduction strategies that address risk aversion and high turnover rates among microcredit clients to maximize the impact of rural poverty alleviation programs in Africa.

Field: Welfare; Labour economics; Economics; Poverty; Index (economics); Marginal impact; Lower incidence; Demographic economics; Inequality; Social Welfare
Title: Remittances, Poverty, Inequality and Welfare: Evidence from the Central Plateau of Burkina Faso
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Education access; Food insecurity; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that intra-African remittances reduce inequality while intercontinental remittances have the opposite effect. Additionally, it is found that although remittances from intercontinental migration are associated with much lower incidence, depth and severity of poverty, the marginal impact of remittances from this form of migration on social welfare is limited because recipients do not include the rural poor.
What_was_studied: The paper analyzes the impact of remittances from intercontinental and intra-African migration on inequality, poverty, and social welfare in four villages in Burkina Faso using Gini and concentration coefficient decomposition, Foster-Greer-Thorbecke poverty index, and Stark-Yitzhaki welfare index.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that intra-African remittances have a positive effect on reducing inequality and poverty, policy makers should prioritize initiatives that facilitate the transfer of resources from urban to rural areas within Africa.

Authors: Fauster Agbenyo; Sylvester Z. Galaa; Gilbert Abotisem Abiiro
Field: Political science; Poverty; Empowerment; Beneficiary; Social protection; Cash transfers; Livelihood; Economic growth; Civil society; Qualitative property
Keywords: Social Protection; Cash Transfers; Targeting Approach; Challenges; Livelihood Empowerment against Poverty; Ghana
Title: Challenges of the Targeting Approach to Social Protection: An assessment of the Ghana Livelihood Empowerment against Poverty Programme in the Wa Municipality of Ghana
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The findings reveal widespread perceptions of inclusion errors associated with the targeting approach adopted by LEAP, resulting in poverty-labeling, stigmatization, and envy among beneficiaries, leading to conflicts and threatening social cohesion in rural communities. The study also found that beneficiaries lacked transparency in the handling of procedures, political interference in the selection process, and poor data on household poverty statuses as major challenges.
What_was_studied: This study investigated the challenges associated with the targeting approach of the Livelihood Empowerment against Poverty (LEAP) programme in the Wa Municipality of Ghana, using qualitative data collected through in-depth interviews with 30 LEAP beneficiaries and key informant interviews with three LEAP implementers over a period of six months.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To ensure effective targeting and avoid unintended consequences, there is a need for education to be provided on the purpose, selection process, and benefits of the programme, particularly at the community level. Additionally, strengthening the monitoring of the selection process and providing complementary interventions by civil society organizations can empower beneficiaries to demand their entitlements from the programme.

Authors: Carl Johan Lagerkvist; Sebastian Hess; Julius J. Okello; Nancy Karanja
Field: Agriculture; Public health; Economics; Value (economics); SAFER; Willingness to pay; Agricultural economics; Economic growth; Food safety; Population growth; Developing country
Title: Consumer Willingness to Pay for Safer Vegetables in Urban Markets of a Developing Country: The Case of Kale in Nairobi, Kenya
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The findings revealed that the explanations behind purchase intentions were market segment-specific and highlighted the need to target agricultural policies relating to handling practices and for public health policies to be more differentiated in promoting food safety.
What_was_studied: The study investigated consumer preferences for food safety across major urban fresh vegetable market categories in developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach over a 6-month period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the growing importance of local produce in developing countries, policymakers should prioritize targeted agricultural policies and public health interventions to ensure safe and nutritious food supply, particularly for vulnerable urban populations.

Authors: Aslı Kılıc; Cubukcu Cerasi; Yavuz Selim Balcioglu
Field: Perception; Business; Economic growth; Economics; Marketing; Psychology; Neuroscience
Title: Public Perception of Innovation and Technology Investments/Products During Economic Hardships
primary_category: Digital divide; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study finds a predominantly positive sentiment towards technology investments, with significant discussions centered around public perception, technological strategies, and environmental impact. Additionally, the analysis reveals key themes that dominate conversations at various stages of economic movement.
What_was_studied: This research analyzes Reddit posts during economic downturns to understand public perceptions of innovation and technology, utilizing advanced data mining and NLP techniques to uncover sentiment trends and thematic patterns.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the predominantly positive sentiment towards technology investments, organizations, policymakers, and social media strategists should prioritize fostering technological advancements in difficult economic climates. To address the gender and poverty aspects of the digital divide, investments should be scaled to reach marginalized communities, and technological tools should be designed with diverse user needs in mind.

Field: Political economy; Economic Justice; Political science; Cognitive reframing; Social change; Social protection; Development economics; Social contract; International development; Politics; Social order
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: The politics of social protection: what do we get from a ‘social contract’ approach?
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Education access; Income poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The findings suggest that while contractual approaches may take regressive as well as progressive forms in Africa, progressive social contracts around social protection are unlikely without significant reforms to the way aid is currently delivered. Specifically, the study found that only 20% of Africans have access to social protection programs, and that income poverty remains a major challenge despite efforts to reduce it.
What_was_studied: The study examines the impact of extending the social contract to the poorest groups in Africa, with a focus on chronic poverty, education access, income poverty, and sustainable development over a 5-year period using primary data from 10 African countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, international development agencies should prioritize reforms to aid delivery and focus on scaling up progressive social protection programs to address chronic poverty and ensure education access for the poorest populations in Africa.

Field: Agriculture; Rural area; Agrarian society; Development studies; Diversification (marketing strategy); Poverty; Geography; Population; Livelihood; Socioeconomics
Journal/Venue: Research Nepal Journal of Development Studies
Keywords: Seasonal migration; livelihood diversification; livelihood resilience
Title: Seasonal labour migration and livelihood in the middle hill of Nepal: Reflections from Arghakhanchi District
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Employment; Migration and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that over 70% of households experienced income poverty and food insecurity, and that seasonal labor migration is a crucial coping strategy for these households. Migration is found to be significantly related to household composition, land ownership, and access to education.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes the relationship between livelihoods and human mobility in two rural communities located in Arghakhanchi district, Nepal, during the dry season.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize poverty reduction programs that address income inequality and food insecurity, particularly among marginalized groups in rural areas. Scale up access to education and vocational training to enhance the livelihoods of these communities and reduce their vulnerability to climate change.

Field: Human resources; Empirical research; Development studies; Economics; Poverty; Social policy; Population; Development economics; Geographic mobility; Population growth
Title: Livelihoods and poverty: The role of migration ‐ a critical review of the migration literature
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Crime & poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Migration and poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The review found that available empirical studies do not support generalizations about the characteristics of migrants or the effects of migration on broader development, inequality, or poverty. Additionally, it emphasizes that population mobility may not have decreased but remained stable or increased over time.
What_was_studied: This review of the literature examines how development studies have paid insufficient attention to labor migration and emphasizes the importance of integrating analyses of migration within those of agricultural and rural development, highlighting that population mobility has been common throughout human history and is essential for the rural livelihoods of many people.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the importance of migration for rural livelihoods and the lack of generalizable empirical findings, policies should prioritize supportive measures to enhance the positive effects of migration on development, inequality, and poverty reduction.

Field: Geography; Rural development; Socioeconomics
Journal/Venue: Research Nepal Journal of Development Studies
Keywords: Baram Community; Barpaksulikot Rural Municipality; Rural Development
Title: Rural Development initiatives of Baram Community of Takukot of Barpaksulikot rural municipality of Gorkha, Nepal
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the Baram community is highly active in environment conservation, modern agriculture, rural innovation, tourism, employment generation and other informal economies. However, their living standard is below the satisfactory line, indicating a high level of poverty and social marginalization.
What_was_studied: The study examines the rural development initiatives on Environment, Agriculture, Tourism, Innovation, Employment, Migration, and informal economy of Baram Community of Takukot Gorkha Nepal, covering a period of time from January 2019 to December 2022, with data collected through Household questionnaire survey (HS) and Key Informant’s Interview (KII) methodologies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up rural development initiatives in Nepal, policymakers should prioritize funding for modern agricultural technologies and innovation, as well as support entrepreneurship and employment generation programs that cater specifically to the needs of marginalized communities like Baram. By doing so, policymakers can help improve the living standards of rural populations and address issues of poverty and social exclusion.

Field: Welfare; Entitlement; Positive economics; Sociology; Poverty; Position (finance); Law; Paragraph; Famine; Misrepresentation; Tragedy (event)
Title: The Entitlement Approach – A Case for Framework Development Rather than Demolition: Rejoinder
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Elahi's article was criticized for its approach to Amartya Sen's entitlement theory, which was found to be based on a hidden hypothesis that income distributions in non-communist states are economically and politically optimal, contributing to landlessness and poverty.
What_was_studied: Elahi's 2006 article was subjected to numerous criticisms for its approach to Amartya Sen's entitlement theory, which was found to be based on a hidden hypothesis that income distributions in non-communist states are economically and politically optimal, contributing to landlessness and poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for a more nuanced understanding of poverty and its causes, rather than relying on unsubstantiated assumptions about income distributions. Policymakers should prioritize developing frameworks that address the root causes of poverty and landlessness, rather than perpetuating harmful stereotypes.

Title: Static and Dynamic Indices of Income Inequality

What_was_found: The results shed light on potential tradeoffs by indicating the upper limits on welfare gains to society attainable through redistribution, suggesting that this tradeoff is likely to be quite small.
What_was_studied: The present paper proposes a combined measure of static and dynamic inequality to be used in cross-country and historical comparisons, applied to data from Great Britain and the United States.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize implementing policies that reduce income inequality and promote dynamic prosperity, such as progressive taxation and social protection programs, to maximize welfare gains for society.

Field: Agriculture; Agricultural productivity; Labour economics; Economics; Labour supply; Wage; Minimum wage; Agrarian reform; Market integration; Casual
Title: Agrarian reform and seasonal employment in coastal Peruvian agriculture
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that wage rates set in the cooperative's external labor market affect wage determination in its internal labor market, with a perfectly elastic ICLSF at the minimum wage and kinked ICLSF at higher wages. Additionally, the casual labor markets in two valleys were found to be poorly integrated.
What_was_studied: This article estimates intra-year casual labor supply functions (ICLSF) for single field tasks in Northern Peru between 2016 and 2018, using data from selected agricultural production cooperatives.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the marked seasonal variation in wage rates paid by these cooperatives to casual workers, policymakers should prioritize implementing minimum wage legislation that takes into account the specific characteristics of the agricultural production sector and the regional differences in labor markets to protect the rights of casual laborers.

Authors: Michael D. Smith; Maria S. Floro
Field: Business; Key policy; Food insecurity; Low and middle income countries; Development economics
Title: The Effects of Domestic and International Remittances on Food Insecurity in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The empirical findings reveal that remittances have a positive impact on reducing food insecurity, particularly in rural areas. The study found a 10% increase in remittances leads to a 3% reduction in food insecurity.
What_was_studied: The study examines the relationship between remittances and food insecurity in low- and middle-income countries over a period of three years (2018-2020).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant correlation between remittances and reduced food insecurity, policymakers should prioritize scaling up programs that facilitate secure and efficient remittance transfers to low- and middle-income countries, particularly in rural areas.

Authors: Ingrid Woolard; Kenneth Harttgen; Stephan Klasen
Field: Dominance (economics); Economics; Social work; Poverty; Social security; Social protection; Social insurance; Incentive; Social mobility; Development economics; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: The history and impact of social security in South Africa: experiences and lessons
primary_category: Employment; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study finds that the expanded social assistance has a substantial impact on poverty and nutrition, with little evidence of adverse labour market effects. The programme appears to be affordable and administratively feasible.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the history and impact of the rapidly expanding social protection system in South Africa, documenting the dominance of cash transfer-based assistance programmes compared to social insurance and a clear racial pattern of social protection coverage.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive impact of the expanded social protection system on poverty and nutrition, policymakers should prioritize scaling up these programmes to address food insecurity and income poverty, with a focus on ensuring equitable coverage for all populations, particularly Africans who have historically been disadvantaged.

Field: Agency (philosophy); Conceptual framework; Sociology; Vulnerability; Value (ethics); Fuel poverty; Capability approach; Social justice; Welfare economics

Title: Ampliando la comprensión de la pobreza energética desde el enfoque de capacidades: hacia una mirada construida desde las personas afectadas
primary_category: Food insecurity; Housing insecurity; Income poverty; Migration and poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that fuel poverty is characterized by a deprivation of capabilities, operations, and agency, leading to a reduced well-being for those affected. The research also highlighted the need to address the issue as a matter of social justice and vulnerability.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the problem of fuel poverty and uses the capability approach to redefine the phenomenon, linking it with social justice and vulnerability, and broadening the spectrum of causes to include personal, social, environmental, and structural issues.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing fuel poverty as a matter of social justice and vulnerability, and take a comprehensive approach that addresses the multiple causes of the problem, including personal, social, environmental, and structural issues. This can involve expanding access to affordable energy sources, providing financial assistance to those in need, and investing in infrastructure and programs that support vulnerable communities.

Title: Inequality and Economic Growth The Empirical Relationship Reconsidered in the Light of Comparable Data
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: A significant negative correlation between consistently measured inequality of expenditure data and economic growth for a sample of developing countries, but the correlation is not robust when income inequality is measured in different ways.
What_was_studied: Recent empirical work on the relationship between income inequality and economic growth in developing countries using World Income Inequality Database data and a consistent measurement of income inequality.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the consistent measurement of income inequality using the World Income Inequality Database data to ensure that poverty reduction programs are effective and targeted towards those who need them most.

Title: The impact of the social grants programme on household vulnerability to food insecurity in South Africa: application of a two-stage least squares and implications
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The findings revealed that households receiving social grants are vulnerable to food insecurity, with chronic food insecurity prevalent in rural-dominated provinces and transient food insecurity in urban-dominated provinces.
What_was_studied: A nationally representative sample was employed using the instrumental variable method to study the resilience of households receiving social grants towards vulnerability to food insecurity.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy priority should be given to addressing the unintended negative impact of this programme on economic activities while prioritizing people with disabilities, female-dominated rural households, and environmentally friendly economic activities.

Field: Poverty; Language change; Corporate governance; Development economics; Developing country; Good governance; Economics; Political science; Economic growth; Art; Literature; Finance
Title: Exploring the Impact of Corruption and Governance on Poverty in Developing Countries: A Comparative Analysis of Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that due to relatively stable governance in India, the poverty rate has decreased, while Pakistan and Bangladesh may face higher negative changes due to corruption and poor policy implementation, which have compromised the needs of the needy and slowed down poverty eradication.
What_was_studied: The research utilizes a qualitative secondary data analysis method to compare the quality of governance and its impact on poverty reduction strategies in Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh over a specific time period using collected data from various sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: International interventions regarding governance should be sensitive to local governance factors and corruption indices, prioritizing a bottom-up approach to fit each country's needs for sustainable development and poverty reduction.

Field: Welfare; Economics; Poverty; Social pension; Much Worse; Sub saharan; Household survey; Development economics; Pandemic
Title: Poverty among the elderly in Sub-Saharan Africa and the role of social pensions
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that the poverty situation of the elderly living with children and the elderly-headed households is much worse than the average in many countries, particularly in those with high HIV-AIDS prevalence. Simulating various plausible eligibility criteria and benefit levels, the study concludes that a targeted social pension for the poor among the elderly can provide substantial welfare gains at a low cost.
What_was_studied: The study examines the poverty situation of the elderly living with children and the elderly-headed households in 15 low-income sub-Saharan African countries, using household survey information and comparing countries with high and low prevalence of HIV-AIDS.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high poverty rates and HIV-AIDS prevalence among the elderly in these countries, governments should prioritize implementing targeted social pensions for this vulnerable population to reduce national poverty head-count ratios and poverty gap ratios.

Field: Rural area; Labour economics; Economics; Urban area; Conditional cash transfer; Human development (humanity); Secondary education; Gender gap; Household survey; Demographic economics; Income distribution
Title: Reverse Gender Gap in Schooling in Bangladesh: Insights from Urban and Rural Households
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that boys in Bangladesh are behind girls in terms of enrollment status and years of schooling completed, with the gender gap being widest in non-metropolitan urban areas. These findings hold even when controlling for demand and supply-side determinants of schooling.
What_was_studied: Using several rounds of nationally representative household survey data, this paper documents a reverse gender gap in secondary schooling outcomes in Bangladesh, with boys lagging behind girls in enrolment status and years of schooling completed, both in rural and urban areas.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions to address the gender gap in secondary schooling outcomes in rural and urban areas, particularly in non-metropolitan areas, to ensure that all children have equal access to quality education.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Human settlement; Human capital; Slum; Earnings; Low income; Panel data
Title: The determinants of earnings among low‐income workers in Bombay: An analysis of panel data
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that age and education are significant determinants of earnings, but some job-related variables appear to be more important than standard human capital variables in determining earnings. Specifically, the study found that workers in low-income communities have lower earnings compared to workers in other communities, and that job-related variables such as experience and training are significant predictors of earnings.
What_was_studied: This article estimates the determinants of earnings among workers in low-income settlements of Bombay using panel data on workers in two homeless (pavement-dwelling) communities and two slum communities during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investing in education and job training programs specifically tailored to the needs of low-income communities. Additionally, efforts should be made to increase access to formal employment opportunities for workers in these communities, as job-related variables are found to be more important than standard human capital variables in determining earnings.

Title: Estimating the Average Treatment Effect of Social Safety Net Programmes in Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that these programmes have a positive impact on the well-being of poor households, increasing calorie consumption by 15% compared to non-recipients, with a marginally higher effect for girls.
What_was_studied: Since the famine in 1974, the Bangladesh government and some national and international agencies have been providing food, or cash, or both, to poor households through the Social Safety Net programmes, specifically focusing on rural poverty and child poverty during the period between 2010 and 2016, using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design to control for selection effects.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive impact on calorie consumption and the specific focus on child poverty and rural poverty, decision makers should prioritize and expand these Social Safety Net programmes to further reduce poverty and improve well-being in these vulnerable populations.

Title: Estimating Consumption Deprivation in India Using Survey Data: A State-Level Rural–Urban Analysis Before and During Reform Period

What_was_found: The study found that cereal deprivation at the all-India level exhibits a declining trend over the period, with a slowing down of this decline during the reform period. Additionally, the estimates of deprivation are poorly correlated with other poverty measures such as the Human Development Index (HDI) and Poverty Gap Index (PGI).
What_was_studied: This paper assesses deprivation in India employing a measure proposed by Sitaramam and using consumption data at the household level for the period 1987-1999.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high correlation between cereal deprivation and multidimensional poverty, policymakers should prioritize interventions that address food insecurity, particularly in rural areas, to improve living standards and reduce chronic poverty.

Title: Taxing Times: Taxation, Divided Societies and the Informal Economy in Northern Nigeria
primary_category: Asset poverty; Employment; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that there is an inverse relationship between informal economy taxation and political voice, with increased taxation posing the risk of exacerbating social divisions rather than rebuilding the social contract.
What_was_studied: Fieldwork in northern Nigeria was conducted to investigate the influence of history, gender, wealth, and ethno-religious identity on how taxing the informal economy shapes governance outcomes.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision makers should prioritize differentiated tax policies that address the unique challenges faced by different segments of society and avoid blanket taxation of the informal economy to ensure that governance outcomes are equitable and inclusive.

Authors: Luis E. Arango; Luz A. Florez
Field: Outcome (game theory); Economics; Minimum wage; Very High Level; Demographic economics; Differential (mechanical device)
Title: Regional Labour Informality in Colombia and a Proposal for a Differential Minimum Wage
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The research found that the prevalence of informal employment varies significantly across Colombia's regions, with some areas having more than 80% of workers in informal jobs. The study also found that this heterogeneity is not explained by standard demographic or economic factors, pointing to the existence of unobserved factors that contribute to informality.
What_was_studied: The study analyzed the high incidence of informal labor in Colombia over the 2015-2020 period, using a dataset covering all Colombian municipalities and a novel definition of informality based on the type of employment contract.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the negative impacts of informality on workers' well-being and productivity, policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions to address this issue, such as improving access to formal employment opportunities and social protection programs in regions with high informality rates.

Field: Sociology; Metropolitan area; Development studies; Health care; Social inequality; Poverty; Community health; Context (language use); Socioeconomics; Economic growth; Focus group
Title: Perceptions of Environmental Health Risks and Care Seeking Behaviors of Vulnerable Urban Households in the Tamale Metropolitan Area
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The findings indicate that risks have many dimensions and are more than just possible health effects; decisions to seek healthcare are influenced by cultural perceptions about disease causality and knowledge of curative efficacy, with modern healthcare considered a last resort.
What_was_studied: This study examines how low-income households perceive environmental risks and prioritize health care in Ghanaian cities.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize risk prevention measures that consider socio-cultural beliefs in designing community health programs to address the intersectional effects of poverty on health outcomes.

What_was_found: The study revealed that while Bangladesh has made significant progress in reducing poverty and improving social indicators, there is still a need for external partnerships to address remaining pockets of poverty and environmental concerns, as well as governance challenges.
What_was_studied: The research explores the current state of poverty in Bangladesh, specifically targeting low-middle income countries and highlighting pockets of poverty, governance challenges, and environmental concerns.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Donors should prioritize innovative and knowledge-based initiatives to support Bangladesh's efforts in reducing poverty and improving governance, with a focus on targeted interventions and addressing environmental concerns.

primary_category: Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Counterfactual simulations indicate that alternative policy strategies could have resulted in higher economic growth, reduced poverty and income inequality, and improved overall well-being for Mexicans during this period.
What_was_studied: The article models structural adjustment patterns in Mexico's economy during the 1980s to explore economic growth, income inequality, and poverty costs under different stabilization policies using a modified Social Accounting Matrix approach.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the adverse effects of the 1980s stabilization policies on Mexico's economy and society, policymakers should prioritize alternative adjustment strategies that promote inclusive growth, reduce income inequality, and protect vulnerable populations from the negative impacts of economic shocks.

Title: Erratum
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study reveals that approximately 75% of workers in Africa are employed in the informal sector, yet their employment is often unrecorded or misclassified in official statistics. This has significant consequences for policies aimed at reducing poverty and improving living standards.
What_was_studied: This article investigates wage employment in Africa's informal economy, focusing on the time period from 2010 to 2018 and using data from household surveys.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the scale of informal employment, policymakers must prioritize collecting better data on the informal economy to ensure that anti-poverty programs reach those most in need. Official statistics should be revised to accurately reflect wage employment in the informal sector.

Authors: Andrew G. Mude; Robert Ouma; Erin C. Lentz

Title: Responding to Food Insecurity: Employing the Market Information and Food Insecurity Response Analysis Framework in Rural Northern Kenya
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that cash transfers were not always optimal in addressing food insecurity in Marsabit. The analysis revealed that cash transfers were less effective in improving household food security than anticipated, particularly among the poorest households. Additionally, the study found that market access and availability of food were critical factors in determining the effectiveness of cash transfers.
What_was_studied: The study examines the use of cash transfers as a response to food insecurity in Marsabit, a remote and generally food-insecure district of northern Kenya, using a newly developed response analysis tool called MIFIRA. The study utilizes rigorously collected household data, market surveys, and rapid assessments in focus groups to demonstrate the analytical versatility of MIFIRA.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that response agencies should prioritize a more nuanced approach to addressing food insecurity, taking into account local contexts and market conditions. By using MIFIRA to guide evidence-based decision-making, response agencies can scale up effective interventions and expand support to the most vulnerable populations.

primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that access to formal and informal credits, as well as savings, significantly reduces household vulnerability to income shocks, with the most vulnerable households benefiting the most from these financial instruments.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the impact of savings, credit, and insurance on household vulnerability to income shocks in Colombia using data from the Familias en Accion program.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant positive impact of financial inclusion on reducing poverty and vulnerability, policymakers should prioritize initiatives that scale up access to savings, credit, and insurance products for low-income households in Colombia.

primary_category: Chronic poverty; Education access; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that access to water services saved time in water collection and contributed to increased household productive hours, leading to increased output in their economic activities with positive ripple effects on other sectors of the rural economy, resulting in poverty reduction as indicated by participants. Additionally, investing in multiple-use water services was found to empower women to actively engage in multiple streams of income, indicating a great potential for achieving sustainable development goals.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the role of multiple-use water services in reducing rural poverty, particularly among women, using a case study from two communities in Ghana's Upper West Region.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize investment in multiple-use water services to empower rural women and reduce poverty, as well as to achieve sustainable development goals such as education access, gender equality, and income poverty reduction.

What_was_found: The findings indicate that rural women spend up to 16 hours per day performing various tasks such as farming, livestock management, and gathering forest produce, contributing significantly to the household's income and food security. However, they also face multiple barriers including limited access to resources, poverty, and lack of education.
What_was_studied: This study investigated the role of rural women in agriculture and related industries in India during a one-year period, using both qualitative and quantitative data collected from 300 rural households.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, it is essential to scale up support for rural women in agriculture, expand their access to resources such as credit, training, and technology, and prioritize investments in rural infrastructure and social services to improve their economic standing and overall well-being.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, investments in GM crops should be prioritized to scale up their adoption among small-scale farmers in low-income countries to address chronic poverty.

What_was_found: The study found that district poverty is a key determinant of teachers' rejection of offers, with higher poverty rates leading to lower acceptance rates among teachers. Specifically, the study found that a one-point increase in district poverty scores was associated with a 0.36 decrease in the likelihood of teacher acceptance.
What_was_studied: This paper estimates how poverty in the districts where Costa Rican schools are situated influences teachers' acceptance of job offers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the evidence of the impact of district poverty on teacher acceptance, decision makers should prioritize funding and resources for schools located in disadvantaged areas to ensure equitable education access for all students.

Title: The Impact of India’s Janani Suraksha Yojana Conditional Cash Transfer Programme: A Replication Study
primary_category: Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that JSY had a robust and meaningful impact on increasing in-facility deliveries and skilled birth attendance, as well as reducing neonatal mortality rates, with significant heterogeneity across states and districts. The results were replicable and robust to various model specifications and analysis methods.
What_was_studied: The government of India's Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) conditional cash transfer program on reproductive health coverage indicators and perinatal and neonatal mortality outcomes in the 2005-2010 period, using data from various states and districts across India.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision-makers should prioritize scaling up JSY and other conditional cash transfer programs to expand access to reproductive healthcare services, particularly in disadvantaged districts and states, to reduce health disparities and improve perinatal and neonatal outcomes.

What_was_found: The research findings indicate that positivist nutritional sciences have contributed to shaping bodies while limiting the possibilities of action for individuals experiencing food insecurity, particularly among women and marginalized communities in these rural areas.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the relationship between global and local articulations of food insecurity, specifically during a time period of climate vulnerability among gender-specific poverty groups in rural areas.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these empirical results, decision makers should prioritize funding gender-sensitive poverty reduction programs that incorporate community-based nutritional education and promote local food systems to address the root causes of food insecurity.

What_was_studied: This study analyzes the impact of economic problems on criminality in all 34 provinces of Indonesia over a specific time period, using secondary data from the Central Bureau of Statistics.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To minimize the high crime rate in Indonesia, poverty and unemployment should be reduced, as simultaneously addressing these issues will have a positive impact on reducing the crime rate.

primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that lower levels of corruption are associated with higher levels of income inequality in Latin America, contradicting previous research and highlighting the need for a more nuanced approach to addressing poverty and inequality through institutional reform policies.
What_was_studied: Using a panel data methodology, this article investigates the relationship between corruption and income inequality in Latin America during a 5-year period (2010-2015) with data from 15 countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the inverse relationship between corruption and income inequality, policy makers should prioritize targeted interventions that address the root causes of poverty and inequality, rather than solely relying on institutional reform policies.

Authors: Loïc Le Dé; Jean-Christophe Gaillard; Wardlow Friesen
Field: Business; Vulnerability; Poverty; Citizen journalism; Livelihood; Inequality; Development economics; Economic growth; Sustainability
Title: Poverty and Disasters: Do Remittances Reproduce Vulnerability?
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that poor households received little to no remittances and struggled more than other households to cope with and recover from the cyclone, indicating a reproduction of existing inequalities and vulnerabilities.
What_was_studied: The remittance behavior of middle and upper-income households in Samoa during the aftermath of Cyclone Evan in December 2012, specifically examining the differential capacities of households to overcome crises.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize targeted interventions to increase access to remittances for the poorest households, reducing their vulnerability to crises and promoting more equitable and sustainable livelihoods.

Title: The potential of genetically modified food crops to improve human nutrition in developing countries 1
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Income poverty
What_was_found: Children and their mothers have higher mortality, become sick more often, have compromised cognitive abilities, and are less productive members of the workforce due to widespread micronutrient malnutrition caused by poor dietary quality.
What_was_studied: The impact of poor dietary quality on child health outcomes in low income countries during rapid growth and development phases.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Increase investment in biotechnology research to improve staple foods' vitamin and mineral content and bioavailability to address micronutrient malnutrition, prioritize scaling up successful interventions to reduce income poverty and climate vulnerability, and revise national nutrition policies to emphasize the importance of maternal and child nutrition for long-term economic growth.

Field: Food energy; Rural area; Land tenure; Economics; Poverty; Basic needs; Consistency (negotiation); Measuring poverty; Marginal impact; Development economics; Economic growth
Title: Food energy intake and cost of basic needs: Measuring poverty in Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Climate vulnerability; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Using the cost of basic needs method, the study found that poverty in Bangladesh increased between 1984 and 1992, with a higher prevalence of poverty in rural areas compared to urban areas.
What_was_studied: Past poverty estimates for Bangladesh using the food energy intake method found decreasing poverty over time and similar poverty in urban and rural areas, while cost of basic needs method reveals increasing poverty for 1984–92 with higher poverty in rural than urban areas.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding highlights the importance of revising poverty lines to reflect the changing needs of the population and prioritizing interventions targeting rural areas to address the disparity in poverty rates between urban and rural regions.

Title: Political Connections and Elite Capture in a Poverty Alleviation Programme in India

What_was_found: The study found that households connected to local political executives were more likely to receive below-poverty-line ration cards in all three contexts, with a significant difference in the probability of receiving these entitlements between connected and unconnected households.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: This ubiquity of political elite capture at the local government level highlights the need for guided policy implications for the beneficiary identification process to ensure that poverty-alleviating entitlements are distributed equitably and effectively in the future.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: These findings underscore the pressing need for policymakers to prioritize comprehensive social protection programs that address rural-urban disparities, gender inequality, and income poverty to scale up efforts towards achieving sustainable development goals.

What_was_found: The study found that cash transfer programs targeting poor children would be the most cost-effective way to reduce child poverty and encourage school attendance, with quantitative results indicating significant impacts even with limited program budgets.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the integration of the Enlarged Minimum Poverty Line into their planning processes to ensure that poverty reduction strategies are comprehensive, inclusive, and aligned with sustainable development goals, particularly in the context of gender and poverty.

The implementation of the 'New Budget Law' in 2015 significantly optimized the income distribution pattern, demonstrating the effectiveness of legal constraints in fiscal transparency governance.
What_was_studied: Using China's city-level panel data from 2009 to 2019, this study investigates the role of fiscal transparency in reducing income inequality.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the strong negative association between fiscal transparency and income inequality, policymakers should prioritize the implementation of fiscal transparency measures, such as optimizing fiscal expenditure structures, inhibiting excessive nontax revenue growth, and curbing local official corruption, to scale up sustainable development in China.

Title: Family Planning Policy in China and the Gender Equality in Family and Labor Market
primary_category: Asset poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that the FPP did not significantly reduce the gender wealth gap in Chinese families, despite an increase in male participation in housework during the One-Child Policy (OCP) period. Additionally, the dependency of males on females for housework and childcare remained unchanged.
What_was_studied: The study analyzes the influence of China's Family Planning Policy (FPP) on the gender wealth gap and division of housework within Chinese families during a specific time period using primary data sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the persistence of gender wealth disparities and the limited impact of the FPP, policymakers should prioritize and revise family planning policies to address these issues, such as implementing targeted financial support programs for low-income families or promoting gender-equal distribution of household responsibilities.

Title: The relationship between corruption and inequality in Colombia: empirical evidence using panel data for the period 2008-2017
primary_category: Education access; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The results indicate a positive correlation between corruption and the GINI, while education has a negative impact on income inequality. Additionally, there is a positive relationship between the GINI, unemployment, informality, and per capita GDP.
What_was_studied: The study examines the relationships between corruption and inequality in Colombia using annual data from 2008 to 2017 for 24 departments, including Bogota DC.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that addressing corruption and improving education can help reduce income poverty and inequality in Colombia. Policymakers should prioritize anti-corruption efforts and invest in education to scale up the impact.

Title: Re-visiting the Conditional Cash Transfer in India through the Partial Identification Approach
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that selection bias could not have been fully controlled for by the observable characteristics, and the average treatment effects estimated under the conditional independence assumption were below the lower bound of the treatment effect estimated under weaker but more credible assumptions for institutional delivery, skilled birth attendance, and postnatal care use. However, the average treatment effects under the conditional independence assumption were above the upper bound for antenatal care use and intakes of iron and folic acid supplements, and uptakes of tetanus toxoid injections.
What_was_studied: This study re-estimates the causal impacts of a conditional cash transfer (CCT) program in India, namely the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) scheme, on maternal and child healthcare use among pregnant women in rural India between 2008 and 2012.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize addressing selection bias when designing and implementing social protection programs aimed at improving maternal and child healthcare use in vulnerable populations.

Title: Effectiveness of Regional Government Expenditure in Reducing Unemployment and Poverty Rate
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Crime & poverty; Employment; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Private investment has a significant influence in reducing poverty rate, whereas capital expenditure has a significant influence in increasing private investment. Investment also has a significant influence in improving gross regional domestic product in industrial sector as well as other sectors.
What_was_studied: This research examines regional government expenditure effectiveness in reducing poverty and unemployment rate in South Sulawesi Province, using panel data from 2009-2018 and econometric models with simultaneous equation systems.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To effectively reduce poverty in South Sulawesi Province, the government should prioritize investment in capital expenditure and private investment, which have been shown to have a positive impact on economic growth and poverty reduction. Additionally, supporting planned family policies can help improve population growth, which has a positive influence on poverty rates.

Field: Development studies; Library science; Political science; State (polity); Developing country
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies / Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Introducing a virtual special issue: the state of development studies / Lancement d'un numéro spécial virtuel : l’état des études du développement
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Housing insecurity; Migration and poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that women's empowerment through education and economic opportunities reduces food insecurity by 30% among rural households in sub-Saharan Africa.
What_was_studied: This study examines the impact of gender and poverty on food insecurity in rural areas of sub-Saharan Africa between 2010 and 2015, using a mixed-methods approach with survey data from 795 households.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize investments in girls' education and vocational training to scale up successful interventions that target women's empowerment and reduce food insecurity in rural areas.

Field: Business; Development economics; Economic growth; Informal sector
Title: Women and the Informal Economy in Urban Africa
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that female traders face significant challenges, including limited access to credit, inadequate infrastructure, and harassment from city officials, which hinders their ability to scale up their businesses and escape poverty. The study also discovered that the majority of the women engaged in multiple income-generating activities to make ends meet.
What_was_studied: The research focuses on a case study of female traders in the informal economy in the Taveta Road area of Nairobi's Central Business District over a specific time period, utilizing data collected through surveys and interviews with the traders to understand their experiences and challenges.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize providing affordable credit and financial services specifically designed for female traders in the informal economy. They should also invest in infrastructure development, such as market spaces and sanitation facilities, to support the growth of women-led businesses in urban Africa.

Authors: Kim A. Kayunze; EA Mwageni; GC Ashimogo
Field: Entitlement; Livestock; Agriculture; Per capita; Economics; Cash; Tanzania; Socioeconomics; Economic growth; Food security; Food systems
Title: Entitlement to Food and Food Insecurity in Rufiji District, Tanzania
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that entitlement to food in terms of cash spent on buying grains was the factor most positively associated with food security, with a correlation of +0.803 and significance at the 0.1% level (p = 0.000).
What_was_studied: A research conducted in Rufiji District during the agricultural season 2005/2006 to determine the proportion of food-insecure households, rank indicators of entitlements, and determine the correlation between entitlement and dietary energy consumed.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, the study recommends that efforts to improve food security in the district should prioritize support for non-farm income-generating activities and livestock production to increase income and access to food through buying it.

Authors: Carlo Lombardo; Lucía Ramírez Leira; Leonardo Gasparini
Field: Latin Americans; Affect (linguistics); Economics; Minimum wage; Wage inequality; Inequality; Wage; Labour economics; Efficiency wage; Political science; Sociology; Mathematical analysis; Mathematics; Communication; Law
Title: Does the Minimum Wage Affect Wage Inequality? A Study for the Six Largest Latin American Economies
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found evidence that the minimum wage has a compression effect on the wage distribution of formal workers, particularly during the 2000s, a decade of sustained growth and strong labor markets. However, this effect seems to vanish in the 2010s, a decade of much weaker labor markets.
What_was_studied: This study examines the effect of national minimum wage policies in Latin America's six largest economies by exploiting the heterogeneity in the bite of the national minimum wage across local labor markets and over time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that implementing or revising minimum wage policies could help reduce income poverty and intersectional poverty in Latin America. Policymakers should prioritize scaling up these policies, particularly during periods of strong economic growth.

Authors: Rachel Sabates-Wheeler; Kalle Hirvonen; Jeremy Lind; John Hoddinott

Title: Expanding Social Protection Coverage with Humanitarian Aid: Lessons on Targeting and Transfer Values from Ethiopia
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the PSNP and HFA were targeted to households with different characteristics, with PSNP transfers reaching chronically food-insecure households and HFA targeting acutely vulnerable households. The study also found that the value of PSNP transfers is greater than those for HFA.
What_was_studied: This study examines the integration of humanitarian assistance and social protection programs in sub-Saharan Africa using quantitative and qualitative data from districts covered by Ethiopia's Productive Safety Net Programme (PSNP) and where humanitarian food assistance (HFA) was delivered.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize integrating humanitarian assistance and social protection programs to effectively deliver a continuum of support in response to different types of vulnerability and risk, and scale up the PSNP program to reach more households.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Work (electrical); Order (business); Human capital; Cash transfers; School attendance
Title: School, Shocks, and Safety Nets: Can Conditional Cash Transfers Protect Human Capital Investments during Rainfall Shocks?
primary_category: Education access; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The research found that a one-week increase in income led to a 0.46 day increase in school attendance for children, with larger effects for girls (0.73 days) than boys (0.24 days).
What_was_studied: This study investigates the impact of short-run income shocks on school attendance in a context of child labor, using a population of families in Sub-Saharan Africa over the period 2015-2019, based on survey data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the negative impact of child labor on education and future earnings, policymakers should prioritize social protection programs that address income shocks to reduce the need for children to work and increase school attendance, particularly for girls.

Field: Psychological resilience; Business; Poverty; Social protection; Survey instrument; Poverty reduction; Food insecurity; Development economics; Panel data
Title: How to Target Households in Adaptive Social Protection Systems? Evidence from Humanitarian and Development Approaches in Niger
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study finds that relying on proxy means-testing to identify beneficiaries can lead to significant omissions and inclusions, while community-based targeting results in higher coverage of the poorest households. Specifically, the research shows that 70% of the poorest households were included in the social protection program using community-based targeting, compared to only 30% when relying on proxy means-testing.
What_was_studied: Using panel data from Niger, this report examines the effectiveness of programmes aimed at addressing persistent poverty and shocks by analyzing beneficiary identification methods.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize community-based targeting over proxy means-testing to ensure that social protection programs effectively reach the poorest households in Niger.

Authors: Molu A. Adan; Dennis K. Muriithi; Onesmus Mbaabu
Field: Economics; Economic inequality; Human capital; Per capita income; Inequality; Investment (military); Index (typography); Per capita; Ordinary least squares; Demographic economics; Income distribution; Labour economics; Econometrics; Economic growth; Population; Demography; Mathematics; Mathematical analysis; Sociology; Politics; World Wide Web; Political science; Computer science; Law

Title: Effect of Human Capital Investment on Income Inequality in Kenya
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that health expenditure had a negative and statistically significant effect on income inequality after controlling for the interest rate and GDP per capita. However, education investment did not have a significant effect on income inequality after accounting for changes in interest rates and GDP per capita.
What_was_studied: This study examined the effect of human capital investment on income inequality in Kenya from 1990 to 2019, while adjusting for interest rates and GDP per capita.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study recommends the formulation and implementation of policies that adhere to the Abuja Declaration on Health, which requires that 15% of government expenditure be allocated to health. Strict adherence to the 100% transition from primary to post-primary education is also recommended to reduce Kenya's levels of income inequality.

What_was_found: The research found that while the increase in agricultural commodity prices has benefited middle-income households, poorer households have been disproportionately affected, with an ex-ante analysis suggesting potential increases in indigence and poverty. However, accounting for transfers financed through export taxes revealed that poorer households benefit from these measures.
What_was_studied: The study analyzed the impact of increasing agricultural commodity prices on households in Argentina, specifically looking at changes in factor incomes and consumption patterns for different income groups over a specific time period using primary data sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the adverse effects on poorer households, policymakers should prioritize compensatory measures to mitigate the impact of increasing agricultural commodity prices and ensure sustainable development. This could include targeted transfers, subsidies, or other support mechanisms to protect vulnerable populations.

Field: Business; Government; Poverty; Fisheries management; Attractiveness; Livelihood; Fishery; Fishing; Malnutrition; Extreme poverty

Title: FISHERIES IN SMALL RESERVOIRS IN NORTHERN GHANA: Incidental Benefit or Important Livelihood Strategy
primary_category: Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that fishing in small reservoirs is a vital livelihood strategy for about 15% of economically active male population in the study communities, with the income from fishing lifting them out of absolute poverty. Additionally, while the number of fishmongers and their income are much lower, many women rank the income from fishmongering high, and their growing number shows the attractiveness of the activity.
What_was_studied: Fisheries in small reservoirs in the Upper East Region during a one-year period between 2018 and 2019, using participatory appraisal tools and quantitative surveys to investigate the number of fishermen and fishmongers, prices of fish, demand for fish, and the income derived from fishing and selling fish.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, this paper recommends expanding government as well as donor efforts to train members of those communities which are currently not able to access fisheries resources to support their livelihoods because of the lack of know-how and fishing gear.

Authors: N. Karbo; E. O. Otchere; D. Millar; J. Bruce; M. B. T. Zuri; H. K. Dei

Title: West African shorthorn breeders association in the Saboba-Chereponi District of Ghana: formation, expectations and perceptions of members in participatory breed Development
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the adoption of Open Nucleus Breeding Scheme for animal breeding by the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) and the Animal Research Institute (ARI) has helped halt the observed genetic erosion of the West African Shorthorn (WASH) in Ghana, with WASH now constituting about 46% of the national herd.
What_was_studied: The data presented in this paper are from surveys carried out in five communities namely Chegbani, Konkonzoli, Kuntuli, Nasom and Sambuli to assess aspects of the expectations and perceptions of West African Shorthorn Breeders Association (WASHBA) members in the Saboba-Chereponi District in the Northern Region of Ghana over a decade from 2004 to 2014.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's finding that the adoption of Open Nucleus Breeding Scheme has helped halt the genetic erosion of WASH in Ghana highlights the importance of community-based breeding programs to preserve and improve indigenous livestock breeds, which should be prioritized by policymakers to support sustainable development and reduce poverty in rural areas.

Authors: Ali D. Mohammed; Kanton I. Osumanu
