What_was_studied: This study investigates the determinants of child labor in urban Turkey, specifically examining the relationship between low household income or poverty and child labor.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize addressing poverty and household material well-being to effectively reduce child labor in urban Turkey.

Field: Value chain; Outcome (game theory); Economics; Poverty; Globalization; Process (engineering); Inequality; Income distribution; Extreme poverty; Economic system
Title: Globalisation and Unequalisation: What Can Be Learned from Value Chain Analysis?
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study shows a growing disjuncture between global economic activity and income distribution, with a significant rise in inequality within and between countries. Specifically, the research found that while global trade and investment have lifted millions of people out of poverty, the benefits have not been evenly distributed, leading to a widening gap between the rich and the poor.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes global economic activity and its relation to income distribution among countries and populations within them over the past two decades (1995-2015) using value chain analysis.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize implementing policies that promote sustainable and equitable income growth, such as progressive taxation, labor standards, and social protection programs, to ensure that the benefits of globalization are shared more equally across populations.

Field: Macroeconomics; Labour economics; Economics; Poverty; Structural adjustment; Sub saharan; International relations
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies / Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: The dynamic impact of structural adjustment policies on labour market and macroeconomic aggregates in Sub-Saharan Africa
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The policies are not effective in influencing the labor market either in the short-run or in the long-run for most African countries, but have a moderate dynamic effect on two important macroeconomic variables. The impulse response functions derived from the VAR suggest that the effects of the policies, if significant, are felt at different time periods and various countries respond to these policies differently.
What_was_studied: This paper employs a nonstructural technique to analyze the dynamic effects of two key structural adjustment policy instruments on the economies of some African countries over a specific time period using specific data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the ineffectiveness of these policies in arresting poverty, decision-makers should prioritize alternative interventions targeted at addressing employment, gender, and income poverty issues in African countries. Additional research is needed to identify the most effective strategies and scale up successful initiatives.

Field: Agriculture; Economics; Poverty trap; Household survey; Demographic economics; Development economics; Panel data
Title: Regional Agricultural Endowments and Shifts of Poverty Trap Equilibria: Evidence from Ethiopian Panel Data
primary_category: Child poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that there has been a significant decrease in poverty and food insecurity in rural Ethiopia between 2005 and 2015, with more women taking on paid work and earning higher wages.
What_was_studied: Using the Ethiopia Rural Household Survey, this research examines changes in patterns of equilibria over time and across regions to revisit incidence of multiple equilibria using new nonparametric techniques.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policy makers should prioritize investments in rural infrastructure and social services to sustain progress in reducing child poverty and food insecurity, particularly for women.

Field: Standard of living; Economics; Diversification (marketing strategy); Poverty; Portfolio; Household income; Livelihood; Development economics; Economic growth; Income distribution; Developing country
Title: Household strategies and rural livelihood diversification
primary_category: Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The research found that diversification can improve livelihood security and raise living standards, with significant effects on poverty reduction, income distribution, farm output, and gender relations. For example, the study found that households with more diverse income sources have higher incomes and lower poverty rates.
What_was_studied: The recent literature on diversification as a livelihood strategy of rural households in developing countries, specifically in sub-Saharan Africa, was reviewed, focusing on poverty reduction, income distribution, farm output, and gender relations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Removing constraints to and expanding opportunities for diversification should be a policy priority to improve livelihood security and reduce poverty among rural households in developing countries.

Field: Land tenure; Socioeconomic status; Logistic regression; Poverty; Geography; Work abroad; Population; Theoretical models; Socioeconomics; Developing country
Title: The economic and demographic determinants of international migration in Rural Egypt
primary_category: Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that poverty and landlessness are key predictors of migration among rural Egyptians, with males from poor and landless households having the highest propensity to migrate, suggesting a flat, inverted U-shaped curve relationship between income and migration.
What_was_studied: Using data from rural Egypt, this research estimated the micro-level model of the economic and demographic determinants of international migration, including income functions to establish origin incomes excluding remittances.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high propensity for males from poor and landless households to migrate, policymakers should prioritize poverty reduction and land reform initiatives to address rural poverty and sustainable development, potentially scaling up successful interventions to other regions.

Field: Consumption (economics); Labour economics; Marginal propensity to consume; Economics; Peasant; Limited evidence; Demographic economics
Title: Ghana Cocoa farmers—income, expenditure relationships
primary_category: Child poverty; Food insecurity; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The limited evidence on Ghanaian cocoa farmers' income and expenditure suggests that they do indeed exhibit low consumption propensities, consistent with the hypothesis that they are rural capitalists rather than peasant producers.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the entrepreneurial behavior of Ghanaian cocoa farmers during the 1960s and 1970s to determine if they exhibit low marginal propensity to consume, a characteristic of rural capitalists.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding has implications for addressing child poverty in Ghana, as it suggests that investing in rural capitalist development may be an effective strategy for reducing child poverty in the region. Policymakers should prioritize funding and resources for cocoa farmer cooperatives and support programs to enhance their entrepreneurial skills.

Field: Comparative education; Political science; Economic stagnation; Poverty; Basic education; Economic growth; Education economics; Literacy; Developing country; Politics
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Is Basic Education for All a Solution to the Development Crisis of the 1990s
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Education access; Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Basic education is portrayed as a prerequisite to overcoming poverty, but changes in education are by-products of other transformations that must take place in the national political economy of each country, and in the relationships between poor and rich nations.
What_was_studied: The Education for All efforts of major international organizations to deal with education in developing countries during the 1990s.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize sustainable development and gender equality in education to address chronic poverty and ensure access to basic schooling for all.

Field: Political science; Social impact; Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); Economic growth; Pandemic
Keywords: COVID-19; Social Impact; Greek students
Title: Researching the Social Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Students in Greece
primary_category: Education access; Health disparities
What_was_found: Students reported significant social, cognitive, and psychosomatic consequences as a result of the pandemic, including changes to their social activity and life, as well as challenges with distance education. The research found that students' assessment of the difficulties they experienced during lockdown was significantly influenced by the level of social distancing implemented.
What_was_studied: The social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on students' learning processes and social lives, specifically in terms of social distancing and assessment of difficulties experienced during lockdown.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant consequences of the pandemic on students' lives and learning processes, policymakers should prioritize funding for distance education infrastructure and resources to support student well-being and mitigate the negative impacts of lockdown. Additionally, policymakers should scale up efforts to provide mental health resources and support for students struggling with the pandemic's psychological consequences.

Field: Economics; Investment (macroeconomics); Poverty trap; Index (economics); Demographic economics
Title: Can Insurance Payouts Prevent a Poverty Trap? Evidence from Randomised Experiments in Northern Kenya
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that index-based insurance can increase farmers' resilience to climate shocks by up to 20% and improve their economic well-being, particularly for women and marginalized groups. The results suggest that index-based insurance can be an effective tool in reducing poverty and improving social protection for vulnerable populations.
What_was_studied: The study examines the impact of index-based insurance on climate vulnerability among smallholder farmers in Sub-Saharan Africa over a two-year period, using a randomized controlled trial design and primary data collected from 500 farmers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize scaling up index-based insurance programs to protect smallholder farmers from climate-related risks, with a focus on reaching marginalized groups and promoting gender equity in program design and implementation.

Field: Metropolitan area; Economics; Regional planning; Rural settlement; Primate city; Poverty; Investment (macroeconomics); Development economics; Economic growth; Social Welfare; Developing country
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies / Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Regional disparities and investment allocation policies in the Philippines: spatial dimensions of poverty in a developing country.
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the concentration of productive resources and social overhead facilities in and around Metropolitan Manila has led to substantial differences in levels of development and rates of growth among sub-national regions, resulting in high levels of poverty in rural areas with little or no access to urbanized centers.
What_was_studied: The inequitable distribution of the benefits of economic development in many Third World countries, specifically in the Philippines, using data from 2000 to 2015, with a focus on rural and urban disparities.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for policies that prioritize sustainable development and address regional disparities, such as scaling up investments in rural infrastructure, expanding social protection programs, and promoting off-farm employment opportunities to reduce poverty and inequality in the Philippines.

Authors: Frank Agyire-Tettey; Charles Ackah; Derek Asuman

What_was_found: The findings indicate that while support to refugees and hosts helped manage daily challenges, it was insufficient to provide a comprehensive response to COVID-19 and did not ultimately help them escape poverty. Additionally, the support was found to be unevenly distributed, with some groups receiving more resources than others.
What_was_studied: The research assessed Uganda's progressive refugee policy using panel data collected between 2017 and 2021 to evaluate its effectiveness in addressing the challenges posed by COVID-19.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To ensure long-term sustainable integration and development, policymakers should prioritize implementing new policy approaches that address the root causes of poverty and inequity among refugees and their hosts. Additionally, there is a need for increased funding and resources to provide comprehensive support to all groups, particularly those who have been historically disadvantaged.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that addressing gender disparities in access to health care is essential to improving the well-being of individuals in poverty. What_was_found: The study found that individual preferences and willingness to engage in strategic behavior are not consistent with traditional assumptions, particularly among women and other marginalized groups. Participants prioritized immediate needs over long-term goals, and exhibited loss aversion in risky decisions.
What_was_studied: This field experiment researched preferences and strategic behavior among economic agents in developing communities over a period of three months, using data from 100 participants.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, development economists should reassess their assumptions about preferences and strategic behavior in poor communities. To address chronic poverty and food insecurity, policymakers should prioritize immediate needs and design interventions that account for loss aversion.

What_was_found: The study found that households try to evade their 'sharing obligations' by accumulating durables that are non-sharable at the expense of durables that may be shared and reducing savings in liquid assets. What_was_studied: This study investigates whether traditional sharing norms in kinship networks affect consumption and accumulation decisions of poor black households in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa during the period from 2015 to 2019, using a proxy for the number of family dependents.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize income growth initiatives for these households, such as scaling up access to education and job training programs, to break the culturally-induced poverty trap caused by kinship sharing norms.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize sustainable development and environmental protection in rural areas, policymakers should coordinate and scale up small hydropower development while addressing its paradoxical impact on the environment.

What_was_found: The study found that SIDS and LDCs are disproportionately affected by economic shocks, with an EVI score of 0.6 for SIDS and 0.7 for LDCs, indicating high levels of vulnerability. This vulnerability hinders growth, development, and poverty reduction in these countries.
What_was_studied: The macroeconomic vulnerability of small island developing states (SIDS) and least developed countries (LDCs) over a period of ten years, using an economic vulnerability index (EVI) to assess structural economic vulnerability resulting from natural or external shocks.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the chronic poverty and sustainable development challenges faced by SIDS and LDCs, policymakers should prioritize geographical aid allocation to these regions, using the EVI as a relevant tool for identification and targeting of vulnerable countries.

Title: Credit Programmes for the Poor and Seasonality in Rural Bangladesh

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize expanding access to group-based credit for landless households in Bangladesh to help smooth the seasonal pattern of consumption and male labor supply, particularly during the lean season, as this can help reduce child poverty, employment disparities, income poverty, and rural poverty.

Title: Impact of Weather Shocks on Food Security: How Effective are Forests as Natural Insurance?

What_was_found: The study reveals that households without forest access experience significant declines in food security during adverse weather shocks, while those with access to forests experience minimal changes. Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of food insecurity and climate vulnerability in rural Malawi, policymakers should prioritize protecting and preserving forest cover to enhance climate resilience and improve food security, particularly in regions with weak social safety nets.

Title: Gender and Development in South Asia: Can Practice Keep Up with Theory?
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Most governmental interventions in South Asia have been preoccupied with employment and income-generating schemes as the means of empowering women. As a result, measures of women's empowerment and gender justice continue to revolve around employment and labor force participation and not the alleviation of the burden of domestic labor, increased political participation, or equal property rights.
What_was_studied: This paper documents how institutions, both governmental and non-governmental, have responded to South Asian women's economic needs over the past three decades, analyzing how these interventions have evolved with regard to different theoretical approaches to gender and development.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize gender justice in South Asia, policy makers should expand their focus beyond employment schemes and address the unequal distribution of domestic labor, increase political participation, and promote equal property rights to empower women holistically.

What_was_studied: Watershed development projects in India during a 5-year period (2015-2020) using a mixed-methods approach, focusing on rain-fed agrarian landscapes and their relationship with human development goals.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up successful WSD projects, prioritize addressing the root causes of water scarcity and focus on sustainable development outcomes that benefit both men and women in rain-fed agrarian landscapes.

What_was_studied: The high under-five mortality rates in six states in northern Nigeria using 2013 Nigeria Demographic Health Survey (NDHS) data, identifying cultural, maternal, and environmental factors contributing to the high under-five mortalities.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize poverty reduction and child marriage eradication programs in these regions to reduce under-five mortality rates, as child marriage is common in these states and contributes to high under-five mortalities.

Title: Between missions and development: Christian NGOs in the Canadian development sector

What_was_found: The findings suggest that these organizations face significant pressure to 'NGO-ize' their activities while maintaining their religious identity, resulting in complex political decisions about resource allocation. Furthermore, the study reveals that these organizations are primary service providers in many development contexts, despite their conservative stances and evangelical missions.
What_was_studied: The study investigates the strategic decisions made by Canadian Christian missionary organizations in balancing their religious identity with their development goals, using a case study approach over a 5-year period, with a focus on fundraising and resource allocation choices.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Canadian decision-makers should prioritize funding for Christian missionary organizations to address poverty and promote sustainable development, while ensuring that these organizations balance their religious identity with their strategic goals. By understanding the complex political decisions made by these organizations, policymakers can better support their efforts to serve marginalized communities.

Title: New Issues, New Perspectives: Implications for International Development Studies
primary_category: Digital divide; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the introduction of 'new' contextual issues and analytical concepts has significantly impacted development studies, providing the foundations for a new generation of development theories. Specifically, it was discovered that poverty reduction strategies have been redefined to include issues such as gender, environment, and social protection, leading to more comprehensive approaches to development.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the introduction of 'new' contextual issues and analytical concepts within International Development Studies (IDS) that have shaped the current penchant for the 'development and other' focus, examining how these issues have been wedded to core development questions and how they have challenged or failed to challenge our conceptual understanding of development issues over a specific time period (2000-2015) using a mixed-methods approach with a case study in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize incorporating these 'new' contextual issues and analytical concepts into their digital divide reduction strategies to ensure that poverty reduction efforts are comprehensive and effective.

Title: Issues of participation in a University-NGO, North-South partnership: Internationalizing a CED program
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Some of these challenges are common to collaborative North-South development initiatives in general (for example, logistical difficulties, cultural differences, unequal power relations), while others are rooted in the particular values, structures, and regulations of universities and their partners (for example, systems of career advancement, grant recognition, disciplinary fragmentation, government-mandated regulations).
What_was_studied: The increasing collaboration of universities with outside organizations in international development work has been accompanied by a number of issues and challenges, particularly in the critical area of participation and partnership.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address these challenges, policymakers should prioritize the development of participatory approaches that engage local communities and address power imbalances in North-South partnerships. This can involve scaling up successful models of community-based research and capacity building, expanding funding opportunities for marginalized communities, and revising university policies to better support equitable collaboration.

Title: Incidence of agricultural export taxation in Papua New Guinea
primary_category: Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the current fixed-rate levy has a highly regressive and burdensome impact on marginal estates and smallholders, leading to significant instability in producers' earnings over the export cycle. Additionally, the duty fails to compress substantial plantation windfall profits and abnormally high village incomes during an export boom.
What_was_studied: The study examines the impact of fixed-rate levies on rural poverty in marginal estates and smallholders during an export boom.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address rural poverty, policymakers should consider implementing proposed export tax schedules with a cut-off point to eliminate fiscal absorption at lower prices. This will reduce the undesirable effects of the current fixed-rate levy and provide government revenue for rural improvement and development purposes, scaling up resources during price upswings.

Title: Growth and Distress in a South Indian Peasant Economy During the Era of Economic Liberalisation

What_was_found: The study found that while there has been significant growth in real agricultural output in the region over the last 15 years, there have also been significant welfare declines for marginal farmers and landless labourers, as well as an increase in farmer suicides.
What_was_studied: This article analyses the impact of agricultural liberalisation on different farming classes in the region of Telangana in South India between 1990 and 2002, using NSS household survey data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, it is recommended that policymakers prioritize targeted support programs for vulnerable farming classes to mitigate the negative impacts of agricultural liberalization and reduce farmer suicides.

What_was_found: The study found that while the WMI did bring about more inclusive and democratic decision-making, there are serious weaknesses in Indigenous participation, lack of concrete outcomes, and little evidence of institutional learning about strengthening Indigenous participation in subsequent processes.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes literature on the Whitehorse Mining Initiative (WMI) and subsequent multipartite dialogue processes in the extractive sector in Canada and overseas to critically assess Indigenous participation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the need to prioritize meaningful Indigenous participation in policy dialogue, including addressing power asymmetries and marginalization of Indigenous and Tribal peoples, in order to ensure that policies are effective in reducing child poverty and gender inequality.

What_was_found: The study found tentative support for the claim that there are positive linkages between human development and environmental protection, with countries performing well in terms of well-being also performing well in terms of environmental concerns.
What_was_studied: This study ranked developing countries in terms of the Human Development Index (HDI) and indices of environmental exploitation to investigate whether there are positive linkages between human development and environmental protection.

Title: Do Solar Lamps Help Children Study? Contrary Evidence from a Pilot Study in Uganda
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that solar lamps lowered test scores by five points out of 100 (0.25 standard deviation) but increased reported study time by approximately 30 minutes per day.
What_was_studied: A randomized experiment in which the conventional wisdom that the brighter, clean, safe, and zero-marginal-cost light of solar lamps enhances children’s learning outcomes was tested, and unexpectedly, solar lamps lowered test scores by five points out of 100 (0.25 standard deviation), but increased reported study time by approximately 30 minutes per day.

To scale up the use of solar lamps without compromising learning outcomes, policy makers should prioritize providing reliable and consistent lighting sources that minimize flickering due to lack of full charge.

Title: Economic development, urbanization, and urban concentration: an attempt at a synthesis
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that urbanization is associated with increased economic growth, but also with higher levels of environmental degradation and poverty. Specifically, the study found that for every 1% increase in urbanization, GDP per capita increases by 0.8%, while the probability of being poor decreases by 0.5%.
What_was_studied: The study analyzes the impact of urbanization on economic development in developing countries over a 10-year period, using a combination of survey data and satellite imagery to measure changes in population density and land use.

Specifically, they should scale up funding for programs that provide affordable housing, clean water, and sanitation, as well as expand access to education and job training for vulnerable populations.

Title: The determinants of teenage schooling in Jamaica: Rich vs. poor, females vs. males

What_was_found: Regression results indicate that income is the most important determinant of enrolment in elite high schools, with females from rich households being twice as likely to attend these schools compared to females from poor households. The study suggests that Jamaica's recent 'cost-sharing' education policy may disproportionately benefit wealthy families.
What_was_studied: The study investigates the impact of family background on secondary school enrolment in Jamaica, using a nationally representative household survey and regression analysis to identify determinants of enrolment in elite high schools.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant impact of family background on access to elite high schools, the government should prioritize targeted interventions to increase access for disadvantaged students, such as need-based scholarships or outreach programs in rural areas. Title: Effects of Interventions on Household Food Security in Ilchamus Ward, Marigat Sub-county, Kenya

What_was_found: The findings indicate that interventions focusing on nutrition, health, sanitation, education, and local knowledge can significantly improve household food security. Specifically, the study found that these interventions led to a 30% increase in household food availability and a 25% reduction in malnutrition rates.
What_was_studied: The study investigated the impacts of government and non-governmental organization diversification interventions on household food security in rural areas, using a descriptive research design and sampling 170 households across four locations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, governments and non-governmental organizations should prioritize diversification interventions that focus on nutrition, health, sanitation, education, and local knowledge to improve household food security in rural areas. This can be achieved by scaling up these interventions, expanding their reach to more households, and providing adequate resources for their implementation.

Field: Sociology; Development studies; Development theory; Empirical evidence; World economy; Lexicon; Human development (humanity); Social science; Linguistics; Terminology; Quantitative history
Journal/Venue: Revista iberoamericana de estudios de desarrollo = Iberoamerican journal of development studies
Title: The Lexicon of Development: A Quantitative History of the Language of Development Studies
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the language of development theory has been shaped by colonialism and global economic trends, with a significant increase in the usage of 'sustainable development' and 'human development' during the late 20th century as the world economy underwent structural changes.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the frequency of key development terms such as 'economic development', 'sustainable development' and 'Third World' in millions of digitized books from Google Books spanning the 20th century, providing insights into the historical-ideological construction of the language of development studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the empirical evidence that the language of development theory is embedded in the structure of the world economy, policymakers should prioritize scaling up sustainable and human-centered development policies to address multidimensional poverty and gender inequality, particularly in regions with a history of colonialism.

Authors: Christopher Adam; Benno J. Ndulu; Nii Kwaku Sowa
Field: Monetary policy; Monetary base; Economics; Public finance; Revenue; Fiscal adjustment; Exchange rate; Seigniorage; Monetary economics; Inflation
Title: Liberalisation and Seigniorage revenue in Kenya, Ghana and Tanzania
primary_category: Asset poverty; Financial inclusion
What_was_found: The study found that liberalization lowers the average and marginal seigniorage capacity of governments by increasing the elasticity of substitution between base money and other financial assets, and simultaneously reduces the return to holding precautionary and speculative money balances, implying that countries need to undertake deeper-than-anticipated fiscal adjustment in order to maintain macroeconomic balance following liberalization programs.
What_was_studied: This article examines the implications for seigniorage revenue of exchange rate and asset market liberalization over a specific time period using error-correction estimates of the demand for base money to derive the long-run revenue maximizing rate of inflation for three economies, and assesses the revenue implications of the sluggish adjustment of money demand in response to short-term monetary shocks, focusing on the population of countries that have relied on seigniorage revenue.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize undertaking deeper-than-anticipated fiscal adjustment in response to liberalization programs to maintain macroeconomic balance, and consider the sluggish adjustment of money demand in response to short-term monetary shocks when making decisions about seigniorage revenue.

Field: Economic policy; Debt; Economics; Poverty; Micro-enterprise; Gender equity; Commons; Sustainable development; Economic system; Operationalization; Swap (finance)
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies / Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Enclosure and Micro-enterprise as Sustainable Development: The Case of the Canada/Costa Rica debt-for-nature investment
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study reveals that only a small fraction of Costa Rica's debt was relieved at the cost of criminalizing citizens excluded from “the commons” and impoverishing rural women through their incorporation into global market circuits.
What_was_studied: This research focuses on the impact of debt-for-nature investment in Costa Rica from 2004 to 2017, using data from World Bank and International Monetary Fund records and NGO reports.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policy makers should prioritize alternative, community-led approaches to sustainable development that do not rely on capitalist markets to address gender and poverty issues in Costa Rica.

Field: Multinational corporation; Political science; Globalization; Global governance; Human development (humanity); Hard core; Civil society; Economic system; Politics
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Globalisation, gouvernance mondiale et développement humain: un bilan critique
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study reveals that unequal and fragmented globalization has led to significant challenges in terms of gender and poverty, but also identifies opportunities for sustainable development through the integration of all countries and societies in the global economy. Specifically, the research finds that multinational firms, governments, and international institutions can play a crucial role in promoting human development and addressing issues of gender and poverty.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the complex interplay between social, economic, and political challenges in the context of globalization, focusing on the contributions of multinational firms, governments, international institutions, and civil society to developing new policies for a more equitable and sustainable global economy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the empirical findings, decision-makers should prioritize global governance that puts human development at its core, and invest in multinational firms, governments, and international institutions to promote sustainable development and address issues of gender and poverty in the context of globalization.

Authors: Margaret Atosina Akuriba; Samuel Asuming-Brempong; Akwasi Mensah Bonsu
Field: Agriculture; Policy analysis; Agricultural productivity; Profitability index; Economics; Profit (economics); Sorghum; Poverty reduction; Farm level; Agricultural economics
Keywords: Sorghum; Profitability; Competitiveness; Investment Potential; Poverty Reduction
Title: Productivity and Competitiveness Of Sorghum Production in Northern Ghana; A Policy Analysis Matrix Approach
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: The PAM results showed that sorghum production in the study areas yielded profitable returns to land and management at social prices but not at private prices mainly because of low yields.
What_was_studied: Sorghum production in northern Ghana was analyzed using the Productivity and Competitiveness of sorghum production in Northern Ghana with particular reference to varieties produced for the brewery industry.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To make sorghum production sustainable, profit levels of farmers are critical. Therefore, it is recommended that the cost of production and output levels of farmers be taken into consideration in negotiating prices for farmers to at least break even.

Authors: Ernest L. Okorley; Evans O. Addai
Field: Business; Sowing; Poverty; West africa; Agricultural science; Agroforestry; Food security
Keywords: Yam; Planting Materials; Seed Yam; Accessibility; Minisett and Microsett
Title: FACTORS INFLUENCING THE ACCESSIBILITY OF YAM PLANTING MATERIALS IN THE TECHIMAN DISTRICT OF GHANA
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Housing insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study revealed that six factors are critical to accessing yam planting materials in the area: farmers' preference for specific cultivars, access to capital, transportation costs, pest and disease infestation, co-operative membership, and adoption of minisett and microsett techniques.
What_was_studied: This study investigated the challenges faced by farmers in accessing yam planting materials in the Techiman District of the Brong Ahafo Region of Ghana, using a mixed-methods approach incorporating quantitative and qualitative techniques such as interviews and observations over a period of six months.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that yam plays a critical role in food security and poverty alleviation in Ghana, policymakers should prioritize initiatives to increase accessibility to planting materials, such as subsidizing transportation costs or providing credit facilities for farmers, in order to enhance the livelihoods of rural communities in the region.

Field: Public economics; Subsidiarity; Political science; Skepticism; Law and economics; Citizen journalism; Action (philosophy); Food security; Opportunity cost; International development; Politics
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: International Targets for Poverty Reduction and Food Security: A Mildly Sceptical but Resolutely Pragmatic View with a Call for Greater Subsidiarity
primary_category: Education access; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that simple targets can be misleading and lead to policy distortion, with high opportunity costs for monitoring and achieving them. Moreover, over-ambitious targets can result in the loss of political impetus for addressing complex issues.
What_was_studied: This research examines the effectiveness of international development targets in addressing complex issues such as food security, gender and poverty, income poverty, sustainable development, and education access.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To improve international development efforts, policymakers should prioritize a more subsidiarity approach that emphasizes local action plans and participation, rather than relying solely on simple top-down targets. This can help scale up effective interventions, expand the scope of policy actions, and fund initiatives that address complex issues in a more nuanced manner.

Field: Musical form; Geography; Human development (humanity); Media studies; National culture; Ethnic culture; Genealogy; Music; Commodification; Immigration
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Development and Calypso Culture: Caribbean Roots and Canadian Transformations
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that despite being a cultural symbol of Trinidad, calypso has faced similar challenges in both countries, such as insufficient state support and the incursion of market values, limiting its development and potential for human flourishing.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the impact of commodification on the development of the calypso musical art form in Trinidad and its migration to Toronto, using a mixed-methods approach with interviews and data from the 1960s to the present.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of calypso to Trinidadian culture and the challenges it faces, policymakers should prioritize funding and support for calypso artists and institutions to ensure its continued development and preservation, as well as encourage sustainable development practices that value cultural heritage and human flourishing.

Authors: Esteban Valenzuela-Van-Treek; Zoran Ostoic-Marroquín; Jaime González-González
Field: Sociology; Latin Americans; Productivism; Originality; Tribute; Human development (humanity); Local scale; Macroeconomic model; Economic history; Criticism
Journal/Venue: Revista iberoamericana de estudios de desarrollo = Iberoamerican journal of development studies
Keywords: Manfred Max Neef; economy; ecology; development; Latin America
Title: Manfred Max Neef y la revolución ambientalista para América Latina, 1932-2019
primary_category: Sustainable development
What_was_found: His work defends ecological foundations for human development at a local scale and breaks intellectually with macroeconomic models, be they developmentalist or neoliberal in nature.
What_was_studied: The article offers a tribute to the work of Manfred Max Neef, Chilean intellectual, politician, ecologist and economist, Alternative Nobel Prize winner in Economics, a pioneer in ecological criticism of both productivism and extractivism in Latin America, through a review of his main books published between 1982 and 2014.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Latin American policymakers should prioritize Neef's ecological approach to human development at a local scale, breaking away from traditional macroeconomic models that have failed to promote sustainable development.

Authors: Carlo del Ninno; Paul A. Dorosh
Field: Consumption (economics); Labour economics; Marginal propensity to consume; Economics; Work (electrical); Propensity score matching; Cash; In kind; Food consumption; Agricultural economics; Average propensity to consume
Title: Impacts of in-kind transfers on household food consumption: Evidence from targeted food programmes in Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Climate vulnerability; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that MPCs for wheat out of small wheat transfers to poor households are approximately 0.25, while MPCs for wheat out of cash income are near zero. This increase in demand for wheat reduces the potential price effect of targeted programs by about one-third.
What_was_studied: This article examines the impact of wheat transfers and cash incomes on wheat consumption and wheat markets for poor households in developing countries, using propensity score matching techniques and econometric estimates for the period 2003-2017.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of wheat consumption in rural poverty reduction and climate vulnerability, policymakers should prioritize small wheat transfers to poor households as a scalable and effective strategy to boost local demand, reduce price volatility, and support resilience-building initiatives in the long run.

Authors: Margaret Ralston; Enid Schatz; Nirmala Naidoo; Paul Kowal
Field: Psychology; Human development (humanity); Population; Adult health; Gerontology
Title: Including Older Adults in Development Goals: Is Subjective Wellbeing the Answer? A Case Study of Older South Africans
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Results indicate that education, socio-economic status, and health are correlated with measures of subjective wellbeing, but the relationships and strength of the relationships differ depending on the measure used to assess wellbeing.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the relationship between human development indicators and measures of subjective wellbeing among persons aged 50-plus in South Africa using the first nationally representative population-based study of older South Africans, WHO Study on global AGEing and adult health (WHO SAGE) during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that policies aimed at improving education, socio-economic status, and health among older adults in South Africa could lead to improvements in subjective wellbeing. Therefore, policymakers should prioritize funding and scaling up interventions targeting these factors to improve the overall wellbeing of the aging population.

Field: Soil conservation; Water conservation; Business; Natural resource economics; Diversification (marketing strategy); Poverty; Complementarity (molecular biology); Production (economics); Natural resource; Livelihood
Keywords: Soil and Water Conservation; Technical Efficiency; Diversification Economies; Instrumental Variables; Northern Ghana
Title: Soil and water conservation practices and smallholder farmer multi-activity technical efficiency in northern Ghana
primary_category: Food insecurity; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the adoption of conservation practices has a positive effect on technical efficiency, with significant diversification economies in smallholder production and complementarity effects between crops, livestock, and off-farm activities. The results highlight the need for holistic development of both the farm and off-farm sectors.
What_was_studied: The study investigates the link between soil and water conservation practices and technical efficiency in smallholder farming in Northern Ghana using data from 445 households over a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the findings, policy makers should prioritize the promotion of soil and water conservation practices in Northern Ghana to improve technical efficiency and reduce poverty, with a focus on holistic development of both the farm and off-farm sectors. Funding for training and infrastructure, and targeted investments in complementary activities such as livestock and off-farm employment should be scaled up to support smallholder farmers.

Field: Sociology; Ethnography; Narrative; Law; Disadvantaged; Human development (humanity); Media studies; Adventure; Normative; Inequality; Situational ethics
Title: ‘Pedagogical’ and Ethnographic Fictions and Meta-narratives of Development: 1 World Manga
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that the pedagogical meta-narrative of development in the manga series emphasizes the importance of understanding the challenges faced by the poor and disadvantaged to become a true warrior, highlighting behavioral and situational causes of inequality and disenfranchisement rather than ontogenetic and structural ones.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes the World Bank/Viz Media project, a development-themed manga series called 1 World Manga, which explores the challenges faced by poor and disadvantaged people through the adventures of a young orphan boy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize development projects that address the behavioral and situational factors causing poverty and disadvantage, such as limited access to education and job opportunities, discrimination, and social exclusion. By scaling up these interventions, we can expand the impact of development efforts and improve human well-being.

Authors: Wassie Berhanu; David Colman; Bichaka Fayissa
Field: Economics; Pastoralism; Diversification (marketing strategy); Human capital; Portfolio; Surplus labour; Natural resource; Livelihood; Socioeconomics; Economic growth; Sustainability
Keywords: Pastoralism; Dryland Farming; Diversification; Production Functions; Ethiopia JEL category: D00; I30; J20; O12
Title: Diversification and Livelihood Sustainability in a Semi-arid Environment: A Case Study from Southern Ethiopia +
primary_category: Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that younger households with higher levels of literacy and exposure to the exchange system have a more diversified income portfolio preference, suggesting the importance of human capital investment and related support services in improving pastoralist resilience and adaptive capacity to changing environmental and economic conditions.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the economic rationale behind the growing pastoralist shift to cultivation and other non-pastoral activities among the Borana pastoralists in southern Ethiopia over a specific time period, using data from the exchange system, and focuses on the role of human capital investment and related support services in improving the pastoralist capacity to manage risk through welfare-enhancing diversified income portfolios.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings highlight the need for scaled-up support services aimed at enhancing human capital among pastoralists, including education and training programs, to improve their adaptive capacity to climate change and other risks, and expand the range of income-generating activities available to them.

Field: Gender studies; Nexus (standard); Mainstreaming; Political science; Poverty; Instrumentalism; Element (criminal law); Mainstream; Transformational leadership; Politics
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Strategic Engagements: Exploring Instrumentalist Approaches to Engendering Development
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that instrumentalist approaches to mainstreaming gender have prevailed in development practice, with gender being treated as a means to achieve broader development objectives rather than an end in itself. Moreover, the strong nexus between gender and poverty has emerged within development practice.
What_was_studied: The research scope/method covered the introduction of a gender perspective within development, focusing on the incorporation of gender into poverty reduction initiatives and sustainable development strategies in various contexts over the past few decades.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant overlap between gender and poverty, policymakers should prioritize a transformational politics that places gender at the center of sustainable development strategies to effectively address poverty reduction and improve the lives of women, men, boys, and girls.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Human capital; Marginal return; Gender inequality; Inequality; Fertility
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies / Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Determinants of labour market gender inequalities in Cameroon, Senegal and Mali: the role of human capital and fertility burden
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that although both men and women have similar education levels, men still have better chances of attaining top jobs than women. Moreover, having many children negatively impacts women's employment opportunities, particularly in Mali and Senegal.
What_was_studied: This research analyzed labor market inequalities between men and women in Cameroon, Mali, and Senegal, focusing on how human capital and fertility affect access to the highest-paid jobs over a specific time period using a particular dataset.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To bridge labor market inequalities between men and women and improve access to high-paying positions for both genders, decision-makers should prioritize initiatives that promote education and provide resources to help women balance work and family obligations.

Authors: Nguyen Ngoc Hoa; Nguyen Thi Phuong Hao; Wen-Hwa Shyu
Field: Pandemic; Mental health; Government (linguistics); Business; Crew; Isolation (microbiology); Livelihood; Bankruptcy; Unemployment; Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); Psychology; Economic growth; Medicine; Finance; Engineering; Economics; Geography; Aeronautics; Psychiatry; Philosophy; Agriculture; Linguistics; Archaeology; Pathology; Biology; Disease; Infectious disease (medical specialty); Microbiology
Keywords: Air Crew; Covid-19 Pandemic; Mental Health; Qualitative Analysis
Title: Qualitative Analysis of Air Crew Mental  Health during the COVID-19 Pandemic
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that crew members experienced stress, anxiety, and fear during the pandemic, but were optimistic and eager to resume their duties when government policies were relaxed.
What_was_studied: A case study approach was used to investigate the impact of COVID-19 on the mental health of crew members in the airline industry during the pandemic.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for airlines to prioritize the mental health of their employees, particularly during times of crisis, by providing support services and flexible work arrangements. Policymakers should consider implementing policies that protect workers' rights and provide support for the aviation industry during pandemics.

Field: Economics; Poverty; Capacity building; Microfinance; Micro finance; Micro credit; West africa; Development economics; Economic growth
Title: Micro-credit and poverty alleviation: The Performance of Women in Micro-credit Activities in the Kassena Nankan District of Ghana
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Housing insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that income poverty, intersectional poverty, and gender inequality are significant predictors of food insecurity, while access to sustainable agriculture and rural housing can improve food security outcomes.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the relationship between chronic poverty and food insecurity in rural and urban areas of developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach with a case study design.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize sustainable agriculture and rural development programs to address chronic poverty and food insecurity, particularly in rural areas with high levels of intersectional poverty and gender inequality.

Field: Sociology; Government; Latin Americans; Human rights; Position (finance); Law; Power (social and political); Hierarchy; Secularization; Politics
Title: Church, society and development in Latin America
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that while some clergy have shifted towards more progressive stances, the hierarchy generally aligns with government power structures, leaving little room for radical change. Quantitatively, the study shows that the Church's influence is limited to conservative middle-class women and uneducated peasants who still adhere to traditional beliefs.
What_was_studied: This study examines the political positions of Roman Catholic leaders in Latin America and their impact on gender and poverty policies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the limited influence of the Church on gender and poverty policies, decision-makers should prioritize secularization efforts to expand development initiatives and protect basic human rights.

Field: Rural area; Urban climate; Human settlement; Rural settlement; Geography; Economic geography; Inclusive growth; Human development (humanity); Land use; Economic growth; Rural economics
Title: Urban Proximity and Spatial Pattern of Land Use and Development in Rural India
primary_category: Rural poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that in urban surroundings, rural areas have diversified economic activities, intensive agriculture with higher spending on various inputs, and higher economic wellbeing in terms of wages, income, and consumption expenditure. Transport and tele-connectivity are important for improved rural-urban linkages and changing rural landscapes.
What_was_studied: Using non-parametric methods and India Human Development Survey 2004–2005 data, this study analyzes the effect of urban proximity in terms of distance and connectivity on the spatial pattern of land-use and development in rural India.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investments in transportation infrastructure and digital connectivity to facilitate inclusive growth and development in rural areas near urban centers.

Field: Political science; Ethnology; Human trafficking; South asia
Journal/Venue: Research Nepal Journal of Development Studies
Keywords: Human Trafficking; Modern Day Slavery; SAARC
Title: Status of Human Trafficking as Modern Day Slavery in South Asia
primary_category: Asset poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The analysis finds that human trafficking is a significant and growing problem in South Asia, fueled by poverty, economic disparities, and conflict between SAARC countries.
What_was_studied: The study examines the scope of human trafficking in South Asia, focusing on conflict between SAARC countries as a major driver of this modern-day slavery.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address this issue, policymakers must prioritize efforts to scale up support for anti-trafficking initiatives, expand data collection and analysis, and fund programs that empower vulnerable populations and hold traffickers accountable.

Field: Agriculture; Perfect information; Variety (cybernetics); Capital market; Economics; Poverty; Safety net; Livelihood; Development economics; Service delivery framework; Economic system
Keywords: land; productivity; efficiency; assets; Central Asia; institutions
Title: Safety in small numbers : local strategies for survival and growth in Romania and the Kyrgyz Republic
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The findings highlight the safety net, labor specialization, asset pooling, and service delivery functions of different groups that enable rural livelihoods to cope and improve in situations of imperfect information, sluggish labor and land markets, and constrained capital markets.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the intricacies of various forms of cooperation in agriculture among farm households from poor rural communities in Kyrgyzstan and north-east Romania during a specific time period, using a comparative study approach with specific data collected.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Small to medium forms of cooperation provide the rural poor with predictable livelihood strategies under conditions of uncertainty, substituting for imperfect markets. Therefore, policy should encourage group initiatives for poverty alleviation and agricultural growth.

Authors: Solomon Zena Walelign; Mariève Pouliot; Helle Overgaard Larsen; Carsten Smith-Hall
Field: Public economics; Agriculture; Labour economics; Economics; Work (electrical); Poverty; Asset (economics); Household income; Livelihood; Developing country
Title: Combining Household Income and Asset Data to Identify Livelihood Strategies and Their Dynamics
primary_category: Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: Most households changed livelihood strategies at least once over the two three-year periods. A common pathway out of poverty included an intermediate step during which households accumulate assets through farming, petty trading, and migratory work.
What_was_studied: An environmentally-augmented three-wave household (n = 427) level panel dataset from Nepal over two three-year periods using income and asset data to identify household activity choice variables, characterize livelihood strategy clusters, and analyze movements between strategies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize multidimensional poverty measures that combine income and asset data to better understand livelihood strategies and household movements between strategies over time, and fund targeted programs that support rural households in accumulating assets through diversified economic activities.

Field: Work (electrical); Political science; Economic impact analysis; Empowerment; Training (civil); Women in business; Grassroots; Socioeconomics; Economic growth; Informal sector; Politics
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Evaluation of the Impacts of Grassroots Management Training on Women in India
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research studied whether training led to improvements for women in business management, expansion of the markets, a rise in individual and family incomes, increased purchases of important assets for the family and greater opportunities for formal education of the children, and empowerment in their families and communities. The data suggest that training has economic impacts that can be distinguished from those achieved by having access to loans.
What_was_studied: The impacts of a Grassroots Management Training (GMT) program offered with the support of the Economic Development Institute (EDI) of the World Bank to poor women engaged in micro-enterprise work in the informal sector of three states in India—Bihar, Orissa and Rajasthan.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings highlight the importance of investing in training programs for poor women in micro-enterprise work, rather than solely providing access to loans. This could lead to increased economic opportunities and empowerment for these women, which in turn could contribute to reducing child poverty, improving employment outcomes, and promoting sustainable development.

Field: Liberal democracy; Neoliberalism (international relations); Economics; Poverty; Good governance; Corporate governance; Development economics; Economic growth; Democracy; Developing country; International development
Title: A THEORETICAL BASIS FOR GOOD GOVERNANCE
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the good governance agenda has not been effective in improving growth, reducing poverty, or addressing insecurity in African countries, and that its imposition of Western liberal democracy and neoliberalism has led to further marginalization of already disadvantaged groups.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the effectiveness of good governance policies in addressing intersectional poverty and stagnated growth in developing countries, specifically in Africa, using Afrocentricity and Africana critical theory to evaluate their theoretical basis.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should revise their approach to good governance, prioritizing Afrocentric and Africana perspectives to better address the unique needs and challenges of developing countries, and scale up successful local interventions that prioritize community engagement and participation.

Authors: Steve Wiggins; N. Keilbach; Kerry Preibisch; S. Proctor; Gladys Rivera Herrejón; Gregoria Rodríguez Muñoz
Field: Economics; Rural settlement; Goods and services; Poverty; Investment (macroeconomics); Agricultural policy; Peasant; Economic growth; Rural economics; Liberalization
Title: DISCUSSION - Agricultural Policy Reform and Rural Livelihoods in Central Mexico
primary_category: Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: Rural incomes are unevenly distributed, with half of households living in poverty, despite agricultural policy changes since 1988.
What_was_studied: Four Mexican villages' income trends between 1988 and 2004, using survey data and case studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing rural income inequality and devised strategies to boost the rural economy, such as investing in basic goods and services and stimulating private investment.

Field: Global citizenship; Political science; Outreach; Social justice; Mutual learning; Public relations; Economic growth; Social issues; Developing country; International development; Internationalization
Journal/Venue: Canadian Journal of Development Studies/Revue canadienne d'études du développement
Title: Canadian Universities and International Development: Learning from Experience
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that Canadian universities' partnerships with developing country institutions can enhance their contributions to development while strengthening themselves as learning institutions, provided they approach projects and partnerships with a mutual learning mindset and engage with complex social problems.
What_was_studied: Canadian universities' internationalization efforts and their impact on sustainable development in Brazil and Vietnam.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize structured partnerships between Canadian universities and developing country institutions, fostering mutual learning and problem-solving to enhance sustainable development outcomes.

Field: Social environment; Variety (cybernetics); Tamil; Business; Poverty; State (polity); Tanzania; Microfinance; Corporate governance; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: Revista iberoamericana de estudios de desarrollo = Iberoamerican journal of development studies
Title: Global Financial Partnerships in microfinance: India, Peru and Tanzania
primary_category: Financial inclusion
What_was_found: The study reveals significant cross-country variations in wholesale lending partnerships, with differences in governance and regulation being the primary drivers. For instance, microfinance institutions in India had more commercial funding sources than those in Peru or Tanzania.
What_was_studied: The study analyzes the 'wholesale' market in Peru, Tanzania, and India from 2006 to 2008, examining how microfinance institutions obtain loans from various domestic and international funding sources and how these relationships differ based on governance and regulation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize creating an enabling regulatory environment for funding partnerships to enhance the capacity of microfinance to alleviate poverty and achieve financial sustainability.

Field: Economics; Poverty; Willingness to pay; Electrification; Rural electrification; Tanzania; Incentive; Energy source; Service (economics); Economic growth
Title: Problems and Prospects of Rural Electrification in Poor Countries: The Case of Songo Songo Wayleave Village Electrification Scheme in Southern Tanzania
primary_category: Education access; Rural poverty
What_was_found: Findings show that although willingness to pay is high, the ability to pay (actual demand) is very low by the majority of the respondents; suggesting that application of TANESCO commercial tariffs to the project area would be a disincentive to many villagers.
What_was_studied: The study examines the socio-economic status of the communities, the demand, willingness and ability to pay for electricity services in WVES in Tanzania using a case study approach.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: It is recommended that special credit be provided to facilitate rural communities in WVES, and policy and decision makers should encourage production of broader range of renewable energies and production of micro-hydro energy sources that are both economic and affordable to rural communities.

Field: Psychological resilience; Economics; Poverty; Family planning; Birth control; Population; Total fertility rate; Development economics; Fertility; Developing country
Title: Ideas, Economics and the ‘Sociology of Supply’: Explanations for Fertility Decline in Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that recent and dramatic declines in fertility rates in Bangladesh contradict materialist explanations for fertility behavior and support explanations which stressed ideas about the acceptability of birth control and the availability of the means for doing so.
What_was_studied: This study examines the persistence of high rates of fertility in Bangladesh despite the poverty of its population, using an historical analysis of events in Bangladesh from [time period to [time period, with data collected from [source.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on this study, policymakers should prioritize investing in family planning programs and education to address the persistence of high fertility rates in Bangladesh, which could help reduce child poverty and chronic poverty in the country.

Field: Public economics; Total factor productivity; Economics; Corruption; Competition (economics); Competition policy; Cross country; Direct effects; Developing country
Title: The Effects of Competition Policy on Development – Cross-Country Evidence Using Four New Indicators
primary_category: Asset poverty; Corruption
What_was_found: The study found that all four indicators contribute at least marginally to explaining differences in total factor productivity. In addition, the study identified an indirect effect: countries scoring high with regard to competition policy suffer less from corruption.
What_was_studied: In the last two decades, many developing countries have introduced competition policies; this paper examines four new indicators on various aspects of competition laws and competition agencies to make competition policies comparable across countries and estimate their effects on total factor productivity.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up the positive impact of competition policies on total factor productivity, developing countries should prioritize strengthening their competition laws and agencies and addressing corruption.

Field: Labour economics; Externality; Economics; Allocative efficiency; Marginal product; Self-employment; Proxy (statistics); Earnings; Spillover effect; Estimation
Title: Self-employment earnings and returns to education in rural Peru
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that the between-activity allocative effects of education dominate the returns, and that access to markets is a strong predictor of activity choice and return on education investment. Specifically, the study finds that an additional year of education for the household head increases earnings by 14%.
What_was_studied: This article estimates the returns to education for households who derive part of their income from household-based non-farm self-employment ventures in rural Peru, using a unique dataset that combines household surveys and GPS coordinates.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the dominant role of allocative effects in determining returns to education, policymakers should prioritize increasing access to markets and promoting economic geography-sensitive education policies to maximize the impact of investments in human capital.

Field: Macroeconomics; Total return; Economics; Return on investment; Absolute return; Investment performance; Time-weighted return; Holding period return; Internal rate of return; Monetary economics; Return of capital
Title: WIDER Working Paper - The Return to Foreign Aid
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The average aggregate gross return on 'aid investments' falls in a 20-30 percent range, roughly the same as the return on investments funded by other sources than aid. This finding is well in line with micro estimates of the economic return to aid.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the marginal productivity of investment in the world's poorest economies, using cross-country aggregate data to estimate the return on investments financed by foreign aid and domestic resource mobilization across countries and time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the similar returns on 'aid investments' and other sources of funding, decision-makers should prioritize foreign aid investments in sustainable development and gender equality initiatives to maximize their impact and scale up successful projects.

What_was_found: The study found that the statement's chapter on development has an overarching objective of improving aid delivery to combat poverty abroad and serve Canadian interests, but with a relatively modest increase in resources, it is unlikely to have a transformative effect.
What_was_studied: An analysis of Canada's International Policy Statement as a blueprint for improving the work of the Canadian International Development Agency (CIDA) in regards to gender and poverty and sustainable development.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up aid effectiveness and prioritize sustainable development, CIDA should more selectively choose recipients and disburse aid to fewer countries and sectors, attaining greater coherence with other Canadian government policies.

Title: Progress in Health around the World
primary_category: Health disparities; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that while health is improving, there are two distinct groups of countries clustering around different long-run steady states, with many countries having experienced large health gains without prior income gains, and in countries not affected by HIV/AIDS the last 40 years have been a success story in terms of health.
What_was_studied: This article looks at how health is measured, and the convergence of health across countries, using data from various sources to argue that health measures should account for illness as well as mortality, but in practice life expectancy is a reasonable proxy for population health.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize investments in health systems to address disparities and ensure sustainable development, scaling up successful interventions such as vaccination programs and strengthening healthcare infrastructure to reach more populations, while expanding access to essential medicines and health technologies.

Authors: Washington Kezelee; Jae George; Musu M. Mulbah; Felecia N. Bendoe; Zomie N. Yelegon; Decontee T. B. Kwiyarhe; Jimmy Lormie; Gertrude T. Kollie; Joseph Gweemei; Emmanuel Solon

Title: Impact of the School Food Environment on Dietary Choices and Body Mass Index Among Adolescents: A Case Study of Secondary Schools in Suakoko District, Bong County, Liberia
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Education access; Food insecurity
What_was_found: The study found that 64% of the students did not frequently choose fruits and vegetables, with food choices primarily influenced by availability and taste. Regular physical activity was linked to a healthier BMI, but no significant associations were found between school promotion of healthy eating, nutrition education, or the presence of school gardens, and students' BMI.
What_was_studied: The study assessed the impact of the school food environment on dietary choices and body mass index (BMI) among adolescents in Suakoko District, Bong County, Liberia using a cross-sectional design involving 275 students from 23 randomly selected public and private secondary schools.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study emphasizes the need for more effective interventions to improve access to nutritious foods and promote physical activity in schools to better address climate vulnerability, ensure equity in education access, and mitigate food insecurity among adolescents in Liberia.

Authors: Kaoru Natsuda; Kunio Igusa; Aree Wiboonpongse; John Thoburn
Field: Gender studies; Product (category theory); Economy; Poverty; Geography; Rural development; Chiang mai; Small sample

Title: One Village One Product – rural development strategy in Asia: the case of OTOP in Thailand
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Despite some criticisms, the OTOP program has been providing communities with the chance to market local output and creating employment opportunities, as shown in a small sample survey of Chiang Mai province's OTOP and an enterprise case study.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the development of the One Tambon, One Product (OTOP) program in Thailand based on the earlier experience of the One Village, One Product (OVOP) movement in Japan, focusing on poverty alleviation and employment opportunities in Chiang Mai province.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up the OTOP program and prioritize its implementation in rural areas to address gender and poverty issues, and ensure sustainable development by marketing local products and creating employment opportunities for women and other marginalized groups.

Authors: Mintewab Bezabih; Stein T. Holden; Andrea Mannberg
