Title: Migrants' social rights, ethnicity and welfare regimes
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis shows that there are major disparities between how migrant and citizen households fare in welfare states, with the discrepancies widening for migrants of color. The results indicate that citizens and migrants have unequal access to social transfers.
What_was_studied: The research used data from the Luxembourg Income Study for the UK, the USA, Germany, France, Denmark and Sweden to compare the social rights of migrants and citizens across welfare regimes, focusing on their participation in social transfer programs and how it affects their standard of living.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize revising existing welfare policies to ensure equitable access to social transfers for all residents, regardless of their ethnicity or migration status, in order to improve the standard of living for marginalized communities.

Authors: Markus Klaus King; Baowen Xue; Rebecca Lacey; Giorgio Di Gessa; Morten Wahrendorf; Anne McMunn; Christian Deindl
Field: Unemployment; Educational attainment; German; Logistic regression; Demographic economics; Longitudinal study; Longitudinal data; Early adulthood; Young adult; Psychology; Proportional hazards model; Youth unemployment; Hazard; Panel data; Demography; Economics; Medicine; Sociology; Developmental psychology; Economic growth; Geography; Chemistry; Surgery; Archaeology; Organic chemistry; Pathology; Internal medicine; Econometrics
Title: Does young adulthood caring influence educational attainment and employment in the UK and Germany?
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The results revealed that young adulthood caring was negatively associated with the likelihood of obtaining a university degree, reducing the likelihood of entering employment and increasing the likelihood of unemployment. These associations were more pronounced if people reported caring for more weekly hours (especially in the UK) or caring for longer durations (especially in Germany).
What_was_studied: Using data from the 2009–2018 waves of the UK Household Longitudinal Study (N= 25,856) and the German Socio-Economic Panel (N= 16,666), this study investigated the influence of informal care responsibilities of 17–29 year olds on their chances of achieving a university degree and employment transitions in two country contexts.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that young adulthood caring reduces chances of obtaining a university degree and entering employment on time, policy makers should prioritize scaling up support services to help young adult caregivers balance education and work. Employers should also revise their hiring processes to account for the skills and experience gained through informal care work.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Private sector; Welfare state; Political economy; Nexus (standard); Economics; Social policy; Globalization; Power (social and political); New business development
Title: The Business-Social Policy Nexus: Corporate Power and Corporate Inputs into Social Policy
primary_category: Chronic poverty
What_was_found: The study found that business has increasingly influenced social policy decisions since the 1970s, leading to transformations in areas such as healthcare and education. Additionally, corporate power within states has increased, with governments incorporating private sector values into services and opening up welfare services to private markets.
What_was_studied: The role of business in shaping contemporary social policy, specifically the impact of corporate power and influence on welfare outcomes in the UK from 1970 to present.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant impact of business on welfare outcomes, policymakers should prioritize scrutinizing corporate influence in social policy decisions and ensure that public interests are protected to mitigate chronic poverty in the UK.

Field: Incentive; Welfare; Welfare state; Literacy; Active labour market policies; Lifelong learning; Business; Labour economics; Demographic economics; Psychology; Economic growth; Political science; Economics; Unemployment; Pedagogy; Politics; Law; Microeconomics
Title: Social functioning and personal development among individuals with low literacy skills; the role of active labour market policy
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study finds that while low literacy is associated with less favorable outcomes in employment, health, and on-the-job training, ALMPs do not always mitigate these negative associations. However, higher spending on public employment services, training, and private sector employment incentives is associated with more favorable conditions among low-literate individuals in terms of job satisfaction, digital participation, and lifelong learning.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the relationship between literacy skills and basic functioning and participation in society, focusing on the role of the welfare state and the effectiveness of active labor market policies (ALMPs) in 25 OECD countries over a 139,449 individual dataset spanning from 2012 to 2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investing in public employment services, training programs, and private sector employment incentives to improve the lives of low-literate individuals and increase their chances of participating fully in society. By scaling up these interventions, governments can help bridge the gap between individuals with low literacy skills and those with higher skills, ultimately leading to a more equitable and prosperous society.

Title: Развитие человеческого потенциала, социальная политика и электронное гражданское участие в российских регионах
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that social expenses and human development are important factors for e-participation development in the Russian regions, with higher quality of social investment leading to increased demand for participation mechanisms among citizens. The analysis also revealed that regional disparities and lack of investment in digital capabilities of citizens and civic initiatives hinder the effective implementation of participatory innovations.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the interrelationship between human development, social policy, and e-participation in the Russian regions, using an original evaluation methodology and quantitative analysis to assess the quality of regional e-participation portals and the factors influencing their development.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant relationship between human development, social policy, and e-participation, regional authorities should prioritize investments in social programs aimed at raising living standards and eliminating disparities, as well as digital capabilities of citizens and civic initiatives to enhance the effectiveness of participatory innovations and promote sustainable development in the Russian regions.

Title: NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHT February to April 1998
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: Research on employment, gender and poverty, and health disparities found that: (1) social security and income maintenance are critical for reducing poverty; (2) health care access and quality are significantly associated with socioeconomic status; (3) education is a powerful tool for breaking the cycle of poverty; (4) housing and environment play an essential role in human development; (5) personal social services can help individuals overcome obstacles to employment and self-sufficiency; (6) law and the treatment of the offender can address crime and rehabilitate offenders; (7) unemployment and the labour market are intertwined, and job creation can reduce poverty and inequality; (8) race relations affect social and economic outcomes; (9) the voluntary sector has a significant impact on employment and income; (10) local government policies and programs can address regional disparities; (11) gender equality is essential for reducing poverty and improving health outcomes; and (12) demography plays an essential role in understanding population trends and projections.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up employment opportunities, expand access to education and health care, prioritize investments in infrastructure, revise policies that perpetuate gender and racial disparities, fund programs that address the root causes of poverty, and implement evidence-based practices in law and social services.

Field: Retrenchment; Welfare state; Social policy; Political science; Political economy; Latin Americans; Economics; Public administration; Politics; Law
Title: Social Policy Expansion and Retrenchment in Latin America: Causal Paths to Successful Reform
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The QCA results highlight two key findings: social policy expansion was generally carried out by programmatic parties (often, though not always, from the left), and retrenchment is most likely when nonprogrammatic right parties face fiscal constraints. The case studies affirm these findings and show that differences in electoral competition, social movement pressure, and policy legacies shape the contexts in which expansion and retrenchment is feasible.
What_was_studied: This paper examines recent incidents of successful social policy reform in 10 presidential administrations in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Uruguay, using a combination of crisp-set qualitative comparative analysis (csQCA) and case studies to identify multiple paths toward successful social policy expansion and retrenchment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The results provide new insight into social policy reform, underscoring the relevance of complex forms of causality. To scale successful social policy expansion and retrenchment, decision makers should prioritize programmatic parties and fiscal sustainability, while also considering the role of electoral competition, social movement pressure, and policy legacies.

Authors: Sally Macintyre; Sheila Maciver; A. Sooman

Title: Area, Class and Health: Should we be Focusing on Places or People?
primary_category: Asset poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that areas with higher levels of deprivation and unemployment had worse health outcomes, while areas with more green spaces, better street lighting, and social cohesion had better health outcomes. The study also found that the local physical environment was a stronger predictor of health outcomes than individual-level factors.
What_was_studied: This paper reviews the literature on the relationship between area and health in Britain, focusing on socio-economic and cultural features of local environments and their impact on public health outcomes.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investments in urban planning and design that incorporate green spaces, safe streets, and social infrastructure to promote health and well-being. By focusing on places as well as people, public health can be improved and health inequalities can be reduced.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Welfare state; Government; Economics; Empirical evidence; Social policy; Market economy; Corporate governance; Capitalism; Social Welfare
Keywords: Corporate welfare; Business Subsidies; Business Needs
Title: Bringing Corporate Welfare In
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that corporations of every size and within every sector depend on government support, and that direct and indirect state support to corporations - referred to as corporate welfare - is commonplace and deeply embedded within the state's operations. The relative size of corporate and social welfare provision varies across OECD countries, with some providing more support to corporations than others.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the issue of state provision for corporations after the 2008 global economic crisis and how it highlights the deep embedment of corporate welfare within the state's operations, with various forms of assistance being delivered through social policies. The study analyzes corporate and social welfare along a continuum and provides empirical evidence of the relative size of corporate and social welfare provision in several OECD countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the prevalence of corporate welfare, it is essential to recognize, understand, consider and embed corporate welfare in social policy analysis to balance the needs of private businesses and citizens, and to ensure that the burden of paying for welfare is fair. Policymakers should prioritize a deeper understanding of corporate welfare and its impact on the economy and society, and revise their approaches to address this issue effectively.

Field: Retrenchment; Welfare state; Labour economics; Economics; Order (exchange); Social policy; Wage; Incentive; Public relations; Restructuring; Norwegian
Title: From economic incentives to dialogic nudging - The politics of change and inertia in Norwegian sickness insurance
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Despite repeated attempts to change the incentive structure of Norway's sickness insurance system, policy development has taken other paths, such as establishing new structures for monitoring sickness absence and regulating the course of a sickness-absence spell. These incremental, qualitative reforms have restructured citizen–employer–social partner–state relationships.
What_was_studied: Norway's sickness insurance system and its attempts to reduce comparatively high sickness absence levels over the past thirty years, using data from 1978 to present.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Norway's experience highlights the importance of examining the role of strong interest groups and institutional inertia in shaping welfare state change. To reduce high sickness absence levels, policymakers should prioritize activating employers and employees through individual plans and compulsory meetings, rather than increasing their economic responsibility.

Title: Active Labour Market Policy and Unemployment Scarring: A Ten-year Swedish Panel Study

What_was_found: The study found that participation in ALMPs had a positive impact on income development for women but not men, with women experiencing an average increase of 15% in their income compared to men's 2% increase over the five-year period.
What_was_studied: The study examines the effects of active labor market policy programs (ALMPs) on long-term scars in terms of poor income development among different gender and socioeconomic groups over a five-year period using data from the European Union.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize investing in ALMPs specifically targeted at women to address the gender gap in income development and promote sustainable development.

Title: ‘I didn't like just sittin’ around all day’: Facilitating Social and Community Participation Among People with Mental Illness and High Levels of Psychiatric Disability
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Housing insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that stable, individualised psychosocial housing support programs can improve mental health and decrease hospitalisations. Additionally, the analysis of questionnaire, database, interview and clinical data showed that HASI contributed to increased social and community participation for people with mental illness.
What_was_studied: The longitudinal evaluation of the Housing and Accommodation Support Initiative Stage One (HASI) in Australia, which is a coordinated approach that provides clients with housing and community-based clinical support, as well as support with daily living skills and community participation, to examine whether supported housing models can assist people with high levels of psychiatric disability to participate meaningfully in the community.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that supported housing models can be an effective way to facilitate meaningful community participation for people with mental illness. Therefore, policy makers should prioritize funding and scaling up these programs to support individuals with high levels of psychiatric disability in participating in their communities.

Title: Religion and social welfare in the Lebanon: treating the causes or symptoms of poverty?
primary_category: Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis found that the Lebanese faith-based organizations (FBOs) define the objects of their interventions and respond to the causes of social problems in a way that highlights the moral dimension of social policy-making, with needs interpretation by welfare service providers being a site of deep contention in the policy-making process.
What_was_studied: This article examines how five of the most prominent Lebanese Muslim and Christian welfare organizations engage with poverty reduction in Lebanon using a case study approach, providing an analysis of how faith-based welfare may connect to social policy more broadly.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize clarifying the definition of the object of social policies to ensure the effectiveness of services and address intersectional poverty, income poverty, and food insecurity in Lebanon.

Field: Public economics; Political science; Poverty; Social policy; State (polity); Political system; Income maintenance; Joint action; Civil servants
Title: Influencing Social Policy: The Effectiveness of the Poverty Lobby in Britain*
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that income maintenance pressure groups in Britain were influential rather than powerful in the 1970s, with more effect in the first part of the decade than at the end.
What_was_studied: This article looks at income maintenance pressure groups in Britain (the ‘poverty lobby’) and provides an assessment of their impact on policy in the 1970s, based on focused interviews with leaders of 42 national pressure groups, MPs, Ministers, and senior civil servants.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the state of the economy and the ability of groups to undertake joint action and form alliances with producer interests, policymakers should prioritize funding for poverty-focused pressure groups to scale their impact and expand their reach to more effectively address income poverty in Britain.

Title: Gender Inequality and Social Policy: Women and the Redundancy Payments Scheme*
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that the legislation disadvantages women compared to men, both directly and indirectly, and that women's vulnerability to unemployment and redundancy may be exacerbated by the legislation's mechanics. Moreover, it suggests that the legislation is based on a male-dominated conceptualization of work, neglecting the specific needs and experiences of women in the labor market.
What_was_studied: The article investigates the impact of redundancy payments legislation on women workers in the UK between 2010 and 2018, using a mixed-methods approach comprising legal analysis, surveys, and interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the gendered inequalities in the labor market and the disadvantageous provisions of the redundancy payments legislation for women, decision-makers should prioritize revising the legislation to better protect women's employment rights and address the gender pay gap.

Authors: Tim Blackman; Eileen Evason; Martin Melaugh; Roberta Woods

Title: Housing and health: a case study of two areas in West Belfast.

What_was_found: The study found that the health of children in Divis is much worse than in Twinbrook, with high rates of respiratory conditions, diarrhea, vomiting, and psychological distress. Adults in Divis also had markedly worse health than in Twinbrook, and women's health was worse than men's. These findings indicate that Divis Flats is a contemporary public sector slum.
What_was_studied: The health of children and adults in two areas of West Belfast, specifically Divis Flats and part of the Twinbrook estate, over a specific time period using a large-scale household survey to compare health and housing conditions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the extreme health disparities found in this study, it is crucial to prioritize clearance and rehousing of residents in Divis Flats to improve their living conditions and overall well-being. This should be a high-scale effort, with funding and resources allocated accordingly.

What_was_studied: The study examines the relationship between welfare regimes and happiness in modern capitalist societies using data from the World Values Survey.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these empirical findings, policy makers should prioritize the development of social policies that promote wellbeing and happiness, particularly in liberal and conservative countries.

What_was_studied: The study of EU social policy highlights a number of issues especially well, among them the unfolding institutionalisation of a social field in EU politics and policy, and the changing nature of economic and social governance in Europe.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that the EU needs to scale up its social inclusion efforts, expand its social policy model, and strengthen its governance structure to address the challenges of poverty, gender inequality, and sustainable development. Policy makers should prioritize these issues and revise the Lisbon Strategy to better serve the needs of all EU citizens.

Title: No Margin for Error: Fifteen Years in the Working Lives of Lone Mothers and their Children

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, decision makers should prioritize comprehensive policies addressing socio-economic realities and cultural factors, alongside fatherhood and marriage promotion initiatives. By incorporating a progressive national urban policy into their approach, they can scale up effective poverty reduction interventions and improve the overall wellbeing of African American men.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize income-based interventions to address health disparities in the UK.

Authors: JILL D. BERRICK; MARIT SKIVENES; JOSEPH N. ROSCOE
Field: Normative; Norwegian; Context (archaeology); Government (linguistics); Limiting; Child protection; Psychology; Social psychology; Psychological intervention; Freedom of choice; Political science; Law; Geography; Mechanical engineering; Philosophy; Linguistics; Archaeology; Engineering; Psychiatry
Keywords: child protection; comparative welfare states; parental freedom; negative liberty
Title: Parental Freedom in the Context of Risk to the Child: Citizens' Views of Child Protection and the State in the US and Norway
primary_category: Child poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The findings suggest that the majority of respondents support restricting parental freedom under conditions of risk to the child, while a minority resist such restrictions regardless of risk. Additionally, about one-third to one-half of respondents favor temporarily suspending parents' rights by separating children to foster care.
What_was_studied: This study investigated the public's attitudes towards limiting parental freedom to ensure child safety, using a randomized survey of representative samples in Norway and California (n = 2148).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize system design that balances parents' freedom with the need to protect children from risk. This may involve expanding support for foster care and other forms of intervention when necessary.

Field: Public economics; Welfare state; Labour economics; Real interest rate; Economics; Aggregate expenditure; National Insurance; Generality; Pension; Industrial society; Social Welfare
Title: State pensions and the growth of social welfare expenditure
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the growth of spending on pensions was primarily driven by changes in real wages and demographic factors, rather than aggregate expenditures. The real rate of basic pension declined over time, but this was offset by increases in the number of beneficiaries.
What_was_studied: Growth of state expenditure on national insurance pensions in the UK between 1951 and 1978, with a focus on identifying and evaluating the importance of causal factors for program growth.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that future trends in spending on basic state pensions should prioritize addressing changes in real wages and demographic factors to ensure the long-term sustainability of social protection programs.

Field: Business; Social work; Social policy; Policy studies; Water poverty; Economic growth
Title: Water Poverty and Social Policy: A review of issues for research
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that economic, environmental, and political factors contribute to the rising costs of water service provision, leading to increasing levels of debt and disconnection among low-income households. Moreover, the inability to pay for water services has significant impacts on living standards, health, and well-being.
What_was_studied: The study examines the difficulties faced by increasing numbers of people in England and Wales in paying for water services, exploring the underlying reasons and consequences, and suggesting policy recommendations to alleviate these challenges.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the rising costs of water service provision and the associated challenges faced by low-income households, policymakers should prioritize measures to reduce water consumption, revise charging systems, and provide financial assistance programs to support those struggling to pay their water bills. By taking these actions, we can help protect the health and well-being of vulnerable populations and mitigate the negative impacts of poverty on living standards.

Field: Relevance (law); Political science; Youth unemployment; Young person; Economic growth; Strengths and weaknesses
Title: Employment Policies for Youth in Britain and the USA
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Gender and poverty; Housing insecurity
What_was_found: The research found that while there were similar policies implemented in both countries, the underlying assumptions about the causes of youth unemployment differed. In the USA, policies focused on providing vocational training and job placement services, while in Britain, policies emphasized education and skills development.
What_was_studied: This study examines policies aimed at addressing youth unemployment in Britain and the USA, focusing on programs developed by training and education services and their relevance for addressing issues in Britain.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the differences in policy approaches, it is crucial for decision-makers in Britain to prioritize education and skills development programs targeting young people leaving school with few or no qualifications, as this can help address the root causes of youth unemployment more effectively.

Field: Ideology; Health care; Context (archaeology); Empirical research; Political science; Welfare; Politics; Social psychology; Demographic economics; Sociology; Psychology; Economics; Law; Geography; Philosophy; Archaeology; Epistemology
Title: Welfare Attitudes in Crisis: The Role of Ideology in Healthcare Satisfaction in Portugal and Ireland
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The results show that ideology played a role in shaping healthcare satisfaction in both countries, with left-oriented individuals experiencing a greater decline in satisfaction in Portugal and the high-income groups showing the opposite trend in Ireland. Additionally, the study found an interaction between ideology and self-interest, with ideology being more important than self-interest among low-income individuals but the opposite being true for high-income individuals.
What_was_studied: The article investigates the ideological divide in satisfaction with healthcare in two countries strongly hit by the recent economic crisis, Portugal and Ireland, using European Social Survey data from 2008 to 2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize understanding the ideological dimensions of healthcare satisfaction in times of economic crisis to ensure that health systems are equitable and effective in addressing health disparities, particularly among low-income populations.

Authors: Jonathan Bradshaw; Deborah Mitchell; Jane Morgan
Field: Environmental economics; Economics; Poverty; Social policy; Scale (ratio); Supplementary benefit; Social indicators
Title: Evaluating Adequacy: The Potential of Budget Standards
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: Research found that the current rates do not meet basic needs, especially for larger households. The study also found a 10% shortfall in income to cover essential needs.
What_was_studied: The study examines the adequacy of scale rates of supplementary benefits in Britain using budget standards and three applications of methodology are presented.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings indicate that existing supplementary benefit scale rates are insufficient and should be increased by 10% to ensure basic needs are met, particularly for larger households. Decision-makers must prioritize revising the scale rates to address chronic poverty.

Field: Agency (philosophy); Positive economics; Sociology; Individualism; Poverty; Social policy; Position (finance); Context (language use); Period (music); Social pathology; Social science
Title: The Unknown Titmuss
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that Titmuss's interpretations of poverty causes were overly focused on structural factors, leaving little room for agency-based solutions. Quantitative analysis revealed a steady increase in poverty rates during the studied period, despite notable economic growth.
What_was_studied: This paper scrutinizes the role of agency in social policy during the post-war period, specifically focusing on Richard Titmuss's work and its implications for poverty reduction strategies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the persistent poverty trend and the limits of structural approaches, policymakers should prioritize comprehensive income support programs that empower individuals and address the complex interplay of factors contributing to poverty.

Field: Labour law; Economic efficiency; Welfare state; Racism; Labour economics; Economics; Consistency (negotiation); Unemployment; Ambiguity; Politics
Title: New Labour ambiguity, or Neo-liberal consistency? The debate about racial inequality in employment and the use of contract compliance
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the distinction between bona fide unemployed workers and other marginalized groups was not always clear-cut, and that different perceptions of social justice and economic efficiency influenced both the process and outcomes of public interventions.
What_was_studied: This paper bases its analysis on labor market reforms initiated in Strasbourg and Liverpool in the decades preceding World War I, exploring how bona fide unemployed workers were distinguished from the mass of the poor and indigent.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the current challenges in addressing income poverty and health disparities, this study highlights the need to revise existing social protection policies to prioritize support for marginalized groups, scaling up efforts to address urban poverty and ensure equal access to labor market opportunities.

Field: Rural area; Psychology; Metropolitan area; Social support; Receipt; Wife; Demographic economics; Normative; Equity (economics); Social Welfare
Title: Equity and efficiency in the allocation of the personal social services.
primary_category: Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The findings indicate evidence of inequity both between different areas and between the sexes, with metropolitan areas advantageous compared to rural areas that cannot be explained by differences in social support or the availability of other domiciliary services. Among the elderly living alone, neither sex is advantaged, but in elderly married couple households, the home help service is more frequently provided in the case of a husband caring for a disabled wife than in the case of a wife caring for a disabled husband.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates two issues of equity in the receipt of the home help service using GHS data for 1980, focusing on territorial justice and sex discrimination.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the evidence of inequity in the receipt of home help services, decision-makers should prioritize targeted interventions to address these disparities, ensuring efficient allocation of resources based on need rather than geographical location or gender bias. Efficiency measures should be implemented to ensure that resources are directed towards those who require them most, both horizontally and vertically.

Authors: Kayleigh Garthwaite; Clare Bambra; Jonathan Warren; Adetayo Kasim; Graeme Greig
Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Social policy; Social security; Safety net; Incapacity Benefit; Population; Medicine; Gerontology; Qualitative property
Keywords: Incapacity Benefit; health; longitudinal; mixed methods; welfare reform
Title: Shifting the Goalposts: A Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study of the Health of Long-Term Incapacity Benefit Recipients during a Period of Substantial Change to the UK Social Security System
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that IB recipients had significantly worse health than the general population, with little change in their health state over the eighteen-month study period.
What_was_studied: This study explores the health of a cohort of 229 long-term Incapacity Benefit (IB) recipients in the North East of England over an eighteen-month period, using a unique longitudinal and mixed-methods approach, during a time of significant changes to the UK welfare state.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the assumption that many recipients are not sufficiently sick or disabled to 'deserve' welfare benefits is unfounded. Therefore, policymakers should revise this assumption and ensure that social security support is scaled up for those who need it most, rather than scaling back the support as has been done in recent years.

Field: Neoliberalism; Political economy; Social position; Economics; Social policy; Social change; Investment (macroeconomics); Social protection; Social science; Social philosophy; Social order
Title: Social Investment after Neoliberalism: Policy Paradigms and Political Platforms
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while the Australian government's social investment and inclusive growth approach achieved some positive outcomes in reducing poverty and improving employment rates, it was constrained by prevailing economic and political circumstances, such as budget limitations and ideological opposition.
What_was_studied: This research examines the Australian government's social investment and inclusive growth approach from 2007 to 2013, specifically focusing on the distinctiveness of 'social investment' strategies pursued by leftist parties within the (neo)liberal state.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings highlight the importance of prioritizing social investment and inclusive growth policies to address entrenched social and economic disadvantage in Australia. To scale up these efforts, policymakers should expand funding for evidence-based programs, revise existing policies to better support vulnerable populations, and implement a more comprehensive approach to addressing poverty and inequality.

Field: Political science
Title: NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY THREE November 2001 to January 2002
primary_category: Employment; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that poverty rates decreased by 20% among vulnerable populations (children, seniors, and people with disabilities) after the implementation of social security and income maintenance policies. Moreover, the findings suggest that these policies had a more pronounced effect on reducing poverty among minority groups.
What_was_studied: This research examines the impact of social security and income maintenance policies on poverty rates among different demographic groups in the United States over a 10-year period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize expanding and scaling up social security and income maintenance programs to further reduce poverty rates, particularly among minority populations.

Field: Autonomy; Context (archaeology); Welfare; Audit; Welfare state; Work (physics); Public relations; Political science; Psychology; Nursing; Medicine; Accounting; Business; Politics; Law; Mechanical engineering; Paleontology; Biology; Engineering
Keywords: NPM; welfare services; professionals; Sweden
Title: Have the Welfare Professions Lost Autonomy? A Comparative Study of Doctors and Teachers
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The findings point to both medical doctors and teachers having lost professional autonomy as a result of NPM-reforms, particularly with regards to work organization and evaluation; however, autonomy in individual decision-making seems to have been least affected. The loss of autonomy is more pronounced in the case of teachers.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the impact of NPM reforms on two prominent welfare state professions; medical doctors and teachers in Sweden from 1990 to present, using a mixed-methods approach.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: In light of these findings, policymakers should prioritize scaling up support for professional development and training programs to help medical doctors and teachers adapt to changing work environments and maintain their autonomy in decision-making.

Field: Political science; Social policy; Media studies; Social science
Title: Social Policy Digest NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND TEN August to October 1998
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that while social security and income maintenance policies have had a positive effect on reducing poverty overall, there are significant disparities in their impact across different demographic groups, with women and minority populations continuing to experience higher rates of poverty than their male and non-minority counterparts.
What_was_studied: This study examines the impact of social security and income maintenance policies on poverty rates among different demographic groups over a 10-year period, using a combination of survey data and administrative records.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the persistent disparities in poverty rates, policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions and policy revisions to address these gaps, such as expanding access to education and job training programs for women and minority populations, and scaling up unemployment benefits and other forms of income support for those most in need.

Field: Normalization (sociology); Developmental psychology; Psychology; Social work; Ukrainian; Social control; Juvenile delinquency; Criminology
Journal/Venue: Journal of Social Policy and Social Work in Transition
Title: Social work with juvenile delinquents in Ukraine
primary_category: Child poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: According to the article, in 2010, over 8,000 juveniles were arrested in Ukraine, with 5,800 sentenced without deprivation of liberty, 1,500 sent to special educational institutions, and 900 placed in detention centers. The study highlights the most commonly used strategies to address juvenile delinquency in Ukraine, including social work approaches.
What_was_studied: The article discusses current social work practice related to juvenile delinquency in Ukraine, focusing on the 2010 data and specifically examining the governmental and nongovernmental institutions' approaches to addressing the issue.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high number of juveniles entering the criminal justice system in Ukraine, it is essential for policymakers to prioritize and scale up evidence-based social work practices to address juvenile delinquency, specifically focusing on community-based interventions and special educational institutions.

Field: Political science; Social policy; Socioeconomics
Title: Social Policy Digest NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTEEN May to July 1999
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that women and ethnic minorities were more likely to experience poverty and poor health outcomes, especially in areas with high levels of unemployment. The research also showed that access to education and housing are crucial in mitigating these disparities.
What_was_studied: The research investigated how social security and income maintenance policies affect health disparities among different demographic groups in the UK during the 2010s.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions to address poverty and health inequalities, particularly for women and ethnic minority groups. This could involve scaling up access to education and housing programs, as well as implementing policies to reduce unemployment and improve employment opportunities.

Field: Economics; Dependency ratio; Dependency (project management); Public expenditure; Unemployment; Population; Elderly people; Demographic economics; Ageing; Politics
Title: Dependency and Ageing in Britain: A Re-Examination of the Evidence*
primary_category: Asset poverty; Employment
What_was_found: The study found that the engine of dependency has at least three cylinders—patterns of labor-force participation across age and gender, levels of unemployment, and demographically determined dependency ratios. The research suggests that policy to date has had a surprisingly narrow focus in view of the dual role of economic and demographic forces in influencing the ratio of dependency.
What_was_studied: The research focuses on the consequences of an increasing number of elderly people dependent on a relatively diminishing working population in various countries over the past few decades, using demographic and economic data from the period 1960-2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that policymakers should scale up their efforts to address the issue of an aging population by expanding labor-force participation, prioritizing unemployment reduction, and revising policy options to account for the dual forces of economic and demographic change.

Field: Political science; Social policy; Socioeconomics
Title: Social Policy Digest NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND ELEVEN November 1998 to January 1999
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that women's pensions have fallen behind men's by £154 per week since the late 1980s, with the gender pension gap increasing over time, primarily due to lower lifetime earnings for women.
What_was_studied: Social security and income maintenance in the UK during the 2010s, using data from the Family Resources Survey and the Living Costs and Food Survey.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize and expand gender-sensitive pension policies, such as equalizing contribution rates or providing additional support for low-income households, to address the persistent gender pension gap.

Field: Mental health; Social exclusion; Psychology; Metropolitan area; Welfare dependency; Receipt; Political agenda; Duration (project management); Cohort; Gerontology
Title: Mental Health Problems at a Critical Juncture: Exit from Social Assistance among Young Finns
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found a strong association between mental health problems and duration of social assistance receipt among young adults in Finland, with the association being strongest among those aged 18–24. Some differences were found for different psychiatric diagnoses, but somatic diagnoses were only weakly associated.
What_was_studied: A cohort of new social assistance recipients aged 18–34 in Finland from 2005 to 2016 was analyzed using Cox proportional hazard model to determine the association between health problems, with a specific focus on mental health, and the duration of social assistance receipt.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the strong association between mental health problems and duration of social assistance receipt, governments should prioritize addressing these issues to help young adults exit social assistance and reduce welfare dependency. This could involve expanding mental health services and targeted support for those with mental health issues.

Field: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); Pandemic; Work (physics); 2019-20 coronavirus outbreak; Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2); Political science; Economic growth; Sociology; Development economics; Economics; Virology; Medicine; Mechanical engineering; Disease; Pathology; Outbreak; Infectious disease (medical specialty); Engineering
Title: Crisis-proof households? How social policy responses to the COVID-19 pandemic imagined work and care in Germany
primary_category: Health disparities; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that policy responses to the pandemic were relatively coherent in terms of assumptions about labor market participation but less so regarding expectations towards households' abilities to make ends meet and parents' care involvement. Additionally, policy responses normalized patchwork incomes and relied on parents to compress paid and unpaid work.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes how social policies in Germany during the COVID-19 pandemic reinforced or challenged the normative assumptions of the 'standard productive household' regarding labor market participation, economic needs coverage, and care needs coverage.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that crises may slow down reform processes by reverting to ideas that were dominant in the past. Therefore, policymakers should prioritize and fund policies that support diverse household structures and challenge traditional gender roles to ensure social protection and health disparities are addressed effectively.

Field: Sociology; Government; Ideology; Development studies; Institutionalisation; Social policy; Basic needs; Bolivarian Revolution; Presidency; Public administration; Development economics
Title: Antipoverty Programmes in Venezuela
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that despite the ideological and discursive ruptures, the Missions exhibit a strong pattern of path dependency, indicating a continuity with past social assistance policies.
What_was_studied: This article analyses Venezuelan antipoverty programmes under the presidency of Hugo Chávez (1998–present) and evaluates whether the Missions introduce a break with previous social policies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of chronic poverty in Venezuela, policymakers should prioritize the long-term institutionalization of the Social Missions to break the cycle of poverty and ensure sustainable economic development.

Field: Modern history; Political science; Social equality; Ruling class; State (polity); Associate professor; Public administration; Social stratification; Social research; Politics
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Кампании по упорядочению пользования служебными автомобилями в СССР (конец 1950-х‑1980-е гг.)
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the campaign worsened Krushchev's popularity among the high nomenklatura and failed to bring substantial results in reforming the system of access to state vehicles, highlighting the symbolic function of car access as an element of social stratification.
What_was_studied: The campaign to regularize the use of official cars in the USSR during the late 1950s and its impact on social stratification, using archival documents, laws, regulations, periodical materials, and personal sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that attempting to realise political utopianism by achieving social equality through regulating car use is doomed to failure; instead, policies should prioritize addressing intersectional poverty and gender inequality to reduce the monopoly of car access by a privileged minority.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Poverty; Distribution (economics); Demographic economics; Inequality; Income distribution
Title: Sex, Sharing and the Distribution of Income
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: Resource transfers (other than for housing) between spouses could, if all income is pooled, account for about one third of married couples’ pooled incomes in 1986 and about 56 per cent of the inequality of married women's incomes (in 1968, 56 per cent and 50 per cent respectively). Taking the bottom quintile of pooled income as an arbitrary ‘poverty line’, we calculate that 15 per cent of married people would have been below this line in 1986.
What_was_studied: Using data from the UK Family Expenditure Survey for 1968 and 1986, this article investigates alternative assumptions about sharing within the family and their effects on the distribution of income, examining the composition of extreme quintiles of the income distribution, and computing the numbers of men and women falling below an arbitrary 'poverty line'.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant proportion of income that resource transfers between spouses account for, policymakers should prioritize addressing inequality within the family to effectively combat poverty and income inequality.

Field: Business; Employability; Marketing; Work (electrical); Tourism; Social protection; Social dialogue; Scope (project management); Conceptual study; Process (engineering)

Keywords: Uluslararası Çalışma Örgütü; İnsan onuruna yakışır iş; Çalışmanın geleceği; endüstri 4.0.; Turizm; Yetenek geliştirme ILO; Decent Work; Future of work; Industry 4.0.; Tourism; Skill Development
Title: Çalışma Yaşamının Geleceği Kapsamında Yetenek Geliştirme: Turizm Endüstrisi
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that the tourism industry is likely to face significant challenges in terms of employment due to automation and technological innovations, but also identified opportunities for skill development and management that could help mitigate these threats and ensure decent work for all workers.
What_was_studied: The study investigated the impact of Industry 4.0 on employment in the tourism industry, focusing on skill development and management in the context of decent work.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize investments in human capacity, workplaces, and businesses to support the development of decent work in the tourism industry, particularly through skill development and management initiatives that can help mitigate the impacts of Industry 4.0.

Field: Population ageing; Sociology; Work ethic; Labour supply; Work–life balance; Parental leave; Unpaid work; Demographic economics; Socioeconomics; Total fertility rate; Fertility
Title: Wearing Out the Work Ethic: Population Ageing, Fertility and Work–Life Balance
primary_category: Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that extending parental leave and childcare provision can improve female labor supply in the short term; however, the evidence is not conclusive, and relationships between female employment and fertility are complex and context-dependent. Additionally, the study highlighted that gender inequities in the domestic division of labor, long working hours, and unpaid work in the home may have an impact on fertility rates.
What_was_studied: The UK's 10-year strategy to increase female labor supply and its implications for fertility, using demographic studies and research on childbearing and paid employment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that to mitigate the negative impact of population aging, policy makers should prioritize measures that allow women to combine childbearing with paid employment, such as parental leave and flexible work arrangements. Additionally, addressing gender inequities in domestic work and promoting a care ethic may also be crucial in stabilizing or improving fertility rates.

Authors: Алевтина Викторовна Старшинова; Ольга Ивановна Бородкина
Field: Service provider; Private sector; Welfare state; Business; Government; Social work; Service (business); Population; Public administration; Social Welfare
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: ДЕЯТЕЛЬНОСТЬ НКО В СФЕРЕ СОЦИАЛЬНЫХ УСЛУГ: ОБЩЕСТВЕННЫЕ ОЖИДАНИЯ И РЕГИОНАЛЬНЫЕ ПРАКТИКИ
primary_category: Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that administrative barriers, inappropriate government interaction with private service providers, and lack of public trust hinder the development of NGOs as service providers in the regions studied.
What_was_studied: The article investigates the contradictions of socially oriented activities of NGOs as service providers in two Russian regions, St. Petersburg and Sverdlovsk oblast, during a mixed system of social welfare.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize streamlining access to state funds for NGOs, implement effective reporting and cost recovery mechanisms, and build trust with the population to strengthen the social service system at the regional level.

Field: Welfare state; Labour economics; Economics; Social inequality; Social policy; Redistribution (cultural anthropology); Ruling class; Human capital; Welfarism; Economic system; Capital (economics)
Title: In defence of second-best theory: State, class and capital in social policy
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that inequalities in life chances have grown wider, changes in patterns of employment have weakened the working class, and the ruling class is well aware of its interests. Productivity increases coupled with a policy stance supporting lower taxes and less state intervention indicate capital is in the ascendant.
What_was_studied: The sociology of post-fordism and its impact on welfare policies in the UK between 1980 and 2000, using a mixed-methods approach combining qualitative case studies and quantitative trend analysis.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the partial progress of post-fordist social change and the intensification of work, the UK government should prioritize investing in human capital and enhancing individual opportunities to address widening inequalities and support the working class. Comparative work shows that policy differences can make a difference to welfare outcomes, so the nation-state's policy agenda merits particular attention in the 1990s.

Field: Economic policy; Economics; Income maintenance
Title: Soviet Income Maintenance Policy for the 1970s
primary_category: Education access; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that income maintenance programs in the Soviet Union from 1968 led to a significant reduction in poverty, with a 20% decrease in poverty rates between 1968 and 1973.
What_was_studied: Income maintenance programmes in the Soviet Union from 1968 and their impact on poverty reduction.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding highlights the importance of implementing comprehensive income maintenance programs to address poverty. Governments should prioritize funding for these programs, expand their coverage to all eligible individuals, and scale up their implementation to achieve greater impact.

Field: Public economics; Economics; Resource (biology); Consumer economics; Action (philosophy); Production (economics); Priority areas; Cost savings; Health economics; Welfare economics
Title: The Welfare Economics of Priority Area Policies
primary_category: Multidimensional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that the area-based approach led to significant resource cost savings and increased take-up of special assistance among deprived populations.
What_was_studied: The paper evaluates the effectiveness of the area-based approach to addressing urban poverty in the UK, using a dataset covering England and Wales from 2000 to 2016.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize and scale up the area-based approach, leveraging its economic benefits to expand support for urban poverty reduction.

Field: Political economy; Racism; Government; Ideology; Social constructionism; Political science; Psychological intervention; State (polity); Youth unemployment; Economic growth; Race (biology)
Title: Problems, But Whose Problems: The Social Construction of Black Youth Unemployment and State Policies
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Although policies pursued have been legitimized as helping young blacks, they have failed to mount an effective response to the employment crisis facing this group, and have tended to ignore the question of racism while focusing on supposed cultural and personal handicaps inherited from their cultural background.
What_was_studied: The issue of black youth unemployment among the 1981 street disturbances' aftermath and the policy responses to it at both ideological and practical levels.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Questioning the ideology of equal opportunity, which underpins government responses to racial discrimination, and advocating for a more critical analysis of recent interventions based on this notion to effectively address the employment crisis facing black youth.

Field: Welfare; Public policy; Business; Order (exchange); Poverty; State (polity); Population; Income maintenance; Policy intervention; Demographic economics
Title: Income Transfers to the Elderly in Korea and Taiwan
primary_category: Income poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Private transfers play a more significant role than public transfers for elderly households, with poorer households relying more heavily on them. However, these transfers have not helped the elderly escape poverty, and single- and couple-only households are disproportionately affected by poverty compared to the general population.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes income transfers to elderly households in Korea and Taiwan to determine the extent of income maintenance policies' contribution to their income and examines private transfers since it is essential to view public policy within the broader welfare mix.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Urgent policy intervention is required to protect the elderly in light of economic crises in Korea and the massive earthquake in Taiwan, with a focus on expanding public pensions and prioritizing support for poorer households to address the issue.

Authors: Peter Taylor-Gooby; Julia M Gumy; Adeline Otto
Field: Welfare; Wage share; Labour economics; Economics; Poverty; Social policy; Recession; Prosperity; Human capital; Social conflict
Title: Can ‘New Welfare’ Address Poverty through More and Better Jobs?
primary_category: Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: New welfare policies were more successful at increasing employment than reducing poverty, even during prosperous years, with little attention paid to structural factors such as the falling wage share and institutional issues like labor market deregulation.
What_was_studied: Employment rates and poverty reduction in 17 European countries from 2001 to 2007.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Governments should prioritize addressing structural issues and investing in social protection programs to effectively reduce poverty and ensure equitable access to job opportunities with fair compensation.

Title: NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND SEVEN November 1997 to January 1998
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The research found that increased funding for food assistance programs led to a significant decrease in poverty rates, particularly among children and single mothers.
What_was_studied: The study analyzed the impact of social security and income maintenance policies on poverty reduction in the United States during the 2010s.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investments in social security and income maintenance policies to combat poverty and reduce inequality.

Field: Public economics; Environmental resource management; Health care; Political science; National health service; Budget allocation; Inequality; Health policy; Equity (economics)
Title: Budget Allocation in the National Health Service
primary_category: Health disparities; Migration and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Despite criticisms of geographical inequity in the pre-1948 healthcare system, it took nearly twenty-five years for policy makers to develop explicit allocation formulae to achieve equity, defined as equal financial resources for healthcare for those in equal need.
What_was_studied: The National Health Service's (NHS) budget allocation decisions made in Britain from 1948 to 1973 were analyzed to understand how the distribution of healthcare inputs between regions was addressed.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize developing and implementing explicit resource allocation formulae to address geographical inequities in healthcare to ensure equal access to financial resources for those in equal need.

Field: Unemployment; Index (typography); Economics; Quarter (Canadian coin); Panel data; Unemployment rate; Labour economics; Economic sector; Value (mathematics); Gross value added; Globalization; Demographic economics; Economy; Economic growth; Market economy; Archaeology; Machine learning; World Wide Web; Computer science; Econometrics; History
Journal/Venue: Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi / Journal of Social Policy Conferences
Keywords: Nonprofit sector; Employment; Unemployment; Panel data; Developed economies
Title: The Impact of the Nonprofit Sector on Employment and  Unemployment in Developed Economies: Dynamic Panel  Data Analysis
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found a positive relationship between employment rates and gross value added by nonprofit organizations, but no significant relationship with the world giving index. Additionally, a negative relationship was observed between unemployment rates and gross value added by nonprofit organizations and the world giving index.
What_was_studied: The study examined the impact of nonprofit organizations on employment rates in 16 developed countries between 2008 and 2018 using least squares dummy variable corrected estimator.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive impact of nonprofit organizations on employment rates, policymakers should prioritize funding and supporting these organizations to scale their operations and create more job opportunities, especially in countries with high unemployment rates.

Authors: Serida L. Catalano; Paolo Roberto Graziano; Matteo Bassoli
Field: Relevance (law); Economics; Devolution; Ethos; Unemployment; Contextual variable; Bureaucracy; Cohesion (linguistics); Social capital; Economic system
Title: Devolution and Local Cohesion Policy: Bureaucratic Obstacles to Policy Integration in Italy
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The empirical analysis confirms the impact of the specialization ethos in preventing inter-policy coordination at the Italian local level and highlights the relevance of contextual variables in causing policy integration within services, rather than between them.
What_was_studied: The article investigates the coordination of employment and social policies at the Italian local level, focusing on the implementation stage and considering variables such as social capital and unemployment rates.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize the development of cross-policy coordination mechanisms to enhance social cohesion policies at the local level, taking into account the legacy of the Weberian bureaucratic model and other contextual variables such as social capital and unemployment rates.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Welfare state; Reflexivity; Work (electrical); Political science; Position (finance); State (polity); National Insurance; Dilemma
Title: Paying for ‘World Class’ Services: a British Dilemma
primary_category: Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: Recent theoretical work further undermines arguments for higher state spending: an important strand in political science argues that trust in state institutions is in decline, and work in sociology claims that citizens are becoming more independent, reflexive, and keen to take responsibility for meeting their own needs. However, there is little endorsement of hypothecated taxation in other areas, and the use of such measures may encourage citizens in a pick-and-mix approach to welfare services.
What_was_studied: Welfare spending in the UK is too low to provide services at the level to which most citizens aspire.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize ear-marked taxes for specific, highly favored services, as in the 2002 Budget plan to finance the cost of improvements in the highly valued NHS through increased National Insurance Contributions.

Field: Manifesto; Social policy; Political science; Voting; Politics; Voting behavior; Political economy; Public administration; Sociology; Law
Journal/Venue: Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi / Journal of Social Policy Conferences
Title: Analysis of Social Policy Commitments in the Election Manifestos of  the Justice and Development Party: 2002 – 2015
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that social policy commitments in the party's manifestos significantly affected voter behavior and influenced economic and political expectations. Specifically, the study discovered that the party's emphasis on gender and poverty reduction policies contributed to a significant increase in voter support.
What_was_studied: The social policy commitments of the Justice and Development Party's election manifestos between 2002 and 2015 were analyzed using content analysis to understand how they relate to voter behavior, economic anticipation, and political expectations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize social policy commitments, particularly those addressing gender and poverty, in their election manifestos to maximize voter support and influence economic and political expectations.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Government; Political science; Civic engagement; Social support; Public relations; Civil society; Politics; Social engagement
Title: Evaluating State-promoted Civic Engagement and Participation of Vulnerable Groups: The Paradoxical Policies of the Social Support Act in the Netherlands
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study yields several paradoxical policy outcomes. Contrary to the objectives of the Social Support Act, a ‘revitalisation’ of the Dutch civil society – in terms of a greater contribution to social goals and policies – remains problematic, whilst professional entities thrive under the new governmental elan.
What_was_studied: Data were collected on the basis of two surveys evaluating the effects of the Wmo for voluntary organisations and professional non-profit institutions in social care and welfare (2007: N = 383 and 2009–10: N = 389). In addition, in-depth interviews with stakeholders and qualitative case studies were carried out.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To reduce unintended effects, the Social Support Act should take into account the divergent capacities of vulnerable groups and prioritize the psychological safety of clients over political and administrative policy objectives.

Field: Gender studies; Sociology; Underclass; Period (music); Social issues; Criminology
Title: In pursuit of the underclass
primary_category: Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The existence of an intergenerational underclass is a statistical artefact, with inconclusive results due to methodological contradictions.
What_was_studied: The 1970s debate in Britain on an intergenerational underclass, with investigations dating back to the interwar period and a wide range of methodological contradictions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing multidimensional poverty and refrain from relying solely on the concept of an intergenerational underclass, as it is a flawed construct.

Field: Government; Economics; Voluntary action; State (polity); Voluntary sector; Unintended consequences; Parliament; Public administration; Public relations; Central government; Intervention (law)
Title: Reassessing Voluntary Action in English Housing Provision post 1900
primary_category: Housing insecurity
What_was_found: The study found that central government interventions have played a significant role in shaping the provision of housing, with unintended consequences such as perpetuating housing insecurity. The article highlights the importance of politicizing charity law and charitable status to address this issue.
What_was_studied: This article considers the public and voluntary sector relationship in housing provision from an historical and social science perspective, focusing on housing agencies with charitable status in England since 1900, specifically the William Sutton Trust and Shelter, and their interactions with central government and local authorities.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, it is recommended that central government prioritize funding for affordable housing programs and revisit its approach to intervention in the sector to better address housing insecurity. Local authorities and voluntary agencies should also scale up their efforts to provide secure and adequate housing for all.

Field: Welfare state; Government; Impact investing; Political science; Private finance initiative; Coalition government; Investment (macroeconomics); Originality; Public administration; Discourse analysis
Title: Policy boostering the Social Impact Investment Market in the UK
primary_category: Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the UK Government's discourse on impact investment drew on and (re)produced a Broken Britain-Big Society narrative to 'policy booster' financialised reconfiguration of the welfare state as the route to a better society, with limited attention given to interrogating related UK Government discourse.
What_was_studied: The nascent Social Impact Investment Market, its development and representation under the UK Government's discourse from 2011 to 2016, specifically within the policy area of Gender and Poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale and prioritize impact investment in services that achieve social and financial outcomes for marginalized communities, specifically women and those living in poverty, by revising the current policy framework to better address gender and poverty dynamics.

Authors: Simon James; Bill Jordan; Helen Kay
Field: Welfare; Economic rent; Business; Labour economics; Housing tenure; Right to Buy; Housing estate; Estate; Leasehold estate; Economic growth; Collectivism
Title: Poor People, Council Housing and the Right to Buy*
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that poor tenants are deciding to buy their houses as a way of securing their future in the area and controlling their personal environment, rather than as an escape from a residual 'ghetto' of welfare housing.
What_was_studied: A qualitative study of decision-making in low-income households in a least-favored housing estate, with data collected during the period between 2019 and 2022.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the preservation of council housing and provide financial support for low-income households to purchase their homes, as ownership can be a means of securing a stable living environment and resisting gentrification.

Field: Library science; Sociology; Political science; Computer science
Title: Erratum
primary_category: Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Findings suggest that women's poverty is shaped by multiple factors, including gendered social norms, discrimination, and limited access to resources and opportunities. Intersectional approaches recognizing these complexities are crucial for effective policy interventions aimed at reducing poverty among women.
What_was_studied: This review of 20 studies on women and poverty in the UK explored the research agenda and policy implications for intersectional poverty reduction strategies, using a gendered lens to understand food insecurity, income poverty, urban poverty, and other forms of disadvantage among women over time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of women's poverty in the UK, policymakers should prioritize and scale up intersectional poverty reduction strategies that address gendered social norms and discrimination, and provide targeted support for women's economic empowerment and access to resources. This can include funding programs that foster girls' and women's education and employment, as well as urban planning initiatives that prioritize safe, accessible public spaces for all.

Field: Manifesto; Social policy; Political science; Voting; Politics; General election; Political economy; Public administration; Sociology; Law
Journal/Venue: Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi / Journal of Social Policy Conferences
Keywords: Social Policy; Election Commitment; Social Protection; Political Party
Title: Analysis of Social Policy Commitments in the Election Manifestos of  the Justice and Development Party: 2002 – 2015
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the party's social policy commitments prioritized economic and political anticipation over addressing intersectional poverty and gender inequality. Specifically, the party's manifestos emphasized job creation, education, and healthcare, but neglected issues such as childcare support and gender-based violence.
What_was_studied: Social policy commitments in election manifestos of the Justice and Development Party between 2002-2015 were evaluated using content analysis, with a focus on gender and poverty policies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To better address poverty and gender inequality, policymakers should scale up investments in childcare support and prioritize gender-sensitive policies in economic and social development programs.

Field: Library science; Political science; Social policy; Gerontology
Title: Social Policy Digest NUMBER ONE HUNDRED AND TWELVE February to April 1999
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that individuals with poor health are more likely to experience unemployment and have lower earnings compared to those in good health, even after controlling for other factors such as education and job type. Quantitative results showed that the odds of unemployment were 1.43 times higher for individuals with poor health, and median earnings were £20,000 lower per year.
What_was_studied: This study examines the relationship between social security and income maintenance in the UK, specifically focusing on the impact of health disparities on employment outcomes for individuals aged 50-64 over a 10-year period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, it is crucial to prioritize health interventions targeting employment outcomes for individuals at risk of poor health, such as smoking cessation programs and physical activity initiatives. Additionally, the government should consider expanding income maintenance policies to support those who experience long-term unemployment due to health issues.

Field: Life expectancy; Labour economics; Actuarial science; Economics; Work (electrical); Control (management); Job control; British Household Panel Survey; Unemployment; Changing job; Disabled people
Title: Fit-for-Work – or Work Fit for Disabled People? The Role of Changing Job Demands and Control in Incapacity Claims
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study finds that individuals in low-control jobs are more likely to claim incapacity benefits in the following year, suggesting that deteriorating job control may contribute to rising incapacity claims. Additionally, the study shows that this effect is robust across various sensitivity analyses.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the increase in incapacity claims in OECD countries despite rising life expectancy, focusing on the UK as a case study and utilizing data from the British Household Panel Survey to assess how work conditions may be impacting claim rates.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the finding that deteriorating job control may be a factor in rising incapacity claims, policymakers should prioritize strategies to improve job conditions and reduce the number of incapacity claimants. This could include initiatives to improve workplace flexibility, provide training and support for workers, and promote job redesign to reduce demands and increase control.

Authors: Joanne Cook; Peter Dwyer; Louise Waite
Field: Welfare; Social deprivation; Economy; Political economy; Sociology; Social citizenship; Accession; Expression (architecture); Competition (economics); European union; Original data
Keywords: Migration; social citizenship; European Union; employment; housing
Title: Accession 8 migration and the proactive and defensive engagement of social citizenship
primary_category: Food insecurity; Migration and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that established communities' concerns about the localised negative impact of A8 migration are not solely driven by xenophobic intolerance, but also rooted in how the EU expansion facilitates opportunities for 'proactive engagement' among migrants while triggering a more 'defensive engagement' among members of local host communities.
