What_was_studied: The study examined the impact of Accession 8 migration on established communities in a northern English city between 2004 and 2015, using original data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that to address food insecurity and poverty, policymakers should prioritize the integration of newly arrived migrants and established communities through targeted social programs and community-led initiatives, rather than relying solely on job creation or welfare resources.

Field: Social environment; Social position; Social work; Political science; Social policy; Social change; Economic growth; Social philosophy; Social Welfare; Social economy
Title: Developmental Roles for Social Work in the Third World: The Prospect of Social Planning
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that social workers play a crucial role in identifying and supporting children living in poverty, with a particular emphasis on addressing intersectional poverty among marginalized groups. The research also revealed that the majority of social workers in developing countries are not involved in national social policy formulation and planning, highlighting the need for greater investment in professional development and public recognition of their expertise.
What_was_studied: The research focused on the role of social workers in addressing child poverty in developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach with data collected from 2018 to 2020.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the critical role that social workers play in addressing child poverty, policymakers should prioritize investments in professional development and public recognition of their expertise to ensure that they are involved in national social policy formulation and planning. This can help to scale up effective interventions and expand support for marginalized communities.

Field: Social class; Interpersonal ties; Sociology; Inclusion (education); Oppression; Disadvantaged; Solidarity; Promotion (rank); Social psychology; Social skills
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Социальный цирк в постсоциалистической России: кейс-стади новой солидарности
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Employment; Food insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the inclusion of socially disadvantaged groups can change the structure of opportunities in practice under three conditions: through a change in the status of socially disadvantaged groups, when negative identification forms a platform for the practical promotion of the special status and differences of participants, considering their interests; attitudes towards achievement strengthens the positions of participants if it is combined with the formation of social skills to coordinate different positions; and opportunities are accumulated if they are fixed in emancipation methods of interaction at the individual, group, and local levels, involving the recognition of the causes of oppression, the promotion of the interests of disadvantaged groups, the reformatting of their experience, and the accumulation of social ties.
What_was_studied: This case study examines the Social Circus, a Russian NGO created in the 2000s that focuses on developing the potential of children from social risk groups in Russia between 2000 and 2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize the development of emancipation methods of interaction at the individual, group, and local levels to recognize the causes of oppression and promote the interests of disadvantaged groups, reformatting their experience and accumulating social ties to scale up the inclusion of socially disadvantaged groups and change the structure of opportunities in practice.

Authors: Эдгарс Шталс; Жанна Цауркубуле; Рита Константе
Field: Business; Latvian; Quality (philosophy); Transparency (behavior); Social work; Population; Local government; Medicine; Public administration; Environmental health; Economic growth; Political science; Computer science; Economics; Computer security; Philosophy; Linguistics; Epistemology
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Keywords: efficiency; Latvia; service quality; social care centres; quality indicators
Title: Usefulness of Administrative Data in Assessing the Service Quality and Technical Efficiency of Social Care Centres
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The authors conclude that the analysis of administrative data does not allow one to determine the quality of SCC because administrative data do not contain predictors of the care process. However, the administrative data of SCC can be used in the evaluation of TE of SCC where, depending on the applied method, set goals, and objectives, the obtained results can be used to determine the effectiveness of local government SCCs and to improve economic activity.
What_was_studied: The authors evaluate the quality of 67 social care centres (SCC) in the period from 2011 to 2017, and technical efficiency (TE) of 64 SCCs in 2017 using publicly available administrative data of SCCs to determine whether administrative data can be used in the evaluation of the quality of care at SCC and TE of SCC.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The authors point out the need to introduce unified quality indicators (QI) of the care process at SCCs of Latvia. This would ensure opportunities for control of the quality of care at SCCs, transparency of the care process, and quality assessment. Additionally, QI can be used as a component in evaluating the efficiency of SCCs. Therefore, the Latvian government should prioritize the development and implementation of unified QIs to improve the quality and efficiency of social care services for the aging population.

Field: Neoclassical economics; Labour economics; Economics; Inheritance; Watt; Inequality
Title: Housing Inheritance and Inequality: A Response to Watt
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the incidence of housing inheritance is higher amongst home owners, higher social classes, and those living in southern Britain, but lower among council tenants, the lower social classes, and those living in the north. The determinants of housing inheritance are influenced by the social characteristics of dying home owners, rather than anything inherent to the individuals who inherit.
What_was_studied: Using data from a survey of beneficiaries, the research assessed the validity of Saunders's (1986, 1990) arguments regarding the importance of home ownership and housing inheritance in the creation of a new consumption cleavage independent of social class, focusing on the distribution of inheritance across different social classes and geographic regions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that current differences in the incidence of inheritance will reflect the class and tenure characteristics of the dying population and their relationship to the class and tenure characteristics of beneficiaries. Therefore, policies aimed at addressing gender and poverty in urban areas should prioritize expanding access to affordable housing and social security programs to ensure that all individuals, regardless of their social class or tenure status, have equal access to inheritance and can maintain a decent standard of living.

Field: Service provider; Psychology; Social work; Poverty; Community health; Residence; Context (language use); Marital status; Public relations; Politics
Title: Parenting skills: Views of Community Health and Social Service Providers about the Needs of their Clients
primary_category: Child poverty; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the concept of 'parenting skills' is drawn on to describe both the needs of women with whom service providers work and their own role in fulfilling some of those needs. It also found that these skills are not only gendered, but that a lack of them might be associated with marital status, age, and place of residence.
What_was_studied: The article explores the concept of 'parenting skills' from the perspective of community health and social service providers working with families deemed to be 'in need', during a specific time period, using qualitative data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the findings, it is crucial to prioritize addressing the systemic issues contributing to poverty and poor housing conditions to support families in need. Expanding social protection programs and funding community-based initiatives can help scale up effective interventions to improve parenting skills and overall family well-being.

Field: Income protection insurance; Self-insurance; Economy; General insurance; Labour economics; Economics; National Insurance; Social insurance; Earnings; Key person insurance; Insurance policy
Title: Workforce Restructuring, Social Insurance Coverage and the Black Economy
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that there are approximately 4 million workers in the periphery of the workforce who are either excluded from or only partially covered by the national insurance system, including up to 2 million non-working people with trivial earnings.
What_was_studied: The national insurance system of contributory work-related benefits was designed for a ‘core’ workforce in continuous full-time employment and its coverage for the rising numbers of people in the peripheral workforce: part-time jobs, temporary work, and self-employment was investigated across a period of 1985–87, with estimates presented for workers whose earnings are below the national insurance threshold and who are thus excluded from social security benefits such as unemployment, sickness, and retirement benefits—roughly 2 million in the period 1985–87, and another million workers at least are within the NI net but outside the income tax net, along with up to 2 million non-working people who have trivial earnings that leave them outside the NI and tax nets, including homeworkers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the rising numbers of people in the peripheral workforce and their limited coverage under the current national insurance system, there is a need for policy interventions that expand and prioritize social protection for these workers, such as revising eligibility criteria or scaling up targeted benefits to address intersectional poverty and ensure inclusive economic growth.

Field: Public economics; Economics; Poverty; Law and economics; Social policy; Reciprocity (social psychology); Identity (social science); Income maintenance; Legitimacy; Reciprocal inter-insurance exchange; Social Welfare
Title: Social Policy: Unilateral Transfer or Reciprocal Exchange†
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis reveals that unilateral transfers, such as grants or gifts, are not effective in reducing poverty without also considering the social bond and reciprocity among community members. In fact, ignoring these aspects can actually exacerbate poverty and create negative social outcomes.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the effectiveness of social policies aimed at reducing poverty in a specific urban area during a one-year period, using a mixed-methods approach that combines surveys, interviews, and administrative data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize programmes that foster mutual support and reciprocity among beneficiaries, such as training and education initiatives that encourage peer-to-peer learning and community engagement. By doing so, they can scale up successful interventions and expand their reach to more vulnerable populations.

Field: Psychology; Stigma (botany); Poverty; Shame; Political rhetoric; Perceived stigma; Social psychology
Keywords: Benefits; social security; welfare; stigma; shame; take-up; survey acknowledgements, bibliography, notes etc, excluding
Title: The stigma of claiming benefits: a quantitative study
primary_category: Crime & poverty; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that 34% of respondents reported either personal stigma (their own view) or stigmatization (perceived stigma by others) for at least one benefit, with over a quarter saying a stigma-related reason would make them less likely to claim. Additionally, one-third of claimants themselves reported some degree of stigma around their claim.
What_was_studied: A 2012 nationally-representative survey in the UK examining sub-types of stigma related to various benefits and their effects on poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize reducing benefits stigma by addressing media/political rhetoric and promoting education on the realities of poverty and benefits to combat negative perceptions and increase take-up rates, especially in high-claim areas.

Authors: John R. Graham; Micheal L. Shier; Marilyn Eisenstat
Field: Sociology; Neighbourhood (mathematics); Interpersonal communication; Qualitative research; Career development; Social mobility; Personal development; Social capital; Social psychology; Interpersonal relationship
Title: Young Adult Social Networks and Labour Market Attachment: Interpersonal Dynamics that Shape Perspectives on Job Attainment
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Respondents identified that interpersonal relationships with employers, family members, and neighborhood/community members influenced their motivation for upward social mobility through securing and maintaining employment. The findings highlight the importance of individual social capital in shaping perceptions of upward social mobility among racial minority young adults.
What_was_studied: A qualitative study of young adults (17-29) in low-income Toronto communities, exploring how social relationships and dynamics influence perceptions of upward social mobility.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy and program solutions should support the mobilization of embedded social resources within the social networks of racial minority young adults to improve personal development and enhance positive perceptions towards upward social mobility, scaling interventions that foster these relationships to more communities and expanding funding for programs that support career aspirations among racial minority youth.

Authors: Esteban Calvo; Fabio Bertranou; Evelina Bertranou
Field: Latin Americans; Political science; Financial market; Globe; Pension; Income maintenance; Development economics; Equity (economics); Market risk; Politics
Title: Are Old-age Pension System Reforms Moving Away from Individual Retirement Accounts in Latin America?
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that pension reform in Latin America has combined significant revival of public components in old-age income maintenance with improvement of IRAs, and that policy prescriptions have been re-evaluated to pay more attention to poverty reduction, coverage, and equity, and to protect participants from market risks.
What_was_studied: This article reviews two rounds of pension reform in ten Latin American countries to determine whether they are moving away from individual retirement accounts (IRAs). The study covers a 10-year period, includes data from ten countries, and focuses on the revival of public components in old-age income maintenance and the improvement of IRAs.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that policy makers should prioritize a comprehensive approach to pension reform that addresses poverty reduction, coverage, and equity, and that protects participants from market risks. This could involve scaling up public components in old-age income maintenance and improving the design and regulation of IRAs.

Authors: Елена Юрьевна Голубева; Андрей Горгоньевич Соловьев
Field: Social exclusion; Psychology; Social work; Social isolation; Social security; Loneliness; Alcohol abuse; Risk factor (computing); Gerontology; Social skills
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Социально-политические и медицинские аспекты употребления алкоголя в старшем возрасте как фактор риска
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that limitations in activities due to reduction or disability, loneliness, inadequate social skills, social isolation, and lack of physical activity directly or indirectly led to alcohol use among the elderly, with loneliness being a particularly significant factor.
What_was_studied: The article analyses the role of alcohol consumption as a risk factor increasing social disadvantage among older age groups, using empirical studies of 713 people aged 60 to 89 in the Arkhangelsk region to evaluate the impact and consequences of alcoholism.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high risk of alcohol consumption and its consequences for social disadvantage, policymakers should prioritize addressing social exclusion and isolation among older adults through targeted interventions and support systems to reduce the burden on healthcare and social security.

Field: Public economics; Variety (cybernetics); Payment; Economics; Poverty; Social security; Convergence (economics); Inequality; Security convergence; Economic security
Title: The Measurement of Social Security Convergence: The Case of European Public Pension Systems since 1950
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study reveals that changes in social security systems have had a significant impact on public pension payments, with individuals experiencing different levels of payment changes depending on their lifetime income levels. The findings indicate that public pension payments have become more progressive over time, with those in lower-income brackets experiencing larger percentage increases than those in higher-income brackets.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes public pension changes in five European countries between 1950 and the present day using formal social security rules to evaluate how these changes impact payments for individuals with different income levels.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant impact of social security system changes on poverty reduction and income inequality, policymakers should prioritize implementing progressive public pension reforms that benefit low-income individuals to scale up social protection and promote sustainable development.

Field: Labour economics; Government; Subsistence agriculture; Economics; Price index; Poverty; Social security; Means test; Pension; Public relations; International security
Title: An End to the Means Test? Social Security and the Attlee Government
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: Labour ministers had no reason to anticipate the problems which were later to arise in the administration of means-tested social assistance, despite the experience of the supplementary pension scheme during the war indicating few problems of take-up or stigma if old people were required to claim assistance as a supplement to their pensions.
What_was_studied: The post-war Labour Government's failure to remove the means test from social security and its consequences on the administration of means-tested social assistance during that period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the abolition of the household means test in 1941 did not remove the cause of much bitterness surrounding the means test in the 1930s, and that the assistance scale was seen as providing more than a bare subsistence income. Therefore, the government should prioritize removing the means test from social security to address these issues and provide more adequate support for those in need.

Authors: Virginie Diaz Pedregal; Blandine Destremau; Bart Criel
Field: Business; Government; Health care; Social policy; Negotiation; Public administration; Health policy; Economic growth; Civil society; Autonomy; Politics
Title: Health Policy in Cambodia: To What Extent Is an Aid-Dependent Country Able to Determine Its Own Policy?
primary_category: Income poverty; Migration and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the Cambodian government makes political decisions incrementally, with a clear long-term vision for improving health care provision and access, but day-to-day decisions are constantly negotiated between stakeholders. Additionally, international stakeholders such as donors and technical organizations play a major role in shaping health policy, while Cambodian civil society is rarely involved in the negotiations.
What_was_studied: This article analyses the design and implementation process of arrangements for health care provision and access to health care in Cambodia during a specific time period using interviews and documentary reviews to understand how ideas, interests, and institutions shape Cambodian health care schemes and how international stakeholders impact policy making.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the need for the Cambodian government to prove its capacity to master risks such as the under-regulated development of the private health care sector. To address this challenge, decision makers should prioritize involving Cambodian civil society in policy negotiations and consider increasing regulation of the private health care sector to ensure equitable access to quality healthcare for all Cambodians.

Field: Welfare state; Political economy; Economics; Social policy; Recession; Celtic Tiger; Social Partnership; Prosperity; Corporate governance; Economic growth; Political culture
Title: Obstacles to the Implementation of an Integrated National Alcohol Policy in Ireland: Nannies, Neo-Liberals and Joined-Up Government
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: A number of explanations are offered for the refusal of successive governments to respond to what its advocates see as the only rational, evidence-based approach to the prevention of alcohol problems, including that unlike the Nordic countries, the political culture of independent Ireland has never been one in which the state could unilaterally impose strict alcohol control policies as a feature of its broader vision of the welfare state, and during the recent period of economic prosperity (the so-called ‘Celtic Tiger’ era) the country was characterised by a neo-liberal policy climate, which was specifically antipathetic to the idea that the state should interfere directly in the alcohol market with a view to preventing related problems.
What_was_studied: This article explores how proponents of a public health model of alcohol policy have, for more than a quarter of a century, argued consistently but unsuccessfully for an integrated national alcohol policy in the Republic of Ireland, focusing on the past decade with increases in alcohol consumption and related problems strengthened the case for such an integrated policy, and when managerial innovations in the sphere of cross-cutting management appeared to provide a template for its implementation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: It is suggested that the social partnership model of governance, to which many people attributed the country’s economic success, created an atmosphere of consensualism within which the state as mediator between the two main protagonists (the public health lobby and the drinks industry) was unwilling to challenge the drinks industry, and it is also concluded that this failure to create a national alcohol policy based on public health principles demonstrates the limitations of the cross-cutting, or ‘joined-up’, approach to public management in those areas of social policy characterised by clashing value systems or fundamental conflicts of economic interest. The findings suggest that Ireland should prioritize the development of a comprehensive national alcohol policy based on public health principles to address the growing burden of alcohol-related harm.

Field: Conformity; Psychology; Narrative; Constructivist teaching methods; Value (ethics); Assistant professor; Meaning (existential); Social research; Human sexuality; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Конструирование старения: секс и интимность в пожилом возрасте
primary_category: Housing insecurity
What_was_found: The research found that older people face problems due to inadequate views on the meaning and value of sexuality in this period of life, and that constructing older age by controlling sexuality and denying the right for sexual activity is another facet of sexism.
What_was_studied: This article investigates intimacy and sexuality among people in the late life period, employing a constructivist approach to aging that views aging as a process constructed by social institutions, and using theoretical approaches and empirical data to challenge inaccurate views on the sexual and intimate life of the elderly during an 18-interview study conducted between 2017 and 2019.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Older people should be prioritized with policies to ensure their access to safe and affordable housing, healthcare, and social services to combat insecurity and improve overall well-being, as well as challenge the societal norms that stigmatize and marginalize them based on their sexual and intimate lives.

Field: Political science; Social policy; Socioeconomics
Title: Social Policy Digest: Number Ninety-Seven
primary_category: Housing insecurity
What_was_found: The study found that while the income of the poorest tenth of society fell by 18% in real terms, their expenditure rose by 14%. Additionally, the study found significant movement in and out of poverty between 1991 and 1992.
What_was_studied: The study examined changes in income and expenditure of the poorest tenth of society in the UK between 1979 and 1992, with a focus on housing insecurity.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding highlights the need for policies that address housing insecurity, such as investing in affordable housing and social security benefits to support those who are most vulnerable to poverty.

Field: Economic policy; Possession (law); Conceptual framework; Economics; Set (psychology); Social policy; Arrears; Financial costs; Economic inequality
Title: The Costs of Unsustainable Home Ownership in Britain
primary_category: Education access; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The paper finds that the financial costs of mortgage arrears and possession are substantial, affecting a wide range of actors and institutions, and contributing to ongoing social and economic inequality. Specifically, it is found that 1 in 8 homeowners experienced mortgage arrears, leading to an average loss of £27,300 per household, with a total loss of £4.5 billion across the study period.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the costs of unsustainable home ownership in Britain as manifested through mortgage arrears and possessions, specifically for a population of homeowners during the period 2014-2018, using data from UK government sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the scale of these financial losses and their ongoing impact on individuals, communities, and institutions, it is crucial to prioritize policies aimed at preventing unsustainable home ownership and supporting those affected by mortgage arrears and possession. This could include increasing access to affordable housing, expanding debt counseling services, and revising existing policies to better address these issues.

Authors: Ole Petter Askheim; Karen Christensen; Synnøve Fluge; Ingrid Guldvik
Field: Mental health; Sociology; Social constructionism; Social rights; Social citizenship; Context (language use); Public relations; New public management; Democracy; Discourse analysis
Title: User participation in the Norwegian Welfare Context: an Analysis of Policy Discourses
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the discourse around user participation policies has evolved over time, with a shift from a democracy/social rights discourse to a consumer discourse in the case of older people, and the emergence of a co-production/co-partnering discourse for all three user groups.
What_was_studied: This article examines the social construction of user participation policies for older people, disabled people, and those with mental health problems in Norway using a historical discourse analysis of national documents from 1970 to 2010.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the adoption of co-production/co-partnering policies for all three user groups to promote more equitable and effective social protection, and scale back consumer-oriented approaches that predominate in policies aimed at older people.

Field: Extended family; Economics; Social policy; Dependency ratio; Social support; Household income; Population; Demographic economics; Development economics; Social stratification; Economic stability
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Семья для среднедоходных слоев населения: тыл или риск?
primary_category: Asset poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Middle-income groups are divided into two fundamentally separate groups with remarkably different levels of exposure to economic risks, and the lower part of this strata, despite their income meeting the ‘national average’ level, is on the verge of vulnerability due to socio-demographic factors such as family structure and dependency load.
What_was_studied: The socio-demographic characteristics of middle-income groups and household characteristics in terms of the potential risks of economic instability based on monitoring data from Institute of Sociology RAS in 2016.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize support for middle-income groups in crisis, particularly the lower segment with higher vulnerability, by strengthening social support systems and providing additional resources for those with high dependency ratios and non-working pensioners.

Authors: Francesca Bastagli; Jessica Hagen-Zanker; Luke Harman; Valentina Barca; Georgina Sturge; Tanja Schmidt
Field: Public economics; Business; Work (electrical); Poverty; Empowerment; Investment (macroeconomics); Cash; Production (economics); Cash transfers; Receipt
Title: The Impact of Cash Transfers: A Review of the Evidence from Low- and Middle-income Countries
primary_category: Child poverty; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Based on evidence extracted from 165 studies, cash transfers contributed to progress in 35 indicators covering six outcome areas: monetary poverty; education; health and nutrition; savings, investment, and production; work; and empowerment.
What_was_studied: This article presents the findings of a review of the impact of non-contributory cash transfers on individuals and households in low- and middle-income countries, covering the literature of 15 years, from 2000 to 2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the consistent positive impact across all outcome areas, policymakers should prioritize investing in non-contributory cash transfers to scale up their social protection programs, particularly targeting child poverty and income poverty in low- and middle-income countries.

Field: Gender studies; Sociology; Government; Social studies; Institutionalisation; Social work; Social policy; Participant observation; Institution; Social science; Interpersonal relationship
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Этнографический взгляд на роль эмоций в российском детском доме
primary_category: Child poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The article found that emotional conflicts between staff and volunteers significantly impact the provision and quality of care for resident children within the institution.
What_was_studied: The Russian Federation's large system of institutional care for orphaned children, using ethnographic work in a Russian orphanage for children with intellectual disabilities to examine the importance of emotion in the lives of staff, volunteers, and resident orphaned children, and how interpersonal relationships impact upon the provision and quality of care.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing these emotional conflicts to ensure the quality of care provided to vulnerable children in institutional settings.

Field: Psychiatry; Economic Justice; Psychology; Poverty; Innocence; Context (language use); Cruelty; Ethnic Cleansing; Child abuse; Criminology; Social order
Title: Abused and Looked After Children as ‘Moral Dirt’: Child Abuse and Institutional Care in Historical Perspective
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that children were not only mistreated due to their poverty but also because they were victims of parental cruelty, which was perceived as contaminating their childhood innocence. This perpetuated a cycle of ethnic cleansing and prevented children from receiving adequate care and protection.
What_was_studied: The experiences of children in institutional care in Ireland prior to the 1970s, specifically the relationship between child poverty and maltreatment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the importance of addressing the root causes of child maltreatment, specifically parental cruelty and poverty, to prevent further abuse and ensure adequate care for all children. Policymakers should prioritize radical reconstruction of traditional status of children in care, full remembrance of the totality of the abuse experienced by survivors, and accountability for those responsible.

Field: Business; Labour economics; Work (electrical); Control (management); Disability insurance; Social security; Unemployment; Spell; Job loss; Shock (economics)
Title: From Working to Applying: Employment Transitions of Applicants for Disability Insurance in the United States
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that most future applicants report a health shock shortly before they stop working, but they typically remain out of work for some months before they apply for DI. Classifying episodes of non-employment by beginning events reveals that spell length, job search, Unemployment Insurance participation and DI application processing time differ notably by reason of job loss.
What_was_studied: This study examines employment transitions preceding applications for Social Security Disability Insurance (DI) in the US using administrative records merged with the Survey of Income and Programme Participation, to document employment transitions preceding applications for DI among people at risk of applying.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize programs aimed at increasing re-employment opportunities for individuals who are at risk of applying for disability benefits. This could include providing job training and placement services, as well as streamlining the application process to reduce wait times.

Authors: Tania Burchardt; Emily Jones; Polina Obolenskaya
Field: Public policy; Political science; Survey data collection; Long-term care; Oecd countries; Older population; Increased risk; Unmet needs; Economic growth; Activities of daily living
Keywords: Long term care; Community care; Informal care; Unmet need
Title: Formal and informal long-term care in the community: interlocking or incoherent systems?
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis of UK Family Resources Survey data found high levels of unmet need, particularly among adults living alone and those with moderate levels of difficulty. Means-tested public entitlements did not fully address the increased risk among low-income households.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates how formal and informal care systems interlock to provide support for people in need, specifically focusing on differences between OECD countries and the UK, and identifying at-risk populations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Public policy should integrate support for formal and informal care to protect at-risk populations, particularly those living alone or with moderate needs. Scale funding and prioritize resources for these groups to fill gaps in care and address chronic poverty.

Field: Erikson's stages of psychosocial development; Sociology; Health care; Pastoral care; Organized religion; Context (language use); Professionalization; Spiritual care; Public relations; Transformative learning
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Между теологией и заботой: обзор исследований больничного служения
primary_category: Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The professionalization and reformulation of the work of priests in hospitals, providing universal spiritual and pastoral care to patients, their relatives, and medical personnel regardless of religious affiliation and beliefs, alongside the transformative impact of neoliberal reforms.
What_was_studied: The development of chaplaincy studies in the English-language tradition since the second half of the 20th century, focusing on non-parish ministries in Christian churches across various secular institutions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize the development of techniques for listening and observation, expand methodological tools, and publish research results to address the increasing marginalization of hospital chaplains in relation to organized religion, which can provide access to the non-churched majority and produce reflective priest-researchers specializing in working with certain categories of patients.

Field: Population statistics; Labour economics; Economics; Unemployment; Test (assessment); Labour power; Reproduction (economics); Disadvantaged; Income maintenance; Affect (psychology)
Title: Health and Labour Force Participation: ‘Stress’, Selection and the Reproduction Costs of Labour Power*
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that socio-demographic characteristics were associated with mortality, and that selective mobility of seriously ill persons into socially disadvantaged positions may be a factor in the relationship between health and unemployment.
What_was_studied: This paper discusses the relationship between health and unemployment by examining the applicability of concepts of ‘stress’ and ‘selection’ using data from European and American studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing socio-demographic disparities in employment opportunities and support for those with serious health conditions to improve overall public health.

Field: Economy; Sociology; Empirical evidence; Work (electrical); Poverty; Corruption; Welsh; Grassroots; Economic growth; Colonialism
Title: International Charitable Connections: the Growth in Number, and the Countries of Operation, of English and Welsh Charities Working Overseas
primary_category: Food insecurity; Health disparities; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that there has been a sizeable increase in the number of charities working overseas since the mid-1990s, with charities more likely to work in countries with colonial and linguistic ties to the UK and less likely to work in countries with high levels of instability or corruption. The study also found significant geographical unevenness in charitable activity, even after controlling for countries’ population size and poverty.
What_was_studied: This paper provides new empirical evidence about English and Welsh charities operating internationally, focusing on the time period from the mid-1990s to 2018 and using a unique administrative dataset recording every country in which each charity operates.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the finding that charities are more likely to operate in countries with colonial ties to the UK, policymakers should prioritize funding small-scale, grassroots registered charitable activity in developed as well as developing country contexts to address food insecurity, health disparities, and sustainable development challenges.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Government; Economics; Work (electrical); Qualitative research; New Deal; Social security; Advisory committee; Public relations; Economic growth
Title: Re-conceptualising Welfare-To-Work for People with Multiple Problems and Needs
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The central finding was that welfare-to-work policies do not accommodate ontological as well as practical life needs, particularly for those whose lives are especially difficult.
What_was_studied: A small-scale qualitative study of the labor market experiences of people with multiple problems and needs was examined, along with an analysis of the discursive strategies used by participants in the study.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Welfare-to-work policies should be re-conceptualized to accommodate ontological as well as practical life needs, and funding should be prioritized for programs that provide individualized assistance to those with multiple problems and needs.

Field: Gender studies; Sociology; Social psychology (sociology); Refugee; State (polity); Intercultural competence; Attachment disorder; Identification (psychology); Face (sociological concept); Immigration
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Дети, охваченные миграционными процессами: разнообразие, вызовы и диверсификация моделей поддержки
primary_category: Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The research found that children of different ages who migrated together with their parents face challenges such as language acquisition, cultural adaptation, and intercultural competence development. Second-generation migrant children demonstrate a greater need for support in their identification and development of intercultural competence, while refugee children require more complex psychological assistance. Left Behind Children experience emotional deprivation and attachment disorders that must be addressed by specialists.
What_was_studied: This study explores the features of child migrant adaptation, a diverse group that requires a differentiated approach to support their adaptation. The study focuses on children involved in migration processes, including those who migrated with their parents, children born in migrant families in another country, refugee children in danger, and 'Left Behind Children' who were left behind by their parents.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the diverse needs of child migrants, policymakers should scale up differentiated support programs for their adaptation, expand existing support systems to reach more children, fund specialized training for psychologists and teachers working with child migrants, prioritize the development of intercultural competence in these children, and revise current policies to address the unique needs of 'Left Behind Children'.

Field: Welfare state; Social position; Sociology; Social work; Social policy; Social change; Public relations; Social Welfare; Social learning; Legislature
Title: Social Workers as Policy Actors
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: Social workers tended to facilitate and enrich the social policy formulation process, while those employed by not-for-profit organisations also challenged policy makers and placed matters on the agendas of committees.
What_was_studied: This article offers an empirical analysis of the role of social workers as policy actors in parliamentary committees, examining their inputs in committee discussions on child poverty, employment, gender and poverty, health disparities, and social protection policies in the Israeli parliament over a 14% participation rate during a specific time period using recorded minutes of three parliamentary committees.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the diverse inputs of social workers in parliamentary committees, decision-makers should prioritize their involvement in policy-making processes to enhance the formulation of social policies, particularly in areas such as child poverty, employment, gender and poverty, health disparities, and social protection.

Field: Welfare; Positive economics; Sociology; Poverty; Social policy; Perspective (graphical); Power (social and political); Subject (philosophy); Social control
Title: Regulating the Poor Revisited
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Crime & poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that Piven and Cloward's general perspective points to a range of important issues in social policy and exposes a number of assumptions. Specifically, it was found that there is a relationship between work and welfare and that power and poverty are closely linked.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the explanation of social policy development through comparative data, specifically looking at the relationship between social policy and social control, work and welfare, and power and poverty using data from 1972.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision makers should prioritize policies that address the root causes of poverty and provide support for those who are struggling to find employment or access social services. This can include scaling up job training programs, expanding access to affordable childcare, and increasing funding for social services in rural areas.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Secondary sector of the economy; Arrears; Wage; Unemployment; Context (language use); Trade union; Industrial relations; Tertiary sector of the economy
Journal/Venue: Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi/Journal of Social Policy Conferences
Keywords: China; Labors' Movements; Protest and Strike; Industrial Relations; Trade Union
Title: Temel Dinamikleriyle Çin İşçi Hareketleri: 2008 Krizi Sonrası Dönemin Çok Yönlü Kuramsal Analizi
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the labor market in China has experienced growing employment and GDP, shrinking agriculture and industrial sectors, and expanding service sectors, with gradually decreasing growth rates and unchanged unemployment and labor force participation rates. The main reason for workers' movements is the issue of wage arrears, primarily in the construction and manufacturing sectors, and mostly concentrated in private enterprises and SEEs or companies without ownership.
What_was_studied: The Chinese labor market in the post-crisis period from 2008 to 2018 was analyzed using data from the Chinese Labor Bulletin, focusing on employment, GDP, industrial sector, service sector, and labor movements.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the issue of wage arrears and labor movements in China's post-crisis labor market, policymakers should prioritize the expansion of social insurance programs and improve labor dispute resolution mechanisms to enhance workers' rights and protect their interests.

Field: Labour economics; German; Economics; Poverty; Core (game theory); Coordinated market economy; Private pension; Pension; Incentive; Liberalization; Economic system
Title: The Liberalisation of the German Social Model: Public–Private Pension Reform in Germany since 2001
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study shows that recent pension reforms have created a system more characteristic of a liberal than a dualized political economy, with projected net pensions for today's young workers closer to the poverty line and a narrowing gap between core and peripheral workers' benefits.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the impact of pension reforms on the German social model since 1957, focusing on public-private pension reform post-2001 and its effects on core and peripheral workers' net pensions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize comprehensive pension reform that addresses the growing income inequality and ensures the long-term sustainability of the German social model.

Field: Welfare; Business; Project commissioning; Work (electrical); Social group; Competition (economics); National Policy; Public relations; Social issues; Localism
Title: Remodelling the Third Sector: Advancing Collaboration or Competition in Community-Based Initiatives?
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities; Housing insecurity; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that while national policy has recognized third sector expertise in working with marginal groups, changing relationships with the state have drawn community organizations into new, often uncomfortable, organizational arrangements affecting their work and roles in relation to service users and community stakeholders. Additionally, recent plans for local area commissioning of services have been found to undermine collaborative work and community trust.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the impact of recent changes in UK public agency collaborations with non-state providers on community-based organizations delivering children and young people's services in deprived localities between 2010 and 2020.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the findings, it is recommended that policymakers prioritize funding for community-based organizations delivering children and young people's services in deprived localities, scale up successful collaborations with non-state providers, and revise centrally driven frameworks to support more effective community-level work addressing challenging social problems.

Authors: Li Ma; Gunnar Andersson; Ann Zofie Duvander; Marie Evertsson
Field: Multinomial logistic regression; Sociology; Metropolitan area; Social inequality; Parental leave; Demographic economics
Keywords: forerunners; laggards; fathers' uptake of parental leave; Sweden Mother's education Below secondary .
Title: Fathers' Uptake of Parental Leave: Forerunners and Laggards in Sweden, 1993-2010
primary_category: Child poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found a bifurcation in trends in recent decades, with better-educated residents of metropolitan areas and surrounding suburbs, as well as Swedish-born fathers taking longer leaves of over two months, while young fathers, low-income earners, and foreign-born fathers lagged behind. The study also found that taking a long leave was associated with higher education and better socioeconomic status.
What_was_studied: This study investigates recent developments towards more gender-equal sharing of parental leave in Sweden, focusing on how fathers' use of parental leave has changed over time before and since the turn of the century, and exploring the socio-economic and demographic characteristics associated with their parental leave uptake.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the extension of reforms reserving part of the leave for fathers, known as 'daddy months', has contributed to a widening of social inequalities in family-related behavior. To address this issue, policymakers should prioritize funding and support for programs that encourage more equitable distribution of parental leave and provide resources for low-income families to access childcare and other family-friendly policies.

Authors: Hannah Zagel; Gitit Kadar-Satat; Myrthe Jacobs; Anthony Glendinning
Field: Developmental psychology; Investment (macroeconomics); Area deprivation; Medicine; Social psychology
Title: The effects of early years' childcare on child emotional and behavioural difficulties in lone and co-parent family situations
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that negative outcomes associated with lone motherhood are primarily explained by material circumstances, area deprivation, mother's age, education, and family constellation, and that maternal employment does not alleviate these risks. However, formal group-based pre-school childcare for at least 25 hours per week is beneficial for all children, regardless of their family situation.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the impact of non-parental childcare use and maternal employment on emotional and behavioral difficulties in children aged four and five living in lone and co-parent family situations, and examines how these factors are influenced by material circumstances, area deprivation, mother's age, education, and family constellation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policy makers should prioritize investing in formal childcare provision and arrangements that allow lone mothers to divide their childcare responsibilities with other main providers, in order to tackle families' material hardship and improve the well-being of children in lone mother households.

Field: Demography; Best practice; Survey data collection; Health equity; Smoking cessation; Context (language use); Demographic economics; Inequality; Medicine; Geographic mobility; Qualitative comparative analysis
Title: Qualitative comparative analysis and health inequalities: investigating reasons for differential progress with narrowing local gaps in mortality
primary_category: Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that smoking cessation services accorded with best practice descriptions were associated with a narrowing mortality gap for circulatory diseases in areas with relatively more people aged 65 or older. Additionally, areas with low population mobility and a professional working culture of individual commitment and championing had a narrower mortality gap for cancers.
What_was_studied: This study investigated health inequalities in 15 local authority areas in North West England between 2001 and 2010, using survey data to analyze the impact of contextual features and ways of working on premature mortality rates for circulatory diseases and cancers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the complexity of meeting health inequality targets, policymakers should prioritize understanding local context and practice to apply evidence effectively. Health authorities in deprived areas should fund smoking cessation services that accord with best practices, and invest in professional development to cultivate a culture of individual commitment and championing.

Authors: Veysel Bozkurt; Aşkın Keser; Haluk Zülfikar
Field: Data collection; Psychology; Negative relationship; Optimism; Unemployment; Loneliness; Life satisfaction; Marital status; Social media; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi/Journal of Social Policy Conferences
Title: Factors Predicting Life Satisfaction Among Social Media Users
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that life satisfaction had a statistically significant negative relationship with loneliness, social media usage time, being unemployed, and age, while it had a positive correlation with trust in people, optimism about the future, religious involvement, marital status, and female gender.
What_was_studied: This study examined the factors predicting life satisfaction among social media users in a sample of 1547 participants, using convenience sampling and an online questionnaire.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that 54.2% of respondents believed that social media increases loneliness, policy-makers should prioritize initiatives to reduce social media usage time and promote trust among users to improve life satisfaction.

Field: Welfare; Labour economics; Economics; Poverty; Wage; Allowance (money); Earnings; Marital breakdown; Distribution (economics); Unit (housing)
Title: Patterns of Money Management within Marriage
primary_category: Financial inclusion; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The article suggests that there are links between the system of allocation within the family, the stage in the life cycle which the family has reached, the income level of the household, and the occupational, regional, and ethnic culture within which the household is located.
What_was_studied: This article focuses on the control and allocation of financial resources within households, drawing on work done in the past and on original material taken from a study of the problems of a group of women whose marriages had broken down because of violence, concentrating on the household type which is composed of a married couple and their dependent children, and outlines three broad types of allocation system – the whole wage system, the allowance system, and the pooling system.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Better knowledge of intra-household money flows would be relevant to discussions concerned with the distribution of poverty, the allocation of welfare benefits, and the contribution made by married women's earnings to family living standards, and would also contribute to a better understanding of marital tension and marital breakdown.

Field: Public policy; Social class; Health education; Positive economics; Political science; Social group; Poverty; Redistribution (cultural anthropology); Socioeconomics; Inequality; Politics
Title: The inequalities in health debate: a critical review of the issues.
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that health inequalities in the UK are widening, with materialist/structuralist variables being the most important explanatory factor. The Registrar General's Decennial Supplement for 1979-1983 and an SSRC Workshop held in November 1983 both support this conclusion.
What_was_studied: The ongoing debate about health inequalities in the UK since the suppressed publication of the Black Report in 1980, with a focus on the measurement and explanation of these inequalities using data from the Registrar General's Decennial Supplement for 1979-1983 and an SSRC Workshop held in November 1983, as well as another half-suppressed report from Health Education Council.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the widening health inequalities and the importance of materialist/structuralist variables, policymakers should prioritize resource redistribution to eradicate poverty, specifically targeting chronic poverty, health disparities, intersectional poverty, and urban poverty to address these inequalities.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Social work; Total cost; Income Support; Social security; Family support; Child support; Child rearing; Demographic economics; Social issues
Title: Estimating the Cost of Contact for Non-resident Parents: A Budget Standards Approach
primary_category: Child poverty; Health disparities; Housing insecurity
What_was_found: The study found that the costs of contact for non-resident parents are high, representing approximately 40% of the costs of a child in an intact couple household with a medium income and more than half of the costs of a child in a household with low income, primarily due to household infrastructure and transportation expenses.
What_was_studied: The research analyzed the costs of children to couple and sole parent households in Western countries over a 10-year period, using the budget standards methodology to estimate the costs for non-resident parents exercising regular contact with their children.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: These findings suggest that the total cost of children increases significantly when parents separate, highlighting the need for scaled-up support for families experiencing this transition. Policymakers should prioritize expanding family support policies to address these increased costs and ensure the well-being of children.

Field: Civilization; Welfare state; Political science; Law and economics; Social policy; State (polity); Social protection; Industrial Age; Industrial society; Population
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Забота о благополучии подданных в ранних государствах
primary_category: Asset poverty; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that social policy has a long history, dating back to ancient times, and that many states of the Ancient world implemented policies aimed at providing an acceptable level of well-being, social protection, and social solidarity. These policies were not accidental but were regular, incorporated into existing formal institutions, and imbued with strong cultural legitimacy.
What_was_studied: The study examines the conceptualization of social policy and its history, challenging the common assumption that it is a modern phenomenon exclusive to industrial society. The research focuses on the policies implemented by ancient states to provide well-being, social protection, and social solidarity, and how these policies were regular, incorporated into existing formal institutions, and imbued with strong cultural legitimacy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the institutional practices of social policy began long before the onset of the industrial age, providing grounds for concluding that fulfilling social obligations to the population has been a key characteristic of the state as a social institution. This highlights the importance of considering the history and cultural context of social policy when developing modern policies to address asset poverty, gender and poverty, and intersectional poverty.

Authors: Олавале Джеймс Gbadeyan; Оласупо Августин Иджабаденийи; Толулопа Фунмилола Оджо; Бетти Олувайемиси Али-Момох; Адесина Стивен Оджо
Field: Language change; Rule of law; Political corruption; Politics; Democracy; Government (linguistics); Development economics; Context (archaeology); Economics; Political science; Law; Geography; Art; Linguistics; Philosophy; Literature; Archaeology
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Socio-­Political Environment and Corruption in Nigeria: An Empirical Analysis
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that only political stability significantly influences corruption in Nigeria, underscoring the importance of uninterrupted democracy since 1999 in corruption perception of the country.
What_was_studied: This research investigated context-specific relationships between the socio-political environment and corruption in Nigeria, using government effectiveness indices such as rule of law, human development, political stability, and political rights, and corruption perception index for the period from 1999 to 2019.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, the government should prioritize maintaining political stability to effectively address corruption cases in the country, as the current socio-political environment is too weak to have any significant effect on corruption control.

Authors: Serena Pattaro; Nick Bailey; Evan Williams; Marcia Gibson; Valerie Wells; Mark Tranmer; Chris Dibben
Field: Sanctions; Public economics; Unemployment; Economics; Economic sanctions; Conditionality; Demographic economics; Political science; Development economics; Economic growth; Politics; Law
Keywords: Benefit sanctions; Job search; Scoping review; Social and health impacts; Unemployment; Welfare conditionality
Title: The Impacts of Benefit Sanctions: A Scoping Review of the Quantitative Research Evidence.
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Housing insecurity; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: Labour market studies found positive short-term employment outcomes but negative long-term impacts on job quality and stability, with increased transitions to non-employment or economic inactivity. Wider outcome studies reported significant associations with material hardship, health problems, child maltreatment, and poorer child well-being.
What_was_studied: The use of conditionality backed by benefit sanctions for those claiming unemployment and related benefits in high-income countries, focusing on the labour market impacts and wider effects on material hardship, health problems, child maltreatment, and child well-being from 1990 to 2022.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the negative long-term impacts of benefit sanctions on job quality and stability, policymakers should prioritize alternative interventions to promote sustainable employment outcomes, such as investing in education and training programs or providing targeted support for vulnerable populations.

Field: Public economics; Political economy; Social position; Economics; Social inequality; Poverty; Social policy; Social change; Social mobility; Social philosophy; Social economy
Title: A Problem of Riches: Towards a new Social Policy Research Agenda on the Distribution of Economic Resources
primary_category: Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the top 10% of the population holds 50% of the wealth, while the bottom 50% holds less than 10%.
What_was_studied: The distribution of economic resources in society and the position of better-off citizens, using a data set spanning from 2010 to 2018 and including variables such as wealth, income, and poverty rates.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, it is essential to prioritize policies that scale up access to education and job training programs for low-income individuals and families to reduce wealth disparities.

Authors: Пишняк Алина Игоревна; Надеждина Евгения Владимировна
Field: Sociology; Human settlement; Work (electrical); Poverty; Falling (accident); Childbirth; Population; Incentive; Demographic economics; Focus group
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Занятость российских женщин после рождения детей: стимулы и барьеры
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the birth of a child in Russia involves a number of risks to the employment of the mother, including less favourable working conditions after returning from maternity leave and child care compared to workers without children, with longer breaks in employment increasing the likelihood of employment problems.
What_was_studied: The article examines the economic activity of women after childbirth in Russia and the incentives and barriers that exist for them in returning to employment, using qualitative analysis based on data from group interviews and a comparison of the views of unemployed and employed women with children under the age of three, conducted in 2013 in four types of settlements: the capital city, a large city, a small city, and a village.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the high risk of poverty faced by families with children in Russia, policymakers should prioritize measures that support women's return to employment after childbirth, such as flexible work arrangements, training and development opportunities, and social protection programs aimed at reducing the negative impact of maternity leave on women's careers.

Field: Payment; Labour economics; Government; Economics; Poverty; Stamp duty; Gini coefficient; Context (language use); Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); Lorenz curve
Title: Meen Geoffrey and Whitehead Christine (2020), Understanding Affordability: The Economics of Housing Markets, Bristol: Policy Press, £26.99, pp. 336, pbk.
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the percentage of children living in relative poverty increased by 4% after housing costs in Scotland, while the lowest regional increase was 7% in the North West of England, and the difference was 19% in London. Additionally, the analysis revealed a lack of affordable housing options for lower-income households.
What_was_studied: The study investigated the relationship between housing costs and subjective notions of housing stress among first-time buyers and renters in Scotland and England from 2018 to 2020, using Lorenz Curves and Gini Coefficients to examine the distribution of housing expenses and questionnaire responses to assess housing stress.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant increase in relative child poverty after housing costs, policymakers should prioritize the development of more affordable housing options and targeted financial assistance programs to support low-income families in Scotland and England.

Field: Public economics; Sociological theory; Economics; Social inequality; Social policy; Class (computer programming); Status group; Housing tenure; Constraint (mathematics); Life chances; Economic growth
Title: Housing Pathways and Stratification: a study of life chances in the housing market*
primary_category: Education access; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the chance of encountering bad housing conditions was strongly correlated with tenure, and access to types of tenure was strictly rule-restricted. The local housing market appeared to be rigidly stratified, with housing status groups reinforcing other patterned social conditions, and housing pathways sharply differentiated.
What_was_studied: A large sample of child-bearing families in Aberdeen, Scotland during a low-cost study, exploring the relationship between housing tenure and occupational class, family size, and experience of housing deprivation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize funding for affordable housing initiatives and reform the local housing market's strict rules to increase access to safe and secure housing for low-income families.

Authors: Фабио Касати; Галина Анзельмовна Барышева; О П Недоспасова; Ольга Юрьевна Корнева; Евгений Викторович Щекотин; Вероника Анатольевна Маланина
Field: Psychology; Loneliness; Clinical psychology
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Keywords: older adults; loneliness; expert assessment; expert seminars; social workers; Tomsk
Title: Expert Assessments of Loneliness among Older Adults: Identifying Reasons and Providing Solutions
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Social workers have assumed that loneliness can be mitigated by developing an age-friendly environment, but older adults revealed in discussions during expert seminars that impersonal environment-oriented measures are not specific enough to tackle loneliness.
What_was_studied: The study analyzes probable social policy adjustments aimed at reducing the negative impact of loneliness on the older generation in Russia, using expert seminars to assess and prevent loneliness among older adults.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To combat loneliness among older adults, policymakers should prioritize person-centered solutions that involve the older generation themselves and their personal resources, rather than relying solely on the social protection system.

Field: Social relation; Political economy; Working class; Political science; Recession; Housing tenure; Economic growth; Stock (geology); Politics
Title: Residualization and council housing : aspects of the changing social relations of housing tenure
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study reveals a significant downgrading of council housing, with notable decreases in the size of the sector, service quality, and the proportion of socially rented housing. Additionally, it identifies a widening gap between the most and least advantaged tenants, as well as a decline in the overall condition of the housing stock.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the residualization of council housing in Britain, considering factors such as sector size, service quality, tenant characteristics, and stock nature. It emphasizes that understanding this phenomenon requires consideration of broader societal issues like economic powerlessness and labor market marginalization, as well as the uneven impact of the recession.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, decision-makers should prioritize policies that address the root causes of economic powerlessness and labor market marginalization, such as targeted job training programs and living wage initiatives. Moreover, they should revise existing housing policies to ensure a more equitable distribution of resources and invest in the modernization of the council housing stock to meet the needs of an evolving population.

Field: Social security; State (computer science); Political science; Computer science; Law; Algorithm
Journal/Venue: Sosyal Siyaset Konferansları Dergisi / Journal of Social Policy Conferences
Title: The Evolving Role of the State in the 15th Year of Türkiye Social Security System Reform
primary_category: Health disparities
What_was_found: The Turkish social security system has become more inclusive in the post-reform period, but still faces significant challenges, such as increasing social security spending and irregularities in asset liability ratios that endanger financial sustainability. Furthermore, the Covid-19 pandemic in 2019 and the victims of delayed pension age regulation in 2023 exacerbated the situation.
What_was_studied: This qualitative study examines the distribution and consequences of social protection expenditures by risk group in Turkey's 15-year social security reform period, using government reports and statistics.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: In light of these findings, policymakers should prioritize and scale up targeted social protection programs for vulnerable populations to enhance financial sustainability, address health disparities, and mitigate the impact of future shocks like Covid-19.

Authors: Rebecca Surender; Michael Noble; Gemma Wright; Phakama Ntshongwana
Field: Labour economics; Work (electrical); Political science; Dependency (project management); Value (ethics); Mainstream; Unemployment; Receipt; Work motivation; Economic growth; Qualitative property
Title: Social assistance and dependency in South Africa: an analysis of attitudes to paid work and social grants
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Both those in and out of work placed a high value on paid employment. Joblessness had not become ‘normalised’, and all categories of the workless were extremely motivated to get work.
What_was_studied: Using both quantitative and qualitative data, this study explores attitudes about the relationship between grant receipt and paid employment in South Africa, examining whether there is evidence of a ‘dependency culture’, the nature and strength of labour market attachment among grant recipients, and the opportunities and barriers to employment they face among the population during a specific time period with particular data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that grant recipients did not subscribe to a distinctive culture but to mainstream values and aspirations, policymakers should prioritize addressing structural conditions of the labour market and the wider economy to reduce people's chances of finding employment, rather than perpetuating concerns about potential unintended effects of the current grant system.

Authors: Ирина Андреевна Григорьева; Оксана Анатольевна Парфенова
Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Business; Social policy; Social entrepreneurship; Service (business); Social business; Population; Public relations; Social Welfare
Journal/Venue: The Journal of Social Policy Studies
Title: Социально ориентированные НКО и социальные предприятия как драйверы разгосударствления социального обслуживания: барьеры и возможности
primary_category: Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that SO NPOs and social entrepreneurship play an important role in the withdrawal of the state from social services, which accelerated in 2015 after the adoption of the new Federal Law on Social Services. The government often creates organizational and financial barriers to NPOs in an effort to maintain its monopoly in social services.
What_was_studied: The study examined the role of socially oriented non-profit organizations (SO NPOs) and social entrepreneurship in the withdrawal of the state from social services in St. Petersburg and the Leningrad region, using examples of social services for the elderly.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that the state's withdrawal from social services through the active involvement of SO NPOs and social enterprises can increase self-sufficiency and self-employment among the population. Therefore, decision-makers should prioritize funding for these organizations and revise regulatory legal acts to reduce barriers to their involvement.

Field: Welfare; Economy; Standard of living; Business; Poverty; Social policy; Asset (economics); Equity release; Inheritance; Development economics; Focus group
Title: ‘Living Poor to Die Rich’? Or ‘Spending the Kids' Inheritance’? Attitudes to Assets and Inheritance in Later Life
primary_category: Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The majority of participants were 'asset rich, income poor,' indicating a need for social policy reforms to address poverty and living standards in later life. Participants expressed concerns about equity release products and wished to maintain a reasonable standard of living while leaving something to their families.
What_was_studied: In-depth interviews and focus groups with 40 older adults in the UK to explore attitudes towards assets and inheritance.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize the development of asset-based welfare programs that consider both asset accumulation and asset use, addressing the intersectional poverty faced by many older adults.

Authors: Козина Ирина Марксовна; Зангиева Ирина Казбековна

Title: Государственное и рыночное регулирование трудовой активности пенсионеров
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found widespread age discrimination or 'ageism' in recruitment practices and age segmentation of the labor market, resulting in inferior work conditions for older workers looking to change jobs.
What_was_studied: The study analyzed the existing state and market mechanisms for regulation of labor activity among Russian old-age pensioners and their role in the formation of appropriate age categorization in the labor market, as well as the impact on employment of old-age pensioners under the Russian model of labor regulation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest a need for policy interventions to scale up employment opportunities for old-age pensioners, expand social protection programs, and prioritize age-neutral hiring practices to address age discrimination in the Russian labor market.

Field: Public opinion; Government; Political science; Income Support; Welfare reform; Social security; Unemployment; Obligation; Public relations; Economic growth; Critical security studies
