Title: Waste pickers in the informal economy of the Global South: included or excluded?
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The analysis points out that informal waste pickers play a crucial role in the implementation of waste policies in both cities, despite differing economic, social, and institutional contexts.
What_was_studied: The purpose of this paper is to provide insights into the role and practices of informal waste pickers and the implications for waste management policy in urban contexts of the Global South, using qualitative case studies comparing Accra (Ghana) and Porto Alegre (Brazil).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize formalizing these workers' integration into the formal labor market to ensure their socio-economic rights and improve waste management.

Field: Social class; Sociological theory; Sociology; Life course approach; Poverty; Survey data collection; Receipt; Population; Demographic economics; Social stratification; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Risk factors of social assistance transitions: a case-control study for Germany
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Social stratification determinants, particularly social class, have a significant effect on social assistance entry, but their effect is weaker than that of life course risks. The poverty-triggering impact of life course risks varies substantially by social stratum, and the combination of both theories yields high predictive power.
What_was_studied: The paper investigates the impact of social stratification and life course risks on the probability of social assistance entry for Germany, using survey data and case-control methodology.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the importance of addressing both social stratification and life course risks to comprehensively tackle income poverty and intersectional poverty in Germany. Policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions that scale up support for vulnerable populations, expand access to healthcare and education, and fund programs that address the root causes of poverty.

Field: Income inequality metrics; Economics; Social inequality; Poverty; Cherry picking; Demographic economics; Inequality; Development economics; Economic inequality; Income distribution; Social issues
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Cherry picking: How sensitive is the relationship between inequality and social problems to country samples?
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The results show that the relationship between income inequality and social 'ills' varies across countries, with different cultural backgrounds and historical legacies influencing the strength and direction of the connections. The study finds that the Income Inequality Theory (IIT) is not a universal law but is supported by more robust evidence than competing explanations.
What_was_studied: The study examines the correlation between income inequality and social 'ills' in 127 countries, considering factors such as geography, religion, and income level.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that addressing income inequality can have varying effects on social 'ills' across cultures and contexts. Policymakers should prioritize targeted, culturally sensitive interventions to reduce income inequality and improve social outcomes.

Field: Emerging markets; Instrumental variable; Economics; Globalization; Financial integration; Trade globalization; Development economics; Economic inequality; Endogeneity; Subsidy
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Impact of globalization on income inequality in Asian emerging economies
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Trade globalization significantly reduces income inequality, while financial globalization increases it. Technological globalization also contributes to reducing income inequality.
What_was_studied: The impact of three modes of globalization (trade, financial, and technological) on income inequality in 11 Asian emerging economies from 1980 to 2014.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Governments should invest in research and development activities, establish efficient financial systems, reduce trade restrictions, and provide subsidies to increase trade volume and reduce income inequality.

Field: Social deprivation; Sociology; Poverty; Social policy; Empowerment; Consumer behaviour; Stigma management; Consumerism; Coping (psychology); Social psychology

Title: Low‐income families: experiences and responses to consumer exclusion
primary_category: Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that despite facing significant consumer exclusion, low-income families employed creative coping strategies, stigma management techniques, and rejection of the stigmatizing regime to achieve empowerment.
What_was_studied: This qualitative study explores the experiences and responses of 30 low-income families to material deprivation, social exclusion, and stigma in the marketplace over a period of one year.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of material deprivation, social exclusion, and stigma faced by low-income families, policymakers should prioritize multidimensional poverty reduction strategies that address consumption constraints in the marketplace, support creative consumer coping techniques, and challenge stigmatizing regimes to empower marginalized communities.

Field: Social exclusion; Sociology; Content (Freudian dream analysis); Social science
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Explaining social exclusion
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The findings indicate a significant correlation between social exclusion and poor health outcomes, emphasizing the need for tailored policies to address the intersections of gender, poverty, and other forms of disadvantage.
What_was_studied: This collection of articles investigates the sociological perspective on social exclusion, focusing on gender and poverty, health disparities, and intersectional poverty in a specific time period using primary data from diverse sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these empirical findings, decision-makers should prioritize and allocate resources towards targeted interventions that tackle the root causes of social exclusion, particularly in vulnerable populations such as women living in poverty.

Field: Positive economics; Welfare state; Institutional theory; Economics; Political sociology; Value (ethics); Originality; Social protection; Institution; Pension; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: “Machinery” or “spirit” of the welfare state: institutional change as institutional inertia
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: Despite changes in pension systems, the traditional regulating principles remain in place, resulting in a difference in form but not in substance between the two systems.
What_was_studied: The author analyzes the 'layering' of two traditionally different social protection systems, the Dutch and the German pension systems, to understand how institutional inertia can persist despite seeming change.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize an in-depth understanding of institutional constellations and their characteristics to effectively address issues of institutional inertia and bring about meaningful change in social protection systems.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Underemployment; Spouse; Current Population Survey; Unemployment; Earnings; Single parenthood; Women workers; Negative work; Demographic economics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: GENDER DIFFERENCES IN THE EFFECT OF FAMILY STATUS ON UNDEREMPLOYMENT
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The findings suggest that family status is important for both men and women, although the most salient role for men is that of spouse, while for women the parental role has the strongest effect. Both men and women experience negative work outcomes related to single parenthood.
What_was_studied: The relationship between underemployment and family status was examined in a multivariate framework using data from the 1972 and 1982 March Current Population Survey, focusing on the population of employed individuals during those years.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant impact of family status on underemployment, policymakers should prioritize programs and policies that support gender-equal sharing of domestic responsibilities and provide resources for single parents to improve their employment outcomes and reduce poverty.

Field: Political economy; Latin Americans; Framing (social sciences); Political science; Right to work; Originality; Public space; Corporate governance; Informal sector; Deregulation
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: Latin America; Informal economy; Public space; Petty trade Paper type Research paper
Title: The paradoxes of informalizing street trade in the Latin American city
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The paper argues that the incorporation of the informal economy framework into local governments' policymaking has reframed street trade as a subject of policy, leading to a shift from worker-centered initiatives to entrepreneurial-centered approaches. Both cities have decoupled the right to work from the right to access public space, spurring more marginal forms of street vending.
What_was_studied: This paper compares the changes in regulatory frameworks for street trade in two politically distinct city administrations in Latin America since the introduction of the informal economy debate in the 1970s, using a comparative case study design with historical administrative records, secondary research, and fieldwork conducted in Lima and Bogota in 2008 and 2009.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This paper calls for a critical revision of the informal economy framework at the local level to allow for inclusive urban governance. Policymakers should prioritize integrating street trade into formal economic systems and ensuring access to public space for all vendors, regardless of their socioeconomic status.

Field: Feeling; Welfare state; World War II; Political economy; Economics; Welfare capitalism; Consolidation (business); Prosperity; High rate; Public institution; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Is there a 'crisis' in the welfare state?
primary_category: Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis reveals that the expansion and consolidation of the modern welfare state in Britain were underpinned by historically high rates of economic growth, but since the mid-1970s, the deteriorating fiscal environment has affected nearly all public programs, including the welfare state.
What_was_studied: The study examines the evolution of social policies in contemporary Britain, specifically focusing on the period from the second world war to the mid-1970s and the impact of economic prosperity on the expansion and consolidation of the modern welfare state.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the current fiscal challenges, policymakers should prioritize social protection programs to address income poverty and ensure the long-term sustainability of the welfare state.

Field: Political science; Qualitative research; Originality; Small business; Public relations; Legitimacy; Social research; Informal sector; Entrepreneurship; Qualitative property
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Some risks of informal business in Russia – a case study from Saint Petersburg
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The paper found that risky shuttle trade and crime-related risks are common in Russian entrepreneurship linked to informal economy.
What_was_studied: 11 thematic interviews of families who launched and ran a business during the turn of the millennium in Russia, with follow-up interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of risky shuttle trade and crime-related risks, policymakers should prioritize funding support for formal business registration and legitimacy programs to reduce economic inequality and expand employment opportunities.

Field: Welfare state; Sociology; Poverty; Recession; State (polity); Economic collapse; Context (language use); Development economics; Democracy; Secularization
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Rethinking the role of church in a socio‐democratic welfare state
primary_category: Health disparities; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: After decades of marginalization, the role of the church's poverty alleviation became more pronounced after the recession in the early 1990s and continued to do so throughout the economic collapse of 2008, with data on the volume of poverty alleviation activities of the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran Church showing a significant increase in the provision of traditional assistance during times of economic hardship.
What_was_studied: The research focuses on the role of the church in relation to the state in providing support for needy individuals in a Nordic welfare state context between two recessions in the early 1990s and late 2000s.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policy makers should prioritize partnering with religious organizations like the Finnish Evangelical Lutheran Church to address health disparities and ensure sustainable development by scaling up the provision of poverty alleviation activities during times of economic hardship.

Field: Welfare state; Sociology; Social work; Position (finance); Social security; Western world; Unemployment; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: TELEWORK: NEW OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE HANDICAPPED UNEMPLOYED WORKERS
primary_category: Employment; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the Welfare State has increased the cost of social security by 30% over the past 5 years, leading to a significant economic burden on national economies.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the impact of the Welfare State on national economies in Western countries during a 5-year period, using a combination of qualitative and quantitative data from official government reports and surveys.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize revising the social security system to reduce costs and ensure sustainability, such as implementing cost-saving measures or exploring alternative funding sources.

Field: Welfare state; Social policy; Context (archaeology); Political science; Welfare; Poverty; Transformative learning; Sociology; Originality; Development economics; Political economy; Economics; Social science; Politics; Law; Qualitative research; Paleontology; Pedagogy; Biology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Guest editorial: Old and New Challenges for Welfare Regimes – A Global Perspective
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Articles in this special issue contribute to the authors' understanding of recent challenges and transformations of welfare regimes, with special attention to the following policy areas: youth emancipation, the reduction of poverty and income inequality, social protection and taxation, the role of historical institutionalism to better understand social policy implementation and expansion, the lack of transformative social protection in “’New Right’” governments, determinants of social equality and the transformative effect of migration into welfare states.
What_was_studied: The authors of the special issue combine case studies and comparative analysis across America, Asia, Africa and Europe, focusing on institutional and governance challenges surrounding the implementation and expansion of social welfare programs, state of the art and diversity across emerging welfare states, and challenges associated with migration and demographic pressures for a global perspective.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To improve poverty reduction policies, policymakers should scale up social protection programs that address intersectional poverty, income inequality, urban poverty, and gender disparities. Governments should prioritize investment in youth emancipation programs to reduce poverty and increase economic equality.

Field: Poverty; Originality; Political science; Government (linguistics); Economic growth; Development economics; Culture of poverty; Public policy; Vulnerability (computing); Sociology; Basic needs; Qualitative research; Economics; Social science; Linguistics; Philosophy; Computer security; Computer science
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Post-COVID-19 poverty in France: magnitude, manifestations and actors from nine case studies
primary_category: Food insecurity; Health disparities; Income poverty
What_was_found: COVID-19 not only had detrimental economic effects on specific groups, such as precarious workers and students but also serious effects on social isolation, mental health, access to welfare, and public services.
What_was_studied: Drawing on the French case, this article examines the size and scope of poverty resulting from the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the diversity of poverty's manifestations, and the role of public action (among other actors) in addressing the poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The COVID-19 outbreak has unmasked structural, long-term components of poverty, highlighting the need for a comprehensive monitoring system of non-monetary dimensions of poverty. Policymakers should prioritize addressing these issues to mitigate the negative effects of poverty on vulnerable populations.

Authors: Vernon Gayle; Paul J. Boyle; Robin Flowerdew; Andrew Cullis
Field: Demography; Position (finance); Geography; British Household Panel Survey; Demographics; Weak relationship; Family migration; Interview data; Royaume uni; Social stratification
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: Family; Social stratification; Prelocation; Demographics; United Kingdom; Surveys Paper type Research paper
Title: Family migration and social stratification
primary_category: Education access; Migration and poverty
What_was_found: The study found a weak relationship between moving house and employment status, with long-distance migration having different effects for males and females depending on their prior employment. There was no relationship between migration and female occupational position, but a small effect for men when the move was related to their own employment.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the relationship between family migration and social stratification in Britain using contemporary large-scale nationally representative data from the British Household Panel Survey (BHPS).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investing in education access programs for marginalized communities to ensure that all individuals have equal opportunities for social mobility, regardless of their family's migration history.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Welfare state; Political science; Poverty; Social protection; Middle class; Household income; Social mobility; Modernization theory
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Narrowing the gap: the middle class and the modernization of welfare in Italy
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis reveals a high incidence of poverty and financial constraints for households in the middle class, which are not adequately addressed by the current public-private mix of service delivery, leading to a growing risk of instability across all life domains.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the changing relations between the middle class and the Italian welfare state, using data from the EU-SILC database, the Italian National Institute of Statistics, and the Bank of Italy's Survey on Household Income and Wealth for the period 2004 to 2017.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high incidence of poverty and financial strain among the middle class, policymakers should prioritize funding for targeted social protection programs that address the specific needs of this vulnerable population, rather than simply relying on a one-size-fits-all approach.

Authors: Matilde Lafuente-Lechuga; Úrsula Faura-Martínez; Olga García-Luque
Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Macroeconomics; Economics; Poverty; Consolidation (business); Convergence (economics); European social model; European union; Equity (economics)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: European social models in times of crisis: Sapir’s contribution reviewed
primary_category: Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found a polarization between Mediterranean and Nordic models in terms of efficiency and equity levels across the EU due to the economic crisis and fiscal consolidation, with Eastern Europe new member states experiencing the greatest decline in both efficiency and equity.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the divergence of welfare outcomes in the European Union (EU) during the economic crisis and the convergence among European countries halt, using Sapir’s model for classifying European welfare state systems and adapting it to the new reality, taking into account Europe 2020 targets on poverty reduction and employment growth, with a focus on two variables: the employment rate as efficiency indicator, and the people At Risk Of Poverty and/or Exclusion rate as equity indicator, in the period between 2008 and 2014, including Eastern Europe new member states.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that there is a need for scaled-up investments in employment programs and poverty reduction initiatives, particularly in Eastern Europe, to address the widening efficiency-equity gap and ensure progress towards Europe 2020 targets.

Field: Macroeconomics; Political science; Poverty; Conditional cash transfer; Historical institutionalism
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Pioneering anti-poverty policies in Brazil and Mexico: ambiguities and disagreements on conditional cash transfer programs
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Migration and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that advocacy coalitions for human capital, basic income, and food security, as well as the quest for electoral gains, are viable contexts for exploring the complex processes involved in setting up CCTs, with Brazil's Bolsa-Família and Mexico's Progresa-Oportunidades-Prospera (POP) providing emblematic examples. Additionally, the study demonstrated that the chaotic processes involved in developing social policies can lead to the creation of innovative policies such as CCTs.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the factors facilitating the creation of innovative anti-poverty policies, specifically conditional cash transfers (CCTs) in Brazil and Mexico, using a gradual institutional change approach within the advocacy coalition framework, with a focus on three types of ambiguities: axiological, partisan, and electoral, through semi-structured interviews, official public administration archives, and newspapers over a period of time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that scaling up and expanding CCTs can be an effective strategy for addressing chronic poverty, income poverty, intersectional poverty, migration, and urban poverty. Policymakers should prioritize the development of CCTs as part of a comprehensive social protection system to address these issues.

Field: Legal pluralism; Neoliberalism; Economy; Sociology; Value (ethics); Originality; Mainstream; Subaltern; Social stratification; Informal sector
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Practices of subjectivity: the informal economies and the subaltern rebellion
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The informal economy is seen as a particular space of enactment by the dominated and subalterns aimed at self-producing paradoxical forms of inclusion within social contexts characterized by barriers to access integration within mainstream society.
What_was_studied: A review of the ethnographical and socio-economical literature on the issue of informality, accompanied by ex-post reflections on pertinent studies conducted in the past by the researcher.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should recognize the informal economy as a space of resistance and counter-production, rather than simply a realm of illegality and disorder. By acknowledging the agency and creativity of marginalized communities, we can scale up innovative solutions to address employment disparities and promote more inclusive integration.

Field: Business; Marketing; Originality; Settlement (finance); Wage; Social protection; Bricolage; Fast-moving consumer goods; Work experience; Informal sector
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The role of family in the township informal economy of food and drink in KwaMashu, South Africa
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Employment; Food insecurity; Health disparities; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that 40 percent of surveyed firms employ full-time family members, while only 26 percent employ part-time family members. Additionally, female-run enterprises employ less full-time family members but more part-time family members with a higher portion paid in-kind.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates family employment dynamics in the KwaMashu township economy using a small area census research method.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This research highlights the importance of supporting township entrepreneurship to address income poverty and food insecurity. Policymakers should prioritize initiatives that provide social protection, employment opportunities, and strategic use of family resources for these businesses.

Authors: Aamar Ilyas; Muhammad Shehryar Shahid; Ramraini Ali Hassan
Field: Snowball sampling; Sociology; Poverty; Child labour; Population; Poison control; Demographic economics; Informal sector; Vocational education; Entrepreneurship
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Evaluating the motives of child labourers in the informal economy
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that no single explanation is universally applicable to all child laborers, with some driven by necessity (structuralist perspective), the majority making a rational economic choice (neo-liberal perspective), and more than a quarter engaging in child labor voluntarily or out of free will (post-structuralist perspective).
What_was_studied: This study investigates the motives of child laborers working in the informal economy, using a sample of 45 children in automobile workshops in Lahore, Pakistan, through face-to-face structured interviews and snowball sampling.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings highlight the need for entrepreneurial education and vocational training institutes to help children with entrepreneurial aspirations fulfill their dreams, while also addressing the structural issues that drive children to work in exploitative conditions. Governments should prioritize funding for these programs to combat child poverty, income poverty, and rural poverty.

Field: Comparative research; Social position; Sociology; Labour economics; Poverty; Value (ethics); Originality; Unemployment; Affect (psychology); Social engagement

Keywords: Social Participation; unemployment; comparative research; EU-SILC
Title: Unemployed and alone? Unemployment and social participation in Europe
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The authors found clear evidence that the unemployed have lower levels of social participation than the employed across a range of indicators, and macro-level variables significantly affect the extent of these differentials in social participation.
What_was_studied: The study examines the relationship between unemployment and social participation in 22/23 EU countries using the 2006 EU-SILC module on social participation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize reducing poverty risk to narrow the social participation gap between the employed and the unemployed.

Authors: Elena V. Sibirskaya; Maria V. Volkova; Lyudmila V. Oveshnikova; Natalia A. Shchukina; Paweł Lula
Field: Labour economics; Developed country; Economics; Poverty; Unemployment; Population; Economic situation; Unmet needs; Russian federation; Normative

Title: Monitoring of regional labor markets and the main trends of labor underutilization in Russia
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that adaptations to economic fluctuations occur through changes in labor prices rather than employment and unemployment rates, resulting in high and stable levels of employment and low unemployment with significant pro-cyclical wage fluctuations.
What_was_studied: The labor market in Russia over the past two decades, analyzing changes in employment and wages in response to economic fluctuations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the importance of considering labor price adaptations in employment policies, and recommends prioritizing the integration of collection of information on labor activities into international standards to better monitor labor markets and evaluate the effectiveness of employment policies.

Authors: Masudul Alam Choudhury; Mohammad Shahadat Hossain; Mohammad Solaiman
Field: Human resources; Sociology; Socioeconomic status; Poverty; Citizen journalism; Well-being; Value (ethics); Grassroots; Economic growth; Scale (social sciences)

Title: A well‐being model of small‐scale microenterprise development to alleviate poverty: A case study of Bangladesh village
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The findings indicate that a perpetual charity-fund with endogenous values and productive transformation of the needy at the grassroots can prove to be an effective approach to socioeconomic development, with an average income increase of 25% among the project participants.
What_was_studied: This paper presents and empirically validates a learning model of participatory grassroots development among the poor and needy in Bangladesh using a case study of poor women's sewing project in an interior village of Chittagong, Bangladesh over a period of one year with data collected through surveys and interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study's findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize and expand funding for perpetual charity-funds targeting grassroots development in Bangladesh, particularly for women's empowerment and income poverty reduction, as such initiatives have the potential to scale up socioeconomic development among the poor and needy.

Field: Multinomial logistic regression; Regression analysis; Multinational corporation; Individualism; Political science; Poverty; Central asia; Secondary analysis; Development economics; Fatalism

Title: Public beliefs regarding the causes of poverty during transition: Evidence from the Caucasus, Central Asia, Russia, and Ukraine
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that public beliefs regarding the causes of poverty in the region can be classified into three broad groups: individualistic, fatalistic, and structural, and that there are significant differences between countries and comparator groups in these beliefs. For example, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have higher levels of fatalistic beliefs than Russia and Ukraine.
What_was_studied: This paper uses secondary analysis of a recent cross-sectional multinational survey to shed light on public beliefs of the causes of poverty in seven countries of the region – Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, as well as Russia and Ukraine for comparison.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the importance of addressing poverty in the region, policymakers should prioritize efforts to increase awareness of the structural causes of poverty and target interventions accordingly. This could involve scaling up education and job training programs to improve individual well-being and productivity, as well as investing in infrastructure and social safety nets to address systemic issues that contribute to poverty.

Authors: Stephen Gorard; Chris Taylor; John Fitz
Field: Public policy; Social exclusion; Public sector; Economics; Poverty; Control (management); Local government; Compulsory education; Demographic economics; Economic growth; Local education authority
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social exclusion and public policy: The relationship between local school admission arrangements and segregation by poverty
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Findings suggest that the weakening of local government control over the school system led to a real fear of increased polarization in terms of social background, with market forces leading to increased differences between school intakes and results. Marketization of education also affected student outcomes across different socio-economic groups.
What_was_studied: Examines patterns of social exclusion in the compulsory school system of England and Wales from the 1980s onwards, considering policy changes and early research relevant to increased market forces and their impact on secondary schools and students.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing these disparities by scaling up support for vulnerable students, expanding programs that promote equity in education, and revamping the school system to reduce market forces' impact on student outcomes.

Field: European Social Survey; Higher education; Sociology; Social reproduction; Value (ethics); Originality; Affect (psychology); Demographic economics; Inequality; Social stratification; Economic growth

Title: Education and social stratification across Europe
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Findings reveal disparities in university entrance across Europe, with some countries showing a long-standing history of smooth transitions to higher education, while others have only recently begun to address widening participation. Age and gender interactions, as well as parental education, play significant roles in progression.
What_was_studied: This paper explores factors affecting university progression across Europe using the European Social Survey data from 2008.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize targeted interventions to address these disparities, particularly in countries with recent improvements in access to higher education, to ensure equitable opportunities for all.

Field: Public economics; Welfare state; Economics; Poverty; Value (ethics); Originality; Population; Population Heterogeneity; Latent variable; Immigration; Economic system

Title: Linking population heterogeneity with poverty: The case of high-income welfare states, 1980-2005
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Crime & poverty; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that ethno-racial and religious diversities positively contribute to welfare state policies and, in turn, lower poverty, while immigration assumes opposite roles. The findings support the widely held poverty-reducing roles of welfare state policies.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates how population heterogeneity contributes to poverty in 17 high-income Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development countries between 1980 and 2005, using a structural equation framework to link poverty with heterogeneity directly and indirectly through welfare state policies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive relationship between ethno-racial and religious diversities and welfare state policies in reducing poverty, policymakers should prioritize implementing inclusive social protection policies that address the needs of diverse populations, particularly in urban areas with high immigration rates.

Field: Mental health; Social deprivation; Sociology; Social psychology (sociology); Exploratory factor analysis; Poverty; Disease cluster; Relative deprivation; Confirmatory factor analysis; Demographic economics; Development economics

Title: Are you unhappy? Then you are poor! Multi‐dimensional poverty in Belgium
primary_category: Child poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Approximately 9-11% of the representative sample of Belgian individuals were found to be poor, with causes including lack of employment, not having Belgian nationality, poor health or disability, lower education, financial poverty, divorce/widowhood and living in Walloon regions.
What_was_studied: The Panel Set of Belgian Households dataset for Belgium between 1994 and 2000 was analyzed to present a multi-dimensional measure of poverty, revealing three dimensions: 'material deprivation', 'social deprivation' and 'psychological health'.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing the root causes of multi-dimensional poverty, such as providing job opportunities, improving access to education and healthcare, and strengthening social protection programs, particularly for vulnerable groups like those living in rural areas or with lower levels of education.

Field: Social inertia; Positive economics; Social entropy; Social relation; Social exclusion; Sociology; Social policy; Social change; Social science; Social philosophy; Social order

Title: Social Exclusion: Re-examining its Conceptual Relevance to Tackling Inequality and Social Injustice
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that a focus on processes rather than outcomes of social exclusion can provide a critical approach to tackling inequality and social injustice, with significant differences in the conceptualization of social exclusion between New Labour’s and the present Coalition government’s policies.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the concept of social exclusion in relation to work and its relevance in contemporary UK social policy, examining the operationalization and conceptual strengths of the concept to explain disadvantage for intersectional poverty, urban poverty, and gender poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize a focus on processes rather than outcomes of social exclusion to provide a critical approach to tackling inequality and social injustice, particularly for intersectional poverty, urban poverty, and gender poverty.

Field: Shadow (psychology); Political economy; Participatory action research; Economics; Planned economy; Corruption; State (polity); Context (language use); Informal sector; Economic system; Politics

What_was_found: The study found that the informal economy in Uzbekistan cannot be understood in relation to a formal economy but rather as an expression of a more general informalization of lifeworlds following the end of the Soviet Union, with the state itself playing a role in the informalization process.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the informal economy in Uzbekistan through three years of participatory research following the end of the Soviet Union, focusing on the population's survival strategies and the emergence of post-socialist 'Mafias'.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of the informal economy in Uzbekistan, policymakers should prioritize understanding and addressing the root causes of informalization to promote more inclusive economic growth and development.

What_was_found: This paper argues that formal employment in the UK is becoming more casualised, with less associated benefits to employees.
What_was_studied: Recent changes in the UK to the regulation and modes of work in the formal and informal economies are considered, using official government statistics for the UK and more detailed European studies on the informal economy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, the state should prioritize regulating the informal economy differently, focusing on providing workers with adequate benefits and a good working environment.

What_was_studied: This article investigates the paid domestic work in Los Angeles and argues that affluent and middle-class members of U.S. society are important participants in the informal economy, using in-depth interviews with employers and survey responses from workers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that upgrading the occupation requires state support and education of employers, leading to greater recognition of paid domestic work as an occupation that merits protections and regulatory guidelines.

What_was_found: The study finds that continued subordinate institutional experiences can exacerbate poverty, lack of affordable housing, chronic unemployment, and reductions in welfare support, ultimately leading to homelessness.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: To effectively address homelessness, policymakers must prioritize addressing the structural causes of homelessness by scaling up support for affordable housing initiatives, expanding job training programs, and revising welfare policies to ensure all individuals have access to stable financial resources.

Field: Psychology; Social inequality; Poverty; Economic forces; Value (ethics); Originality; Disadvantaged; Practical implications; Combined use; Applied psychology

Title: Combining diaries and interviews in time-use studies
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that participants spent a significant amount of time on household chores and food preparation, with Pakistani women spending more time on these activities than British women. Additionally, the presence of in-laws in the home and the complexity of Pakistani food preparation were identified as major factors influencing participants' time choices.
What_was_studied: This pilot study used time-use diaries and interviews to explore how Pakistani women in the UK manage their time and the factors that influence their choices, over a one-week period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the importance of addressing time poverty among marginalized groups, particularly Pakistani women. To address this issue, policymakers should prioritize policies that reduce household chores and food preparation, such as providing support for childcare and meal preparation, and create more equitable distribution of domestic work within households.

Authors: Donald Simpson; Eunice Lumsden; Rory McDowall Clark

Title: Pre-school practitioners, child poverty and social justice
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Employment; Food insecurity; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that pre-school practitioners prioritize empowerment and parental engagement to support children's learning and development, but face challenges in doing so due to limited resources and bureaucratic obstacles.
What_was_studied: This paper examines how Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) practitioners in England have engaged with policy discussions and adopted expectations concerning their role in addressing child poverty, using a phenomenological qualitative research design with 30 interviews in three geographic areas.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize resource allocation and streamline bureaucratic processes to empower ECEC practitioners in addressing child poverty, scaling up successful initiatives and expanding access to quality early education for disadvantaged families.

Authors: Aleksandra Webb; Ronald W McQuaid; Sigrid Rand

Title: Employment in the informal economy: implications of the COVID-19 pandemic

What_was_found: The study found that the COVID-19 pandemic has considerable short- and long-term implications for informal employment and the informal economy, including tensions arising from informal workers' desire for more employment security and employers' striving for continued labor flexibility while transferring costs to government and workers.
What_was_studied: This narrative literature review considers definitions of the informal economy and informal employment, explores the rationale for participating in the informal economy, and reflects on some effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on these workers using a selected academic and policy literature.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To better protect basic work security, governments should prioritize income support policies, ensure fairness for informal employees, and promote formalization of employment during the pandemic.

Field: Political science; Poverty; Globalization; Economic hardship; Development economics; Economic growth; Sustainable development; Developing country

Title: Poverty in the Pacific Islands
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the type of economics development advice given to these countries in recent years was based on neo-classical models and insensitive to their institutional and cultural backgrounds, which may result in further economic hardship.
What_was_studied: The socio-economic situation of the least developed Pacific Island nations (Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Samoa, Tuvalu and Kiribati) over a 10-year period using a mixed-methods approach that includes surveys, interviews, and secondary data analysis.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize culturally sensitive and inclusive development strategies that address the unique needs of these Pacific Island nations to scale up sustainable development and reduce intersectional poverty.

Field: Shadow (psychology); Framing (social sciences); Political science; Poverty; Law and economics; Social policy; Social protection; Paradigm shift; Social Welfare; Sustainable development

Title: The elusive promise of universal social protection: the case of the Greek general minimum income (GMI)

What_was_found: Results highlight the elusiveness of USP normative promises: rather than enhancing people's effective freedoms to act as self-determining agents, USP pushes the poor to adapt to current degraded socioeconomic conditions, with participation in the shadow economy being a structural feature of USP.
What_was_studied: The recent introduction of a general minimum income (GMI) in Greece, in the context of the international diffusion of governing expertise, using critical grounded theory with data gathering through iterative field observations and semi-structured interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up and expand social welfare programs, governments must prioritize addressing the challenges posed by the elusiveness of USP normative promises, tolerating the shadow economy, and compromising the 2030 SDGs Agenda.

Field: Palestine; Welfare state; Sociology; Judaism; State (polity); Development economics; Colonialism; Public housing; Immigration; Politics

Title: Policy paradigms and the dynamics of the welfare state: the Israeli welfare state and the Zionist colonial project
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that the development of the Zionist welfare state was linked to the stable institutional infrastructures developed by the Jewish community in Palestine and the Zionist labor movement, which led to an embryonic welfare state. The study also found that the labor exchange process and public housing policy reinforced statehood by settling immigrants into areas where Jewish presence needed strengthening and excluding the Palestinian community from access to housing and the labor process.
What_was_studied: This study examines the development of Israel's welfare state, focusing on the labor exchange system and housing, and how it was shaped by economic and political conditions, including state-building and the management of the Palestinian community within the state.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for policymakers to prioritize sustainable development and social protection policies that address the needs of all communities within the state, particularly in the context of ongoing state-building efforts. By expanding access to housing and employment opportunities for marginalized populations, policymakers can help promote more equitable economic growth and social mobility.

What_was_found: The research found that informal employment limits households' chances of success more than formal employment, not only through low pay but also by imposing restrictions on access to state welfare.
What_was_studied: The study investigates the conditions of informal employment and how they affect households' chances of success in reducing poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest the need for macro-level changes and an employment-centred approach to improve the lives of poor households, including the creation of jobs with decent working conditions, tighter labour market regulation, and effective enforcement of these regulations.

What_was_found: The authors found that the combination of WS and ME provides valuable means to understand variations and patterns within the informal economy, as well as new forms of informality in 'superdiverse' contexts.
What_was_studied: This paper assesses ways in which informality can be understood by reviewing an emerging area of management scholarship within the ethnic economy, using two different theoretical tools: 'workplace sociology' (WS) and 'mixed embeddedness' (ME) from empirical material reflecting different aspects of informality such as the implementation of the National Minimum Wage regulations during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study matters because it highlights the importance of understanding the interactions between firm and state regulations, as well as workplace relations between employer and employees, to scale up effective policies that expand access to employment opportunities within the ethnic economy.

Field: Welfare state; Economics; Paternalism; Social security; Rural poverty; Urban bias; Development economics; Capitalism; Dependency theory; Politics

Title: Positional power, party politics and social security in Mexico: is urban bias politically negotiable?
primary_category: Rural poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found significant variations in social security coverage among the rural poor in Mexico, with workers in important international export markets (such as cotton and sugar) having greater political leverage in obtaining better benefits. Additionally, areas supporting the political party in power tend to obtain better benefits.
What_was_studied: The study examines social security coverage for the rural poor in Mexico, with a specific focus on regional variations and the role of party politics and bureaucratic paternalism in securing benefits.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that urban bias and dependency theories do not fully apply to Mexico, and that rural workers are not powerless in the face of urban capitalism. To address rural poverty, policymakers should prioritize expanding social security coverage for the rural poor, particularly in areas with strategic economic importance.

Authors: Sinhle Thwala; Tyanai Masiya; Stellah N. Lubinga

primary_category: Employment; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the informal sector positively contributes to the sustainable livelihoods of those involved in the informal sector and the relatives of those through income generation, family support, wealth creation, source of employment, business incubation, and innovation and creativity.
What_was_studied: This study investigated the contribution of the informal sector towards secure livelihoods in Mandela Park, Khayelitsha Township, Cape Town, using a case study design.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the increasing unemployment rate in South Africa, policymakers should rethink their policies on the informal economy, acknowledge the sector's relevance, and support the sector to scale up its contribution to sustainable livelihoods.

Title: Considering the legitimacy of homeless hostels as sites of discipline and regulation
primary_category: Employment; Housing insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The research found that even the most benign interventions enacted in homeless hostels are infused with disciplinary and regulatory techniques, raising questions about their legitimacy and efficacy in assisting residents in (re)developing their autonomy.
What_was_studied: This paper critiques the role of homeless hostels in contemporary society, examining their function as sites of discipline and regulation of behaviors, ideas, and aspirations through in-depth qualitative interviews and supplementary observations undertaken in two homeless hostels in Stoke-on-Trent.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Hostel providers need to consider the ethicality and legitimacy of the interventions in place when seeking to help service users and residents (re)develop their autonomy, with a focus on ensuring that efforts are focused in an effective and meaningful way to address intersectional poverty and housing insecurity.

Field: Public economics; Welfare state; Business; Scenario analysis; Social change; Retirement age; Pension; Restructuring; Social Welfare; Delphi method

Title: Retirement timing in a future welfare state: a Finnish Delphi study
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: While the experts perceived that a raised state pension age and a removal of early retirement options will inevitably delay retirement on average, multiple scenarios were believed to hinder this trend.
What_was_studied: The study employs the Delphi method by interviewing anonymous experts from a variety of relevant organisations and fields in Finland, then sending them a scaled on-line questionnaire from the initial findings to elicit views on the likelihood of different scenarios influencing retirement timing over the next 20 years.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study suggests that a significant policy challenge in face of upcoming societal trends is to make delayed retirement a more equally viable option. Therefore, policymakers should prioritize strategies that foster equal opportunities for extended careers and retirement planning to address widening socioeconomic inequalities in retirement timing.

Title: FULL EMPLOYMENT AND SOCIAL WELFARE POLICY

What_was_found: The study found that the US official unemployment rate was at 5.9%, above the 16-year low of 5.0% earlier in the year, and that a majority of economists considered this level to be near the natural rate of unemployment, which is associated with labor shortages and higher inflation.
What_was_studied: The US official unemployment rate in November 1990 and its relationship with the natural rate of unemployment, labor shortages, and inflation during an economic recovery.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the relationship between unemployment and inflation, policymakers should prioritize strategies to address labor shortages and prevent inflation from rising too quickly, such as investing in education and training programs to enhance the skill levels of the workforce, or implementing policies that promote the entry of more women and minorities into the labor market.

What_was_studied: This paper investigates the relationship between ethnic diversity, social exclusion, and institutional quality in Pakistan from 1970 to 2015 using autoregressive distributed lags modeling approach.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant negative impact of ethnic diversity and social exclusion on institutional quality, policymakers should prioritize initiatives that promote cohesion and address social exclusion, such as establishing dense social networks and promoting economic growth, to improve Pakistan's institutional quality and reduce poverty.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize funding for support services that help social assistance recipients navigate the complex bureaucracy and capitalize on their creativity to develop effective coping strategies.

What_was_found: The data indicates that young individuals have a strong belief in the government's role as a social support and a mechanism of social welfare for all citizens. Additionally, the results suggest that women place more emphasis on government responsibility than men do, and men emphasize individual responsibility for social issues.
What_was_studied: This study investigates young people's attitudes towards social welfare and their perceptions of who is responsible for providing social welfare benefits, using a sample of 725 students from 12 high and vocational schools in south Finland.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision-makers should prioritize investing in social welfare programs that support young individuals, particularly women, and ensure that these programs are designed to address the root causes of social issues, such as housing insecurity and health disparities.

Field: Social class; Social status; Economics; Empirical evidence; Human capital; Conventional wisdom; Salary; Demographic economics; Social stratification; Income distribution; Economic system

Title: Effects of power, status and class on “who gets what” income

What_was_found: The study found that income inequality is strongly linked to pre-existing social stratification, including class, power, and status differences. Specifically, the research revealed that individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds experience significantly lower wages than those from higher backgrounds, even after controlling for education and other factors.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the relationship between income distribution and social stratification in a given population over a specific time period, using a particular dataset and methodology.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize interventions aimed at reducing social stratification and addressing income inequality, particularly in the education and healthcare sectors. This could include targeted funding for schools serving low-income communities and implementing policies to reduce health disparities.

Field: Ethnic group; Sociology; Order (exchange); Ukrainian; Self-employment; Hidden populations; Public relations; Sample (statistics); Economic growth; Informal sector; Entrepreneurship

Title: Methodological issues in studying hidden populations operating in informal economy
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that these hidden entrepreneurs face unique challenges such as lack of access to financial services, limited legal protections, and vulnerability to exploitation. Additionally, the authors discovered that semi-structured interviews were not effective in capturing the complexities of their experiences due to the sensitivity of the issues.
What_was_studied: The study explores the methodological challenges in investigating hidden populations, specifically Ukrainian illegal self-employed construction workers operating in London, using semi-structured interviews to understand their experiences and limitations of current research methods.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for a more comprehensive approach to studying hidden populations, prioritizing the use of intermediaries and culturally sensitive methods to gain access to these vulnerable groups. Policymakers should scale up support for financial services and legal protections to empower these entrepreneurs and reduce their vulnerability to exploitation.

primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: An algorithm is proposed for diagnosing the level of poverty development and a mechanism has been developed to reduce it due to the development of self-employment of the population.
What_was_studied: The article considers the causes of such a fundamental problem as poverty, analyzing the interdependence of poverty and the development of the digital economy in Russia.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To improve the quality of life of the population of Russia's regions by reducing poverty and increasing employment through self-employment, policymakers should prioritize and fund digital economy development initiatives that support entrepreneurship and skill-building programs for underprivileged communities.

Field: Positive economics; Social status; Sociology; Social reproduction; Social change; Social science; Social mobility; Social transformation; Individual capital; Social capital; Social order
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Young people's explanations and experiences of social exclusion: retrieving Bourdieu's concept of social capital
primary_category: Housing insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that Putnam's concept of social capital is limited in its emphasis on bridging, linking, and bonding, neglecting material, economic, and political factors. Specifically, the research revealed that children and young people from marginalized groups experience higher levels of social exclusion, which can have negative impacts on their well-being.
What_was_studied: The research explored how a group's social capital is related to levels of social exclusion among children and young people, with a focus on gender, ethnicity, age, trust, and community factors in a school-based setting over a one-year period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize the development of social capital through a more comprehensive approach that addresses material, economic, and political factors to counter intersectional poverty and housing insecurity. This can involve scaling up community-based programs that foster trust, linking marginalized groups with resources and opportunities, and revising policies to ensure equitable access to education and employment.

Authors: Benjamin Sunday Uzochukwu; Chinyere Okeke; Joyce Ogwezi; B.O. Emunemu; Felicia Onibon; Bassey Ebenso; Tolib Mirzoev; Ghazala Mir
Field: Social exclusion; Ethnic group; Functional illiteracy; Political science; Vulnerability; Stakeholder; Disadvantage; Humiliation; Economic growth; Sustainable development
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Exploring the drivers of ethnic and religious exclusion from public services in Nigeria: implications for sustainable development goal 10
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the drivers of social exclusion at the macro level include ineffective centralized federal states, competition for resources and power among groups, geographic developmental divides, and socio-cultural/religious issues. At the meso-level, institutional rules and competition for resources, stereotypes and misconceptions, barriers to access and service provision are prevalent. Lastly, at the micro-level, socio-economic status and health-seeking behavior are significant factors.
What_was_studied: This scoping review of literature and stakeholder workshops aimed to identify the key drivers of social exclusion of religious and ethnic minorities in public institutions in Nigeria during a specific time period, with a focus on SDG 10.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To effectively address social exclusion of minority ethnic and religious populations in Nigeria, policymakers must prioritize decentralization, address resource competition and power imbalances, bridge geographic developmental divides, and challenge socio-cultural/religious biases. By doing so, they can reduce illiteracy, increase employment opportunities, improve healthcare services, mitigate social vices, and prevent communal clashes and insurgencies.

Field: Policy analysis; Welfare state; Political economy; Political science; Social policy; Institutionalism; Social Right; Waqf; Solidarity; Social pension
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Between welfare state and (state-organised) charity: How Turkey’s social assistance regime blends two competing policy paradigms
primary_category: Child poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study finds that Turkey's social assistance regime is characterized by two competing policy paradigms: a welfare state paradigm and a state-organized charity paradigm, which have shaped the ambivalent structure and design of the regime. These findings contribute to comparative social policy research and discursive institutionalism by uncovering the historical and ideational foundations of a largely neglected case, social assistance in Turkey.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the ideational roots of Turkey's social assistance regime over the last four decades, using a discursive institutionalist approach and focusing on two central laws: the social pensions law of 1976 and the Law that established the Fund for the Encouragement of Social Cooperation and Solidarity in 1986.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of child poverty and intersectional poverty in Turkey, policymakers should prioritize strengthening the welfare state paradigm to ensure comprehensive coverage of vulnerable populations and revise the state-organized charity paradigm to align with human rights standards.

What_was_found: The social politics theory is a theoretical idea based on observations of how social, political, legal, and economic changes within “Weak” and “Failing” states create an environment conducive to human trafficking for sex and labor purposes as well as other forms of injustices.
What_was_studied: The paper develops a social politics theory to connect concepts from social stratification to the study of human trafficking, drawing on data provided by the US Department of Health and Human Services' Rescue and Restore program for trafficked victims to illustrate how traffickers move victims trans-nationally, and citing sources from Australia and Sweden to show how national laws and policies regarding prostitution can contribute to or discourage human trafficking for sex and labor purposes.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Governments should prioritize addressing intersectional poverty, sustainable development, and education access in.

Field: Welfare; Sociology; Work ethic; Perception; Popularity; Universalism; Moral culture; White (horse); Social psychology; Qualitative property
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The importance of moral culture in questions of welfare deservingness – the case of the US
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The author found that interviewees in both cases defined deserving individuals as those whose neediness is due to factors beyond their control and undeserving individuals as those whose neediness is caused by their own poor work ethic. Furthermore, the author found three so-called context-related criteria that do not fit into the existing deservingness framework: a criterion following a cost-benefit logic, the principle of universalism and a principle based on family obligations.
What_was_studied: The study explored how deservingness theory is applied in the study of American perceptions of deservingness and which criteria Americans use when deciding the deservingness of needy individuals, using qualitative data from two cases: liberal northeastern city of Boston, Massachusetts, and conservative southern city of Knoxville, Tennessee.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings confirm trends in recent deservingness studies indicating that the sensitivity of deservingness theory to the importance of moral culture in the use of both deservingness criteria and context-related criteria must continue to develop, suggesting policymakers should prioritize understanding the role of moral culture in shaping perceptions of deservingness when designing social protection policies.

Title: Post-Soviet informality: towards theory-building
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study reveals that the informal sphere of post-Soviet countries is distinct from other post-socialist regions and requires its own conceptual framework for proper analysis. Specifically, the study shows that the legacy of the Soviet regime and challenges of post-communist transition have created a unique set of informal practices and institutions in these countries.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the informal practices and institutions of post-Soviet countries, using a comprehensive analysis of secondary sources to argue for the concept of 'post-Soviet informality' that encompasses economic, social, and political spheres.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of informality in post-Soviet countries, policymakers should prioritize developing targeted social protection programs that address intersectional poverty and support vulnerable populations, such as women and minorities, who are disproportionately affected by informal practices and institutions.

Field: Racism; Political science; Disadvantage; Unemployment; Face (sociological concept); Policy initiatives; Argument; Demographic economics; Development economics; Immigration

Title: UNEMPLOYMENT AND MINORITY IMMIGRANTS IN CANADA
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that racial minorities face significant employment barriers, with a higher likelihood of being unemployed or underemployed, and experience lower earnings than their white counterparts. For instance, black Canadians were found to have an unemployment rate twice that of white Canadians in 2006.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the labour-market status and experience of racial minorities in Canada from 1981 to 2006, using data from the Census and the Labour Force Survey.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, it is essential to scale up anti-racism initiatives and expand support services for racial minority immigrants. Labour-market policies must prioritize addressing the systemic barriers that prevent these individuals from finding suitable employment.

Title: Socially embedded workers at the nexus of diverse work in Russia: An ethnography of blue‐collar informalization
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that workers with a strongly embedded work-related social identity and characterized by a significant number of weak social ties move with little effort between formal and informal work.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the interdependence of social networks, employment, class identity, and informal work in Russia using extensive ethnographic data from the Russian provinces over a year-long fieldwork period (2009-2010).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Russian policymakers should prioritize the development of formal employment opportunities that align with these workers' social identities and provide incentives for them to transition into formal employment, as this could lead to a significant increase in productivity and economic growth.

Field: Public economics; Welfare state; Ambivalence; Economics; Variables; Social rights; Cash; Unemployment; Receipt; Generosity
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social expenditure, social rights, and benefit receipt as indicators of welfare state generosity: Three peas in a pod, or a different kettle of fish altogether?
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that higher levels of social expenditure were positively associated with more generous social rights and higher levels of benefit receipt. Additionally, the study revealed an ambivalent relation between benefit access and benefit levels within indicators as well as across them, suggesting competing policy choices in European welfare states.
What_was_studied: Using time series cross-sectional analysis of unemployment cash benefits data from 16 European countries between 2003 and 2011, this study investigates how three indicators of welfare state generosity (aggregated social expenditure, social rights, and social benefit receipt) relate to each other.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study's findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize social expenditure and social rights to increase the generosity of their welfare states. Additionally, they should consider the ambivalent relation between benefit access and benefit levels when designing policies to ensure that benefits are both accessible and adequate.

What_was_found: The results point to different types of informal street selling, which are mainly executed by illegal migrants as a survival strategy. The case illustrates the interrelations between the formal, informal and criminal economy.
What_was_studied: The purpose of this paper is to gain insight into the organisation of informal street selling in the capital of Belgium, its association with formal and illegal selling and the perceptions, choices and decisions of the sellers during a specific time period (not mentioned) using qualitative research methods (case study, interviews, observations, document analyses) on a specific population (illegal migrants as a survival strategy) with no mention of sample size.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale and expand funding for social safety nets and prioritize policies that neutralise informal selling as a better alternative to stealing or committing crimes which inflict physical harm and feelings of insecurity.

What_was_found: The results suggest that involvement in parental roles has a moderating influence on unemployment mental health outcomes among both men and women, although it has a higher effect on the female workforce. Moreover, the study shows that “not living far from the family of origin” could be considered a crucial moderating factor for both gender categories.
What_was_studied: Using the European Health Interview Survey data for 2015, the authors adopt linear regression models to evaluate the effect of family settings on the mental health outcomes of unemployment, in particular on the likelihood of developing depression.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize programs and services that support families and address the gender gap in occupation, particularly those that promote parental involvement and geographic proximity to family origins. These interventions can help mitigate the negative mental health effects of unemployment on individuals and their households.

What_was_found: The main empirical finding was a range of quantitative results detailing the impact of unemployment on individuals, families, and societies during this period, as documented in reviews by Eisenberg and Lazarsfeld (1938) and Garraty (1978).
What_was_studied: The research scope was social and psychological research on unemployment in the 1930s, with data from continental Europe and English-speaking countries like Britain and the United States.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision-makers should prioritize evidence-based policies to address the root causes of unemployment and support individuals and families affected by job loss, especially in regions with high rates of interwar unemployment.

Field: Political science; State (polity); Elder care; Asian country; Care provision; South asia; Development economics; Social stratification; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Shifting boundaries of care in Asia: an introduction
primary_category: Asset poverty; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that there have been significant changes in care policies and practices in Asian countries over the past few decades, with a trend towards more market-based and community-based care provision, but also with persisting state and family-based support. The findings suggest that these changes are linked to social stratification by class and gender in Asia.
What_was_studied: This special issue examines recent policy and practice changes in care for the elderly and young children in different regions of Asia, with a focus on complicated boundary shifts in care provision and financing between the state, market, community, and family in East, Southeast, and South Asia.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings highlight the need for policymakers to prioritize and expand access to affordable, high-quality care services for all populations, particularly disadvantaged groups such as low-income families and women. Policymakers should scale up support for community-based care initiatives and invest in data collection and monitoring systems to better understand the evolving care landscape in Asia.

Field: Neoclassical economics; Economics; Optimism; Unemployment; Capitalism; Full employment; Feature (computer vision); Economic system

Title: CHANGING CONCEPTS OF FULL EMPLOYMENT: DIVERGENT CONCEPTS, DIVERGENT GOALS
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The research found that substantial unemployment has become commonplace in most Western industrial nations, erasing the optimism that pervaded the early post-World War II era. The study also discovered that full employment is not a permanent feature of Western economies, as it was believed to be.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed employment data from Western industrial nations over the past few decades to investigate whether capitalism has solved the problem of unemployment, using a combination of time series and cross-sectional methods on a population of approximately 20 countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize addressing unemployment and poverty issues in their countries, particularly among gender groups. They should also consider revising their policies and strategies to ensure full employment and eradicate poverty, rather than relying solely on the belief that capitalism has solved these problems.
