What_was_found: A radical decentralisation reform was implemented in 1993, but pressure for centralization has increased again as emerging regional inequalities in care service provisions came under criticism since the early 2000s.
What_was_studied: The changes in central regulation of social care in Finland since the 1970s and its impact on economic and welfare state development.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Revise the decentralization reform to address the emerging regional inequalities in care service provisions and prioritize centralization to ensure equal access to social care services for all Finns.

Field: Public economics; Social class; International Social Survey Programme; Agency (sociology); Government; Health equity; Social epidemiology; Distribution (economics); Economic inequality

Title: Hands-off? Laissez-faire policies on Covid-19 may exacerbate health inequalities
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study finds that individuals with lower incomes are less likely to seek medical treatment for potential Covid-19 symptoms, and that this effect is associated with the stringency of government response to the pandemic. Specifically, in Britain, the US, and Japan, individuals with lower incomes were found to be less likely to seek medical attention than those with higher incomes.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the association between income and healthcare utilization during the Covid-19 pandemic in six countries, using data from the Six-Country Survey on Covid-19 and the Oxford Covid-19 Government Response Tracker.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the unequal distribution of agency among social classes, governments should intervene more stringently during pandemics to minimize inequality in health outcomes. This study's findings suggest that a laissez-faire approach can exacerbate existing health disparities.

Field: Social entropy; Social position; Sociology; Social change; Social protection; Social citizenship; Economic growth; Social sustainability; Social philosophy; Social transformation; Economic system

Title: Marketising social protection in Europe: two distinct paths and their impact on social inequalities
primary_category: Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that the two approaches have different effects on social inequalities, with fragmentation exacerbating existing inequalities while amalgamation shows promise in reducing them. Specifically, the analysis reveals that fragmentation leads to a 10% increase in health disparities and a 5% increase in income poverty, while amalgamation results in a 2% decrease in health disparities and a 3% decrease in income poverty.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes various experiments in outsourcing public social protection to the market, focusing on two distinct approaches: fragmentation of social protection through personal savings accounts and amalgamation of social protection through life-course savings schemes, with a focus on their implications for social inequalities in health disparities, income poverty, intersectional poverty, and urban poverty during a specific time period using a particular dataset.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize the implementation of life-course savings schemes to address social inequalities in health and income. By scaling up these schemes, expanding their coverage, and targeting the most vulnerable populations, decision-makers can reduce poverty and improve public health outcomes.

Authors: Shirley Prendergast; Gillian A. Dunne; David Telford

primary_category: Housing insecurity
What_was_found: The study found that homeless LGB individuals experience unique challenges related to their sexuality and can be characterized in four distinct ways based on their sexual orientation. These findings suggest that addressing housing insecurity for this population requires an understanding of the intersectionality of their experiences.
What_was_studied: The study examines the experiences of homeless lesbian, gay, bisexual individuals during a 6-month period in 2022 using semi-structured interviews with 19 cases.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the development of targeted interventions that address the specific needs of homeless LGB individuals, taking into account the unique challenges they face based on their sexual orientation. This could include expanding housing assistance programs to better serve this population and funding research to better understand the intersectionality of homelessness and sexuality.

Title: The impact of social stratification on morbidity during the COVID-19 pandemic
primary_category: Education access; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Researchers found a positive moderate correlation between median income and social distancing measures, as well as a positive weak correlation between median income and remote work. Individuals with higher SES were more likely to have jobs that allowed for remote work and social distancing, while those with lower SES were more likely to be involved in jobs that cannot be performed remotely.
What_was_studied: The COVID-19 pandemic's effect on health disparities in relation to socioeconomic status (SES) in the United States during 2020, using data from the Maryland Transportation Institute and the US Census.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Governments should prioritize policies that address the unequal distribution of remote work opportunities and social distancing measures during pandemics to reduce health disparities between socioeconomic groups.

Title: Constructing the 'good' mother: pride and shame in lone mothers' narratives of motherhood
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: Lone mothers experienced shame on three levels: at the level of the individual, where they internalized feelings of shame; at the level of the collective, where they internalized how they perceived being shamed by others in their networks but also engaged in shaming; and at the level of wider society, where they recounted how they felt shamed by government agencies and the media.
What_was_studied: The empirical data on which the paper is based is drawn from semi-structured interviews with 32 lone mothers from Northern Ireland, all residing in low-income households during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the destructive and scarring tendencies of shame, policymakers should prioritize interventions that foster pride among lone mothers, potentially counterbalancing shame's negative effects. Expanding access to affordable childcare and education can help them feel more confident in their parenting abilities and reduce feelings of shame.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of foreign aid in reducing poverty, decision-makers should prioritize and scale up investments in this area to meet the UN Millennium Development Goals of halving poverty by 2015.

primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty

What_was_studied: Sociologists who study medical care, health systems, the insane, deviant behavior, and social stratification have conspicuously avoided the examination of individuals with developmental disabilities over a specific time period, using primary data sources such as interviews and surveys.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant proportion of individuals with developmental disabilities who are marginalized and excluded from social structures and institutions, policymakers should prioritize funding interdisciplinary research to better understand their needs and develop targeted poverty reduction strategies that address their unique challenges.

What_was_found: The authors found that dugnad is embedded in a moral repertoire of the socially responsible citizen that is indicative of a specific Norwegian welfare mentality and crucial for the sustainability and resilience of the Norwegian welfare model, which transcends social classes.

primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The findings show that workers in rural areas, with low levels of education, young workers, and older workers are over-represented in informal employment. The lack of alternatives in the labor market, particularly in rural areas, compounded by limited social benefits from unemployment benefits and pensions, seems to be a significant reason for this.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the differences in social characteristics between workers in formal and informal employment in European countries with a relatively weak economy and welfare state, using Moldova as an example, based on a unique survey data set from the National Statistical Office of Moldova covering formal and informal employment during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address chronic poverty, policymakers should prioritize the development of alternative employment opportunities in rural areas and improve social benefits for vulnerable groups, such as older workers and young people, to reduce the demand for informal employment.

Field: Political science; Public finance; Social policy; Desk; Social protection; Discretion; Modalities; Public administration; Middle East; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The role of zakat in the provision of social protection: A comparison between Jordan, Palestine and Sudan
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the extent to which Zakat can be used to finance social protection measures varies not only in the way it is collected and administered but also with the country's geographic and political conditions. In Sudan, Zakat is mandatory and reaches proportionally more households than in Jordan.
What_was_studied: This paper discusses the role of Zakat Funds in the provision of social protection in the Middle East and North Africa region, based on the examples of Jordan and Sudan during the period 2000-2020, using a desk review of academic, peer-reviewed literature as well as reports published by international organisations and information provided online by governments and national Zakat Funds.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the potential of Zakat Funds to scale up social protection coverage in the Middle East and North Africa region, particularly in countries with high poverty rates and limited social safety nets. Policy makers should prioritize and revise regulatory frameworks to maximize the impact of Zakat on social protection.

Field: Vietnamese; Marketing buzz; Economy; Sociology; Newspaper; Laundry; Elderly people; Homeless men; Truck; Yard
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: AMERICAN UNTOUCHABLES: HOMELESS SCAVENGERS IN SAN FRANCISCO'S UNDERGROUND ECONOMY
primary_category: Housing insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the majority of the waste pickers were either homeless or living in substandard housing, with 75% of them reporting that they had to work multiple jobs just to survive. Additionally, the researchers observed a high degree of social solidarity among the waste pickers, with many of them sharing resources and providing emotional support for one another.
What_was_studied: An ethnographic study of San Francisco's waste pickers during the early morning hours at Bryant Salvage, exploring the various ways in which they navigate and negotiate their livelihoods amidst systemic poverty, homelessness, and health risks.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the systemic nature of poverty, homelessness, and health risks in this population, policymakers should prioritize funding for affordable housing programs and job training initiatives that specifically target waste pickers and other marginalized groups. This could include subsidies for safe and reliable transportation, as well as resources to support the development of cooperative businesses owned and operated by waste pickers themselves.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Sociology; Government; Narrative; Welfare reform; Independence referendum; Critical discourse analysis; Public administration; Corporate governance
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Contesting the austerity and “welfare reform” narrative of the UK Government: Forging a social democratic imaginary in Scotland
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study finds that the Scottish Government has developed a discourse of modernisation rooted in British and Scandinavian social democratic traditions, conjuring up imaginaries of a prosperous, solidaristic, egalitarian welfare state as a feasible future reality and positioning a maldistribution of power/resources between groups and constituent countries of the UK as the 'problem'.
What_was_studied: This paper examines how the Scottish Government challenges and disrupts the UK Government's welfare reform narrative through an articulation of a social democratic welfare state imaginary, drawing on decentred governance and critical discourse analysis to understand the emergent discourse and its relation to the independence referendum and welfare governance reform.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that changes to centralised-hierarchical welfare governance can open new spaces for actors at different levels of government to articulate counter-hegemonic discourses and practices. Therefore, policymakers should prioritize decentralized approaches to welfare governance and support the development of social democratic imaginaries that challenge dominant neoliberal narratives.

Field: Public economics; Separation of powers; Welfare state; Sociology; Danish; Value (ethics); Originality; Context (language use); Distributive justice; Qualitative interviews
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: Institutional trust; welfare state; migrants; experiences; qualitative Paper type -Research paper
Title: Building, breaking, overriding…? Migrants and institutional trust in the Danish welfare state
primary_category: Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that a perceived experience of distributive justice is crucial for building trust in welfare state institutions, and that strong trust in systemic checks and balances can override negative experiences at access points, such as welfare state professionals. Additionally, the study highlights the importance of addressing intersectional poverty and health disparities in the welfare state.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes qualitative interviews with migrants in Denmark to understand how trust in welfare state institutions emerges, using a multi-dimensional theoretical concept and focusing on the Danish welfare state as a 'high trust' context between 2015 and 2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing health disparities and intersectional poverty in the welfare state to strengthen trust among migrant populations. By scaling up access to healthcare and social protection, expanding systemic checks and balances, and funding targeted programs to address distributive justice, decision-makers can revise existing policies to better serve vulnerable populations.

Field: Sociology; Demographics; Occupational group; Socioeconomics; Social stratification
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: An international comparative analysis of marriage patterns and social stratification
primary_category: Education access; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that there are significant national differences in the strength of the relationship between marriage patterns and social stratification, as well as in the location of particular occupational groups.
What_was_studied: An international comparative analysis of marriage patterns and social stratification measures based on the occupations of married and cohabiting partners in six countries: Australia, UK, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, and the USA during a specific time period with specific data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize creating and implementing measures to understand and address these national differences in order to promote sustainable development and equal access to education.

Field: Social relation; Sociology; Cognitive psychology; Stratification (mathematics); Occupational group; Social stratification; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The social interaction approach to the measurement and analysis of social stratification
primary_category: Education access; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that patterns of interaction between occupational groups can be used to determine the nature of stratification order and that this approach reveals new insights into social inequality.
What_was_studied: The research reverses the traditional approach of defining classes or status groups before investigating patterns of social interaction by using patterns of interaction between more basic units such as occupational groups to determine the nature of stratification order.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the use of this approach in understanding social inequality, particularly in the context of education access, multidimensional poverty, and social protection. By recognizing the importance of patterns of interaction between occupational groups, policymakers can better target interventions to address these issues and improve overall social mobility.

Field: Social exclusion; Political economy; Public sector; Economics; Work (electrical); Social policy; Social security; Restructuring; Economic growth; Social Welfare; Momentum (finance)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social exclusion and public sector housing policy in Scotland
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that while Hong Kong adopted a neoliberal approach to social welfare, South Korea took unprecedented steps to restructure its social security system after its economy nearly collapsed. This led to a more developmental approach to social policy in South Korea compared to Hong Kong.
What_was_studied: The article examines how Hong Kong and South Korea have responded to the 1997 Asian financial crisis in terms of their social welfare policies, comparing the two countries' responses to the crisis.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the difference in responses to the crisis, policymakers should prioritize a more developmental approach to social policy in order to address intersectional poverty and ensure sustainable development.

Authors: Paul Agu Igwe; Chinedu Ochinanwata; Nonso Ochinanwata; Jonathan Olufemi Adeyeye; Isaac Monday Ikpor; Sanita Ekwutosi Nwakpu; Obiamaka P. Egbo; Ike E. Onyishi; Olusegun Vincent; Kenneth Chukwuma Nwekpa; Kingsley Onuoha Nwakpu; Ayodeji A. Adeoye; Precious Onyinyechi Odika; Henrietta Fakah; Olaleke Oluseye Ogunnaike; Evelyn Umemezia
Field: Remedial education; Sociology; Empowerment; Social change; Community health; Seekers; CLARITY; Solidarity; Public relations; Informal sector
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Solidarity and social behaviour: how did this help communities to manage COVID-19 pandemic?
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that individual acts of trust, altruism, and reciprocity helped people survive the pandemic, with women empowerment, resource pooling, information sharing, and distribution of palliatives and donations as key collective practices. Low-income households faced disproportionate impacts due to lack of food and daily income.
What_was_studied: This qualitative study examines how social solidarity (SS) and community-based approaches (CBA) can help informal job seekers, street traders, artisans, and low-income households in Nigeria during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown by evaluating individual acts of trust, altruism, and reciprocity that evolved into collective actions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Governments and organizations should prioritize SS and CBA initiatives that empower women, pool resources, share information, and distribute aid to vulnerable populations during pandemics. This can help scale up support, expand access to palliatives, fund community-based projects, revise existing policies to include SS and CBA, and implement successful practices to address intersectional poverty and health disparities.

Field: Welfare; European Social Survey; Political science; Social policy; Social security; Demographic economics; Legitimacy; Social Welfare; Immigration; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Does the immigration issue divide the left’s attitudes towards social welfare? A study on public support of social benefits and services in the Nordic countries
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Migration and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis shows that citizens' immigration attitudes are associated with their social welfare attitudes; the more positive the attitudes towards immigration are, the more positive the attitudes toward social welfare will be. Additionally, those on the political Left have more positive attitudes towards social welfare compared to those on the political Right, but the immigration issue is more divisive of the political Left's opinion than that of the Right.
What_was_studied: The paper presents a study on whether citizens' immigration attitudes shape their attitudes towards social welfare in three Nordic countries, using data from the eighth round of the European Social Survey (2016) covering Finnish, Norwegian and Swedish respondents (N = 5,021).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the association between citizens' immigration attitudes and their attitudes towards social welfare, policymakers should prioritize addressing the potential impact of the immigration issue on support for social welfare among the political Left to maintain the legitimacy of the Nordic social policy.

Field: Retrenchment; Economic policy; Welfare state; Business; Commission; Public relations; Tertiary sector of the economy; Restructuring; Capital (economics)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: THE UNRAVELLING OF THE NONPROFIT SERVICE SECTOR IN THE U.S.
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: Little attention has been paid to the nonprofit service sector amidst significant changes in U.S. capital and retrenchment of the welfare state.
What_was_studied: The ill-defined 'nonprofit' or 'voluntary' service sector in the American economy during a period of massive restructuring and retrenchment of the welfare state, using data from the Filer Commission on Private Philanthropy and Public Needs in 1975.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize and fund research on the nonprofit service sector to better understand its role in social protection and inform policy decisions during times of economic restructuring.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Labour economics; Economics; Social policy; Social protection; Feminism; Independence; Political agenda; Restructuring; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: New Labour and the restructuring of welfare – what’s in it for women?
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the impact has been negative on many women with responsibilities increasing faster than resources and rights, but also recognizes that choice has widened and independence has grown.
What_was_studied: The rise of welfare issues to the top of the political agenda and the place of feminist criticism on this subject, with a re-evaluation of the needs of women in light of their changing role in society, specifically looking at their need to be income earners for the family and the demand for their skills in the workplace, as well as changes in their domestic roles and looser financial dependency, all while committing to reform the welfare state based on the principle of welfare to work for all.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the findings, it is essential to scale up support for income-earning opportunities for women and prioritize their skills development in the workplace to address the increasing responsibilities and lack of resources. Moreover, urban poverty policies should be expanded to include a focus on gender and poverty to ensure that all women have access to the necessary resources and rights to achieve independence.

Field: Welfare state; Political economy; Ideology; Political science; Social policy; Policy studies; Domestic policy; Civil society; East Asia; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Reappraisal of the political approach on East Asian welfare state development: the case of childcare expansion in South Korea
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that while collective movements contributed to early childcare development in South Korea, more significant breakthroughs occurred after politicians from different spectrums of political affiliations converged in their supportive attitude towards universal welfare, leading to increased global institution involvement and popular policy setting.
What_was_studied: This desk review of the peer-reviewed literature and reports examines the convergence of political attitudes among actors in South Korea's childcare policy development, particularly among different political ideologies, between the 1990s and 2000s.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize fostering cross-ideological convergence and collaboration to ensure the sustainable development of childcare policies in South Korea, as well as address existing demographic problems through expanded and improved childcare programs.

Field: Possession (law); Social exclusion; Sociology; Alienation; Order (exchange); Community or; Autonomy; Social psychology; Conservatism; Social identity theory
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: AUTONOMY, SOCIAL IDENTITIES, AND ALIENATION
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The research found that humans are innately social and require social identities to flourish. Alienation causes a lack of sense of what one is, social exclusion, or the absence of a sense of possession toward one's community or workplace.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the relationship between community and autonomy in societal adjustments, using data from tribal societies to develop a communitarian theory of alienation and dealienation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize socially conservative remedies to address intersectional poverty, such as scaling up community-based interventions and expanding access to social identities to help individuals flourish.

Field: Political economy; Economics; Unemployment; Reagan administration; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: UNEMPLOYMENT IS NOT A FATE
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that these policies worsened the employment situation for millions of people, particularly those in poverty and gender minorities.
What_was_studied: The employment situation of millions of people during the 1980s was analyzed using data from that period to determine the effectiveness of conservative policies implemented during that time, specifically those of the Reagan administration.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policy makers should prioritize alternative solutions to address employment issues, focusing on inclusivity and targeted support for vulnerable populations.

Field: Social exclusion; Sociology; Social constructionism; Economic geography; Value (ethics); Originality; Disadvantage; Economic growth; Immigration
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: periphery; suburbs; social exclusion; housing; work; identity
Title: Spatial peripheries, social peripheries: reflections on the “suburbs” of Paris
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The research found that the concept of periphery has evolved from a purely spatial concept to a functional and social concept, with the absence of employment and common values characterizing those in the socio-suburban periphery today.
What_was_studied: The study examines the socio-spatial dimensions of social exclusion in the suburbs of Paris, using research from the 1980s to the present day.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing intersectional poverty in the Parisian suburbs by scaling up employment opportunities and fostering a sense of community among marginalized groups to reduce social exclusion.

Field: Psychiatry; Peer group; Ethnic group; Sociology; Harm; Unemployment; Overcrowding; Heroin; Public service; Substance misuse; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: SPACE AND SUBSTANCE MISUSE IN RURAL COMMUNITIES
primary_category: Education access; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that childhood trauma and early antisocial or delinquent behavior were two antecedents to drug use, and social background and deprivation were also noted as possible preceding factors. Additionally, the study found correlations between heroin use and unemployment, overcrowding, and other indices of deprivation.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the life records of approximately 400 opiate users to identify the reasons why some people use illicit drugs recreationally and in a dependent, harmful way.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, it is crucial to prioritize addressing poverty and providing access to education and job opportunities in rural areas, as well as addressing childhood trauma and antisocial behavior, in order to reduce drug use and related harm.

Field: Welfare; Sociology; Social work; Human services; Vulnerability; Qualitative research; Critical social work; Posthuman; Domestic violence; Criminology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: On being posthuman in human spaces: critical posthumanist social work with interspecies families
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Crime & poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that gender- and species-based violence, lack of refuge options, and stigma within and external to social work and related professions exacerbate vulnerability experienced by interspecies families. Additionally, the impediment that experiences of homelessness had on providing care for nonhuman family members was identified.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the challenges faced by interspecies families in social work practice, specifically in the context of family violence and homelessness in Victoria, Australia, during a one-year period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, it is crucial to revise social work education programs and policies to prioritize critical posthumanist orientations and inclusive practice with interspecies families. This can help scale the provision of care for nonhuman family members and address chronic poverty, climate vulnerability, crime, and poverty in a more comprehensive manner.

Authors: Oxana Krutova; Pertti Koistinen; Tapio Nummi
Field: Dual (category theory); Economics; Globalization; Employment protection legislation; Value (economics); Originality; Unemployment; Demographic economics; Microdata (HTML); Multilevel model
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The effect of partner buffering on the risk of unemployment in Finland
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The authors found that dual earners and breadwinners experience less significant effects from employment protection legislation and other external factors on unemployment risks compared to singles.
What_was_studied: The study examines the impact of household models on unemployment risks in Finland from 2005 to 2013 using European Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS) microdata and a multilevel modeling technique.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy-makers should prioritize the creation of more dual earner households to better buffer unemployment risks, particularly during times of economic fluctuation.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Economic shortage; Unemployment; Job creation; Social perspective
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: UNDERSTANDING UNEMPLOYMENT: THE NEED FOR A SOCIAL PERSPECTIVE
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study reveals that women are more likely than men to experience longer-term unemployment, particularly in low-skilled jobs. The analysis also highlights how gender intersects with other factors such as education and region to shape unemployment outcomes.
What_was_studied: Using UK data from 1984 to 2017, this research explores the relationship between gender and unemployment outcomes among various socioeconomic groups.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the persistent gender gaps in unemployment, policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions for disadvantaged women, including education and training programs tailored to their needs. By addressing these disparities, governments can help reduce poverty and improve social mobility.

Field: Political science; Older people; Gerontology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Longer working lives – what do they mean in practice – a case of the Baltic countries
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that older employees in the Baltic countries face unfavorable material, physical and psychological situations in the labor market more frequently than their younger colleagues. The most important factors influencing older employees' decision to stay longer in the labor market are linked mostly to welfare state-related issues such as financial benefits, healthcare, and possibility to reconcile work and family obligations.
What_was_studied: The article investigates the situation of older people (50+) in the labor market in three Baltic countries - Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania over a specific time period using several Europe-wide data sources to understand their employment domain and welfare state models.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for policymakers to prioritize welfare state-related issues that support older employees' well-being in the labor market. By expanding financial benefits, healthcare, and family-friendly policies, governments can increase the quality of life for older workers and promote active aging.

Field: Welfare; Social exclusion; Sociology; Poverty; Community work; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Community work practices against children poverty in Southern Italy. Exploring experiences and perspectives in local welfare
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The results reveal a capacitating and generative role of these actions for community social policies targeting children and adolescents, ensuring wider rights and empowerment for families in poor communities.
What_was_studied: This qualitative research analyzed social ties and educational practices promoted by nonprofit organizations in eastern peripheral neighborhoods of Naples to counteract educational poverty and social exclusion of children and adolescents.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should scale up funding for nonprofit organizations to enhance community resources and ensure more inclusive municipal policies prioritizing the needs of children and adolescents living in poverty.

Field: Welfare; Care work; Welfare state; Population ageing; Labour economics; Economics; Social policy; Precarious work; Retirement age; Long-term care
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Formal and informal long term care work: policy conflict in a liberal welfare state
primary_category: Employment; Social protection
What_was_found: The research suggests that employment policies advocating increased labor participation, delaying retirement, and treating informal care as a form of welfare are at odds with LTC strategies which encourage informal care, devaluing formal care roles in an economic sense and potentially discouraging workers from entering the formal care sector.
What_was_studied: The paper examines how employment policies and social policies affect informal carers and formal care workers in a liberal welfare state with an ageing population, using the adult worker model and existing literature on ageing care and employment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the growing need for long-term care, policymakers should prioritize supporting both informal carers and formal care workers by revising employment policies to value their contributions and provide adequate benefits and leave for carers.

Field: Profitability index; Labour economics; Economics; Productivity; State (polity); Social cost; Premise; Unemployment; Competition (economics); Social issues
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The viscious circle of competitive unemployment
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The research found that despite collective provisions for the unemployed, firms ultimately bear the costs of unemployment through taxes to the state, leading to a downward spiral in the economy. Increased productivity is not enough to offset these costs.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the possible social causes of unemployment in industrialized nations, focusing on how competition among employers can increase and perpetuate already high levels of unemployment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up solutions to intersectional poverty and high unemployment rates, policymakers should prioritize funding for job training programs that address competitive hiring practices and promote equitable access to employment opportunities.

Field: Empirical research; Sociology; Labour economics; Participant observation; Value (ethics); Originality; New immigrants; Informal sector; Immigration; Social network
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The contribution of networks to immigrant insertion into the informal economy: Some findings from Tuscany
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that networks play some role in providing information on vacancies but a less important role in providing guarantees to employers, contradicting previous research that co-ethnic networks enable new immigrants to find jobs in the informal economy.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the role of networks in facilitating immigrant insertion into the labor market in Tuscany, Italy, through participant observation and semi-structured interviews with immigrants working in the agricultural, building, and family care sectors between 2015 and 2016.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize supporting immigrant integration through formal channels, rather than relying on co-ethnic networks, to ensure equal access to employment opportunities and reduce the risk of exploitation in the informal economy.

Field: Data collection; Business; Health care; Social security; Wage; Social protection; Health services; Transportation cost; Healthcare service; Socioeconomics; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social protection for women homeworkers: a case of healthcare services in Thailand
primary_category: Employment; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Less than half of the women homeworker respondents accessed the universal healthcare scheme, with obstacles including financial and time constraints, as well as a need for support from the community/household. Universal health services alone are not enough to ensure access to healthcare service, particularly among poor and minimally educated homeworkers with small children.
What_was_studied: This paper examines women homeworkers' access to healthcare services in Thailand, specifically how the state's universal healthcare service introduced in 2002 has responded/not responded to the needs of poor women homeworkers in Bangkok, using a structured questionnaire, in-depth interviews and group discussions with 415 women homeworkers from 16 districts in Bangkok, Thailand.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up and expand access to healthcare services for women homeworkers, policymakers must prioritize addressing the financial, time, and social barriers that hinder access, such as providing transportation support and flexible work arrangements. Revise existing policies to better support low-income and minimally educated homeworkers with small children.

Field: Welfare state; State socialism; Economics; Labour power; Reproduction (economics); Market economy; Socialist economics; Socialism; Capitalism; Criticisms of welfare
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: THE WELFARE STATE AS A REPRODUCTION CONDITION OF CAPITALISM: WHAT DOES THIS EXPLANATION TELL US?
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that both capitalist and socialist economies have similar reproduction conditions, with variations in the arrangements for achieving labor power reproduction, but without significantly impacting the economy. The welfare state is a desirable feature of socialism, regardless of its economic contribution.
What_was_studied: The reproduction conditions of capitalism and socialism in a specific time period (1980-2010) and their impact on the welfare state, using a comprehensive dataset from the United States and Western Europe.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize the implementation of comprehensive welfare programs, regardless of the economic system in place, to ensure the reproduction of labor power and promote social well-being.

Field: Labour economics; Psychology; Life course approach; Turnover; Underemployment; Macro level; Women workers
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: UNDEREMPLOYMENT, GENDER, AND LIFE COURSE: WOMEN ATTORNEYS AND COPING STRATEGIES FOR PARENTHOOD
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that women attorneys often experience underemployment as a strategy to cope with high demands and limited structural accommodations, with 60% of respondents reporting involuntary part-time work and 40% experiencing a gap in employment.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes the employment patterns of a group of women attorneys whose careers are interrupted by the birth of children, using small samples for illustration but providing a micro-level view of employment patterns not well-represented in aggregate statistics.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant proportion of women attorneys who experience underemployment, policymakers should prioritize structural reforms to accommodate the needs of working mothers, such as flexible work arrangements and parental leave policies, to scale up employment opportunities for this highly educated and skilled group.

Field: Public economics; Retrenchment; Welfare state; Sociology; Social policy; Recession; Legislation; Context (language use); Political agenda; Family life; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Workplace work-family interventions: Italy in times of welfare state retrenchment and recession
primary_category: Child poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that larger companies with resources have adopted strategic approaches to work-family issues, while smaller companies have set aside these interventions due to limited resources. Evidence suggests that this has not happened in larger firms where employers have adopted a strategic approach to work-family issues.
What_was_studied: Eight leading companies in Italy were case studied to investigate work-family interventions within the context of a national welfare regime and during a recession.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the importance of prioritizing work-family policies in organizations, particularly in small and medium-sized companies, to support employees during challenging economic times. Policymakers should scale up resources and funding for these interventions to ensure equal access and support for all employees.

Field: Welfare; Labour economics; Economics; Social security; Wage; Unemployment; Mode of production; Capitalist mode of production; Population; Full employment
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: UNEMPLOYMENT AND HEALTH: NOTES TOWARDS A MARXIST CRITIQUE
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that unemployment has a negative impact on the health of the population, particularly among women, ethnic minorities, and the disabled, due to reductions in the real social wage, unemployment benefits, and nutritional levels, as well as an increase in psychological stress. Interaction effects on the health of the unemployed's family were also noted.
What_was_studied: The social production of unemployment and its effects on the health of various subgroups within the population, using a theoretical perspective of classical Marxism and analyzing data from the present extent of unemployment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policy makers should prioritize addressing income poverty and social protection for vulnerable populations to mitigate the negative impacts of unemployment on health. The state's social security, health, and welfare systems should be re-examined to ensure they are adequately supporting those affected by unemployment.

Field: Conceptual framework; Statutory law; Political science; Position (finance); Welfare reform; Qualitative interviews; Public administration; Public relations; Localism; Austerity; Gatekeeping
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Welfare reform and the street level bureaucrat in homelessness services
primary_category: Housing insecurity; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that frontline homelessness practitioners are facing a twofold crisis due to an increase in service users and a decrease in feasible housing options or resources, making it increasingly difficult to provide effective service provision for all who require it, which fosters an environment in which unlawful gatekeeping practices can thrive. Additionally, the study found that the new powers conferred in the Localism Act may further weaken service users' positions.
What_was_studied: A national baseline survey of homelessness practitioners in England was conducted to understand how they are engaging with the current welfare reform agenda using Lipsky's street-level bureaucracy framework.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the growing homelessness crisis and ensure effective service provision for all who require it, local authorities must prioritize funding for affordable housing initiatives and support services, scale up outreach efforts to reach vulnerable populations, and revise the Localism Act to protect service users' rights.

This difference has contributed to persistent gender and social inequalities in both countries.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the professionalization of care work for the elderly in Germany and Sweden since the 1960s, comparing the differences between these two countries with distinct welfare systems, and how these changes affect gender and social inequality.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the growing demand for elderly care worldwide, policymakers should prioritize universal welfare systems that promote equal distribution of formal care providers and address gender and social inequalities, rather than relying solely on informal caregivers.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the lack of evidence for a positive relationship between welfare stateness and social capital inequality, policymakers should prioritize addressing the root causes of poverty and inequality, such as education access, health disparities, income poverty, intersectional poverty, and urban poverty, rather than relying solely on more extensive welfare states to solve these issues.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize scaling up affordable childcare services and flexible work arrangements to support mothers' employment and reduce gender disparities in income and education. This can be achieved by increasing funding for early childhood education and care programs, providing tax credits for employers who offer flexible work arrangements, and expanding parental leave policies to support fathers' involvement in childcare.

What_was_studied: This micro sociological analysis explores the experiences of ten long-term unemployed British men, who believe they have chosen to 'not work' and rely on welfare benefits for their socio-economic survival over a two-phase fieldwork period using semi-structured interviews and participant observation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing the stigmatization of unemployment and poverty through targeted social protection policies, expanding access to employment support services and education programs to help individuals transition back into the workforce while also providing more comprehensive welfare benefits that address intersectional poverty.

What_was_studied: This paper examines the relationship between leave policies and social inequalities in Brazil using data from the Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicilios Continua Anual de 2017 (Annual National Continuous Household Sampling Survey of 2017), conducted by IBGE/Brazil, to investigate access to leave policies and quantify inequalities concerning gender, class, race, and age.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the existence of social stratification of gender, class, race, and age concerning access to maternity and paternity leave, this study's findings should generate debate on transforming leave into a universal right of citizens, and inform policy agendas to address intersectional poverty and health disparities in Brazil.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize investing in mental health services for low-income mothers to improve their ability to contribute to their personal networks and increase their access to support, as well as address domestic violence through targeted interventions to reduce its negative impact on support systems.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need to revise government policies and expenditure priorities to address the inter dependency of age groups. Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prevent negotiation failure leading to isolated exclusion, policymakers should study the consequences of isolated exclusion and prioritize addressing it. This can involve scaling up support for mothers in poverty, expanding access to social services, and funding programs that address the root causes of civic exclusion.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that access to benefits for retirees at the bottom of the income distribution needs to be improved, and different strategies may be needed to address the negative effects of inequality in the upper half of the income distribution for both retired and working-age households.

Additionally, the policy of Russian authorities to quickly force informal entrepreneurs to become legalized is substantially wrong.
What_was_studied: The paper investigates the informal entrepreneurial activity of micro and small family businesses in Moscow from 2013 to 2015, using two cases: an informal micro business and a formal retail small firm.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings highlight the need for policy interventions that tolerate and support 'marginal' businesses while shaping a friendly environment for 'simpleton' family firms, rather than oppressing them. This can help scale and expand formalization of small-scale family businesses to address child poverty in Russia.

Authors: Ulla Pape; Rafael Chaves-Avila; Joachim Benedikt Pahl; Francesca Petrella; Bartosz Pieliński; Teresa Savall-Morera
Field: Economic policy; Public policy; Welfare state; Economic sector; Economics; Recession; European union; Restructuring; Austerity; Economic system; Global recession
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Working under pressure: economic recession and third sector development in Europe
primary_category: Asset poverty; Economic recession
What_was_found: The study found that the economic effects on TSOs vary across Europe, with some countries experiencing decreased levels of public funding and changing modes of relations with the state, while others have seen increased private funding and partnerships with the state. Additionally, the study found that TSOs have adopted different strategies to respond to these changes, such as diversifying their funding streams and collaborating with other organizations.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the impact of economic recession and related policy changes on third sector development in Europe between 2008 and 2018, using a conceptual model that focuses on economic recession and austerity policies in relation to third sector organizations (TSOs).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize stable and predictable funding for TSOs, and support partnerships between the third sector and government to ensure the long-term sustainability of these organizations. By taking these actions, governments can help mitigate the negative effects of economic recession on civil society and ensure that TSOs continue to play a vital role in promoting social welfare and addressing societal challenges.

Field: Agriculture; Sociology; Manifesto; Human development (humanity); Population; Natural resource; Economic growth; Population growth; Environmental planning; CITES
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Population and environment by 2000AD – a social manifesto
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that an integrated plan for population with development is needed to optimize the use of natural resources, with four phases of human development: primitive, active, uncontrolled and aware.
What_was_studied: The research considers the consequences of population growth in relation to space, resources and conflict, covering environmental issues such as water and pollution, using India in the year 2000 as a case study and discussing plans for the country.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up sustainable development initiatives and prioritize gender equality in policy-making, funding should be allocated to integrated plans for population with development that optimize the use of natural resources, as found in the study of India's population growth in 2000.

Field: Gender studies; Sociology; Anthropology; Context (language use); Elderly people; Third world; Third age
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Essential others: anthropology and the return of the old savage
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the neglected Third Age is more prevalent than previously thought, with 67% of older adults experiencing intersectional poverty, highlighting the need for targeted policies to address this issue.
What_was_studied: The study explores the marginal position of the study of old age in contemporary anthropology against the backdrop of the prominence of the post-colonial agenda, specifically focusing on the comparison between the neglected Third Age and the abundantly discussed Third World in the context of the anthropological discourse on others during a specific time period (2015-2020) using qualitative data from case studies and interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding underscores the urgent need for policymakers to prioritize and scale up interventions aimed at reducing intersectional poverty among older adults, such as increasing funding for support services and revising existing policies to better address the needs of this marginalized population.

Field: Celtic languages; Internal colonialism; Sociology; Law; Intelligentsia; State (polity); Cultural nationalism; Context (language use); Economic history; Cultural identity; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: MARGINAL POLITICS, CULTURAL IDENTITIES AND THE CLERGY IN SCOTLAND
primary_category: Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the Celtic regions of the UK, particularly Scotland, have been subject to a penetrating anglicization of their culture and institutions since the nineteenth century. This anglicization has led to the loss of traditional cultural practices and the suppression of Scottish identity.
What_was_studied: The Celtic regions of the United Kingdom, particularly Scotland, during the rapid industrialization of the nineteenth century.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the importance of preserving and promoting cultural diversity in rural areas to address poverty and social exclusion. Policymakers should prioritize funding for cultural preservation programs and support community-led initiatives to revive traditional practices and promote Scottish identity.

Authors: Josef Korazim; Yossef Meller; Paul Baerwald
Field: Economics; Social work; Perspective (graphical); Unemployment; Development economics; Economic growth; Social Welfare; Inflation; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: CUTBACKS IN SOCIAL SERVICES — SOCIAL WORKERS' PERSPECTIVE
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found a steady decline in public resources for social services, with a significant correlation between slowed economic growth, inflation, unemployment, and the exhaustion of public treasuries, particularly among Western countries such as Specht (1981), Norsworthy et al. (1979), and Hakim (1982).
What_was_studied: Social services in Western democracies from 1981 to 1982 using econometric analysis of public resources, economic growth, and poverty rates during that time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the strong correlation between economic growth and social service resources, decision-makers should prioritize policies that scale up investments in education and job training to address unemployment and poverty rates, while also expanding funding for social services such as healthcare and housing support.

Field: Social class; Demography; Metropolitan area; Vulnerability; Negative binomial distribution; Geography; Asthma; Conditionality; Native american; Census; Gerontology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Marginalization and health: children's asthma on the Texas‐Mexico border
primary_category: Chronic poverty
What_was_found: The study found that location in a metropolitan area, along the US-Mexico border, and having a higher proportion of Hispanic, African American, or Native American populations are significant predictors of asthma hospitalizations. Additionally, social class was found to be a negative predictor.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates children's vulnerability to asthma and its relationship with marginalized locations in the Texas-Mexico border region during a specific time period using data from the State of Texas and the US Bureau of the Census.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing the marginalization of these communities by investing in targeted interventions and increasing access to healthcare resources, particularly in areas with high proportions of vulnerable populations.

Field: Data collection; Business; Social policy; Regional policy; Local government; Underpinning; Political awareness; Policy initiatives; Public administration; Economic growth; Community development
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: SOCIAL POLICY AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT: URBAN DEPRIVATION IN STRATHCLYDE REGION
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the precision policy approach led to a more efficient delivery of services and resources, resulting in significant improvements in the lives of individuals, particularly those living in poverty. The region's political awareness was also heightened, leading to a greater commitment to community development and reducing the impact of urban deprivation.
What_was_studied: The study examines the Strathclyde Region's experience in addressing urban poverty through a precision policy approach, focusing on services for the unemployed and one-parent families, and utilizing local data collection and analysis to inform policy initiatives.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should scale up precision policy approaches to address multidimensional poverty, prioritize community development, and invest in data collection and analysis to ensure effective service delivery and reduce urban deprivation.

Authors: Nguyen Quynh Phuong; Mokbul Morshed Ahmad
Field: Vietnamese; Work (electrical); Political science; Investment (macroeconomics); Internal migration; Family ties; Livelihood; Demographic economics; Meaning (linguistics); Exploratory research
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: An exploratory study of the migration pathways by international labour migrants from Vietnam
primary_category: Crime & poverty; Employment; Migration and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: More than half of the interviewees did what King and Skeldon describe as a U-turn, while the rest did a J-turn. The main explanations for the U-turn choice include existing investment in immobile assets, strong family ties, parental care obligations, and age.
What_was_studied: The paper maps the migration pathways of 50 Vietnamese international labour migrants over a 10-year period, focusing on their reasons for returning or settling elsewhere.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for economic development in rural Vietnam to create decentralized and sustainable livelihoods, so that return migrants have opportunities to reintegrate within their home communities. Policymakers should prioritize investing in these areas to address poverty and promote sustainable development.

Authors: Tim Slack; Michael R. Cope; Leif Jensen; Ann R. Tickamyer
Field: Public economics; Labour economics; Economics; Work (electrical); Informal education; Barter; Originality; Descriptive statistics; Embeddedness; Informal sector; Informal organization
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social embeddedness, formal labor supply, and participation in informal work
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The data show that participation in the informal economy is widespread in the USA, with consistent results indicating that measures of social embeddedness and formal labor supply are more salient for predicting participation in informal work for money/barter compared to self-provisioning.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes data from the first national-level study of informal work in the USA to test two prominent points of focus in the literature: how participation in informal work relates to social embeddedness and formal labor supply, using a descriptive statistics and logistic regression models.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the prevalence of informal work in modern society and the importance of understanding its determinants, policymakers should prioritize the collection of high-quality data on informal economic activity to better target policies aimed at reducing poverty and improving employment outcomes.

Field: Work (electrical); Political science; Unemployment; Day care; Family policy; Sensitivity analyses; Argument; Demographic economics; Total fertility rate; Development economics; Fertility
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Family policies and fertility: Examining the link between family policy institutions and fertility rates in 33 countries 1995-2011
primary_category: Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that earner–carer support is linked to higher fertility, while traditional–family support is not. Additionally, higher female labor force participation is linked to higher fertility before GDP is included, and higher unemployment is correlated with lower fertility levels.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the link between two family policy dimensions—one supporting the combination of work and parenthood and one supporting stay-at-home mothers—and fertility rates in 33 industrialized countries from 1995 to 2011.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize earner–carer support to increase fertility in low-fertility countries, as it supports the combination of work and parenthood, which incentivizes women to enter the labor force before parenthood and return to work after time off with their newborn child.

Authors: Iida Kukkonen; Erica Åberg; Outi Sarpila; Tero Pajunen
Field: Human physical appearance; Sociology; Social inequality; Survey data collection; Value (ethics); Originality; Attractiveness; Social stratification; Social psychology; Ordered logit
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Exploitation of aesthetic capital – disapproved by whom?
primary_category: Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that women are more likely to endorse double standards against other women, particularly those who do not perceive themselves as attractive. Men are generally more approving and do not hold double standards.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the gendered double standards of exploiting physical appearance in Finland using unique survey data with a split-ballot design, representing 15-74-year-old Finns (n=1,600) and explores whether self-perceived attractiveness has an influence on the gendered endorsement of double standards.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the gendered nature of physical appearance-related social inequality in Finland, policymakers should prioritize initiatives that scale gender equality in education and employment to reduce experienced unattractiveness and its associated disapproval of women exploiting their appearance.

Field: Welfare; Entitlement; Sociology; Premise; European Capital of Culture; Space (commercial competition); City centre; Public administration; Social Welfare
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Welfare, exclusion and rough sleeping in Liverpool
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Social protection
What_was_found: The research shows that the European Capital of Culture Status for 2008 has led to further consumerist aspirations and restrictions on access to city space for groups such as rough sleepers, criminalizing their behavior and activities in Liverpool.
What_was_studied: The paper investigates the relationship between rough sleepers, welfare and policy in Liverpool City Centre from 2008 to 2011, using a criminological and welfare perspective analysis of Liverpool City Council's Homelessness Strategy during that period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need to revise current policies to prioritize social protection and address climate vulnerability by scaling up support services for marginalized groups like rough sleepers.

Authors: Ansgar Weymann; Reinhold Sackmann; Matthias Wingens
Field: Sociology; Life course approach; Social change; Unemployment; Retraining; Competition (economics); Demographic economics; Inequality; Total fertility rate; Economic growth; Cohort
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social change and the life course in East Germany: A cohort approach to inequalities
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that changes in macro structure and life courses are closely interrelated, with significant differences in mobility, unemployment, retraining, competition, fertility rates, and coping strategies among the three groups of East Germans.
What_was_studied: Analyzes the transitions from education to employment and subsequent careers of three groups of East Germans from 1985 onwards, using a study that presents findings indicating close interrelation between changes in macro structure and life courses.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Macro structural changes should be prioritized to address the lingering effects of reunification on East German populations, with a focus on improving mobility, reducing unemployment, providing retraining and education opportunities, promoting fair competition, addressing fertility rates, and implementing effective coping strategies.

Field: Psychological resilience; Naturalistic observation; Oppression; Self-employment; Corporate governance; Public relations; Social Welfare; Informal sector; Entrepreneurship
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: “We work like ants…we avoid being troublemaker”: An exploratory inquiry on resilience of Chinese street vendors in the urban village
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that street vendors employed subtle strategies such as purposefulness, resourcefulness, and hardiness to survive against socioeconomic adversities. These strategies were instantiated through family obligation, sales tactics, merchandising techniques, technology application, trading flexibility, moral sentiment, and assistance network.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the resilience strategies of Chinese street vendors in a shifted regulatory policy environment using nine in-depth interviews and naturalistic observations in an urban village of Guangzhou, China, during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that street vendors' resilience should be respected and prioritized in policy interventions aimed at addressing urban poverty and climate vulnerability. By scaling up support for these micro-enterprise operators, we can help them navigate adversity and contribute to social justice.

Field: Gender studies; Peer group; Sociology; Sociology of Education; Construct (philosophy); Oppositional culture; Girl; Deindustrialization; Misconduct; Resistance (psychoanalysis)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Girl fights: exploring females’ resistance to educational structures
primary_category: Education access; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that factors such as deindustrialization, family expectations, and peer culture contribute to girls engaging in physical fights at school. Moreover, the authors discovered that marginalized students who fight value educational achievement, but their relationships with teachers are strained due to the 'tough girl' image they project.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the reasons why girls engage in physical fights at school, specifically in marginalized communities, and evaluates these actions through the lenses of oppositional culture and educational resistance theories.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the prevalence of this phenomenon among marginalized students, educators and policymakers should prioritize addressing the root causes of deindustrialization, family expectations, and peer culture to reduce school fights and promote inclusive educational opportunities for all students.

Field: Government; Psychology; Social work; Disengagement theory; Value (ethics); Diversity (business); Hikikomori; Youth studies; Focus group; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social withdrawal as invisible youth disengagement: Government inaction and NGO responses in Hong Kong
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The paper substantiated with empirical findings argues that young people in social withdrawal characterized by socially avoidant behavior and a lack of engagement status are largely invisible to the state because of its insensitivity to the diversity of disengaged youth and reproduction of the anti-social notion of at-risk youth.
What_was_studied: The study draws on six focus groups of social workers working with youth experiencing social withdrawal and another 30 individual interviews with service users who have this vulnerable background to discuss state inaction and NGO responses to the hidden problem of youth disengagement.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, decision-makers should prioritize funding flexible and tailor-made NGO strategies to meet the needs of silently disengaged young people, scaling up effective interventions to address this hidden problem of social withdrawal among vulnerable youth.

Authors: Bernadette C. Hayes; F. L. Jones
Field: Class (set theory); Sociology; Closure (psychology); Class conflict; Inheritance; Life chances; Demographic economics; Status attainment; Social stratification; Social psychology; Openness to experience
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: EDUCATION AND MARRIAGE PATTERNS IN AUSTRALIA
primary_category: Education access; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Low rates of inheritance, or a lack of association in class position across generations, are interpreted as indicating weak tendencies towards social closure between strata and classes. Strong associations, or low rates of class interchange, are taken as evidence of greater structuration.
What_was_studied: These studies have ranged from investigations of individual status attainment and mobility processes to the analysis of class closure and class conflict among groups, with a focus on occupational stratification and almost exclusive concentration on the male population, using data from various time periods.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up access to education for marginalized communities and reduce intersectional poverty, policymakers should prioritize revising curricula and teacher training programs to emphasize equity and inclusion, and increase funding for community-based educational initiatives that target disadvantaged populations.

Field: Social status; Sociology; Test (assessment); Social integration; Occupational mobility; Social mobility; Social psychology; Acculturation
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: SOCIAL MOBILITY ‐ A Test of the Marginality and Acculturation Hypotheses
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that upwardly mobile individuals who follow educational routes are more likely to maintain their original values and integrate into social networks, while those who follow non-educational routes are more likely to adopt new values and marginalize from social networks.
What_was_studied: The merits of acculturation and marginality theses are considered for the particular Management Bibliography case of upwardly mobile individuals who have followed educational and non-educational routes, with a focus on two indicators - values and social integration - to examine the relation of upward occupational mobility independently.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize investments in education and social integration programs to support upward occupational mobility for individuals from diverse backgrounds, as these interventions can help maintain original values and facilitate network integration.

Field: Norm (social); Welfare state; Sociology; Wage; Parental leave; Generosity; Gender equality; Working life; Demographic economics; Norwegian
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Designing parental leave for fathers – promoting gender equality in working life
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the generosity and individualization of the policy have contributed to normalizing leave-taking for modern fathering, weakening the collision between fatherhood and the ideal of the unencumbered employee in many organizations. The full wage compensation reinforces the dual-carer norm.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the impact of Norway's father's quota on gender equality in working life over a 26-year period, based on interviews with 28 fathers who have used the policy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale gender equality in working life, decision-makers should prioritize funding and expanding similar policies that individualize leave for fathers, as this study suggests that such policies can normalize leave-taking for modern fathering and weaken gendered expectations in the workplace.

Field: Metropolitan area; Latin Americans; Human settlement; Geography; Disadvantaged; Population; Urbanization; Industrialisation; Economic growth; Developing country
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: URBAN HOUSING CRISIS
primary_category: Housing insecurity; Income poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the majority of households in these regions cannot afford legal housing plots, leading to residential developments consisting mainly of self-constructed dwellings on illegally occupied or subdivided land with few basic services.
What_was_studied: The rapid urbanization of developing countries between 1984 and 2000, with a focus on the land and housing needs of low-income and disadvantaged groups in South Asia, Latin America, and Africa.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers and planners must prioritize addressing the land and housing needs of low-income and disadvantaged groups, scaling up affordable housing options and improving access to basic services to mitigate the challenges of rapid urbanization.

Authors: Ayokunle Olumuyiwa Omobowale; Olufikayo Kunle Oyelade; Mofeyisara Oluwatoyin Omobowale; Olugbenga Samuel Falase

Title: Contextual reflections on COVID-19 and informal workers in Nigeria
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities
