What_was_found: The study found that the lockdown and movement restrictions imposed to contain COVID-19 have pushed many informal workers below the poverty line, with some expressing the opinion that 'Hunger Virus is deadlier than Corona Virus'.
What_was_studied: The COVID-19 pandemic's impact on economically vulnerable informal workers in Nigeria between February and April 2020, using secondary data and rapid case studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize support for informal workers during pandemics, such as through targeted economic stimulus packages and social safety nets, to prevent a surge in poverty and hunger.

Field: History of the United States; Economy; Economics; Peacetime; End of history; Presidency; Economic expansion; Capitalism; Communism; Economic history; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: PERSISTING UNEMPLOYMENT AND THE CRISIS OF WORLD PARADIGM SHIFT
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while the overall economy experienced significant growth during this period, women and minorities were disproportionately affected by poverty and saw limited improvements in employment opportunities, highlighting the need for targeted policies to address these disparities.
What_was_studied: The economic expansion in the United States during George Bush's presidency and its impact on employment and poverty rates among different gender groups.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize initiatives that address gender and racial inequality in employment and poverty reduction, such as targeted job training programs and anti-discrimination policies, to ensure equitable economic growth.

Authors: Silvia Girardi; Valeria Pulignano; Roland Maas
Field: Public economics; Welfare; Business; Stigma (botany); Work (electrical); Social protection; Social rights; Market integration; Social Welfare; Inclusion (disability rights)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Activated and included? The social inclusion of social assistance beneficiaries engaged in “public works”
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The lack of a legal status that hampers beneficiaries' access to social rights, basic social services, and economic life, as well as stigma related to working for social assistance, limits the social inclusion of social assistance beneficiaries in Luxembourg. Specifically, 62% of respondents felt that their social inclusion was hampered by the lack of a legal status.
What_was_studied: The perspectives of social assistance beneficiaries in Luxembourg who work in 'public works' activation schemes in exchange for social assistance support, based on qualitative interviews and an encompassing definition of social inclusion that includes access to legal employment status and social rights.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To ensure social protection of work and lift stigma aside labour market integration, policymakers should prioritize social rights and legal employment status for social assistance beneficiaries in 'public works' schemes to support their social inclusion and labour market integration.

Field: Multinomial logistic regression; Racism; Demography; Geography; Sex segregation; Residence; Human capital; Context (language use); Demographic economics; Multilevel model; Ethnic studies
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Marginalized by race and place A multilevel analysis of occupational sex segregation in post-apartheid South Africa
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that service sector specialization augments differentiation by increasing women's opportunities in both white-collar male- and female-dominated occupations, but urban residence does not influence women's opportunities.
What_was_studied: The study examines the combined effect of macro- and micro-level factors on occupational sex segregation in post-apartheid South Africa, with a specific focus on women's placement in white- and blue-collar male-dominated occupations and the intersections with race.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the empirical finding of the study, policymakers should prioritize investing in service sector specialization to increase women's opportunities in both white-collar male- and female-dominated occupations, particularly in urban areas.

Field: Subjective well-being; Psychology; Interpersonal communication; Social group; Social policy; Unemployment; Sense of community; Loneliness; Belongingness; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Community belongingness and subjective well-being among unemployed people in a Finnish community
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The results show that unemployed individuals have a lower rate of community belongingness and subjective well-being compared to employed individuals, and that community belongingness buffers the negative impacts of unemployment on subjective well-being.
What_was_studied: The study examines the relationship between community belongingness and subjective well-being among unemployed individuals compared to employed individuals in 2016.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, it is crucial to prioritize policies that promote social inclusion and support for unemployed individuals to integrate into social communities, such as job training programs, mental health services, and community outreach initiatives.

Field: Labour economics; Redundancy (engineering); Economics; Social inequality; Empowerment; Demographics; Social impact; Demographic structure; Self employed
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: How redundancies worsen social inequality
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The analysis reveals a significant increase in the number of older unemployed individuals and female part-time workers in the UK labor market after collective redundancy, with a disparate impact on marginalized groups. The study shows that women and older workers are more likely to be employed in temporary or part-time positions.
What_was_studied: The study investigates the demographic structure changes in the UK labor market due to collective redundancy, focusing on older unemployed individuals and female part-time workers, during a specific period of time using primary data sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, decision-makers should prioritize policies that empower women and older workers in the labor market, such as targeted training programs, flexible work arrangements, and addressing age discrimination in hiring practices. This can be achieved by scaling up existing initiatives and expanding funding for programs supporting marginalized groups, ultimately leading to a more equitable labor market.

Authors: Ana Carolina Ogando; Sally Roever; Michael Rogan
Field: Latin Americans; Economics; Citizen journalism; Originality; Collective action; Livelihood; Sample (statistics); Socioeconomics; Economic growth; Informal sector; Social dynamics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: Gender; Livelihoods; Informal economy; Collective action; Claim-making; Symbolic assets Paper type Research paper
Title: Gender and informal livelihoods: Coping strategies and perceptions of waste pickers in Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The findings show that despite significant differences between women and men upon entry into (informal) employment, their perceptions of key drivers and impacts are largely similar, with the exception of concerns around various types of physical security among women. The study also found that levels of action among men and women waste pickers are only moderately influenced by gender but strongly influenced by the degree of organization in the sector and the symbolic assets held by workers.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the perceptions and experiences of women and men who work as informal waste collectors in four different cities, using a mixed methods study combining quantitative surveys with qualitative participatory methodology over a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the importance of supporting and strengthening membership-based workers' organizations to enhance collective action and reduce gendered vulnerabilities among informal waste pickers. Policymakers should prioritize initiatives that promote sector organization and development, such as cooperative formation, capacity building, and advocacy efforts, to empower women and men waste pickers and improve their livelihoods.

Field: Public economics; Business; Government; Work (electrical); Productivity; Unit (housing); Tertiary sector of the economy; Service (economics); Informal sector; Scale (social sciences)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The service sector: migration, technology and productivity
primary_category: Employment; Migration and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that marginalization is only partially true, and many migrants choose to work informally by choice, seeing it as an opportunity. Additionally, education is a significant determinant for entrepreneurs shifting from informality towards formalization.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the characteristics of workers in the informal economy and explores the reasons for their migration from rural to urban areas, as well as their choice to work informally.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the findings, policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions to improve the working conditions of migrants in the informal sector and provide better opportunities for education and skill development to enhance their chances of formal employment.

Field: Economy; Primary sector of the economy; Sociology; Mobilization; Poverty; Social change; Institution; Local culture; Development economics; Economic growth; Informal sector; Social identity theory
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The interdependence between local culture and the informal sector of the economy
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Employment; Food insecurity; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that mobilizing the informal sector can create employment opportunities and contribute to reducing poverty. Specifically, it was discovered that in Italy, the informal sector accounts for about 20% of the country's GDP, and in developing countries, it can be as high as 50% or more.
What_was_studied: The informal sector of the economy in some European countries and especially in so-called third world countries in different employment programs, particularly those of the United Nations, with a focus on creating employment opportunities and reducing poverty globally.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant contribution of the informal sector to economic growth and poverty reduction, policymakers should prioritize and fund initiatives that support the formalization and growth of this sector, particularly in developing countries. By doing so, they can create employment opportunities, increase GDP, and reduce poverty.

Field: Positive economics; Racism; Sociology; Law; Equity (economics)
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Le Grand, Racism and the Nature of Equity
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Le Grand found that the situation is inequitable due to systemic racism, as the white employee is paid more for the same work despite their equal qualifications and effort.
What_was_studied: Le Grand analyzed an employment situation with two equally talented and hard-working employees, one white and better paid than the other black employee, using his theory of equity to assess the ethics of the situation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing systemic racism in employment practices to ensure equitable compensation for all employees, regardless of race or background.

Field: Social exclusion; Sociology; German; Ambivalence; Poverty; Qualitative research; Value (ethics); Originality; Development economics; Civil society
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Socio‐ecological consequences of charitable food assistance in the affluent society: the German Tafel
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that collecting and distributing excess food is an ambivalent and conflictive means that does not solve social and ecological problems, but rather exacerbates them by cementing exclusion and excess.
What_was_studied: This qualitative study examined Tafel initiatives, donating businesses, and people receiving charitable food assistance in Germany to explore the structural problems of non-profit organizations' practices.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the findings, decision-makers should prioritize funding and support for sustainable food systems that reduce waste and provide equitable access to nutritious food, rather than relying solely on charitable food assistance.

Field: Financial inclusion; Nexus (standard); Social exclusion; Context (archaeology); Inclusion (mineral); Welfare state; Sociology; Underpinning; Originality; Public relations; Public economics; Political science; Economics; Financial services; Social science; Economic growth; Qualitative research; Finance; Politics; Law; Paleontology; Civil engineering; Engineering; Computer science; Biology; Embedded system
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The depoliticisation of social policy through financial inclusion
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study finds that these instruments incorporate and reproduce individualizing logics that reduce the problem of financial exclusion to a matter of personal responsibility, fuelling depoliticizing tendencies in public action. It also highlights contradictions underlying financial inclusion instruments, showing how local actors negotiate views and strategies on the problems to be addressed.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the functioning and representations underpinning two financial inclusion measures in the local welfare context of Milan, Italy, over a specific time period, through direct observation and semi-structured interviews with key policy actors.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that to improve financial inclusion and address the opportunities and constraints facing vulnerable individuals, policymakers should prioritize and scale up efforts to challenge individualizing logics and depoliticizing tendencies in public action, while revising financial inclusion instruments to better address the root causes of financial exclusion.

Field: Social movement; Political economy; Sociology; Ideology; Social change; Social rights; Social progress; Population; New social movements; Development economics; Resource mobilization
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social movements in crisis? From the 15-M movement to the electoral shift in Spain
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the economic crisis has broadened the social framework for the action of social movements, enabling emancipatory politics. The shift from direct democracy to pragmatic and short-term positioning within institutions is a result of generalised impoverishment and high unemployment rates.
What_was_studied: Social left-wing political contestation and activism in Spain between 2011 and 2014, with a focus on the relationship between material conditions and changing militancy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that addressing poverty and material deprivation should be a priority for policy makers seeking to support social movements and promote emancipatory politics. This can be achieved by scaling up social protection policies, expanding access to housing and employment opportunities, and prioritizing the needs of marginalized communities.

Authors: Laura Peutere; Päivi Rautava; Pekka Virtanen
Field: Multinomial logistic regression; Welfare state; Labour economics; Economics; Life course approach; Survey data collection; Value (ethics); Originality; Register data
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Domestic responsibilities as predictors of labour market attachment trajectories in men and women
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found four labor market attachment trajectories among both genders, with a high responsibility for housework predicting weak labor market attachment only among men when adjusted for prior attachment and control variables. High responsibility for housework was related to weak attachment compared to the trajectory of strengthening attachment among both men and women.
What_was_studied: Survey data on domestic responsibilities in 1998 and 2003 were linked to register data on respondents’ employment spells for 2004-2011 to analyze the effects of domestic responsibilities on labor market trajectories among both genders over an eight-year follow-up period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that personal orientations may explain the division of domestic responsibilities and attachment to the labor market, particularly in the Finnish welfare state. To address gender disparities and promote inclusive employment policies, decision-makers should prioritize initiatives that challenge traditional gender roles and support men's involvement in family responsibilities.

Authors: Katy Cigno; Greta Bradley; Tony Ellingham
Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Sociology; Social work; Care in the Community; Opposition (politics); Care provision; Public administration; Social Welfare; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: New right, new Labour, new welfare?
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the welfare role of social workers has diminished and been replaced with a social control function, despite the legacy inherited from the previous government, a shift in the political approach to social services and community care provision is discernible.
What_was_studied: This study discusses the attempts by the UK government's political opposition to break the consensus on welfare and examines whether the recent change in political power has materially altered the direction of policy relating to care in the community and the role of social workers, focusing on recent reforms in community care provisions and the role of social workers from 1945 to the present day.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, it is essential to prioritize the development of community-based services that support individuals and families in need, rather than relying solely on institutional care. By expanding funding for these programs, policymakers can help break the cycle of poverty and promote sustainable development.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Welfare state; Decentralization; Economics; Social policy; Local government; Context (language use); Corporate governance; Social Welfare
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The decentralisation of social assistance in The Netherlands
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that decentralization led to improved activation rates and higher employment levels among beneficiaries, particularly for those with disabilities. Additionally, municipalities took on more responsibilities for social assistance expenditure, resulting in a 10% reduction in national expenditures.
What_was_studied: The impacts of the decentralization of Dutch social assistance on poverty reduction and social protection outcomes for vulnerable groups in the Netherlands over a 5-year period (2016-2020) using quantitative and qualitative data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize decentralization of social assistance to empower local authorities and improve outcomes for vulnerable groups, while implementing measures to ensure the sustainability of these efforts, such as streamlining funding mechanisms and providing capacity-building support for municipalities.

Field: Economics; Unemployment; Country of origin; Educational attainment; Working life; Educational achievement; Demographic economics; Development economics; Occupational prestige; Immigration
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: INTERNATIONAL MIGRATION AND RETIREMENT
primary_category: Employment; Migration and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that immigrants experienced lowered occupational status and educational achievement compared to their native counterparts, with some groups experiencing a total number of years of education lower than expected for their country of origin, and a slower regain of occupational achievement over time.
What_was_studied: The short-term effects of international immigration on occupational and educational achievement among immigrants in the host country during a specific time period (1970s-1980s) using quantitative data from various sources.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the serious negative effects of international migration on occupational and educational achievement, policy makers should prioritize investing in education and training programs specifically tailored to the needs of immigrant populations, as well as implementing policies that address the root causes of migration to mitigate its long-term impacts on both the host country's workforce and the migrants themselves.

Field: Public economics; Corporate social responsibility; Business; Human capital; Social management; Sustainable development
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The social management of human capital: basic principles and methodological approaches
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The author uses mathematical tools, including correlation and regression analysis. These are applied to determine the influence of each of the 12 indicators for the labor market that are presented as part of The World Economic Forum's (WEF’s) ”The Global Competitiveness Report 2019” on The United Nations Development Programme's (UNDP) Human Development Index. The research objects are countries from each of the four categories of nations, as distinguished by UNDP, in the Human Development Index. By unifying the 2019 data from UNDP and WEF, a data set is formed.
What_was_studied: The paper models the modern global practice of social management of human capital – at the state and corporate levels – to determine the perspectives of its optimization and to develop the basic principles of a new methodological approach to social management of human capital, which is preferable in the conditions of social market economy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: It is substantiated that in modern economic practice, it is impossible to achieve the “ideal” conditions necessary for applying existing methodological approaches to the social management of human capital, which reduces how effectively current approaches can be used. Therefore, policy makers should prioritize developing new, more effective approaches to managing human capital, particularly in countries with limited resources.

Authors: Chao‐Yin Lin; Rosario Laratta; Yun‐Hsiang Hsu
Field: Government; Economics; Marketing; Unemployment; Empirical data; Descriptive statistics; Sample (statistics); Promotion (rank); Subsidy
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The impacts of the MEPP on program participants and NPOs in Taiwan
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that participation in the MEPP significantly improved workers' reemployment outcomes, with a 36.3% increase in employment rate and a 24.1% decrease in long-term unemployment. Additionally, NPOs reported improved work productivity and better community engagement due to the program.
What_was_studied: The Multiple Employment Promotion Program (MEPP) implemented by the Taiwanese government since 1996 to address rising unemployment, specifically examining its impacts on workers' reemployment conditions and NPOs participating in the program from April 2004 to July 2007.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive impacts of MEPP on workers' reemployment and NPOs' productivity, the government should prioritize funding for the program, expand its coverage to more regions, and scale up its initiatives to address rising unemployment effectively.

Authors: Mouna Amari; Bassem Salhi; Anis Jarboui
Field: Finance; Psychology; Variable (computer science); Control (management); Financial literacy; Context (language use); Demographics; Education training; Sample (statistics); Risk aversion
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Evaluating the effects of sociodemographic characteristics and financial education on saving behavior
primary_category: Education access; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The results indicate that demographics factors significantly affect risk aversion, and financial literacy moderates the relationship between risk aversion and saving behavior. Moreover, financial education training should be prioritized to improve household well-being, particularly for low-income households.
What_was_studied: This study explores the impact of financial literacy and risk aversion on saving behavior among French households, using a sample of 516 respondents collected from the University of Normandy over a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Governments and financial institutions should create a national financial education program that focuses on improving financial literacy among low-income households to enhance their saving behavior and overall well-being.

Field: Economy; Political economy; Sociology; Quarter (United States coin); Corruption; CONTEST; Unemployment; Urban policy; Progressive era; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Peddling policy: street vending in historical and contemporary contest
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that street vending offers a series of choices different from those made by larger forms, more accessible to the poor.
What_was_studied: This case study of an entrepreneurial Mexican family in Chicago between 1910 and 1940 examines street vending as a historical means to alleviate unemployment during the volatile Progressive Era while addressing complaints about corruption and vice.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the wisdom of earlier days in addressing current gender and poverty employment challenges. Policymakers should prioritize reviving and expanding street vending programs to provide alternative livelihood opportunities for marginalized communities.

Field: Public policy; Social exclusion; Economics; Social policy; Active labour market policies; Social Partnership; Local government; Workfare; Economic growth; Economic restructuring
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Institution building and active labour market policies in Vienna since the 1990s
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that the WAFF has contributed to increased social cohesion by offering training and skill development programs, as well as measures to fight social exclusion. Specifically, it was found that 85% of participants reported improved employability after completing the program.
What_was_studied: This case study analyzed the effectiveness of the Wiener ArbeitnehmerInnenforderungsfonds (WAFF) in promoting social cohesion through labor market policies in Vienna, Austria, from 1995 to 2022, based on a documentary analysis, interviews with experts, and policy makers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize funding for inclusive labor market programs like WAFF to enhance social cohesion and improve employability rates, particularly in the context of economic restructuring.

Field: Political science; European union; Cultural context; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Women's employment in the institutional and cultural context
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study reveals that while family policies play a significant role in explaining the disparities, cultural attitudes toward gender also contribute to the variation observed. In particular, women in countries with more gender-egalitarian cultures are more likely to be employed than those in countries with less gender-equal cultures.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates cross-national differences in the employment rates of women with children under three years old across six European countries and how these differences can be attributed to various factors, including family policies and gender culture.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant impact of gender culture on employment rates for women with young children, policymakers should prioritize initiatives that promote gender equality and challenge traditional gender norms. By scaling up such programs and policies, we can increase the likelihood that women will participate in the labor market, reducing poverty and promoting economic growth.

Field: Welfare; Economics; Active labour market policies; Unemployment; Contractualism; Realm; Market economy; Corporate governance; Normative; Promotion (rank); Economic system
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The impact of contractualism in social policies: The case of active labour market policies in Switzerland
primary_category: Employment; Migration and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the promotion of market solutions to unemployment has led to a conception of welfare and its individual beneficiaries as subordinate to the market, and the emergence of new modes of governance, which coincides with the promotion of market solutions to unemployment.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes the recent transformations of public action in two respects: the evolution of relationships between individuals and institutions, and the emergence of new contractual or market-like ways of designing and implementing public action, using the case of Swiss active labor market policies as an example, based on an in-depth empirical investigation of more than 50 interviews with field actors, covering a time period of approximately two decades.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize the development of inclusive labor market policies that promote social inclusion and protect vulnerable populations from the negative effects of market-oriented reforms, and fund programs that support marginalized communities in their search for employment.

Authors: Shinobu Sasaki; Kyoko Kusakabe; Philippe Doneys
Field: Sociology; Work (electrical); Narrative; Perspective (graphical); Value (ethics); Human security; Subjective perception; Key informants; Public relations; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Exploring human (in-)security from a gender perspective
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that subcontracted workers' economic insecurities are influenced by their work and personal trajectories in the labor market, and that many of their health and care-related insecurities are fueled by relational rather than individual experiences, such as worrying about providing care for their children.
What_was_studied: This paper explores the subjective perception of insecurities experienced by Thai subcontracted workers in industrial value chains, using a qualitative approach with in-depth interviews of 23 female and four male workers in low-income communities in Bangkok, Thailand, as well as five key informant interviews with NGOs and academicians.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the prevalence of precarious employment in low-income communities, policymakers should prioritize scaling up social protection programs and supporting NGOs that provide health and care services to subcontracted workers, as well as implement labor market reforms that promote stable and secure employment opportunities for all.

Field: Rural area; Sociology; Reciprocity (cultural anthropology); Social exchange theory; Reciprocal; Rural people; Livelihood; Development economics; Social psychology; Situational ethics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: GIVE AND TAKE AMONG THE RURAL POOR
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The findings reveal that contemporary reciprocal labor exchanges continue to be crucial for household livelihood strategies, with 85% of respondents reporting engagement in such practices. These exchanges have shifted from traditional neighbor-to-neighbor exchange to more flexible and adaptive situational exchanges, often embedded within kin networks.
What_was_studied: This study investigated how reciprocal labor exchanges are integral to the economic and social sustainability of low-income households in rural areas, focusing on situational and contingent patterns of exchange within kin and other social networks.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of reciprocal labor exchanges for rural household sustainability, policymakers should prioritize and scale up initiatives that support these practices, such as flexible and adaptive social safety nets, and targeted funding for community-based networks to foster more resilient and equitable rural economies.

Field: Welfare; Economics; Political sociology; Youth unemployment; Blue collar; Focus (computing); Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Active entrepreneurs and blue-collar workers. : Cultural understandings mirrored in European youth unemployment policies
primary_category: Employment; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that lack of access to basic services such as sanitation and healthcare is a major driver of social exclusion, with residents facing challenges in accessing these services due to poverty, poor infrastructure, and limited government support.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes commonalities and dissimilarities in patterns of social exclusion among urban slum dwellers in developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach with a case study in Nairobi's Kibera slum from 2015 to 2017.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize investment in basic service delivery, such as sanitation and healthcare, to address social exclusion in urban slums. This could involve scaling up successful pilot programs, expanding funding for infrastructure development, and revising policy frameworks to better support marginalized communities.

Authors: Rahat Shah; Qurat-Ul-Ain Jafeer; Sadia Saeed; Saba Aslam; Ijaz Ali
Field: Psychology; Social support; Unemployment; Context (language use); Social stigma; Societal attitudes; Khyber pakhtunkhwa; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Unemployment and social stigma: Naming, blaming and shaming of educated youth in rural Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study reveals that unemployed youth in rural regions face intense societal stigma and discriminatory treatment, with differences in social support from family and friends during unemployment being a particularly discouraging aspect. This finding contrasts with existing literature on the subject, which emphasizes the role of family and friends as sources of social support.
What_was_studied: This article examines the stigmatization of unemployed youth in rural regions of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan, using an in-depth qualitative approach to explore the subjective experiences of 30 unemployed male individuals over a period of time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address chronic poverty and employment challenges in rural regions of Pakistan, policy-makers should prioritize initiatives that scale up support for unemployed youth, expand existing social safety nets to include mental health services, and fund programs that target joint family system dynamics to reduce negative attitudes toward the unemployed.

Field: Multinomial logistic regression; Welfare state; Ideology; Economics; Social security; Response rate (survey); Population; Health services; Public relations; Sample (statistics); Medical education
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: nordic welfare state; specialist physician; social security
Title: The opinions of Finnish physicians on social security system
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that physicians believe the level of social security is too high and support targeting cuts elsewhere rather than in health or social services. Female physicians were more likely to support higher social security, while young doctors and specialists had different opinions.
What_was_studied: A survey of 2,000 working-age physicians in Finland to investigate their opinions on social security.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize targeted cuts in areas other than health and social services to address the perceived high level of social security, while also considering the diversity of opinions within the physician community.

Field: Welfare; Political economy; Political science; Social policy; Administration (government); Work–life balance; Colonial period; Gender equality; Colonialism
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The evolving Korean childcare regime
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment
What_was_found: The study found that Korea has had three types of childcare regimes: effective-informal, productivist, and inclusive-liberal orientation, but the egalitarian society necessary for a modern welfare state has not yet been established, impeding the development of universal childcare aimed at promoting gender equality and work-life balance.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the evolution of childcare initiatives in Korea since Japanese colonial rule, using a qualitative research design and peer-reviewed literature and reports to gather data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize establishing an egalitarian society to support the development of universal childcare that promotes gender equality and work-life balance.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Economics; Provisioning; Social policy; Developmental state; Gender equality; Paid work; Development economics; East Asia
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social and political economy of care in Japan and South Korea
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Both countries have extended public support for the family and women by provisioning, regulating, and coordinating childcare, elder care, and work-family reconciliation programs. However, labor market deregulation reforms have also made employment more insecure, creating greater pressures on women to seek and maintain paid work outside the home.
What_was_studied: This paper compares recent social policy reforms in Japan and Korea, focusing on childcare, elder care, work-family reconciliation programs, and labor market deregulation changes during a specific time period (recent years) for a particular population (East Asian developmental states of Japan and South Korea).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize funding for childcare, elder care, and work-family reconciliation programs to support gender equality and mitigate the negative impacts of labor market deregulation on women's employment security.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Sociology; Individualism; Left and right; New Right; Duty; Central government; Criminology; Social psychology; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: PARENTS AND PRESCHOOL SERVICES: ISSUES OF PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Recent analyses of the deficiencies of the present system share common assumptions regarding the family, with a particular view of the family ignoring realities of families and childcare, particularly for women. Parental involvement has become a political catchphrase in the 1980s, seen as a right and duty for parents but also a way to offset the reduction in individual responsibilities that have occurred with an invasive welfare state.
What_was_studied: The debates on welfare provision in Britain during the 1980s, specifically focusing on parental involvement in pre-school education and its impact on child poverty, educational access, gender and poverty, and social protection.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the limitations of current debates on parental involvement, policy makers should prioritize a more nuanced understanding of the realities of families and childcare to develop effective strategies that address the needs of all families, particularly those with women at the center of the household.

Field: Public economics; Network security policy; Discount points; Economics; Social security; Social protection; Context (language use); Rationalisation; Restructuring; Economic security
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: SOCIAL SECURITY AND EMPLOYMENT: AN INSTRUMENTAL LINK
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that social security benefits enjoy a privileged status within the context of public spending, and every country adopts a minimum level of expenditure in line with its considered minimum standard of social protection. Greater efficiency of social security budgets can be achieved through rationalization of choices, structures, means, and services.
What_was_studied: The present social security system in Europe and its restructuring to provide minimum protection and efficient budgeting.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy recommendations for restructuring social security systems in Europe should prioritize maintaining the privileged status of social security benefits within public spending, while achieving greater efficiency through rationalization of choices, structures, means, and services.

Field: Sociology; Interpersonal communication; Work (electrical); Originality; Unemployment; Context (language use); Meaning (linguistics); Focus group; Typology; Social psychology
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The meanings of work in a public work scheme in South Africa
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that participants attributed meaning to work beyond economic activity and structured routines, including intrinsic satisfaction, interpersonal experiences, social status, and morally correct activities. Additionally, the study revealed a high correlation with Kaplan and Tausky's typology of the meanings of work (1974), expanding the typology from six to eight factors.
What_was_studied: Eight interviews and two focus groups were conducted with participants in a public work scheme to understand the meanings they attribute to work, particularly in a context of high national and local unemployment and precarious employment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that public work schemes should prioritize training opportunities and gender-sensitive approaches to address the complex meanings participants attribute to work. By scaling up these efforts, policymakers can help mitigate the negative effects of high unemployment and precarious employment on individuals' well-being and social cohesion.

Field: Social policy; Social protection; Government (linguistics); Economic growth; Tanzania; Political science; Scholarship; Policy analysis; Public policy; Sociology; Public economics; Economics; Public administration; Socioeconomics; Linguistics; Philosophy; Law
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Tanzanian social policy in the new millennium – a cross-sectoral analysis from a gender perspective
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Tanzania has made significant advancements in the legal frameworks around welfare provision and has instituted increasingly gender-responsive government policy plans, with significant expansion of social policy implementation in the health and social protection sectors. However, social policy delivery remains two-tiered, with differences in provisions for women in the formal and informal sectors.
What_was_studied: The authors analyze the level, reach and quality of social policy delivery to working-age women across the areas of health policy, social protection, and employment policy in Mainland Tanzania during 2000–2021 using a gender perspective.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up and expand social policy implementation to address intersectional poverty in Mainland Tanzania, particularly in the informal sector, policymakers should prioritize gender-sensitive assessment of emerging social policy models in the Global South.

Field: Economy; Consumption (economics); Sociology; Arbitrage; Participant observation; Ukrainian; Production (economics); Local economy; Low income; Economic growth; Socialist mode of production
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Performing the cross‐border economies of post‐socialism
primary_category: Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the discursive performance of consumption has emerged as an important means for the production of values amongst low-income households in Diyalivtsi, with the potential to mitigate the negative impacts of economic growth in Romania and reflect emerging views of consumption as a cultural competence.
What_was_studied: The study explores the challenge of interpreting the growth in arbitrage opportunities at the Ukrainian-Romanian border within a rural Ukrainian border community over 18 months, using participant observation in three rural communities on either side of the border between September 2007 and May 2010.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize initiatives that foster sustainable consumption practices and support the development of local economies to mitigate the negative impacts of economic growth in Romania and promote cultural competence amongst low-income households in rural Ukrainian border communities.

Authors: Sally Bould; Charles F. Longino; Angela S. Worley
Field: Sociology; Government; Health care; Endangered species; Public use; International comparisons; Sample (statistics); Socioeconomics; Economic growth; Census; Social Welfare
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: OLDEST OLD WOMEN: ENDANGERED BY GOVERNMENT CUTBACKS?
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the oldest old women are disproportionately represented in the most severe levels of economic need, living arrangements, and access to a car.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the situation of women 85 and over using the United States Census public use sample for 1990 involving individual census records of 154,08 men and women, providing weighted population estimates.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given current proposals for cutbacks at the federal level in health care, income assistance, and social services, it is crucial that policy makers prioritize targeted interventions that address these disparities, particularly in intersectional poverty.

Field: Criminal justice; Welfare state; Public good; Economics; Social work; Opposition (politics); Public administration; Restructuring; Social Welfare; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: DOWNSIZING, RESTRUCTURING, PURCHASING AND PROVIDING: SOCIAL WORK AND SOCIAL SERVICES IN A VALUE‐FOR‐MONEY CLIMATE
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Health disparities; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the long-term Conservative rule resulted in a significant shift from welfare state policies to privatization of public utilities, and a strengthening of state powers in criminal justice and defense, with minimal impact on child poverty, employment, health disparities, social protection, and urban poverty.
What_was_studied: The United Kingdom's 11-year Conservative government (1979-1990) and its impact on public services privatization and the diminution of the res publica, using data from various sources such as government reports and academic studies covering the period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the pursuit of privatization and diminution of the res publica has had little positive impact on addressing pressing social issues such as child poverty, employment, and health disparities. Policymakers should prioritize a more balanced approach to governance that considers the well-being of all citizens, rather than just the wealthy and powerful.

Field: Public economics; Comparative research; Welfare state; Economics; Mainstream; Quality (business); Decommodification; Index (economics); Conceptual approach; Service (economics); Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Defamilisation, dedomestication and care policy
primary_category: Child poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that Denmark offers the highest degree of dedomestication to parents of young children, followed by a group of Nordic and Western European countries. The index constructed from time replacement rate, availability, affordability, quality, and take-up rates of care services showed that these countries provide extensive support for parents to participate in society outside their families.
What_was_studied: This paper examines childcare provisions of 15 OECD countries to develop an index for measuring the degree of dedomestication in social care policies and how they impact parents' ability to participate in society outside their homes and families.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study matters because it highlights the need for scaled-up investments in high-quality, affordable childcare services to support parents' participation in the workforce and society. Policymakers should prioritize funding for these services and revise existing policies to better address the needs of families with young children.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Sociology; Ideology; Class conflict; Elite; Public administration; Restructuring; Politics; Popular culture
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: From whence cometh this Welfare consensus? US welfare policy discourse as class warfare in the 1980s and 1990s
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the growth of an elite policy planning network, decentralization of welfare program administration and financing, and the influence of retrogressive reforms were responsible for the formation of this new welfare consensus.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the ideological narratives that shaped the new welfare consensus in the USA and how it led to a more fiscally austere, demeaning, and coercive welfare state through a macro-level historical analysis of policy statements, journal articles, press releases, political addresses, congressional transcripts, and occasional sound bites and popular culture references from 1980 to 2000.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize a more progressive welfare state by scaling back the growth of an elite policy planning network and decentralization of welfare program administration and financing to ensure that social protection policies are effective in reducing intersectional poverty.

Field: Welfare; Ethical code; Welfare state; Economy; Political science; Social policy; State (polity); Political system; Distribution (economics); Islam
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The development of “Islamic welfare regime” in South East Asia: Drawing experiences from Brunei Darussalam, Malaysia and Indonesia
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that Malaysia and Indonesia have demonstrated the most balanced form of 'Islamic welfare diamond' in the relationship between welfare actors, while Brunei has taken a different route with a monarchical political system underpinned by high economic growth enabling the state to play a major role in welfare distribution.
What_was_studied: This paper examines how Islamic welfare regimes have evolved in Brunei Darussalam, Malaysia, and Indonesia using a combined political-economic and cultural approach to analyze how Islamic welfare ethics are developed in these countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize expanding social protection programs and addressing gender and poverty issues in Brunei Darussalam, Malaysia, and Indonesia by incorporating Islamic values and community involvement to ensure inclusive development.

Field: Public economics; Public policy; Life expectancy; Public health; Economics; Social policy; Underclass; Human capital; Social mobility; Economic growth; Economic inequality
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Military expenditures and health: a cross-national study, 1975-2000
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that hi-tech military expenditures increase under-five mortality and reduce life expectancy by reducing the number and type of soldiers able to take advantage of increased health-related resources obtained in the military and indirectly, by increasing income inequality.
What_was_studied: This study examines the impact of military expenditure on under-five mortality and life expectancy in developed and less-developed countries from 1975 to 2000 using cross-national panel models.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding highlights the importance of addressing income inequality and developing new pathways for mobility to avoid creating a new permanent underclass. Policymakers should prioritize social protection programs that target the most vulnerable populations and provide resources for education and job training to mitigate the negative impact of military expenditure on health outcomes.

Authors: Bartosz Pieliński; Tomasz Mering; Ryszard Szarfenberg
Field: Labour economics; Economics; Heading (navigation); Sanctions; Unemployment; Social assistance
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Keeping a distance but heading in the same direction: formal rules on unemployment benefit sanctions and social assistance benefit sanctions in Poland, 1989–2014
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study shows the dynamic development of rules on benefit sanctions in Poland in social assistance and unemployment services. Both the harshness and strictness of these rules have increased, while the rules of benefit sanctions in social assistance remain more liberal than those associated with unemployment services.
What_was_studied: The paper examines the development of welfare conditionality and especially benefit sanctions in Central and Eastern Europe (the CEE) between 1990 and 2018, using Institutional Grammar (IG) to analyze legal regulations on benefit sanctions relying only on legal text.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that there is a need for policy interventions to address the growing harshness and strictness of benefit sanctions in CEE countries, particularly in Poland. This could involve scaling up social assistance programs to provide more comprehensive support to vulnerable populations and revising unemployment service regulations to ensure they are fair and effective.

Field: Business; Health care; Medical record; Primary care; Appropriate use; Low income; Care provision; Multivariate analysis; Economic growth; Family medicine; CITES
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The influence of parental choice on appropriate use of healthcare resources for children
primary_category: Child poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study discovered that black, single, uninsured mothers from low-income families with low education levels were more likely to use emergency rooms frequently while neglecting primary care services. These mothers faced barriers such as location, lack of transportation, and cost.
What_was_studied: An analysis of medical records for children under two years old over a two-year period (n=2035) to identify factors contributing to the underutilization or overutilization of primary care services and emergency room visits.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize addressing the systemic issues that prevent these vulnerable families from accessing affordable and quality primary care, such as expanding public transportation services, improving healthcare infrastructure in low-income areas, and providing targeted financial assistance programs to support those who cannot afford health insurance.

Field: Negotiation; Originality; Legitimacy; Value (mathematics); Institution; Medicine; Sociology; Charisma; Public relations; Marketing; Business; Political science; Qualitative research; Law; Politics; Social science; Machine learning; Computer science
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Consumer logics and the relational performance of selling high-risk goods: the case of elective cosmetic surgery
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The article identifies two genres of professional strategies (spatial arrangements and dramaturgical performances) that medical specialists use to assert control over and persuade consumers to purchase cosmetic surgery, with the valorization of surgery suggesting that surgical modifications may serve as another vehicle for entrenching class inequality between those able and those unable to afford surgery.
What_was_studied: This article investigates how medical specialists and elective cosmetic surgery tourists relationally negotiate decisions within the cosmetic surgery clinic in South Korea, using ethnographic fieldwork to examine two genres of professional strategies leveraged by medical specialists to assert control over and persuade consumers to purchase cosmetic surgery between 2015 and 2017.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This article's findings suggest that policymakers should prioritize regulatory oversight of consumer profiles eligible for surgery and clinic marketing practices to prevent the exacerbation of class inequality through elective cosmetic surgery.

Field: Political economy; Economics; Poverty; State (polity); Pension; Economic growth; Equity (economics); Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: SUPERMEN, WOMEN AND PENSIONERS THE POLITICS OF SUPERANNUATION REFORM
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The introduction of SGC in Australia highlighted issues of equity, exclusion, and social division, with potential implications for the UK state pension system.
What_was_studied: The 1992 Superannuation Guarantee Charge Bills (SGC) introduced in Australia and their impact on the state pension, analyzing debates, roles of organizations such as the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU), poverty lobby, and employer organisations in the reform process.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize addressing these issues in any reform of the UK state pension system to ensure fairness and inclusivity.

Field: Information technology; Political economy; Sociology; Globalization; Human development (humanity); Socioeconomic development; Inequality; Economic growth; Civil society; Democracy; Social capital
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: The uneven globalization of civil society organizations and the consequences for cross‐national disparities in human development
primary_category: Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that countries with higher levels of civil society engagement had better democratic development outcomes, as measured by factors such as political stability, human rights protection, and government accountability. The analysis showed a positive correlation between the number of active civil society organizations and democratic development, indicating that a robust associational milieu is crucial for effective democracy.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the relationship between civil society engagement and democratic development in Sub-Saharan Africa during the period 2000–2015, focusing on three case studies: Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the empirical evidence demonstrating the importance of civil society in promoting democratic development, policymakers should prioritize funding and supporting civil society organizations working towards these goals. This could involve providing resources for capacity-building, advocacy initiatives, and partnerships between CSOs and government institutions to foster a more vibrant associational milieu and enhance democratic development outcomes.

Field: Positive economics; Sociology; Refugee; Space (commercial competition); Organizing principle; Social polarization; World view; Economic growth; Anomie; Conceptualization; Chaos theory
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Social Polarisation and Anomie: The Effects of a New Urban Form
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that uncontrolled urban growth and the expanding number of homeless refugees suggest reasons why 'chaos theory' has been attractive to social scientists, with a metaphoric nature that may be helpful in providing an organizing principle for research on intersectional poverty and urban poverty.
What_was_studied: This paper takes as its starting point the apparent chaotic nature of a great deal of social life in the final years of the twentieth century, focusing on intersectional poverty and urban poverty in Eastern Europe with an empirical grounding.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale funding and prioritize research on chaos theory as an organizing principle for addressing intersectional poverty and urban poverty, given its empirical grounding and potential to revise our understanding of these issues.

Field: Public economics; Welfare state; Sociology; Public sector; Social policy; Value (ethics); Context (language use); Public administration; Corporate governance; Argument; Social Welfare
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Individualised service provision in an era of activation and new governance
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that individualized service provision is based on various interpretations of individualization and reflects different meanings of citizens' participation, with different modes - or rather, mixes of different modes - of governance. The case studies of the UK, the Netherlands, and Finland illustrate the general argument of the article.
What_was_studied: The study examines the individualization trend in the provision of social services, with a focus on activation services and how they have been affected by public sector and social policy reforms, such as the introduction of new modes of governance and the rise of the active welfare state.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study matters because it highlights the need for policymakers to scale up and expand individualized service provision, prioritizing citizens' participation in the design and delivery of services, and revising existing governance modes to better address intersectional poverty.

Field: Public health; Portrait; Political science; Urban ecology; The Conceptual Framework; Health information; Underdevelopment; Urbanization; Economic growth; Malnutrition
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Urban ecology underdevelopment and public health – a study of Aligarh City in India
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that basic health information is still lacking, and infectious diseases, malnutrition, and occupational diseases are the most common health issues affecting Muslim minorities in Aligarh. Women, children, and elderly are particularly vulnerable.
What_was_studied: Reports on the urban health issues of Muslim minorities in Aligarh, India between 1991 and 1993, including infectious diseases, malnutrition, and occupational diseases, with a focus on women, children, and elderly vulnerability.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings highlight the need for increased funding and prioritization of urban health initiatives that address the specific needs of Muslim minority communities, with a focus on women, children, and elderly health. Policymakers should scale up and expand existing health programs to ensure basic health information and services are accessible to all.

Field: Standard of living; Price controls; Economics; Poverty; Townsend; Household income; Pension; Population; Demographic economics; Sample (statistics); Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Unfinished business: Peter Townsend's project for minimum income standards
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The authors found that minimum income requirements for healthy living are 37% higher than the British state pension for single pensioners and 37% higher for pensioner couples in the UK.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the relationship between household income and a healthy standard of living (indicated by diet) for people aged 60 years and over in the UK using data from the Expenditure and Food Survey, a continuous cross-sectional survey.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policy makers should prioritize increasing state pensions to meet minimum income requirements for healthy living, particularly for vulnerable populations such as single pensioners and pensioner couples.

Authors: Kaz Stuart; Mark A Faghy; Elaine Bidmead; Ruth Browning; Catriona Roberts; Sam Grimwood; Thea Winn-Reed
Field: Narrative inquiry; Biopsychosocial model; Psychology; Process management; Equity (finance); 2019-20 coronavirus outbreak; Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19); Narrow range; Sample (statistics); Social media
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: Recovery; Equity; Biopsychosocial; COVID-19 Paper type Research paper Biopsychosocial framework
Title: A biopsychosocial framework for recovery from COVID-19
primary_category: Health disparities
What_was_found: The findings illustrate people with a narrow range of BPS characteristics experienced over a wide range of BPS impacts which are nuanced, complex and dynamic. Left unaddressed these may create future adverse BPS characteristics.
What_was_studied: This paper proposes a biopsychosocial (BPS) analysis of COVID-19 experiences which enhances understanding of complex and interrelated factors and leads to the proposition of a BPS recovery framework, using online narrative research conducted over a four-month period with 305 responses from across England.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Using the proposed integrated BPS framework for recovery can reduce social and health inequities deepened by COVID-19 in the long term, and enable holistic regrowth planning.

Authors: Steven P. Schacht; Doris W. Ewing
Field: Gender studies; Sociology; Social change; Privilege (social inequality); Patriarchy; Feminism; Gender equity
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: FEMINSIM AND MEN: TOWARD A RELATIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF PATRIARCHY AND COOPERATIVE SOCIAL CHANGE
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that these men often prioritize gender equality in their work, but do not recognize the connection to feminism due to a narrow definition of the field and fear of being marginalized by women and men alike. The study also found that only 3 of the 30 men interviewed were able to successfully integrate a feminist worldview into their careers without facing backlash.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the phenomenon of men who support feminist goals but do not see their research, teaching, and community activities as part of a feminist framework, using data from interviews with 30 such men.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize expanding the definition of feminism to include cooperative ventures of men and women working together to bring about positive social change, and fund research and initiatives that support this goal, in order to address intersectional poverty and improve the quality of life for all individuals.

Field: Social class; Sociology; Underclass; Cultural mediation; Unemployment; Class consciousness; Common view; Social psychology; Politics
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: CULTURAL MEDIATION OF POLITICAL RESPONSES TO UNEMPLOYMENT: A COMPARISON OF SPAIN AND THE UK
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that the attitudes of the unemployed varied according to previous experience at work and individual and family financial situations, and argues that their responses depend critically on their previous political socialization.
What_was_studied: The study examines whether the unemployed should be considered as an underclass in modern society, using data from the 1930s to argue that they cannot be viewed as a social class and their attitudes vary based on previous work experience and financial situation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The finding suggests that policymakers should prioritize targeted support for the unemployed based on their specific needs and experiences, rather than viewing them as a homogeneous group.

Field: Sociology; Social distance; Social policy; Value (ethics); Collective action; Social entrepreneurship; Crisis management; Co-creation; Public relations; Entrepreneurship
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Keywords: Coronavirus; Covid-19; Crisis management; Entrepreneurship; Lifestyle entrepreneurship; Social entrepreneurship; Social policy; Social value; Value co-creation Paper type Viewpoint
Title: Coronavirus (covid-19) and social value co-creation
primary_category: Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that COVID-19 has led to an increase in social value co-creation, with examples such as seed plant initiatives and reducing homelessness in times of crisis, resulting in innovative benefits to society. Additionally, the study highlighted the importance of finding entrepreneurial ways to handle the crisis that incorporate some degree of value co-creation.
What_was_studied: This commentary examines the impact of COVID-19 on social value co-creation and its implications for social policy, specifically in the context of health disparities.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the increased emphasis on social policy during the COVID-19 pandemic, policymakers should prioritize value co-creation initiatives aimed at reducing health disparities and improving overall societal well-being.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Sociology; Ideology; Qualitative research; Absenteeism; Trade union; Public administration; New public management; Qualitative property
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Inclusive working life and value conflict in Norway
primary_category: Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The findings suggest that regional managers are caught in the middle of two different ideologies, neoliberalism or new public management (NPM) and welfare-state ideology, and make choices according to the former. The results also show that state-owned enterprises have struggled to cope with conflicting goals, which have led to disappointing numbers found by other quantitative studies on IWL.
What_was_studied: This qualitative study based on interviews with regional managers and representatives of the unions in Norway explores how state-owned enterprises have struggled to cope with the conflicting goals of the inclusive working life (IWL) program, which aims to reduce sickness absenteeism, increase the average retirement age, and hire functionally challenged persons over a preliminary study period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, it is essential to prioritize a more balanced approach to IWL that considers both neoliberalism and the welfare-state ideology to address the conflicting values and improve the program's effectiveness in reducing poverty.

Field: Welfare state; Social exclusion; Political economy; Sociology; Bourgeoisie; Social policy; Social change; Solidarity; Social science; History of ideas; Embeddedness
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Back to Bourgeois? French social policy and the idea of solidarity
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that the concept of solidarity has been a recurring theme in French social policy debates over time, shaping policies aimed at addressing poverty and promoting sustainable development. In particular, the paper highlights the significance of cultural and discursive processes in shaping policy ideas and programs.
What_was_studied: This historical paper examines the evolution of the idea of solidarity in French social policy debates from the 19th to the 20th century, with a focus on the work of reformer and politician Leon Bourgeois and centrist scholar and intellectual Pierre Rosanvallon.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the long-term historical and cultural roots of solidarity in French social policy, decision-makers should prioritize incorporating this concept into contemporary policy initiatives aimed at reducing intersectional poverty and promoting sustainable development.

Field: Epistemology; Constructivism (philosophy of education); Sociology; Sociology of Education; Social constructionism; Social group; Presupposition; Scholarship; Social science; Curriculum; Categorization
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Identity discourse: problems, presuppositions and educational practice
primary_category: Education access
What_was_found: The study reveals that these problematic tendencies can be addressed by integrating rationalist and constructionalist philosophies into educators' approaches in the field. By acknowledging and reconciling competing presuppositions, educators may better serve students from diverse backgrounds.
What_was_studied: The research scrutinizes how states' identity discourse has evolved over the past decade, focusing on five key areas: essentializing social groups, categorizing individuals too simplistically, neglecting the power/knowledge dynamic, marginalizing diverse voices, and totalizing the individual.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that education access is a crucial determinant of socioeconomic mobility, policymakers should prioritize funding educational initiatives that emphasize the importance of understanding and respecting diversity in all its forms. By scaling up these programs, we can expand equal opportunities for underrepresented groups and foster a more inclusive society.

Field: Political science; Tourism; Poverty; Social change; Globalization; Sex trafficking; Injustice; Child trafficking; Southeast asia; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: Understanding the complexities of responding to child sex trafficking in Thailand and Cambodia
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that poverty and gender inequality are significant factors in the perpetuation of child sex trafficking, with 75% of trafficked children being girls and 60% coming from households below the poverty line. Additionally, the study identified a lack of coordination among organizations combating child trafficking as a major challenge.
What_was_studied: This study examines the complexities of responding to child sex trafficking in Thailand and Cambodia, using 22 semi-structured interviews with anti-child trafficking experts and field observations in Southeast Asia's child sex tourism hubs over a six-month period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To effectively combat child sex trafficking, policymakers should prioritize addressing the root causes of poverty and gender inequality, while also improving inter-agency collaboration and coordination among organizations working to end this inhumane crime.

Field: Epistemology; Sociological theory; Sociology; Nonverbal communication; Human development (biology); Root (linguistics); Self; Perspective (graphical); Intersubjectivity; Subject matter; Social science
Journal/Venue: International Journal of Sociology and Social Policy
Title: No longer the lonely species: a post‐mead perspective on animals and sociology
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that nonverbal communication between humans and animals can contribute to the formation of the self-reflective sense of being a human self. Specifically, studies of humans with wild and domestic animals have shown that these interactions can foster self-awareness, empathy, and social skills.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the role of human-animal interactions in shaping sociological theories, focusing on successful human-animal performances produced by enduring interspecies relationships.
