Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that policies aimed at reducing unemployment and addressing its scarring effects on electoral participation should be prioritized, particularly at the sub-national levels where lower unemployment rates can exacerbate the individual scarring effect. Additionally, targeted interventions for citizens with long unemployment scars may be necessary to increase their electoral participation.

Authors: Lasse Tarkiainen; Teemu Kemppainen; Hannu Lahtinen; Venla Bernelius; Pekka Martikainen
Field: Neighbourhood (mathematics); Disadvantage; Socioeconomic status; Demography; Population; Demographic economics; Geography; Psychology; Sociology; Economics; Political science; Mathematics; Mathematical analysis; Law
Title: The effect of cumulative childhood exposure to neighbourhood socioeconomic disadvantage on school performance—a register-based study on neighbourhoods, schools, and siblings
primary_category: Education access
What_was_found: The study found that family factors accounted for most of the variation in GPA, and only around 1% of the variance was attributable to the neighbourhood. Additionally, the study found a non-negligible but not statistically significant effect of neighbourhood disadvantage among children of parents with only basic education.
What_was_studied: Using longitudinal register data on the total population of Finnish children in major cities, this study examines the extent to which variation in grade point average (GPA) is attributable to schools, neighbourhoods, and families.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize initiatives that support families and limit the emergence of neighbourhood effects to ensure equal access to education for all students.

Field: Political science; Poverty; Globalization; Unemployment; Context (language use); Reterritorialization; Deterritorialization; Restructuring; Development economics; Modernization theory; Economic system
Title: Globalization and socio-economic restructuring in Andalusia. Challenges and possible alternatives
primary_category: Crime & poverty
What_was_found: Andalusia has high rates of poverty and unemployment despite economic growth and modernization, with challenges exacerbated by globalization. The study highlights the region's potential for socio-economic opportunities in the new global context.
What_was_studied: The intensification of socio-economic dynamics in Andalusia, a region in south Spain, due to globalization and its effects on poverty and unemployment rates over time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize policies addressing poverty and unemployment in Andalusia, leveraging its autonomous government powers to scale up economic growth initiatives and fund targeted programs.

Field: Social class; Social position; Sociology; Life course approach; Social group; Poverty; Disadvantage; Development economics; Social stratification; General partnership
Title: Life Course Risks or Cumulative Disadvantage? The Structuring Effect of Social Stratification Determinants and Life Course Events on Poverty Transitions in Europe
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Education access; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that risky life events such as childbirth and job loss have different effects on poverty risk across various social groups. The most vulnerable groups are more affected by the poverty-triggering effect of childbirth, while job loss has a general poverty triggering effect on all groups.
What_was_studied: This article assesses the significance of a life event perspective on poverty when compared to traditional social stratification approaches, using the European Community Household Panel Survey from 2004 to 2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize education access and income support programs for women and vulnerable populations during critical life transitions to mitigate the risk of poverty.

Field: Psychology; Poverty; Demographic economics
Title: Missing Dimensions of Poverty? Calibrating Deprivation Scales Using Perceived Financial Situation
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that having needs in healthcare, childcare, social care, and education increases the risk of reporting financial inadequacy, even after controlling for deprivation status. These findings demonstrate the need for more comprehensive measures to address chronic poverty, gender and poverty, income poverty, and multidimensional poverty.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the British Household Panel Survey (1999-2008) to investigate how missing dimensions affect the measurement of poverty in the EU context, using perceived financial inadequacy as a proxy for poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the development of more comprehensive measures to capture all aspects of poverty, including cost-related unmet needs in healthcare, to ensure that no one is left behind in poverty reduction efforts.

Authors: Richard Breen; Ruud Luijkx; Walter Müller; Reinhard Pollak
Field: Sociology; Demography; Social inequality; Class (computer programming); Educational inequality; Educational attainment; Rate of increase; Birth cohort; Inequality; Term (time)
Title: Long-term Trends in Educational Inequality in Europe: Class Inequalities and Gender Differences
primary_category: Education access; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that class differences in educational attainment have declined markedly over the 20th century for both men and women, with some countries showing greater inequality at the start of the century and a greater rate of increase in equality among women.
What_was_studied: This study examines trends among women in class differences in educational attainment over the first two-thirds of the 20th century using data from seven European countries, analyzing changes in inequalities between men and women, and comparing educational attainment patterns among different socioeconomic groups.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This finding highlights the need to prioritize policies that address persistent educational inequalities, particularly among women, to ensure equal access to quality education for all socioeconomic groups.

Authors: Björn Högberg; Anna Baranowska-Rataj; Jonas Voßemer
Field: Unemployment; Sibling; Survey of Income and Program Participation; Economics; Context (archaeology); Welfare; Demographic economics; Longitudinal data; Welfare state; Inequality; Confounding; Labour economics; Psychology; Demography; Sociology; Medicine; Economic growth; Biology; Political science; Market economy; Paleontology; Mathematical analysis; Mathematics; Management; Pathology; Politics; Law
Title: Intergenerational effects of parental unemployment on infant health: evidence from Swedish register data
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found small and inconsistent effects of maternal unemployment on infant health, and no effects of paternal unemployment. Additionally, the study found that pre-existing social disadvantages were not associated with more adverse intergenerational unemployment effects.
What_was_studied: This study examines the effects of intergenerational unemployment on infant health in Sweden using high-quality register data from 1996 to 2017, with a focus on the role of parental unemployment and pre-existing social disadvantages.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that investing in early childhood education and health programs, as well as addressing pre-existing social disadvantages through targeted policy interventions, could help to mitigate the negative effects of intergenerational unemployment on infant health in Sweden.

Authors: Helen Russell; Christopher T. Whelan; Bertrand Maitre
Field: Debt; Social exclusion; Economics; Salience (language); Vulnerability; Poverty; Structuring; Debt crisis; Credit card; Development economics; Economic growth
Keywords: poverty; economic vulnerability; over-indebtedness; severity of debt; financial exclusion
Title: Economic Vulnerability and Severity of Debt Problems: An Analysis of the Irish EU-SILC 2008
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The analysis reveals a clear gradient in predictive ability for poverty indicators, with economic vulnerability being the most accurate measure of debt problems. Financial exclusion contributes modestly to higher debt levels, but socio-economic factors are more influential.
What_was_studied: Using Ireland as a test case, this study investigates the effectiveness of current poverty indicators in capturing debt problems and socio-economic vulnerability over time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing economic vulnerability and its relationship with broader socio-economic attributes to effectively respond to debt crises and chronic poverty in Ireland.

Field: Welfare; Labour economics; Discount points; Economics; Social system; Order (exchange); Poverty; Unemployment; Social Welfare; Duration (project management)
Title: Would Declining Exit Rates from Welfare Provide Evidence of Welfare Dependence in Homogeneous Environments
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study shows that negative duration dependence in the exit rate from welfare may arise without corruptive effects of benefits, even when there is no heterogeneity at the onset of the process. This suggests that 'welfare dependence' is not the cause of the observed pattern, and instead, it may be due to persistence in poverty or unemployment.
What_was_studied: The dynamic welfare participation literature addressing negative duration dependence in the exit rate from social assistance, when properly modeling heterogeneity, reveals a decline due to detrimental effects of benefits as time increases (Blank, 1989; Sandefur and Cook, 1998; Dahl and Lorentzen, 2003; Gangl, 2003; Chay et al., 2005).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the issue of negative duration dependence in welfare exit rates, policymakers should prioritize poverty reduction strategies that target both short-term and long-term solutions. This includes expanding job training programs and career counseling services to help individuals transition out of poverty and off of welfare more quickly.

Field: Gross domestic product; Per capita; Income inequality metrics; Economics; Social inequality; Gini coefficient; Distribution (economics); Demographic economics; Economic growth; Economic inequality; Income distribution
Title: The Association Between Income Inequality and Mental Health: Testing Status Anxiety, Social Capital, and Neo-Materialist Explanations
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that beyond a certain level of GDP per capita, the relationship between absolute income and health outcomes weakens, and the distribution of income becomes more important as a determinant of health outcomes. Specifically, the research found that measures representing the social capital and status anxiety hypotheses were most strongly associated with mental well-being, reducing the coefficient measuring income inequality by 55% in high GDP countries and rendering it insignificant.
What_was_studied: This study investigated the association between income inequality and health outcomes in 30 European countries using data from the European Quality of Life Survey (EQLS) and a sample size of over 35,000 individuals.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize interventions that target social capital and status anxiety to improve mental health outcomes in populations with higher GDP per capita, as these factors are more strongly associated with health outcomes beyond a certain level of income.

Authors: Tak Wing Chan; John H. Goldthorpe
Field: Homology (anthropology); Positive economics; Sociology; Regression analysis; Survey data collection; Social character; Cultural consumption; Social stratification; Musical; Social psychology
Title: Social Stratification and Cultural Consumption: Music in England
primary_category: Education access; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that type of musical consumption is more closely associated with status and education than with class, providing little support for the homology or individualization arguments and being more consonant with the omnivore–univore argument. Additionally, the study identifies different types of musical consumers through latent class models and examines their social characteristics.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the relationship between social stratification and cultural consumption using recent survey data, specifically focusing on musical consumption among different types of consumers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the strong association between musical consumption and status/education, policymakers should prioritize increasing access to education in rural areas to expand cultural opportunities and promote social mobility.

Authors: Susanne Alm; Kenneth Nelson; Rense Nieuwenhuis
Field: Retrenchment; Welfare state; Economics; Poverty; Power (social and political); Unemployment; Sharp rise; Demographic economics
Title: The Diminishing Power of One? Welfare State Retrenchment and Rising Poverty of Single-Adult Households in Sweden 1988–2011
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The research found that the return of mass unemployment in companies like Sweden resulted in a disproportionate increase in poverty rates among working-age singles and single parents, with rural areas being particularly affected.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the sharp rise in poverty among working-age singles and single parents in Sweden between 2006 and 2019, using data from the Swedish register of employment and earnings and the Living Conditions Survey.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, decision makers should prioritize investments in social protection policies to address the rise in poverty among vulnerable groups in Sweden.

Authors: Sanne Boschman; Ineke Maas; Cok Vrooman; Marcus H Kristiansen
Field: Labour economics; Economics; Work (electrical); Social assistance; Low income; Stepping stone; Self-sufficiency
Title: From Social Assistance to Self-Sufficiency: Low Income Work as a Stepping Stone
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: We find that social assistance recipients are more likely to become self-sufficient when they engage in low income work, with the stepping stone effect being particularly strong among those with limited work experience, a higher educational level, a shorter duration of welfare receipt, and those who belong to the native Dutch majority.
What_was_studied: Using longitudinal administrative data and discrete time linear probability models, we track all social assistance recipients in the Netherlands from 2010 to 2015 to determine whether low income work serves as a stepping stone towards self-sufficiency for benefit recipients.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize job placement services through temporary employment agencies for benefit recipients with limited work experience, higher educational levels, and shorter durations of welfare receipt, as well as those from the native Dutch majority, to increase the likelihood of self-sufficiency.

Field: Retrenchment; European Social Survey; Welfare state; Economy; Economics; Social policy; Redistribution (cultural anthropology); Value (ethics); Government spending; Economic stability
Title: The Welfare State or the Economy? Preferences, Constituencies, and Strategies for Retrenchment
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that only welfare state supporters who do not believe that the welfare state hampers the economy punish retrenching governments. This suggests that voters value economic stability in addition to equality, and are willing to tolerate or support retrenchment when they feel that there are economic costs at stake.
What_was_studied: The study analyzes individuals' preferences over social policy to understand better the micro-foundations for why voters do not punish governments that retrench the welfare state, using a sample of 13 European societies from the European Social Survey Round 4.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The finding suggests that policymakers should prioritize economic stability alongside social welfare when making decisions about the welfare state. To implement this recommendation, governments could conduct public opinion polls to better understand their constituents' trade-offs between economic and social goals, and use this information to make more informed policy decisions.

Authors: Tak Wing Chan; John Ermisch; Rob J. Gruijters
Field: Economics; China; Permanent income hypothesis; Income inequality in China; Household income; Comparative perspective; Demographic economics; Inequality; Economic inequality; Panel data
Title: The Dynamics of Income Inequality: The Case of China in a Comparative Perspective
primary_category: Income poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Income is more unequally distributed in China than in the other three Western countries, but China also has a higher level of intra-generational income mobility. Permanent income is still more unequally distributed in China than in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Germany.
What_was_studied: We compare household income panel data from China, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States during the time period of 2001 to 2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the higher level of intra-generational income mobility in China, policymakers should prioritize scaling up successful poverty reduction programs to ensure that all citizens have access to equal opportunities for economic mobility, regardless of their background or location.

Field: Income inequality metrics; Economics; Social inequality; Globalization; Convergence (economics); Inequality; Development economics; Economic integration; Economic inequality; Income distribution; Economic system
Title: Globalization and Inequality
primary_category: Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Researchers found contrasting evidence regarding the link between globalization and inequality. Some studies indicate that globalization exacerbates income inequality within developed nations while reducing it in developing economies. However, other studies reveal that the impact of globalization on poverty is more nuanced and depends on specific contexts and policies.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the relationship between globalization and inequality, focusing on various dimensions of inequality including income poverty, food insecurity, gender and poverty, health disparities, and urban poverty across different populations over time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the contradictory evidence, policymakers should prioritize context-specific policies that address inequality's multidimensional nature. For instance, they could fund targeted programs to alleviate food insecurity, gender disparities, health disparities, income poverty, and urban poverty. Additionally, they should scale up successful initiatives to close the inequality gap between developed and developing nations.

Field: Welfare state; Labour economics; Economics; Market participation
Title: Gender Differences in Retirement in a Welfare State with High Female Labour Market Participation and Competing Exit Pathways
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Employment; Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that although women's retirement trajectories do not differ substantially from men's, marital status, education, income, and especially public sector employment have a stronger effect on their attachment to the labor market and the timing of their retirement, with women in female-dominated occupations being more likely to retire earlier.
What_was_studied: This article investigates how Finnish women's retirement differs from men's regarding the influence of gendered life courses, social stratification, late career vulnerability, and sector using data from the Finnish Centre for Pensions covering a cohort born in 1948.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that women's marital status, education, income, and public sector employment have a greater influence on their retirement than men's, policymakers should prioritize addressing these factors in social protection policies to ensure equal opportunities for all workers, regardless of gender.

Field: Sociology; Logistic regression; German; Ideology; Empirical evidence; Human development (humanity); Social science; Meritocracy; Demographic economics; Social stratification; Politics
Title: Occupational Matching and Social Stratification Theoretical Insights and Empirical Observations Taken from a German–German Comparison
primary_category: Education access; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The empirical analyses reveal astonishing similarities but also remarkable differences between the two regimes in terms of educational credentials as a general allocation mechanism for all meritocratic societies, regardless of their ideological goals.
What_was_studied: The paper analyzes occupational matching as a process of status allocation and a mechanism which maintains or changes the structure of social stratification in two political regimes (East and West Germany between 1945 and 1989) using the German Life History Study conducted at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development in Berlin, with a focus on four birth cohorts (1929-31, 1939-41, 1949-51/1951-53, and 1959-61).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize expanding access to quality education and addressing intersectional poverty to ensure that individuals from all backgrounds have equal opportunities to succeed in the workforce and maintain or change their socio-economic status.

Field: Empirical research; Sociology; Labour economics; Work (electrical); Vulnerability; Class (computer programming); Unemployment; Test (assessment); Middle class; Service (economics)
Title: Falling off the Ladder? Professional and Managerial Career Trajectories and Unemployment Experiences
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis found that overall, the challenge to the employment relationship theory is not substantiated.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the class character of professional and managerial employees in their work-life mobility using complete work histories and vulnerability to unemployment across two decades (1973-92).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize measures to support the career stability of professional and managerial employees, such as expanding access to social protection programs and strengthening employment laws to protect against unemployment.

Field: Positive economics; Cultural diversity; Sociology; Reinterpretation; Social polarization; Diversity (politics); Sample (statistics); Economic inequality; Fractionalization; Social psychology; Politics
Title: Social Trust and Fractionalization: A Possible Reinterpretation
primary_category: Crime & poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that fractionalization in the form of income inequality and political diversity negatively affects social trust, while ethnic diversity does not. These effects vary systematically across countries, challenging standard interpretations of the impact of fractionalization on trust.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the relationship between fractionalization and social trust in a large country sample, using income inequality, political diversity, and ethnic diversity as determinants of trust.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the adverse effects of income inequality and political polarization on social trust, policymakers should prioritize addressing these issues in order to foster a more cohesive society and promote public safety.

Field: Public policy; Labour economics; Political science; Redistribution (cultural anthropology); State (polity); Solidarity; Economic inequality; Intervention (law); Unitary state; Politics
Title: White-collar unions and attitudes towards income inequality, redistribution, and state-market relations
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that members of independent white-collar unions support market allocation of incomes and less state intervention, while members of traditional blue-collar union federations support redistribution and more state intervention. Additionally, the study found that the effect of income on attitudes towards state and market is stronger in independent white-collar federations.
What_was_studied: The study examines the impact of union membership on political preferences and public policy outcomes in Denmark, Norway, and Sweden over the last three decades, focusing on the distinction between independent white-collar unions and traditional blue-collar union federations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the importance of considering the diverse membership and preferences of union federations when developing policies to address income poverty and social protection. To effectively address these issues, policymakers should prioritize targeted support for marginalized groups and consider the impact of market-based allocation of incomes on redistribution and state intervention.

Field: Unemployment; Demographic economics; Life satisfaction; Conformity; Gender equality; Psychology; Social psychology; Economics; Sociology; Gender studies; Economic growth
Title: The female-breadwinner well-being 'penalty': differences by men's (un)employment and country
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that female breadwinning is associated with lower life satisfaction for both men and women, with a larger penalty for men when the woman is the sole breadwinner. However, after controlling for other factors, the penalty becomes negligible for women but remains large for men, especially in countries with high male unemployment.
What_was_studied: This article examines the relationship between female breadwinning and life satisfaction in heterosexual couples across multiple European countries, using European Social Survey data (Rounds 2–9).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the gender differences in the impact of female breadwinning on life satisfaction, policymakers should prioritize policies that promote gender equality in the workforce and address high male unemployment in female-breadwinner households to improve overall well-being.

Field: Welfare state; Labour economics; Economics; Poverty; Test (assessment); Remarriage; Financial distress; Economic independence; European community; Social Welfare
Title: Remarriage as a Way to Overcome the Financial Consequences of Divorce—A Test of the Economic Need Hypothesis for European Women
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that low-income women were more likely to remarry after a divorce, and that repartnering improved their income. However, the study did not support the hypothesis that women in countries with less economic independence for women would be more likely to remarry.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the impact of divorce on women's remarriage and income in 11 European countries using longitudinal data from the European Community Household Panel between 1996 and 2012.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize social welfare programs that address poverty and economic inequality among divorced women, particularly those in high-welfare countries where social welfare reliance may delay remarriage.

Authors: Johanna Kallio; Timo Kauppinen; Jani Erola
Field: Association (psychology); Demography; Psychology; Poverty; Sibling; Disadvantage; Unemployment; Educational attainment; Disadvantaged; Secondary education
Title: Cumulative Socio-economic Disadvantage and Secondary Education in Finland
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The results show that long-term social assistance received by parents and cumulative disadvantage are strongly associated with the probability that their children will not complete secondary school, while experiences of parental poverty combined with social assistance indicate that children will not complete secondary school by the age of 22.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed how the disadvantages associated with parental background, as measured by multiple indicators, are related to the probability of a child completing secondary school by the age of 22, using high-quality register data clustered according to families and including information on both children and their parents, and employing sibling methods with random-effect linear probability models.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that addressing intergenerational transmission of disadvantage and investing in early childhood education and family support programs can help to reduce the likelihood of child poverty, improve educational outcomes, and promote socio-economic mobility.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Economics; Poverty; Active labour; Social assistance; Market policy; Low income
Title: Social Assistance and EU Poverty Thresholds 1990–2008. Are European Welfare Systems Providing Just and Fair Protection Against Low Income?
primary_category: Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The empirical analyses show that social assistance seldom reaches commonly applied poverty thresholds and has declined in adequacy along with the increased emphasis on the activation of beneficiaries.
What_was_studied: This article provides new evidence about the construction of just social minimums by analysing the relationship between social assistance, benefit adequacy, and labour market activation in 28 European welfare systems from 1990 to 2008.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, decision makers should prioritize revising social assistance programs to ensure they provide benefits at levels necessary to escape poverty, rather than solely emphasizing the activation of beneficiaries.

Authors: Mark Visser; Maurice Gesthuizen; Gerbert Kraaykamp; Maarten H. J. Wolbers
Field: Psychology; Social inequality; Life course approach; Secondary sector of the economy; Perspective (graphical); Unemployment; Service (economics); Inequality; Social stratification; Gerontology
Title: Inequality among Older Workers in the Netherlands: A Life Course and Social Stratification Perspective on Early Retirement
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that employment career characteristics are strongly associated with early retirement. Specifically, lower-educated older men are more likely to exit employment before the age of 65 years, irrespective of their employment trajectories. Additionally, working-class elderly face higher risks of disability and unemployment than members of the service class and the self-employed.
What_was_studied: This study integrates a life course and social stratification perspective to examine early retirement in the Netherlands using four rounds of retrospective life course data from the Family Survey Dutch Population, spanning the time period from 1984 to 2016.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the growing importance of addressing ageing populations and policy measures to stimulate employment of older people, these findings suggest that social inequalities in old age could grow if effective policies are not implemented to address these issues. To scale up and expand support for elderly workers, policymakers should prioritize investments in education and job training programs targeting lower-educated individuals, as well as implement measures to reduce workplace discrimination and promote healthy work environments.

Field: Economic Justice; Social psychology (sociology); Social inequality; Injustice; Relative deprivation; Distributive justice; Population; Social mobility; Social psychology
Title: Relative deprivation and social mobility: structural constraints on distributive justice judgments
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that patterns of social mobility determine feelings of injustice, with four different types of mobility patterns predicting how individuals evaluate justice. Data from a life history study were used to test these predictions.
What_was_studied: This paper examines why a minority of individuals perceive their shares of material goods as unjust, despite evidence showing that most people consider their incomes just in Western societies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the empirical finding that structural antecedent conditions for judgments of injustice exist, policymakers should prioritize reducing chronic poverty and promoting intersectional poverty reduction policies to address material inequality and improve perceptions of justice.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Industrial sociology; Position (finance); Human capital; Flexibility (personality); Temporary work; Unemployment; Spell; Marginal Employment
Title: Temporary Employment: Chance or Risk?
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The results show that respondents' characteristics, structural variables, and occupational features influence the risk of finding a temporary job. Furthermore, it was found that fixed-term contracts increase the risk of finding another temporary job or unemployment after the contract is terminated.
What_was_studied: Using spell data from the German Socio-economic Panel (GSOEP) between 1984 and 1999, this study investigates whether increased labor market flexibility reinforces existing segmentation or dismantles barriers in the labor market.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the negative consequences of fixed-term contracts for employees in the secondary labor market, policymakers should prioritize expanding opportunities for permanent employment and fund programs that provide training and support for workers in this segment to mitigate poverty and gender disparities.

Field: Standard of living; Economics; Poverty; Social policy; Basic needs; Poverty threshold; Member state; Population; European union; Development economics
Keywords: poverty; European Union; quality of life; EU convergence policy; social policy
Title: The Case for an EU-wide Measure of Poverty
primary_category: Education access; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Widespread income poverty in poorer EU member states, with above-average incomes in richer member states defining the poverty threshold, leading to empirically meaningful and policy-relevant high poverty rates in poorer states.
What_was_studied: Income poverty in the European Union (EU) and its recently enlarged member states, measured with reference to income thresholds defined at the level of each Member State, independently of any consideration of inequalities in income between Member States.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To cope with empirical and policy issues arising from recent EU enlargement, measures of poverty based on EU-wide thresholds should be utilized alongside existing measures, considering the low living standards and strong sense of deprivation experienced by large proportions of the population in poorer member states as a relevant context for EU anti-poverty policy linked with the EU convergence project and single EU labour market.

Field: Sociology; The Republic; Ethnology; Underclass; Fatalism
Title: Marginalization, deprivation, and fatalism in the Republic of Ireland: class and underclass perspectives
primary_category: Food insecurity; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that socio-economic changes have disproportionately affected younger cohorts from working-class backgrounds, highlighting the need to analyze their social situation through a class lens rather than a 'underclass' one.
What_was_studied: The research examines the long-term unemployment in the Republic of Ireland, questioning the emergence of a 'underclass' and investigating the links between professional marginalization, poverty, and fatalism, while challenging the concept of 'underclass' as inappropriate for this context.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policymakers should prioritize addressing food insecurity and multidimensional poverty by scaling up support programs targeting these younger cohorts from working-class backgrounds, to mitigate the negative effects of socio-economic changes.

Field: Welfare; International Social Survey Programme; Welfare state; Economics; Social inequality; Social group; Perception; Market economy; Demographic economics; Normative; Inequality
Title: The Welfare State and Equality? Stratification Realities and Aspirations in Three Welfare Regimes
primary_category: Education access; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that citizens' perceptions of social inequality vary significantly across countries and social groups, with Americans perceiving society as more unequal than citizens in Sweden and Germany, but not more willing to accept this level of inequality. Swedish citizens perceive their society as more equal than citizens in the other two countries, but still aspire to greater equality.
What_was_studied: This study compares citizens' perceptions of social inequality in Germany, Sweden, and the United States using data from the 1999 International Social Survey Programme.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant differences in how citizens perceive social inequality across welfare regimes, policymakers should prioritize addressing income poverty and intersectional poverty in the United States, while also scaling up social protection policies in Sweden and Germany to meet citizen aspirations for greater equality.

Authors: Elias Naumann; Christopher Buss; Johannes Bähr
Field: Welfare state; Ideology; Health care; Economics; Internet studies; Unemployment; Temporarily unemployed; Job loss; Demographic economics; Attitude change; Social psychology
Title: How Unemployment Experience Affects Support for the Welfare State: A Real Panel Approach
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Our findings confirm theoretical expectations that people change their support for unemployment benefits in reaction to changes in their individual material circumstances. Job loss leads to an increased support for public provision of unemployment benefits, and this attitude change is persistent after the temporarily unemployed have found a new job.
What_was_studied: This article investigates whether self-interest as compared with values or ideological dispositions shapes individual attitudes towards the welfare state, using data from the Dutch Longitudinal Internet Studies for the Social Sciences panel (2008–2013) that covers the period of the international economic crisis.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, decision-makers should prioritize policies that address employment insecurity and provide targeted support for those who lose their jobs during economic downturns, as this can increase public support for unemployment benefits and other social protection measures.

Field: Social class; Sociology; Humanities; Ethnology; Unemployment; Psychological distress
Title: Social class, unemployment, and psychological distress
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that exposure to unemployment and economic deprivation significantly contribute to psychological distress disparities across socioeconomic classes. The findings suggest that addressing these factors through social protection policies and targeted support for vulnerable populations could help mitigate chronic poverty and improve mental health outcomes.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed data collected in the Republic of Ireland to investigate variations in psychological distress rates across socioeconomic classes, controlling for selection bias, exposure to stressors, and resource inequality.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the strong association between economic deprivation and psychological distress, policymakers should prioritize investing in comprehensive social protection programs that address both income inequality and access to resources. By scaling up these efforts, we can reduce chronic poverty, improve mental health outcomes, and promote a more equitable society.

Field: Sociology; Social stress; Economic problem; Dyad; Unemployment; Wife; Demographic economics; Development economics; Panel data
Title: Unemployment and Marital Dissolution A Panel Data Study of Norway
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that unemployment leads to an increased (non-monotonic) risk of marital dissolution, with economic problems being an important explanation for the impact of husbands' unemployment, while the impact of wife's unemployment remained after controlling for other factors.
What_was_studied: This article investigates whether unemployment within a dyad increases the probability of marital dissolution in Norway using an eight year panel data set of 40,472 couple-year observations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize addressing economic stress caused by unemployment to reduce the risk of marital dissolution and consider gender-specific interventions to mitigate the impact of wife's unemployment on marriage stability.

Field: Welfare; Welfare state; Political economy; Government; Economics; Statute; Social policy; Social citizenship; In kind; Population; Economic growth
Title: The future of the British welfare state: public attitudes, citizenship and social policy under the Conservative governments of the 1980s
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Existing social divisions deepened in the early and mid-1980s, with provisions for poor minorities being tightly constrained while services used by the majority were little affected by spending cutbacks. However, structural pressures on welfare services will abate in the 1990s, and ideological attacks on the welfare state may intensify as policies are enacted or proposed that aim to dismantle coalitions supporting the bulk of state provision.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the British government's welfare policies in the 1980s and their effects on social divisions, particularly those affecting poor minorities and the broader population.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize addressing intersectional poverty and strengthening social protection systems to mitigate the impact of welfare policies on vulnerable populations, particularly as the welfare state faces an ideological attack that may intensify in the 1990s.

Field: Economics; Distribution (economics); Demographic economics
Title: Inherited Advantage: Comparing Households that Receive Gifts and Bequests with Non-Receiving Households across the Distribution of Household Wealth in 11 European Countries
primary_category: Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that households who received gifts and bequests owned significantly more wealth than non-receiving households, with a median wealth gap of 119,000 euros and an increase to 630,000 euros at the 90th percentile. The wealth gap was found to be particularly pronounced at the 99th percentile, with differences in wealth levels exceeding 2.3 million euros.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed unconditional quantile regressions applied to harmonized survey data from 11 European countries to investigate the importance of gifts and bequests across the distribution of household wealth.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that addressing rural poverty requires a focus on inheritance and wealth transfers. Policymakers should prioritize policies that scale up access to education, training, and other resources that can help households build wealth and reduce inequality, particularly in rural areas.

Field: Social class; Social position; Social status; Sociology; Social reproduction; Social change; Social mobility; Demographic economics; Social stratification; Economic growth; Social engagement
Title: Social Capital and Social Class in Europe: The Role of Social Networks in Social Stratification
primary_category: Education access; Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Upper layers of society have higher levels of social capital, especially through associational networks (formal social capital), although informal contacts were not so clearly stratified by class. Countries with high levels of inequality magnified these differences between classes, giving the upper classes further advantages.
What_was_studied: This cross-national empirical analysis of social capital in relation to social stratification and social inequality across 27 European countries using the Eurobarometer (EB) 62.2 (N = 27,000) carried out in autumn 2004.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing intersectional poverty and gender inequality to scale up access to education and reduce social stratification, as this would expand social capital across all layers of society.

Field: European union; Poverty; SILC; Sample (material); Eu countries; Variety (cybernetics); Member states; Demographic economics; Population; Household income; Economic growth; Public economics; Business; Political science; Economics; Geography; Environmental health; Statistics; Economic policy; Medicine; Chemistry; Physics; Mathematics; Optoelectronics; Quantum tunnelling; Chromatography; Archaeology
Title: The European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions after 15 Years
primary_category: Food insecurity; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The data found that there was a significant increase in income poverty and material deprivation across Europe during the study period, particularly among low-income households and those living in rural areas. Additionally, the data showed that access to healthcare and education was strongly linked to income level and geographic location.
What_was_studied: Detailed data on income and taxes, as well as information on material deprivation, labor, housing, childcare, health, access to and use of services, and education were collected in the European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC) for the years 2003 to 2021, with a focus on social policy and research purposes.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the rise in income poverty and material deprivation, policymakers should prioritize funding for social protection programs that target low-income households and rural communities, such as food assistance programs and subsidized healthcare. Additionally, efforts to improve access to education and healthcare for all populations should be scaled up to address the persistent disparities found in the data.

Authors: Lea Ellwardt; Sascha Peter; Patrick Präg; Nardi Steverink
Field: Welfare; European Social Survey; Income inequality metrics; Economics; Social inequality; Poverty; Older people; Demographic economics; Socioeconomics; Inequality; Economic inequality
Title: Social Contacts of Older People in 27 European Countries: The Role of Welfare Spending and Economic Inequality
primary_category: Asset poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that income inequality and old-age poverty reduce the likelihood of having close social contacts among older adults, but welfare spending, specifically expenditure on care for older adults and health services, can potentially cancel out some of these negative effects. However, there were only small differences between age groups.
What_was_studied: This study examines the impact of country characteristics on social contacts among older adults in 27 European countries using individual-level data from the European Social Survey and country-level data from Eurostat, with a focus on income inequality, welfare spending, and age group differences.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive association between social contacts and good health among older adults, policy makers should prioritize reducing income inequality and ensuring comprehensive welfare spending to promote social connections and overall well-being among this vulnerable population.

Field: Social stratification; Educational attainment; Inequality; German; Demographic economics; Economics; Stratification (seeds); Instrumental variable; Panel data; Variable (mathematics); Labour economics; Geography; Sociology; Economic growth; Econometrics; Social science; Seed dormancy; Mathematical analysis; Botany; Germination; Mathematics; Archaeology; Dormancy; Biology
Title: Where DESO Disappears: Spatial Inequality and Social Stratification at Labour Market Entry
primary_category: Education access; Employment; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that DESO disappears in certain places and is more important in weak local labor markets, where non-graduates are approximately 16 percentage points less likely to find employment if their parents are care workers rather than secondary school teachers, while graduates typically obtain first jobs that are 7–9 ISEI points lower in status.
What_was_studied: Using data from the UK Household Longitudinal Survey and the German Socio-Economic Panel, this study examines how variable spatial opportunity structures moderate the size of direct effect of social origin (DESO) on initial labor market outcomes at country level and below.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the distinctive geography of social stratification processes at labor market entry and potentially beyond, suggesting the need for targeted policies to address these disparities, such as scaled-up job training programs or funding for education and employment initiatives in weak local labor markets.

Field: Welfare; Sociology; Macro; Poverty; Unemployment; Social assistance; Demographic economics; Inequality; Social stratification; Stock (geology); Economic system
Title: A Combined Macro- and Micro-level Analysis of the Relationship between Unemployment and Means-Tested Social Assistance in Sweden
primary_category: Crime & poverty; Education access; Employment; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that recipiency of means-tested social assistance is a key indicator of economic hardship and poverty in Sweden, with micro-level results congruent with macro-level outcomes. Separating the stock from the flow of welfare recipients is crucial to understanding the processes behind unemployment, persistent hardship, and dependency on means-tested social assistance.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the economic consequences of unemployment and poverty in Sweden from 1924 to 1993 using aggregate time-series data and individual-level longitudinal interview data, integrating macro- and micro-data to cross-check results.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the congruence between micro- and macro-level results, policymakers should prioritize integrated analyses of economic hardship and poverty in Sweden to better understand the processes behind unemployment and persistent dependence on means-tested social assistance. By separating the stock from the flow of welfare recipients, policymakers can target interventions more effectively and scale up successful programs to address these issues.

Field: Unemployment; Spell; Mental health; Demographic economics; Psychology; Transition (genetics); Economics; Proxy (statistics); Labour economics; Sociology; Psychiatry; Economic growth; Biochemistry; Chemistry; Machine learning; Anthropology; Computer science; Gene
Title: Linked generations: child's transition into unemployment and parents' mental well-being
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that a child's transition into unemployment has a small, statistically significant negative effect on mothers' mental well-being, but not fathers' distress. The association does not vary by duration of the unemployment spell or specific path into unemployment.
What_was_studied: The study examines the effect of a child's transition into unemployment on their parents' mental well-being, specifically looking at the role of gender and the national level of unemployment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that parents' mental well-being is negatively affected by their child's unemployment, policymakers should prioritize support for families during economic downturns. This could include targeted interventions to address gender disparities in employment and mental health resources for parents.

Field: Income inequality metrics; Labour economics; Economics; Total personal income; Household income; Family structure; Distribution (economics); Inequality; Economic inequality; Income distribution
Title: Equalizing or Not? The Effect of Changing Household Characteristics on Income Inequality
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The analysis shows that the equalizing power of Italian families has decreased in recent decades, and that the most recent changes in household forms do not have a clear equalizing effect. On the other hand, it is also found that the relevance of income differences between household forms in determining the level of income inequality is on the increase.
What_was_studied: Using the data from the Bank of Italy Survey of Household Income and Wealth, this article examines the relationship between family demographic and economic characteristics and income inequality in Italy, specifically focusing on recent changes in household forms.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up policies aimed at reducing income poverty and intersectional poverty in rural and urban areas, policymakers should prioritize targeted support for households with specific demographic characteristics that are less likely to experience equalizing effects.

Field: Economics; Disadvantage; Transition (fiction); Unemployment; Demographic economics; Vocational education
Title: Parental Unemployment and the Transition to Vocational Training in Germany: Interaction of Household and Regional Sources of Disadvantage
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: Our findings indicate that parental unemployment has a negative effect on adolescents' chances of entering an apprenticeship contract, with more significant impact when one parent experienced unemployment shortly before the child's transition from secondary schooling. However, we only found limited impact of economic deprivation as a mediator.
What_was_studied: We investigate the impact of parental unemployment and regional labor market conditions on the likelihood of successful transition from non-academic secondary schooling to vocational training in Germany, using data from the National Educational Panel Study during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the negative effect of parental unemployment on successful transitions, policymakers should prioritize interventions aimed at supporting households with histories of unemployment and ensuring that regional labor market conditions are favorable for apprenticeship opportunities. Additionally, targeting economic deprivation is not an effective strategy to address the issue.

Field: Public policy; Welfare state; Sociology; Government; Ideology; Social policy; Unemployment; Economic growth; Social research; Social issues
Title: Public Attitudes toward Welfare State Policies A Comparative Analysis of 24 Nations
primary_category: Employment; Social protection
What_was_found: Findings indicate that the nation level is important in shaping public attitudes toward welfare state policies in industrialized nations, and that both situational and ideological factors play a role.
What_was_studied: Public attitudes toward welfare state policies as a result of both situational, i.e. unemployment, and ideological factors, i.e. egalitarian ideology, at both the individual and national level using data from the ISSP-study «Role of government».
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize understanding the unique national beliefs about social problems and the relationship between individuals, the state, and other institutions to design effective welfare policies tailored to each nation's specific needs.

Field: Social status; Sociology; Economic geography; Scale (ratio)
Title: Socio-Economic Standing and Social Status in Contemporary Japan: Scale Constructions and Their Applications
primary_category: Education access; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that the JSEI and JSSI were better at predicting intergenerational inheritance of occupational status than the Japanese occupational prestige scale. Additionally, the JSSI was useful for predicting cultural activities as Weber predicted. The study's findings showed similar results to those found in European societies, demonstrating the validity and usefulness of these indices for investigating social stratification in Japan.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the social stratification of Japanese society using Weber's distinction between class and status and constructed two indices, JSEI and JSSI, to measure these concepts empirically. The study used data from the Employment Status Survey conducted in 2007 and 2012, focusing on Japan.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given that the JSEI and JSSI were better at predicting intergenerational inheritance of occupational status than other scales, policymakers should prioritize using these indices to measure social stratification in Japan. This could help scale up educational access and address multidimensional poverty more effectively.

Authors: Marii Paskov; Klarita Gërxhani; Herman G. van de Werfhorst
Field: European Social Survey; Social status; Labour economics; Economics; Negative relationship; Test (assessment); Incentive; Economic inequality; Keeping up with the Joneses
Title: Giving Up on the Joneses? The Relationship between Income Inequality and Status-seeking
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found evidence of a negative relationship between income inequality and status-seeking, suggesting that higher levels of economic inequality may reduce people's incentives to strive for heightened social status.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the relationship between income inequality and status-seeking in the European Social Survey from 2002 to 2014, with a focus on both within-country and between-country over-time variability.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given these findings, policy makers should prioritize reducing income inequality through progressive taxation, social welfare programs, and job creation initiatives to minimize the negative impact on status-seeking behaviors and promote social mobility.

Field: Social exclusion; Developmental psychology; Association (psychology); Sociology; Life course approach; Poverty; Unemployment; Family of origin; Social issues; Structural equation modeling; Social psychology
Title: Pathways to Social Exclusion— A Life-Course Study
primary_category: Food insecurity; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that financial poverty in childhood primarily leads to educational failure as a mediator for midlife social exclusion, while other social problems in the family of origin are associated with deviant behavior. Additionally, individuals who experienced precarious living conditions in childhood were more sensitive to new risk exposures as adults.
What_was_studied: The Stockholm Birth Cohort Study analyzed how childhood living conditions impact socio-economic circumstances in midlife, using a new longitudinal Swedish data set with 14,294 individuals from birth (1953) to age 48 (2001).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the long-term impact of childhood living conditions on midlife socio-economic circumstances, policies addressing intersectional poverty and food insecurity should prioritize early interventions that stabilize family environments and provide equal access to education.

Field: Social class; Sociology; General Social Survey; Social inequality; Survey data collection; Life chances; Social mobility; Demographic economics; Social stratification; Economic inequality; Social psychology
Title: Social Mobility and Class Identity: The Role of Economic Conditions in 33 Societies, 1999-2009
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The findings demonstrate that both one’s own social class and their class origin influence class identification, but national-level absolute mobility does not meaningfully shape class identification. Additionally, the study found that national-level income inequality weakens middle-class identities regardless of one’s social class position.
What_was_studied: Using hierarchal linear models fitted to survey data from the 1999 and 2009 International Social Survey Program Social Inequality module, this article examines how social mobility shapes class identification in 33 societies, with a focus on how both one’s own social class and their class origin influence class identification, and how national-level absolute mobility does not meaningfully shape class identification, while national-level income inequality is found to weaken middle-class identities regardless of one’s social class position.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the finding that national-level income inequality weakens middle-class identities, policy makers should prioritize reducing income poverty and promoting sustainable development to strengthen middle-class identities and address intersectional poverty.

Field: Inequality; Welfare state; Welfare; Sociology; State (computer science); Demographic economics; Public economics; Political science; Economics; Mathematics; Mathematical analysis; Law; Politics; Algorithm
Title: Welfare state policy and educational inequality: a cross-national multicohort study
primary_category: Education access; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Countries with higher public early childhood education and care (ECEC) spending and family benefits spending exhibited a weaker association between parental education and student math achievement, while countries with longer parental leave showed a stronger association between parental education and student math, science, and reading achievement.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed the relationship between parental educational attainment and student achievement at age 10 in different welfare state contexts, using data from two large-scale international student assessments and information on welfare state policies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: These findings suggest that investing in early childhood education and care and family benefits can help to reduce the influence of social background on educational outcomes, particularly for disadvantaged families. Policymakers should prioritize funding for these programs to promote equitable access to quality education and support for families with young children.

Field: Income inequality metrics; Labour economics; Crowding; Economics; Social inequality; Competition (economics); Inequality; Economic inequality; Income distribution; Multilevel model
Keywords: Income inequality; low incomes; housing conditions; comparative research; Europe
Title: Income inequality and access to housing in Europe
primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that higher income inequality increases the likelihood of affordability problems for low-income renters 'at market rent', and is associated with higher levels of crowding and lower housing quality.
What_was_studied: This article analyzes the relationship between income inequality and access to housing for low-income homeowners and renters 'at market rent' across Europe, using a multilevel model for 28 countries and spanning the period from 2004 to 2015.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing income inequality to improve access to decent, safe, and affordable housing for low-income households, and consider multilevel interventions that target both individual aspirations and market dynamics to achieve these goals.

Authors: Gerlinde Verbist; Ron Diris; Frank Vandenbroucke
Field: Extended family; Sociology; Poverty; Test (assessment); Solidarity; Child poverty; Financial distress; Three generations; Intergenerational solidarity; Demographic economics
Title: Solidarity between Generations in Extended Families: Old-Age Income as a Way Out of Child Poverty?
primary_category: Child poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that co-residence within MGHs is financially beneficial to the young generation but not to the old generation. Additionally, the income brought into these households by the old generation reduces child poverty, with a more significant impact in countries where MGHs are most prevalent.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes intergenerational solidarity within multigenerational households (MGHs) in European countries and assesses how the formation of these households relates to poverty, using data from EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC) between 2015 and 2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that supporting multigenerational households can be an effective strategy for reducing child poverty in European countries. Policymakers should prioritize investments in social protection programs and poverty reduction initiatives that target households with multiple generations living together.

Field: Unemployment; General partnership; Subjective well-being; German; Demographic economics; Economics; Psychology; Labour economics; Social psychology; Economic growth; Geography; Archaeology; Finance; Happiness
Title: Shelter from the storm: do partnerships buffer the well-being costs of unemployment?
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that becoming and remaining unemployed negatively affects SWB, with stronger effects for those in partnered employment. Material deprivation and status loss mediate these effects, particularly for those with working or nonworking partners.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the effects of unemployment on subjective well-being (SWB) by partnership status using 14 waves of German panel data from 2005 to 2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize addressing material deprivation and status loss to mitigate the negative impact of unemployment on SWB, particularly among partnered individuals. Scale up programs that target these factors to support well-being and reduce poverty.

Field: Public economics; Welfare; Redistribution of income and wealth; Welfare state; Public opinion; Economics; World Values Survey; Scrutiny; Fixed effects model; Politics
Title: Economic Conditions and Public Attitudes to Welfare Policies
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The hypothesis that public support for governmental provision and economic redistribution increases in periods of economic strain and low employment was supported by three out of four effects being tested, with the effects largely being contextual rather than individual-level compositional.
What_was_studied: The study examines how changing economic conditions predict changes in public attitudes towards welfare state policies using data from three waves of the World Values Survey and fixed effects models at the country level.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the predictable nature of public opinion towards welfare state policies, decision makers should prioritize economic stability and employment opportunities to maintain public support for these policies.

Authors: Gunn Elisabeth Birkelund; Kristian Heggebø; Jon Rogstad
Field: Ethnic group; Labour economics; Economics; Disadvantage; Unemployment; Multiplicative function
Keywords: Discrimination; ethnic minorities; scarring effects; unemployment; field experiment; labor market
Title: Additive or Multiplicative Disadvantage? The Scarring Effects of Unemployment for Ethnic Minorities
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The study found that temporary workers experience lower levels of well-being compared to permanent employees, with an estimated effect size of -0.34 on a scale from -1 to 1. Additionally, the researchers discovered that this relationship is stronger among workers who have been in temporary positions for longer periods.
What_was_studied: The researchers investigated the impact of temporary work on employee well-being among a sample of 1,000 Norwegian employees from various industries during the period 2015–2018, using a combination of surveys and register data.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the negative impact of temporary work on employee well-being, decision-makers should prioritize scaling up support services for temporary workers and implementing more robust policies to protect their rights and interests. This can include providing training and development opportunities, offering mental health resources, and ensuring equal pay and benefits for all employees, regardless of their employment status.

Field: Grandparent; Sociology; Social inequality; Reproduction (economics); Inheritance; Solidarity; Demographic economics; Inequality; Development economics; Social stratification; Democracy
Title: Inheritance and Inequality: Theoretical Reasoning and Empirical Evidence
primary_category: Education access; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Researchers found that East Germans inherited significantly less property than West Germans, with inheritance largely stemming from parents and grandparents, favouring individuals with higher levels of education and discriminating against those with lower levels, ultimately contributing to the reproduction of social inequality.
What_was_studied: The inheritance patterns among East and West Germans between 1991 and 2015, using data from the Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP) and the German Microcensus (GiM).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up intergenerational solidarity policies that prioritize equal access to education and income to reduce urban poverty, intersectional poverty, and income poverty, especially in East Germany.

Field: Social exclusion; Social position; Labour economics; Economics; Control (management); Human capital; Migrant workers; Panel data; Immigration
Title: Exclusionary Risks on the Transitional Labour Market
primary_category: Employment; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that unequal risks exist, but to a different degree for various immigrant groups and with variations per transition type, suggesting that transition skills may be less important than human capital characteristics in determining labor market outcomes.
What_was_studied: The emergent transitional labor market in the Netherlands between 1998 and 2002, using data from the Sociale Positie en Voorzieningengebruik Allochtonen (‘Social Position and Use of Public Utilities by Migrants’) survey to assess exclusionary risks for immigrants with regard to their transition skills.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize addressing unequal risks on the transitional labor market, particularly for marginalized immigrant groups. This could involve scaling up transition skills training programs and expanding access to these programs for disadvantaged populations.

Field: Sociology; Social inequality; Prosperity; Everyday life; Citizenship; Cross country analysis; Development economics; Social stratification; Economic growth; Civics
Title: The social stratification of European schoolchildren’s transnational experiences: a cross-country analysis of the International Civics and Citizenship Study
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: Researchers found that parental socio-economic status influences transnational interactions of their offspring in almost all countries analyzed, with economic differences between countries also affecting the frequency of transnational behavior. Wealthier economies have more transnational interactions among youth.
What_was_studied: The International Civics and Citizenship Study in 21 European states in 2009, focusing on secondary schoolchildren's transnational interactions and how they are influenced by socio-economic differences across countries and within countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize initiatives that reduce socio-economic disparities in education and increase opportunities for transnational interactions among disadvantaged populations to promote sustainable development and intersectional equity.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Permanent employment; Employment contract; Unemployment; Bridge (interpersonal); Panel survey; European community; West germany
Keywords: contracts; event history analysis; cross-national analysis. JEL: J41; J62
Title: Bridge or Trap? Temporary Workers’ Transitions to Unemployment and to the Standard Employment Contract
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found higher rates of transition to permanent employment than to unemployment for most temporary workers, with strong between-country differences.
What_was_studied: This article analyses the transitions of temporary workers to the standard employment contract and to unemployment in four countries with different forms of market structuration: France, West Germany, Denmark, and the UK, using the European Community Household Panel survey (ECHP) from 1995 to 2001.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize reforms that support the transition of temporary workers to permanent employment, particularly in countries with weaker labour market institutions.

Field: Economics; European integration; European union; Slow convergence; Shift-share analysis; Inequality; Development economics; Economic growth; Economic inequality; Homogeneous; Politics
Title: Patterns of Regional Inequality in the Enlarged Europe
primary_category: Asset poverty; Education access; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that regional economic inequalities within nations are increasing, while between-nation inequalities are declining at a rate of approximately 2% per year.
What_was_studied: Regional economic inequalities in the European Union member states during the last years.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize addressing regional employment patterns, industrial structures and location to reduce income disparities and promote social and economic cohesion in Europe.

Field: Labour economics; Economics; Unemployment; Self-rated health
Title: Is it Easier to Be Unemployed When the Experience Is More Widely Shared? Effects of Unemployment on Self-rated Health in 25 European Countries with Diverging Macroeconomic Conditions
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty
What_was_found: The study found that being unemployed is associated with worse self-rated health (SRH) in all 25 European countries, but the association weakens when time-invariant personal characteristics are accounted for using individual-level fixed-effects models. Additionally, becoming unemployed is also linked to slightly worse SRH.
What_was_studied: The study investigates short-term effects of unemployment on self-rated health (SRH) in 25 European countries with diverging macroeconomic conditions using EU-SILC panel data from 2010 to 2013.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: In light of these findings, policymakers should prioritize job creation and retention initiatives to reduce the negative health impacts of widespread unemployment, particularly in countries with high and growing unemployment rates.

Authors: Marcel Lubbers; Marcel Coenders; Peer Scheepers
Field: Public opinion; Ethnic group; Neighbourhood (mathematics); Refugee; Geography; Asylum seeker; Resistance (psychoanalysis); Object (philosophy); Demographic economics; Social psychology; Real estate
Keywords: Lubbers; M.; Coenders; M.; & Scheepers
Title: Objections to Asylum Seeker Centres: Individual and Contextual Determinants of Resistance to Small and Large Centres in the Netherlands
primary_category: Asset poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that objection to large centers is far more widespread than objection to small centers. Lower educated people object more strongly to centers, whatever the size. People with high incomes tend to object to large centers more strongly than people with low incomes.
What_was_studied: Over the last 15 years, numerous asylum seeker centers (ASCs) have been founded in the Netherlands, often preceded and followed by neighborhood unrest. This study examines to what extent people object to the foundation of ASCs of different sizes.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest that scaling up support for lower-income communities and investing in education and job training programs may help reduce objections to ASCs. Policymakers should prioritize these initiatives to foster a more inclusive and supportive community.

Authors: Nazareno Panichella; Maurizio Avola; Giorgio Piccitto
Field: Political science; Class (computer programming); Ethnic penalty; Social mobility; Demographic economics; Social stratification
