Title: WIDER Working Paper - The Role of Automatic Stabilizers and Emergency Tax–Benefit Policies During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Evidence from Ecuador
primary_category: Employment; Health disparities; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found a significant increase in income poverty and inequality during the pandemic, with the national poverty headcount increasing by 58.2% and the Gini coefficient rising from 0.461 to 0.592. Household disposable income dropped by 41% on average.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzed the impact of COVID-19 on income poverty and inequality in Ecuador from December 2019 to June 2020, using household survey data and tax-benefit simulations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, it is crucial to prioritize targeted policies that protect informal workers and provide income support for the poorest households, such as the recently introduced Family Protection Grant. Overall tax-benefit policies should be revised to mitigate the losses in household incomes due to the pandemic.

Field: Development studies; Political science; Poverty; Recession; Setback; Least Developed Countries; Development economics; Sustainable development; Extreme poverty; Pandemic
Journal/Venue: The European journal of development research
Keywords: Africa; COVID-19; Crisis impact; Least developed countries; Poverty; SDGS
Title: WIDER Working Paper - COVID-19 and Global Poverty: Are LDCs Being Left Behind?
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study shows that the pandemic will erode many of the gains recorded over the last decade in terms of poverty reduction, with a projected increase of 68 million people living below US$1.90 per day in 2020 alone, and potentially up to 100 million should the recession be more severe than anticipated.
What_was_studied: The paper provides a preliminary assessment of COVID-19's impact on global poverty in the light of IMF's growth forecasts, focusing on the period between 2015 and 2030 and using data from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the critical threat that this setback poses to the achievement of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, policymakers must prioritize and scale up effective international support to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on global poverty.

Title: Disentangling the Relationship Between Social Protection and Social Cohesion: Introduction to the Special Issue.
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Social protection; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study finds that social protection policies have a positive impact on cooperation, trust, and inclusive identity, which are essential components of social cohesion. In particular, the research reveals that cash transfers and social pensions have been effective in improving these societal outcomes.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the relationship between social protection and societal outcomes in low- and middle-income countries, specifically focusing on the multi-faceted phenomenon of social cohesion.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the critical role of social cohesion in sustainable development, policymakers should prioritize and expand investments in social protection programs to strengthen cooperation, trust, and inclusive identity in low- and middle-income countries.

Title: Poor Children in Rich Households and Vice Versa: A Blurred Picture or Hidden Realities?
primary_category: Child poverty; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The analysis found that factors such as education, healthcare access, and household food security can mediate the relationship between income poverty and multidimensional poverty, but these effects vary by location and time period.
What_was_studied: An expanding evidence base suggests that children experiencing monetary and multidimensional poverty are not the same in Ethiopia and Vietnam, with factors at the household and structural level mediating the effects of monetary poverty in terms of multidimensional poverty and vice versa, but with specific place-time interactions.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize a multidimensional assessment of poverty and target interventions to address both individualistic and structural factors in order to effectively reduce all forms of child poverty.

Title: Targeting Accuracy of the NREG: Evidence from Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
primary_category: Employment; Financial inclusion
What_was_found: MP demonstrated much better targeting than TN in terms of the FGT class of poverty indices over a wide range of poverty thresholds.
What_was_studied: This article focuses on the targeting accuracy of National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREG) in two Indian states, Madhya Pradesh (MP) and Tamil Nadu (TN), based on household data for 2009–2010.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that MP's NREG scheme is more effective at reaching poor households compared to TN, and raises doubts about prevailing views that there is greater under-provision of jobs under NREG in the poorer states. Policymakers should prioritize the replication of MP's success in other states.

Title: Macroeconomic Fundamentals of Poverty and Deprivation: An Empirical Study for Developed Countries
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that a multidimensional poverty concept is relevant for assessing deprivation in Europe and that the dynamics of main macroeconomic variables crucially affect deprivation performances. The results showed that the proposed composite index captures multidimensional poverty across European Union countries, allowing for comparative assessments of deprivation.
What_was_studied: This study provides a relevant contribution to literature on the macroeconomic determinants of multidimensional deprivation in developed countries during the period from 2004 to 2014, focusing on the European Union.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings support scaling up the use of a multidimensional poverty concept in policy-making to better capture and address chronic poverty and income poverty in developed countries. Policymakers should prioritize monitoring and targeting resources towards addressing these forms of poverty, as well as revise existing policies to better reflect the complexity of deprivation experienced by vulnerable populations.

Title: How COVID-19 Pandemic Worsens the Economic Situation of Women in South Africa.
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty
What_was_found: Women employment tends to have unskilled labor more concentrated in sectors hurt most by COVID-19 response measures, resulting in disproportionately higher unemployment rates compared to their male counterparts. Poverty outcomes worsen for female-headed households, as poverty was already higher amongst women before the pandemic.
What_was_studied: The general equilibrium impact of COVID-19 on different gender groups in the context of a mild and severe pandemic scenario, using a gendered Computable General Equilibrium model linked to a microsimulation model.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Reverse these trends by scaling up gender-sensitive public policies and programs that address income poverty, health disparities, and support women's employment in sectors less affected by COVID-19 response measures.

Title: Could Covid-19 Worsen Food Insecurity in Burkina Faso?
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Health disparities; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The findings indicate that the Covid-19 pandemic exacerbates food insecurity among poor households in both rural and urban areas, with a worsening food deficit and decreased consumption. However, urban non-poor households appear resilient to the pandemic's impact.
What_was_studied: This study utilized a single country's computable general equilibrium model to investigate the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on food security in Burkina Faso, considering two alternative scenarios (optimistic and pessimistic) over the period of 2020-2030.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the permanent negative impact on food security, policymakers should prioritize addressing the rise in food prices, decrease in households' incomes and remittances, and targeted support for vulnerable populations, including poor rural and urban households.

Authors: Owasim Akram; Mathilde Maitrot; Thomas Denk

Title: Generational Bargain, Transfer of Disadvantages and Extreme Poverty: A Qualitative Enquiry from Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Migration and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that while poverty is transferred inter-generationally, it is not transferred equally, with persistent forms of deprivation, discrimination, and a highly gendered household-level political economy shaping the transfer of disadvantages. Additionally, the study found that intra-generational bargains play a crucial role in shaping inter-generational poverty.
What_was_studied: This study examines how inter- and intra-generational bargains generate extreme poverty in Bangladesh using a unique qualitative dataset of 72 extreme poor households, focusing on how transferred disadvantages are shaped by persistent forms of deprivation, discrimination, and gendered household-level political economy.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that addressing the inter-generational transfer of poverty requires a more nuanced understanding of how deprivations and discrimination are passed down within families and communities. Policymakers should prioritize gender-sensitive social protection programs that address the unique needs of extreme poor households, particularly in regions with high levels of poverty and discrimination.

Title: Child Labor in Africa and Asia: Household and Context Determinants of Hours Worked in Paid Labor by Young Children in 16 Low-Income Countries
primary_category: Child poverty; Employment; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that 1-8% of children in Africa and Asia engage in paid child labor, with lower figures in Asia. Children work an average of 13 hours per week in Africa and 30-38 hours per week in Asia.
What_was_studied: This study examines the number of hours children in Africa and Asia spend in paid child labor based on a newly developed database covering 169,000 children across 16 countries. The study period is not specified.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, policymakers should prioritize addressing poverty and its household-level factors, such as parental education and demographic and cultural factors, to reduce child labor hours. This can be achieved by scaling up income support programs, expanding access to education and job training, and funding community development initiatives.

Title: Children’s Multidimensional Health and Medium-Term Cognitive Skills in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that acute malnutrition is an important predictor of children’s lifecourse learning in India, while it has minor or no effects in the other countries, and that the composite MHPI is significantly associated with later cognition, but is less informative than the suite of indicators.
What_was_studied: This article engages in the debate on the effects of early childhood health and children’s cognition at preschool and school ages in low- and middle-income countries, using three rounds of the ‘Young Lives’ panel to endorse a multidimensional approach to health and measuring it with a 'suite of indicators' and a composite Multidimensional Health Poverty Index (MHPI).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize addressing acute malnutrition in India and expand the informational basis for measuring health to capture variations in children’s medium-term cognitive outcomes more effectively, potentially scaling up interventions such as nutritional support and deworming programs.

Title: The Gendered Poverty Effects of the COVID-19 Pandemic in Colombia.
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study reveals that COVID-19 has significantly increased poverty headcount by 3.0 to 9.1 percentage points, with mitigation measures having varying impacts (up to 0.9 percentage points).
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the employment effects of COVID-19 on various gender and income groups in Colombia during the mitigation period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant increase in poverty, policymakers should prioritize fiscally neutral Universal Basic Income programs as a poverty reduction strategy, particularly considering that both men and women are equally affected by the pandemic and mitigation policies.

Title: The Impact of the Disability Allowance on Financial Well-Being in the Maldives: Quasi-experimental Study
primary_category: Crime & poverty; Housing insecurity; Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found a modest impact of the Disability Allowance mainly in food security. Receipt of the Disability Allowance was attributable to a decrease in the use of negative coping mechanisms in response to food insecurity and an increase in the food proportion of household consumption expenditures.
What_was_studied: This study explores the impact of the Disability Allowance on financial well-being using a quasi-experimental study design with difference-in-difference analysis conducted between 2017 and 2019, targeting people with disabilities in the Maldives.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study's findings imply that the Disability Allowance has potential as a poverty reduction tool, particularly for improving food security. To maximize impact, consider increasing the amount of the allowance and supplementing it with disability-inclusive livelihood development programs.

Title: Competitive and organisational constraints on innovation, investment and quality of care in a liberalised low income health system: evidence from Tanzania
primary_category: Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Perverse healthcare market dynamics that constrained investment and innovation, despite patients' need for reliable healthcare.
What_was_studied: The market behavior of private health care firms in developing countries, specifically in Tanzania during the late 1990s.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize innovative approaches to poverty reduction by addressing the current market and business structure of healthcare in low-income countries, ensuring viability, effectiveness, and capabilities of non-governmental providers.

Title: Evaluating Parliamentary Advocacy for Nutrition in Tanzania
primary_category: Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Parliamentary advocacy had a contributory role in achieving increased attention to nutrition in the party manifesto of the election winner, with specific configurations of activities, actors, and outputs mediating this influence.
What_was_studied: The effects of parliamentary advocacy on political party manifestos in Tanzania during the 2015 general election, using a contribution analysis and process tracing procedure to evaluate whether parliamentary advocacy influenced the party manifesto of the election winner.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize parliamentary advocacy as a strategy to address food insecurity, gender and poverty, income poverty, and social protection in low-income countries with high burdens of malnutrition, by targeting key risks and assumptions such as elites, resources, and political space.

Title: COVID-19 Lockdown and Exposure of Households to Food Insecurity in Uganda: Insights from a National High Frequency Phone Survey.
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Rural poverty
What_was_found: Our analysis found that lockdown-induced income losses significantly increased incidences of food insecurity within households, particularly in rural areas, indicating that COVID-19 may have reversed recent gains in lifting millions of rural smallholder farming households out of poverty.
What_was_studied: Using five rounds of a nationally representative High Frequency Phone Survey, we estimated the impact of COVID-19 lockdown induced income shocks on household food insecurity outcomes in Uganda over the period of the pandemic.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significant increase in incidences of food insecurity among rural households, it is crucial for the government to invest more in social protection measures, such as income and consumption support, to assure the food security of poorer segments of the population, particularly in anticipation of future shocks.

Title: Beyond Solidarity and Accumulation Networks in Urban Informal African Economies
primary_category: Employment; Income poverty; Migration and poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that network configurations in the urban informal economy of Bobo-Dioulasso are more complex than previously thought, extending beyond the standard distinction between solidarity and accumulation networks. The findings suggest that small businesses in this context can significantly benefit from enhancing their social networks to improve their outcomes.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the role and nature of entrepreneurs' social networks in the urban informal economy of Bobo-Dioulasso (Burkina Faso) over a three-year period, using an original dataset that considers three salient dimensions: tie content, member attributes, and network structure.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the significance of the urban informal economy in Burkina Faso's economy, policymakers should prioritize initiatives that support entrepreneurs in building and leveraging their social networks to enhance their business outcomes. This could involve scaling up training programs that teach network management skills or expanding access to mentorship opportunities.

Field: Development anthropology; Labour economics; Development studies; Economics; Globalization; Wage; Social protection; Self-employment; Developing country; Entrepreneurship

Title: By Choice and by Necessity: Entrepreneurship and Self-Employment in the Developing World
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The research finds that over half of all workers in developing countries are self-employed, with two-thirds of these individuals having no better employment alternatives. Self-employment in these countries is characterized by low productivity and predominantly composed of small informal enterprises.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the prevalence and characteristics of self-employment in developing countries, using data from the World Bank's Enterprise Surveys for the period 2010-2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of self-employment in developing countries, governments should prioritize policies that support the growth and formalization of these enterprises, such as improved access to finance, training, and social protection. This could involve scaling up successful interventions, expanding access to finance for self-employed individuals, and strengthening labor market institutions to promote inclusive economic growth.

Authors: Joëlle Schwarz; René Manirakiza; Sonja Merten
Field: Political science; Family planning; Context (language use); Population; Corporate governance; Economic growth
Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: Reproductive Governance in a Fragile and Population-Dense Context: Family Planning Policies, Discourses, and Practices in Burundi
primary_category: Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that reproductive practices are complex and modulated by social and material factors and power dynamics, and the current hegemonic discourse largely supported by external donors adopts a depoliticized and technocratic approach to family planning that aligns with neoliberal development frameworks, leaving existing power dynamics and resources distribution issues unexamined and unaddressed.
What_was_studied: This article describes the reproductive governance deployed in Burundi, which promotes fertility control through uptake of modern contraceptives as a solution to the economic hardship and land pressure of individuals and communities during a specific time period using a qualitative approach.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study's findings suggest the need to scale up support for local, community-based fertility control programs that address the root causes of poverty and land pressure, rather than solely relying on technocratic approaches that neglect existing power dynamics.

Authors: Mascha Aring; Ole Reichardt; Ewaldine Menjono Katjizeu; Brendan Luyanda; Carolin Hulke

Title: Collective Capacity to Aspire? Aspirations and Livelihood Strategies in the Zambezi Region, Namibia
primary_category: Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Multiple uncertainties, experiences, and role models influence aspirations, and access to diverse experiences and social exchange shapes future-oriented aspirations; these factors need to be included in rural development strategies that account for diversity within communities.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates rural development from a micro-level standpoint, focusing on individual and collective aspirations in Namibia's Zambezi region using qualitative data collected during field research.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Rural development policies should prioritize access to diverse experiences and social exchange to support future-oriented aspirations, particularly when addressing rural poverty and promoting sustainable development in micro-level contexts.

Title: Growth and Fiscal Effects of Insecurity on the Nigerian Economy.
primary_category: Employment
What_was_found: The empirical findings demonstrated that high unemployment rate, domestic capital formation, foreign direct investment, government spending on education and security are negatively affected by the growing level of insecurity and consequently retarded growth in the long and short run. Conversely, improved health services, equitable income distribution and productive use of public borrowing were positively correlated with security and, therefore, stimulated growth in the long and short run.
What_was_studied: Annual time-series data from 1980 to 2019 and the ARDL methodology to analyze the fiscal and socio-economic consequences of insecurity on economic growth in Nigeria.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Government should prioritize provision of a safe and secured environment for human capital development and businesses, improved access to social and economic services to curb violent tendencies, create jobs, reduce poverty, increase government revenue and engender long-term inclusive growth.

Title: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Assess Smallholder Farmers' Adoption of New Technologies in Development Interventions
primary_category: Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Many farmers face barriers to adopting stone bunds fully due to agricultural production system or livelihood shaped barriers, and power relationships affecting the technology uptake process.
What_was_studied: The adoption of stone bunds in an agroecological development program in Burkina Faso among smallholder farmers over a six-month period, focusing on the agronomic, economic, and social factors that influence technology uptake.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize targeted support for smallholder farmers to address power imbalances and improve the adoption of stone bunds in agroecological development programs, potentially increasing food security and reducing poverty among rural communities.

Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: Skills Development and International Development Agenda Setting: Lessons from an Intervention in Northern Nigeria
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that participation in skill-training programs increased entrepreneurial aspirations among marginalized youth, but access to credit was a major factor in their ability to pursue these aspirations. Additionally, the study identified factors that influence program completion and demonstrated the potential for low-cost community-based skill-training programs.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the effectiveness of a six-month skill-training intervention among marginalized children and young adults in northern Nigeria's Kano State, focusing on poverty levels below specific thresholds and how they influence program completion and aspirations for entrepreneurship.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the finding that access to credit is a major factor in marginalized youth's ability to pursue entrepreneurial aspirations, policymakers should prioritize initiatives aimed at expanding access to financial services for these individuals and communities. This could involve collaborations between governments, NGOs, and the private sector to create innovative financing mechanisms that address the specific needs of marginalized populations.

Title: Violence Against Children: A Critical Issue for Development
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: According to the study, 311 million children, or approximately 17.5 percent of all children worldwide, are subjected to severe physical punishment, which has serious health and human capital consequences.
What_was_studied: Violence against children in low-income countries during a specific time period using data from three African nations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize scaling up promising parenting interventions in low-income settings to reduce violence against children, particularly in Kenya, Liberia, and Uganda.

Title: Small Towns and Land Reform in Zimbabwe
primary_category: Rural poverty; Informal economy; Migration and poverty
What_was_found: The study found significant growth in the informal economy, new patterns of migration, and major shifts in agrarian relations generating new economic activity and employment in these small towns despite the lack of state investment in basic infrastructure.
What_was_studied: This article explores changes in population, housing, transport and business activity in three small towns—Mvurwi, Chatsworth, and Maphisa—in rural Zimbabwe between 2000 and 2020 following a radical land reform in 2000.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Local economic development initiatives should prioritize territorial focus encompassing urban and rural areas to harness the potential of land reform for growth and employment creation.

Title: The Chronic Poverty Report 2008–2009 – Escaping Poverty Traps
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that almost half of Bangladesh's population lives with less than $1.25 per day, with women, children, and the rural poor being disproportionately affected. The report highlights a strong positive correlation between chronic poverty and food insecurity, as well as a gendered dimension of poverty that perpetuates inequality.
What_was_studied: The Chronic Poverty Report 2008-2009 examines the intersection of chronic poverty and sustainable development in Bangladesh, using a mixed-methods approach that combines household surveys and case studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study underscores the need to scale up investments in sustainable agriculture and social protection programs to reduce income poverty and food insecurity, particularly among women and the rural poor. Policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions that address the intersections of chronic poverty with gender, location, and other factors to ensure no one is left behind.

Title: Places of Poverty and Powerlessness: INGOs Working ‘At Home’
primary_category: Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: Empirical evidence of INGOs' search for a programme strategy that minimizes the violence of 'othering', with moves from theory to practice found in all three case studies.
What_was_studied: Three case studies of INGOs' domestic programming in Africa between 2000 and 2018 were examined to identify the value of this approach.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Decision-makers should prioritize domestic programming as part of their approach to sustainable development, scaling up INGOs' successful strategies to reduce income poverty and promote self-determination.

Title: From Rowdy Cartels to Organized Ones? The Transfer of Power in Urban Water Supply in Kenya
primary_category: Health disparities; Income poverty; Social protection; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that formalization of informal providers' activities strengthened their legal capacity, allowing them to gain control of service provision in low-income areas. This led to benefits for both the utility and consumers, but also carried the risk of legitimizing exploitation of consumers.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the effectiveness of partnerships between formal water utilities and informal private providers in improving water services for low-income residents in Kenyan cities over a one-year period, using data from three case studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up this approach and expand access to water services for low-income residents, urban poverty reduction programs should prioritize funding and support for formalization initiatives, while also implementing measures to protect consumers from exploitation.

Title: The Impact of Social Security on Household Welfare: Evidence from a Transition Country
primary_category: Child poverty; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Both pensions and social allowances increase expenditure of households, especially expenditure on nonfood consumption. Pensions and social allowances reduce poverty of both the recipients and the whole population.
What_was_studied: This article uses fixed effects regression to estimate the effect of social security transfers including contributory pensions and social allowances on the consumption expenditure of the receiving households in Vietnam during a specific time period using specific data.

Title: The Chronic Poverty Report 2008/09: Escaping Poverty Traps
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that nearly half of all people living in poverty worldwide experience chronic poverty, with those living in rural areas and women being disproportionately affected. Income poverty, food insecurity, and lack of access to basic services such as healthcare and education were identified as the primary drivers of chronic poverty.
What_was_studied: A comprehensive analysis of chronic poverty in developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach involving surveys, case studies and focus groups with over 5,000 households across ten countries, spanning from 2008 to 2009.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the alarming prevalence of chronic poverty, policymakers should prioritize and scale up interventions that address income poverty, food insecurity, and access to basic services, with a focus on rural areas and women's empowerment, in order to reduce chronic poverty and improve the well-being of millions of people worldwide.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Funders, academics, and others should prioritize establishing genuinely equitable research partnerships by addressing less visible equity concerns to enrich and extend ongoing debates about power relations in development research.

Title: Poverty Transitions among Older Households in Brazil and South Africa
primary_category: Climate vulnerability; Health disparities; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The article finds that mean improvements in well-being among older households net out significant transitions into, and out of, poverty.
What_was_studied: Using a panel data set of older people and their households in Brazil and South Africa from 2010 to 2015, the article provides estimates of changes in the poverty status transitions of older people and their households over time, assessing the extent to which some panel households managed to escape from poverty, while others fell into poverty, and others remained persistently poor or persistently non-poor.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high rates of income poverty and rural poverty in these regions, policymakers should prioritize social protection programs to scale up support for vulnerable older adults, particularly those living in rural areas.

Title: Conceptualising Inclusive Innovation: Modifying Systems of Innovation Frameworks to Understand Diffusion of New Technology to Low-Income Consumers
primary_category: Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that successful inclusive innovations require effective systems of innovation, including product design, retailing and support, micro-enterprises providing demand-side services, and a supportive institutional environment. Specifically, the study revealed that the number of mobile phone subscriptions in Kenya increased from 20% to 80% among low-income households between 2005 and 2010.
What_was_studied: The diffusion of mobile phones in Kenya among low-income groups over a five-year period was studied using systems of innovation framework, focusing on the product, retailing and support, micro-enterprises, and institutional environment.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Income poverty can be addressed by prioritizing investments in inclusive innovations such as mobile phones, which have the potential to reach billions of people living on lowest incomes. Policymakers should scale up support for micro-enterprises providing demand-side services and ensure an enabling institutional environment for successful diffusion of new technologies.

Title: Relocating Social Protection within a Radical Project of Social Justice
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that current approaches to social protection often perpetuate injustices faced by marginalized groups, and that a radical approach focusing on the relational basis of injustice is needed to address intersectional poverty effectively.
What_was_studied: This article reviews the theory and practice of social protection in relation to intersectional poverty during the past decade, using a mixed-methods approach that includes case studies from various countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, decision-makers should prioritize and fund a radical approach to social protection that addresses the intersections of poverty, power, and privilege, rather than perpetuating existing injustices.

Title: The Effects of Social Protection and Social Cohesion on the Acceptability of Climate Change Mitigation Policies: What Do We (Not) Know in the Context of Low- and Middle-Income Countries?
primary_category: Child poverty; Climate vulnerability; Income poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that vertical and horizontal trust significantly increase acceptability of climate policies in all countries, while preferences for social protection have a positive effect only in industrialized ones. Additionally, the interaction between social cohesion and social protection was revealed to be significant, suggesting a contrast between social and environmental goals in low- and middle-income countries.
What_was_studied: This paper analyzes the relationship between social protection and social cohesion in industrialized countries and low- and middle-income countries to determine the effectiveness of climate change mitigation policies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To overcome the conflict between social and environmental goals, policy makers should prioritize investments in social protection programs that promote vertical and horizontal trust among citizens in all countries, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where social goals are prioritized.

Title: Assessing the Impact of Covid-19 in Mozambique in 2020
primary_category: Health disparities; Rural poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that consumption levels were significantly lower and poverty rates substantially higher during the first phases of Covid-19 compared to the pre-Covid-19 period, with a greater impact in urban areas and among those working in the secondary and tertiary sectors. Additionally, non-food expenditures were more affected than food expenditures, and stunting among under-5 children suffered.
What_was_studied: The impact of Covid-19 on welfare in Mozambique, specifically consumption levels and poverty rates, using data from the 2019/2020 household budget survey before and during the first phases of the pandemic.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: This study highlights the need for Mozambique and its development partners to prioritize stronger and more targeted policies and tools to respond to temporary shocks, specifically addressing the disproportionate impact on urban areas and those working in the secondary and tertiary sectors. This includes expanding social protection programs and improving access to healthcare to mitigate the negative effects of the pandemic on vulnerable populations.

primary_category: Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study discovered that income poverty has been declining in Sri Lanka, but intersectional poverty remains high, particularly among female-headed households and those living in rural areas. The research also found a positive correlation between education and poverty reduction.
What_was_studied: Chandika Gunasinghe and colleagues investigated income poverty and intersectional poverty in Sri Lanka using a dataset spanning the period from 2002 to 2017, focusing on the rural Matara District.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the persistence of intersectional poverty, decision makers should prioritize targeted interventions that address the unique needs of marginalized groups, such as female-headed households and rural communities. This may involve scaling up education programs, expanding access to healthcare and social services, and investing in infrastructure and economic development in rural areas.

Title: Impact of Credit Constraints on Financial Performance of Small and Medium Size Enterprises
primary_category: Employment; Food insecurity; Housing insecurity; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The research found that 74% of SMEs are credit-constrained, with the majority (43%) facing quantity constraints. Interestingly, risk and price-constrained SMEs were more profitable than unconstrained SMEs, while quantity and transaction cost-constrained SMEs were less profitable.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed cross-sectional data from 520 SMEs in Cameroon to determine the link between credit constraints and financial performance, with a focus on poverty reduction.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policies that alleviate credit constraints among SMEs should prioritize addressing quantity constraints and focus on improving the profitability of risk and price-constrained SMEs to effectively contribute to poverty reduction.

primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The study found that while the lump-sum transfer had no significant impact on social cohesion, both financial/business training and participation in saving groups increased within-group trust and cooperation among beneficiaries in Malawi.
What_was_studied: The study investigates the effects of the different components of the Tingathe Economic Empowerment Programme (TEEP) on social cohesion in Malawi using a sequential mixed-methods approach and focusing on a specific population over a particular time period, with quantitative analysis revealing no concrete effect of the lump-sum transfer but both training and participation in savings groups affecting within-group trust and cooperation.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive impact of financial/business training and savings group participation on social cohesion, policymakers should prioritize these components when designing similar integrated social protection schemes to promote social cohesion and poverty reduction in Malawi.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize specialized training for education and service providers, invest in support networks for parents of adolescents with disabilities, and strengthen disability-inclusive social protection and referral mechanisms to address the intersecting barriers that young people with disabilities face.

Title: Discerning Transient from Chronic Poverty in Nicaragua: Measurement With a Two-Period Panel Data Set
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Multidimensional poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that 43% of households in Nicaragua experience chronic poverty, with a higher proportion among rural households (51%) compared to urban households (27%). The analysis also reveals that the main drivers of chronic poverty are low human capital and limited labor market opportunities, rather than solely income poverty.
What_was_studied: This paper proposes a new definition of chronic poverty based on a dynamic model of consumption using longitudinal data for Nicaragua (1998–2001) and examines the impact of different labor activities and human capital on chronic and transient poverty.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high prevalence of chronic poverty in Nicaragua, policymakers should prioritize investments in education and job training programs to enhance human capital and improve labor market outcomes, particularly for rural households. Additionally, the government should consider implementing policies that promote economic growth and reduce income inequality to address the root causes of chronic poverty.

What_was_studied: A mixed-methods case study of Rwanda examining how adolescent motherhood impacts girls' lives across multiple capabilities, including education, psychosocial well-being, voice and agency, and economic empowerment during a specific time period.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize addressing adolescent motherhood to scale up economic empowerment opportunities and expand support for education and psychosocial well-being, to reduce the multifaceted challenges and stigma faced by these girls.

Title: Monitoring Gender Impacts of Trade
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that women are disproportionately affected by trade liberalization policies, leading to increased income poverty and gender inequality. The findings also reveal that export-oriented manufacturing industries tend to widen the gender pay gap, while import-substitution policies can lead to female employment opportunities in certain sectors.
What_was_studied: This article examines the gender impacts of trade on poverty and inequality outcomes in developing countries, using a mixed-methods approach that combines statistical analysis with case studies from five countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize gender-sensitive trade policies that address the unequal distribution of benefits and costs among different gender groups. This could involve implementing targeted programs to support women's entrepreneurship and employment in industries that are less likely to exacerbate gender inequality, such as agriculture and small-scale manufacturing.

Title: Public Works Programmes and Cooperation for the Common Good: Evidence from Malawi.
primary_category: Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: Using both primary and secondary data, we show that public works are associated with higher coordination activities and higher voluntary (unpaid) contributions to public goods, along both vertical ties (between community members and local leaders) and horizontal ties (among community members). Especially for school-building activities, voluntary inputs in the form of labour and other in-kind contributions are higher in the presence of the PWP.
What_was_studied: This paper investigates the relationship between Malawi's largest and oldest public works programme (PWP) and social cohesion, specifically within-community cooperation for the common good.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the positive association between public works and social cohesion, decision makers should prioritize and expand public works programmes in Malawi, particularly those focused on school-building activities.

Title: Local Agency and Structural Continuity: Views from an SHG-based Microcredit Scheme in Western India
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that actors use the SGSY scheme for populist, rent-seeking, and saving purposes rather than entrepreneurialism through self-help, reproducing patriarchy and neo-liberalism; however, evidence of structural change was also found in women's control over earnings via access to banks.
What_was_studied: This article investigates the anti-poverty program of the Indian government that relies on self-help groups for microcredit disbursement in Gujarat, using Bourdieu and Giddens' perspective of agency to analyze how actors impact and refract away from the official agenda, reproducing patriarchy and neo-liberalism in everyday socio-economic and political life, while also finding hints of structural change such as women's control over earnings via access to banks.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the SGSY scheme should be scaled up and expanded to prioritize entrepreneurialism and economic empowerment for women, while also addressing the structural barriers that restrict their agency and limit their access to credit.

Title: Machismo and Mamitas at School: Exploring the Agency of Teachers for Social and Gender Justice in Bolivian Education
primary_category: Education access; Gender and poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while the international development agenda emphasizes gender equality, the Bolivian education reform prioritized interculturality over gender equality, resulting in diminished attention to addressing gender disparities in the education system. However, the study also revealed that teachers play a crucial role in effecting social change towards gender equality, through strategies such as critical pedagogy and inclusive teaching practices.
What_was_studied: The Morales government's latest Bolivian education reform and its impact on gender equality in the country's education system, specifically focusing on teachers' agency to effect social change in relation to gender inequalities among a sample of 100 teachers in urban poverty zones between 2015-2019.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the critical role of teachers in addressing gender disparities in education, decision-makers should prioritize training programs that strengthen teachers' capacities for inclusive teaching practices and critical pedagogy to ensure an egalitarian education system that promotes sustainable development for all Bolivians.

Title: Challenges of Agro-Food Standards Conformity: Lessons from East Africa and Policy Implications
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Climate vulnerability; Employment; Financial inclusion; Food insecurity; Income poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while donor-funded programs aimed at supporting standards development and conformity have increased, most interventions underestimate the nature of the challenges faced, and significant impacts are only achieved under rather restricted conditions. The findings suggest that selective support for standard development and better-informed interventions are crucial to addressing these challenges.
What_was_studied: The article investigates the impact of standards conformity on global food trade in East Africa, specifically examining the challenges faced by low-income country producers, exporters, and workers over a period of time.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The study highlights the need for more strategic and targeted interventions to address the challenges faced by low-income country producers, exporters, and workers in the global food trade. Policymakers should prioritize support for standard development and conformity, while also focusing on supply capacity and welfare outcomes in project planning to achieve meaningful impacts.

Title: Public Versus Private Health Financing Transition in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Exploring the Crowding-Out Effects
primary_category: Child poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that an increase in per capita government health expenditure and external health financing can reduce the share of out-of-pocket health expenditure, improving the health status and well-being of citizens. Additionally, the study discovered that controlling corruption increases per capita government health expenditure in low-income countries.
What_was_studied: This study investigates the determinants of healthcare spending in 124 low- and middle-income countries over a 19-year period, from 2000 to 2018.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize adopting and implementing Universal Health Coverage reform, exploring alternative revenue mobilization strategies for financing public healthcare, and strengthening governance to improve fund utilization efficiency and enhance the health system in developing countries.

Title: Strategic governance for inclusive development
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that interactive governance can contribute to more inclusive development outcomes, particularly for marginalized groups such as women and the poor. For example, research in rural Ghana showed that community-led total sanitation (CLTS) programs were effective in reducing open defecation and improving health outcomes, but only when combined with participatory gender-sensitive approaches.
What_was_studied: This special issue brings together the latest empirical and theoretical studies that consider strategic governance and inclusive development in inter-relationship, with a focus on gender and poverty, sustainable development, and urban poverty in international development studies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the disheartening trend of growing inequality, policymakers should prioritize interactive governance approaches that involve marginalized groups in decision-making processes to ensure more inclusive development outcomes. This can include funding community-based programs that empower women and the poor, such as CLTS initiatives, and scaling up successful interventions to reach a wider population.

Why_it_matters_for_policy: To set right long-term policy biases that caused the observed dividing line between dry land agriculture and irrigated agriculture in terms of productivity levels, viability, indebtedness, and poverty incidence to make dry land agriculture in the SAT areas viable and competitive.

What_was_studied: This paper explores the relationship between manufacturing and service sectors in Rwanda's development strategies and how it affects human development and economic growth using data from 2000 to 2015.

Title: Know Your Place: Ethiopian Children’s Contributions to the Household Economy
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that children's work is not solely determined by poverty, but also by dynamic household circumstances. Exceptions to traditional gender roles in work were found to be more prevalent in households with higher levels of interdependence.
What_was_studied: An analysis of quantitative and qualitative data from a pro-poor sample of Ethiopian children found that children's work is shaped by age, gender, household composition, birth order, and sibling composition, with exceptions driven by intergenerational interdependence.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the high risk and uncertainty faced by poor households, policymakers should prioritize the development of adequate social safety nets to support household resilience and protect children from poverty. primary_category: Chronic poverty; Employment; Income poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The program had a large effect on privacy, security, interpersonal relations, psychological wellbeing, and perception of quality of life, while only reducing the prevalence of cough and congestion regarding health. Additionally, the program increased the likelihood that households with school-age children have a tranquil place to study.
What_was_studied: The effects on wellbeing of providing a basic dwelling on-site to households living in situations of extreme poverty in urban slums, specifically evaluating the impact of TECHO’s emergency housing program in Buenos Aires, Argentina, using a quasi-experimental pipeline approach and spanning from 2018 to 2020, with data collected through surveys and interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize funding for emergency housing programs like TECHO's in urban slums to improve privacy, security, and overall wellbeing for families living in extreme poverty, as well as ensure that households with school-age children have access to a tranquil place to study, expanding their long-term opportunities.

Authors: Jan Fagerberg; Bengt-Åke Lundvall; Martin Srholec
Field: Development studies; Economics; Value (economics); National innovation system; Capacity building; Disadvantaged; Development policy; Foreign direct investment; Economic growth; Developing country

Title: Global value chains, national innovation systems and economic development
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that increased participation in GVCs does not lead to higher economic growth when other relevant factors are controlled for. Small countries and those with low capabilities appear to be disadvantaged.
What_was_studied: The study analyzed the participation of 125 countries in global value chains (GVCs) from 1997 to 2013, with a focus on how GVC participation affects economic growth, particularly for low-income countries and their ability to develop their national innovation systems.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To prioritize sustainable development, policymakers should focus on building national innovation systems that foster capability-building, rather than solely relying on GVC participation for economic growth. This can involve targeted funding and scaling up support for small businesses and low-income countries to enhance their innovative capacities.

Field: Development anthropology; Development studies; Ethnology; Economic geography; Curse; Resource curse; International political economy; Authoritarianism; International development; Territorial waters
Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: Oil in Chad and Equatorial Guinea: Widening the Focus of the Resource Curse
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while the resource curse theory explains some aspects of the socio-economic and political dynamics, it does not fully account for all the complexities of these dynamics. Specifically, the research revealed that historical trajectories, the strategies of local and non-local actors, and the international political economy play a crucial role in shaping the socio-economic and political landscape of these countries.
What_was_studied: The socio-economic and political dynamics among the populations of Equatorial Guinea and Chad's southern region of Doba resulting from oil exploration and extraction in their territorial waters were studied, specifically focusing on how these dynamics are influenced by the 'resource curse' concept and its limitations in explaining all similarities and differences between the cases.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Therefore, policymakers should prioritize a more comprehensive understanding of the interplay between oil extraction, local and international factors, and historical contexts to develop effective poverty reduction strategies in these regions.

Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: Gender, Land and Water in the Poverty Reduction Strategy and Country Assistance Strategy for Sri Lanka
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study finds that while gender mainstreaming is still high on the donor agenda, operationalization of gender mainstreaming strategies remains a challenging task, and strong institutions are lacking to support adequate financial and human resources for effective integration of gender concerns at the country level.
What_was_studied: This study assesses the implementation of gender mainstreaming strategies in Sri Lanka's poverty reduction strategy and the World Bank's country assistance strategy for Sri Lanka, with a focus on the agricultural sector, over a 10-year period since the adoption of the Beijing Declaration.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that the World Bank should prioritize strengthening institutions and providing adequate resources to effectively integrate gender concerns in poverty reduction strategies, particularly in the agricultural sector, to scale up successful interventions and expand their reach.

Title: Introduction to the Special Issue: Policies for Inclusive Development in Africa.
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The case studies revealed that inclusive development strategies in employment, social protection, and governance have positive effects on reducing poverty and improving well-being among marginalized groups.
What_was_studied: This paper examines the empirical outcomes and processes of inclusive development policies in selected African countries.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the findings, policy makers should prioritize investments in education, healthcare, and social protection programs to reduce poverty and improve well-being for all, especially women and children.

Title: The Luxury of Lockdown.
primary_category: Health disparities
What_was_found: The study found that containment policies have a significant impact in reducing the fatality rate, with a three-week lag. The effectiveness increases with per capita income, but workplace closure is ineffective in low-income countries.
What_was_studied: Regression analysis based on data from Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker and the World Bank datasets for 169 countries during the pandemic's early stages.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize implementing containment policies with at least a three-week lag and targeted lockdown measures for low-income countries to reduce the pandemic's fatality rate.

Title: Donors' Interest in Water and Sanitation Subsectors.
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found that donors allocated W&S aid by focusing on governments in general with higher governance indicators, and poorer countries received a higher allocation of aid.
What_was_studied: This study analyzes the commitment of donors to water and sanitation (W&S) aid, comparing it with the Sustainable Development Goals' (SDGs) intentions, during the period between 2002 and 2004.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on the finding, it is essential to revise aid allocation strategies to prioritize infrastructural targets and ensure that W&S aid reaches poorer countries to achieve the SDGs' goals in this sector.

Title: Financing for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the Era of COVID-19 and Beyond.
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), global economic growth is expected to slow down from 6.1% in 2021 to 3.2% in 2022 and further to 2.7% in 2023 due to external shocks and the pandemic's impact, which has constrained fiscal capacity and impedes SDG achievement, particularly for low-income countries.
What_was_studied: The economic and social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on developing countries, including supply chain disruptions due to the Ukraine war and their effect on global economic growth, SDGs achievement, and poverty reduction strategies.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To address the challenge of achieving SDGs and sustaining livelihoods in developing countries, policymakers should prioritize resource mobilization from both domestic and international sources to support poverty reduction strategies, healthcare systems, and sustainable development initiatives.

Title: WIDER Working Paper - Poverty and ethnicity among black South Africans
primary_category: Employment; Gender and poverty; Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that there is a significant ethnic gap in poverty levels and flows between the Xhosa and Zulu groups compared to the Sotho/Tswana, with the former experiencing more disadvantages in location, demographic structure, education, and labor market outcomes.
What_was_studied: This article investigated inequalities across the major black ethnic groups in South Africa, accounting for 80% of the country's population, during the post-apartheid era (1994-2016) using data from various surveys and censuses.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the persistent ethnic disparities in poverty and socioeconomic outcomes, policymakers should prioritize targeted interventions to address these inequalities, particularly in location-specific economic development, education reform, and labor market access for marginalized groups.

Title: Prioritizing Rural Investments in Africa: A Hybrid Evaluation Approach Applied to Uganda
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Rural poverty
What_was_found: The study found that AR&ES is the most effective strategy for promoting economic growth and reducing poverty in rural Uganda, while investments in irrigation infrastructure may potentially reduce the overall benefits of the agricultural investment plan.
What_was_studied: This article evaluates the effectiveness of agricultural research and extension services (AR&ES), rural feeder roads, and irrigation infrastructure on economic growth and poverty reduction in rural Uganda using ex post evaluation data combined with an economy-wide model.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the findings, the government should prioritize investments in AR&ES to maximize economic growth and poverty reduction in rural Uganda, and revise its recent shift in emphasis from extension services to irrigation infrastructure.

Title: From Civil Wars to Drug Wars: The Limits of Decentralization Policies in Central America
primary_category: Health disparities; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that decentralization policies have led to increased local participation in social programs, but the weak capacity of the state to reduce social inequalities and the absence of national governments to supervise policy implementation have generated unforeseen consequences, including exacerbated poverty and violence.
What_was_studied: This study examines the impact of decentralization policies on poverty reduction, social cohesion, and conflict resolution in post-conflict reconstruction contexts, specifically in Central America.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the challenges associated with severe weather and increased violence, it is crucial for decision-makers to prioritize strengthening the state's capacity to reduce social inequalities and ensure accountability and transparency in policy implementation, especially in post-conflict reconstruction contexts.

Authors: Mequanint B. Melesse; Amos Nyangira Tirra; Yabibal M. Walle; Michael Hauser

Title: Understanding the Determinants of Aspirations in Rural Tanzania: Does Financial Literacy Matter?
primary_category: Child poverty; Education access; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Rural poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The study found a robust positive correlation between financial literacy and aspirations, suggesting that improving financial literacy can raise aspirations and potentially improve future investments and forward-looking behavior among poor individuals.
What_was_studied: This study analyzed financial literacy and aspirations of over 2000 Tanzanian households to determine if financial literacy is associated with aspirations.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Based on these findings, policymakers should prioritize programs that improve financial literacy to raise aspirations and promote sustainable development for marginalized populations.

Authors: Elizabeth Presler-Marshall; Nicola Jones; Sarah Baird; Rebecca Dutton; Workneh Yadete
Field: Gender and development; Context (archaeology); Service provider; Poison control; Criminology; Sociology; Psychology; Service (business); Political science; Social change; Social transformation; Medicine; Geography; Environmental health; Business; Archaeology; Marketing; Law

Title: 'Mind the Gaps': Exploring Regional and Gender Patterns in Threats to Ethiopian Adolescents' Bodily Integrity
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: Girls are less able than boys to enjoy freedom of movement and control over their bodies, and age-related violence is often deeply gendered in ways that are context specific. Differences in service provisioning augment already large gaps between adolescents in different regions.
What_was_studied: This article assesses violence against adolescents in Ethiopia using mixed methods data collected in 2019 and 2020 from three diverse rural regions, including surveys completed by 5539 girls and boys as well as 819 qualitative interviews with adolescents, caregivers, community members, and service providers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To tackle threats to adolescents' bodily integrity, awareness-raising efforts should be twinned with improved access to education, health, social protection, and justice services. Policymakers should scale up investments in these areas and prioritize them in regional development plans to address the identified gaps.

Title: Gender Inclusivity of India's Digital Financial Revolution for Attainment of SDGs: Macro Achievements and the Micro Experiences of Targeted Initiatives.
primary_category: Gender and poverty; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while India has made great advances in promoting digital financial inclusion, it has struggled to achieve gender parity even within specific finance-focused programmes designed to improve gender inclusivity.
What_was_studied: This paper takes stock of how India's digital financial revolution has affected financial transactions and services with a focus on gender inclusivity for the attainment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up the benefits of digital financial inclusion for women, policymakers should prioritize and fund initiatives that promote gender inclusive finance and monitor progress towards gender parity in these programs.

Keywords: Microfinance; Participation; Village Banks; South Africa
Title: Wither Participatory Banking? Experiences with Village Banks in South Africa
primary_category: Financial inclusion; Food insecurity; Income poverty; Intersectional poverty
What_was_found: The study found that while members of the Village Bank reported high levels of participation, including attending meetings and contributing to decision-making processes, there was limited actual participation and a lack of transparency in organizational operations. Furthermore, conflicts were often resolved through informal means rather than through formal mechanisms.
What_was_studied: Four communities in South Africa that belong to a Village Bank, an organization that promotes member ownership and control, were examined through interviews and observations to analyze members’ experiences of participation and organizational transparency.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policymakers should prioritize the development of democratic participatory processes within microfinance institutions to ensure that members have a real voice in decision-making and to promote transparency and accountability. This could include implementing more robust governance structures, providing training on conflict resolution mechanisms, and increasing civil society engagement with Village Banks.

Field: Development anthropology; Per capita income; Development studies; Economics; Poverty; Chronic poverty; Household income; Human development (humanity); Socioeconomics; Development economics; International development
Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: Consumption insurance and vulnerability to poverty : a synthesis of the evidence from Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Mali, Mexico and Russia
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Intersectional poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The research found that households with lower levels of consumption insurance are more vulnerable to poverty, and are more likely to use informal coping mechanisms such as reducing food intake or selling assets to cope with shocks. The study also found that the use of formal coping mechanisms is associated with higher levels of well-being among household members.
What_was_studied: This paper brings together some of the empirical work conducted by IFPRI researchers which investigates linkages among the degree of consumption insurance, households' vulnerability to poverty, and household use of formal and informal coping mechanisms using the same empirical approach in five different countries during the period 2015-2019.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Policy makers should prioritize the development and implementation of comprehensive consumption insurance programs to protect vulnerable households from poverty, and ensure access to formal coping mechanisms to support household well-being.

Authors: Maheen Sultan; Jennifer Saeger; Sabina Faiz Rashid; Mohammed Ashraful Haque; Sahida Khondaker

Title: ‘Do Poor People’s Dreams Ever Come True?’ Educational Aspirations and Lived Realities in Urban Slums in Dhaka, Bangladesh
primary_category: Child poverty; Chronic poverty; Education access; Housing insecurity; Income poverty; Rural poverty; Urban poverty
What_was_found: High educational and professional aspirations among adolescents and their parents, with parental support being an important predictor of both current enrolment and adolescent aspirations. Location is also an important predictor of adolescent aspirations and enrolment.
What_was_studied: Quantitative and qualitative data collected in 2017 and 2018 by Gender and Adolescence: Global Evidence (GAGE) with adolescents aged 10–17 across three low-income areas in Dhaka to explore adolescent educational attainment, aspirations, and environmental factors that constrain both.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up support for adolescent education in urban slums, policymakers should prioritize infrastructure and services, integration into the city, and stability of the community (including schools and facilities), along with higher incomes and better employment opportunities for households.

Field: Agriculture; Psychological resilience; Development studies; Natural disaster; Political science; Poverty; Empowerment; Livelihood; Economic growth; Developing country
Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: Understanding the Aspirations of Farming Communities in Developing Countries: A Systematic Review of the Literature
primary_category: Chronic poverty; Income poverty; Sustainable development; Urban poverty
What_was_found: The analysis of 22 studies identified from 419 research articles sheds light on the relationships between aspirations, agriculture, women’s empowerment, poverty, and rural youth. Aspirations of the rural poor play a significant role in shaping their activities and investments.
What_was_studied: This study surveys the panorama of research on the importance of aspirations of farming communities, identifies research gaps and prospects for future research.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: To scale up successful programs that raise the aspirations of rural farming communities, expand support for women's empowerment, and prioritize resilience-building efforts in areas prone to natural disasters.

Field: Development anthropology; The Imaginary; Sociology; Human rights; Law and economics; Basic needs; Ethnology; Relationalism; Closet; Gender and development; International development

Title: Hiding Relations: The Irony of ‘Effective Aid’
primary_category: Child poverty; Gender and poverty; Sustainable development
What_was_found: The research found that while UK aid did lead to some improvements in child poverty indicators, the results were often short-lived and inconsistent, suggesting that a more relational approach to development may be necessary for sustainable impact.
What_was_studied: The study analyzed the impact of UK aid on child poverty reduction in sub-Saharan Africa between 2010 and 2015, using a mixed-methods approach combining surveys, case studies, and interviews.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: Given the mixed results of UK aid in reducing child poverty, decision makers should prioritize a relational approach to development, investing in long-term partnerships with local organizations and emphasizing capacity building and empowerment of marginalized communities.

Field: Cash transfers; Politics; Social policy; Cash; Conditional cash transfer; Development studies; Development anthropology; Political science; Sociology; Economic growth; Social transformation; Political economy; Public economics; Development economics; Economics; Social change; Poverty; Gender and development; Law; Finance
Journal/Venue: The European Journal of Development Research
Title: The Politics of Who Gets What and Why: Learning from the Targeting of Social Cash Transfers in Zambia
primary_category: Intersectional poverty; Social protection
What_was_found: The analysis finds that local ideas of deservingness led to the rejection of eligible fit-for-work recipients, and changes to the targeting model were made to prioritize incapacitated households. The study highlights the importance of considering popular perceptions of deservingness in the design and analysis of targeting mechanisms.
What_was_studied: This in-depth study examines the implementation of a contested cash transfer model in Zambia and its targeting mechanisms, using interviews with government and policy actors, as well as focus group discussions in communities receiving cash transfers.
Why_it_matters_for_policy: The findings suggest that targeting mechanisms should prioritize incapacitated households and take into account local notions of deservingness to ensure that social protection policies are effective and equitable. Policymakers should scale up cash transfer programs and revise targeting models to better reflect the needs of the most vulnerable populations.

Authors: Jean-Francois Trani; Parul Bakhshi; Ayan A. Noor; Ashraf Mashkoor
